News.title: Youth minimum wage hikes are costing people jobs, Kemi Badenoch warns
News.content:
Next

KEMI Badenoch has warned that generous hikes to the youth minimum wage have made it harder for them to get jobs.

The Tory leader condemned Labour’s manifesto commitment to bring the 18-20 pay floor in line with over-21s.

Since the election ministers have been steadily “equalising” the two rates, which currently stand at £10.85 and £12.71 respectively.



But Ms Badenoch claimed it had led to a youth unemployment crisis, along with tax rises on employers.



She told The Sun: “I don’t think it was the right thing for them to equalise the minimum wage for young people across the board.

“No one has done that in the 30 years that we’ve had the minimum wage.

“There was a reason for that, and that is that a young person who doesn’t have experience is harder to employ than an older person who does have experience, so you need to make it easier to hire young people.

“Labour will tell you that they were being fair by making it the same. All that’s happened is that young people aren’t getting jobs anymore.”

She said that young people need a better chance to get their foot on the jobs ladder, rather than being priced out before they have even started.

The Conservative leader also claimed youth unemployment had risen by 175,000 under Labour, totalling three-quarters of a million.

The Tories have pledged to halve employers’ National Insurance for young workers to make hiring them more affordable.



She argued that businesses need incentives to give young people their first opportunity, particularly in sectors that rely on apprenticeships and practical skills.

Ms Badenoch also highlighted the importance of apprenticeships, saying the Conservatives want to put money into training rather than university courses that leave graduates struggling to find work.

Touring a beauty salon in Essex, she said: “Too many young people are going to university when actually something else would be better for them.

“And whether it’s jobs like this in the beauty sector or in construction, things that AI can’t take away from you.

“AI-proof jobs that do require a human element are something we’re very interested in supporting.”

News.title: Dirty NAPPIES, children’s toys & a caravan dumped in huge fly-tip outside abandoned school have left our road in ruin
News.content:
TRASH TALK Dirty NAPPIES, children’s toys & a caravan dumped in huge fly-tip outside abandoned school have left our road in ruin







Next

DIRTY nappies, kids’ toys and even a caravan have been dumped in a massive fly-tip outside an abandoned school, leaving the road in ruins.

Locals are up in arms about the rubbish being allowed to spill out onto a quiet, residential street in Gloucester.



And shocking piles of waste have built up outside the abandoned Colwell Grammar School, with councillors demanding action to clear the mess and find those responsible.

Gloucester City Councillor Roseanna Marshall said residents had also raised concerns about fires and anti-social behaviour at the site.



She said: “The caravan and other rubbish is just sitting there left to rot.

“I had feedback the other day about how bad it was getting.



“It would just make it a lot nicer if there was something done with the building.”

Cllr Usman Bhaimia was just as shocked.



He said: “The state of this site is appalling and completely unacceptable.

“Residents deserve better than a derelict building surrounded by rubbish.

“The sheer amount of waste that has accumulated is shocking, and some of it is now spilling out towards the pavement.

“It needs to be dealt with before the situation gets any worse.

“We are asking the relevant authorities and the owner to work together to get the waste removed, prevent further fly-tipping and investigate who is responsible.”



He added that clearing the rubbish would only solve the immediate problem, with the future of the building also needing to be addressed.

“We want to see progress on the planning application.

“Four years after it was submitted, there is still no decision.

“We need clarity about what remains outstanding, what needs to happen next and how the application can finally be brought to a determination.

“Leaving a prominent site like this in limbo for years benefits nobody.



“Residents need to know there is a clear plan for its future.”

The former grammar school closed in 1988 before later becoming part of Gloucester College, which vacated the building in 2007.

The site has remained empty for years and parts of the building have fallen into disrepair.

A planning application to convert it into flats was submitted in 2022, with amended plans lodged in 2023 and consultations continuing into this year.

No decision has yet been made.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Cllr Marshall said the building’s current owner lived abroad and was “really hard to get in contact with”.

The Sun Online has contacted Gloucester City Council for comment.

News.title: Civil servant ‘fraudulently held down FIVE taxpayer-funded jobs at same time to rake in hundreds of thousands of pounds’
News.content:
JOB 'JUGGLER' Civil servant ‘fraudulently held down FIVE taxpayer-funded jobs at same time to rake in hundreds of thousands of pounds’







Next

A CIVIL servant fraudulently held five different taxpayer-funded jobs as part of an alleged £250,000 con, a court has heard.

Kashim Chowdhury was contracted to work a staggering 183 hours a week, jurors at Southwark Crown Court were told.



The 55-year-old, from Whitechapel, east London, is accused of lying about his work status to get a string of full- time roles across government departments and bodies.

Between February and September Chowdhury earned a staggering £350,000 from eight different employers, the court was told.



Prosecutors say Chowdhury “exploited” the work from home culture which began during the Covid-19 pandemic.

He hid his multiple jobs and took sick leave from some employers to manage the workload.

In one incident, described by prosecutor Lucy Organ as “laughable”, Chowdhury allegedly wore white make-up during a video call to appear sick.

He is accused of but denies nine counts of fraud.

At the opening of his trial on Tuesday, the court heard that he began working for Tower Hamlets Council in February 2020.

He then went on to take a second job with the Department for Environment Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) in April 2021.



The two roles overlapped for more than a year, the court heard, and for four months in 2022, he also held a third position with East London NHS Trust.

After leaving the council, prosecutors say Chowdhury continued working for Defra.

He also gained further jobs with the Department of Health and Social Care, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office.

In May 2023, he was allegedly being paid a salary for five full-time jobs.

Jurors were told that Chowdhury made false representations about his existing employment when applying for the roles.



Ms Organ said: “Clearly, he would not have been employed by his employers if they had known he had multiple other full-time jobs.”

The court heard that Chowdhury had told his various bosses that he had to work from home to care for his “unwell” mother.

His workload eventually became “too much to cope with” and his performance suffered, the court was told.

He then allegedly took sick leave from some jobs while continuing to work in his other positions.

The court heard that Chowdhury was signed off work for some jobs due to “mixed anxiety and a depressive disorder.”



However he did not hand his sick note to all his employers and continued to work in various roles.

In May 2023, his UKHSA manager Aleesha Adams arranged a video call to discuss Chowdhury’s sick leave.

The civil servant appeared on camera “coughing and blowing his nose”, the court heard.

Ms Adams said that his face appeared white while his neck was a different colour, prosecutors say.

During the meeting she saw the make-up on his forehead begin to separate, showing his real skin underneath, the court heard.



Ms Organ told jurors: “There could be no doubt about it, the defendant had applied make-up to his face for this Teams meeting to try and pretend to his line manager that he was unwell.

“This almost laughable incident demonstrates, we say, quite how far the defendant was willing to go in his deceit.”

The alleged fraudster also “messed up” by logging on to the meeting with a Defra email address, the court was told.

He allegedly told his manager that it could be an old email address.

However the prosecutor said this was a “lie” to conceal the fact he was working elsewhere at the same time.



Jurors heard that the alleged frauds came to light after the National Fraud Initiative alerted DEFRA to them.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Ms Organ said that between March 2020 and September 2023, Chowdhury had over £300,000 in credits into his three bank accounts and nearly £250,000 in debits.

The trial continues.

News.title: Bear ‘steals woman’s corpse from grave’ as a dozen more human skulls spark fears of rampage
News.content:
Next

A RAVAGING bear is feared to have dug up a woman’s grave and stolen her corpse as Russia reels from a record wave of deadly attacks.

A family made the gruesome discovery while visiting their grandmother’s resting place in Magadan, Russia.



Her grave had been ripped apart, with the woman’s clothes scattered across the desecrated burial plot and her body nowhere to be found.

Initial reports claimed around a dozen human skulls had been discovered just 350 yards from the empty grave, with bear tracks spotted nearby.



But officials searching the cemetery later found no trace of the missing remains or the reported skulls.

Authorities are now investigating whether a marauding bear raided the grave and dragged away the woman’s corpse.

READ MORE IN WORLD NEWS UNBEAR-LIEVABLE Moment family of FOUR bears climb into car after opening driver's door

City hall official Ekaterina Kramnik said: “Following an inspection of the cemetery grounds by a commission involving relevant specialists, no human remains were discovered at the burial plot or in the surrounding area.”

She added: “The activity of wild animals is being considered as one possible cause of the grave being disturbed, but this theory requires further investigation.”

Officials have yet to establish what happened to the missing body, with plans now underway to install an electric fence around the cemetery.

The macabre discovery comes as Russia battles what has been described as its worst summer for bear attacks in living memory.



At least 29 people have reportedly been killed this year, while hundreds more have suffered injuries in terrifying encounters with the predators.

Four more suspected victims have now emerged in the Irkutsk region, where a string of fatal attacks has sparked fresh alarm.

A 71-year-old man was reportedly mauled to death near the River Ilim in a savage attack captured on camera.

The pensioner could not be saved, and the killer bear was subsequently shot dead.



Elsewhere, the body of a 56-year-old man was discovered near a remote hunting cabin close to the Tareya River.

Investigators found numerous wounds consistent with a vicious bear attack.

Human remains were also discovered near Kaimonovo, believed to belong to a 47-year-old man who had vanished several months earlier.

In another horror incident, a 55-year-old worker was mauled to death by a bear at a residential cabin in the Kazachinsko-Lensky district.



Experts fear the predators are increasingly losing their fear of humans as dwindling food supplies drive them out of forests and towards populated areas.

The growing threat has sparked panic across parts of Russia, with authorities scrambling to respond to reports of bears roaming near settlements.

The cemetery mystery follows another terrifying bear attack in Russia in which a teenager reportedly escaped death after his mobile phone exploded while the predator was mauling him.

The 15-year-old was savaged by the beast after climbing a tree in a desperate bid to escape.

But the ferocious animal dragged him to the ground before sinking its teeth into his body.



Moments later, the boy’s phone reportedly exploded and caught fire, scaring the bear off in the process.

A 24-year-old witness who was with the boy recalled: “I heard him scream, turned my head, and saw the bear already dragging him down from the tree, so I unleashed the dogs.”

He said the phone battery apparently exploded when the bear “sank its teeth into the teenager’s buttocks”.

The teenager suffered devastating injuries to his head and body, alongside burns from the exploding phone.

He was rushed to hospital for a gruelling three-hour operation after suffering serious injuries to his chest, brain and abdomen.



Sergei Kovyazin, chief physician of Biysk Central City Hospital, said: “The patient arrived with multiple injuries to his head, scalp, facial bones and neck.

“These injuries presented the greatest challenge.”

The horror unfolded around 12 miles from the remote village of Solton, where the teenager and his companion had reportedly ventured into the forest to check on his family’s bees.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Three rapid-response teams and at least a dozen hunters were deployed to track down and kill the bear.

But treacherous weather hampered the search as authorities continued their hunt for the dangerous predator.

News.title: Breaking Bad star RJ Mitte’s devastating texts to friend reveal his own private struggles over ‘brutal’ rejection
News.content:
Next

TRAGIC Breaking Bad star RJ Mitte was crushed by continual rejection in Hollywood, a series of text messages have revealed.

The actor, 34, who died by suicide on Monday, was open about the obstacles he encountered as a performer with cerebral palsy.



MailOnline claims that in messages spanning eight years, Mitte questioned why casting directors were hesitant to consider actors with disabilities for characters whose stories were not specifically about disability.

His experience on iconic TV show Breaking Bad – in which he played the son of Brian Cranston’s central character – had brought him considerable recognition.



But the runaway success of the show did not guarantee a steady stream of acting work.

In an April 2017 message, Mitte described how casting professionals sometimes ruled him out because a character had not been written as disabled.

Read more on RJ Mitte 'my person' What we know about RJ Mitte’s fiancee Kennedy Suarez



“When I go for a part, they sometimes tell me that it’s not a character with a disability, and I’m like why can’t the character be disabled?” he wrote, according to the outlet.

“They get real uncomfortable when I say that.”

Mitte wanted casting professionals to understand that disability did not have to define a character or determine whether an actor was suitable for a role.

His frustration became more explicit in another message that month.



“I can do any role, but some of [the casting agents and directors] are a**h***s who won’t even look at me,” he wrote.

“I want to put them on blast, but I won’t now.”

Mitte spent five years on Breaking Bad, earning worldwide plaudits, while establishing himself as a familiar face on television.

But once the show finished, he spoke about how difficult it was to turn that visibility into consistent employment.

The actor continued taking on projects, including international productions, but not every opportunity led to lasting work.



In December 2017, he described the disappointment of a television pilot that never moved forward.

“Worked on a pilot that didn’t go, a few months ago. Brutal biz,” he wrote.

A little over a year later, he was weighing the realities of working abroad while trying to maintain a career at home.

After filming an independent project in Sydney, Australia, he told his friend he was concerned about finding enough work in the United States.

“I did a job in Sydney, and it was fun,” he wrote in February 2019.



“But it’s a film not going to be here, it’s Australian, I hope I can find stuff here. I would like to work enough to keep my [health] insurance. Pain in the ass lol.”

The financial uncertainty behind his career was another source of stress. Even with a major television credit to his name, Mitte still had to think about the practicalities of securing regular employment and health insurance.

When the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted film and television production, he looked for other ways to remain active. In June 2020, he discussed completing work in Canada and taking on voice-over projects.

He also recognized the importance of staying visible to casting directors.

“I’ve got to figure out more work,” he wrote. “I need to keep myself relevant lol.”



He offered to participate in interviews and promotional appearances, hoping they would help bring new opportunities his way.

“I just need to remind people to book me.”

By March 2021, Mitte was raising another concern: the possibility that the pandemic had intensified existing prejudices against performers with disabilities.

“Gotta convince people that I’m not going to die of Covid,” he wrote.

“There’s a backlash about people with disabilities, they think that we can’t be insured or that we are going to die in the middle of a scene, its bullshit.”



Mitte was diagnosed with cerebral palsy when he was three.

As a child, he wore leg braces and sometimes used crutches or a wheelchair. In adulthood, the condition was most noticeable in his left hand and speech.

He used his platform to advocate for a more inclusive entertainment industry, becoming an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children’s.

His message was consistent: disabled actors should be considered for a broad range of characters, rather than being limited to stories about their medical conditions.

In a public statement in 2016, he described the kind of television representation he wanted to see.



“I would love to switch on my TV and see a disabled person talking about something they are genuinely interested in or acting out a part that doesn’t just focus on their impairment,” he said.

Privately, however, the lack of meaningful roles continued to weigh on him.

In April 2022, Mitte told his friend that many of the scripts arriving on his desk offered little opportunity to develop a character.

“Looking for interesting stuff to do, getting a lot of scripts where I would be a prop and they don’t want to give any depth, 3 lines if that,” he wrote.

His response was to begin creating his own material.



“I’m writing my own s**t now.”

By August that year, he was still struggling to secure on-screen work.

“Just doing animation, no one wants me on screen.. it’s annoying as f*.”

Rather than abandon his efforts to reach audiences, Mitte began considering other formats. In July 2025, he discussed the possibility of joining a reality competition, including Dancing with the Stars.

He saw the show as a potential opportunity to demonstrate his abilities to people who knew him primarily through his television role. But he also wanted to avoid being presented as an object of amusement.



“Now I would do a good reality show, was thinking that dancing would be a good fit, just to show that I can do that s*,” he wrote.

“But I would have to make sure that any reality would be dignity, I don’t want to be laughed at, but would consider something that could give me a platform.”

The messages capture a performer who continued searching for new ways to work, even as he questioned whether the industry was willing to look beyond established assumptions about disability.

“There’s a lot I could do, if given the chance,” he wrote in another message.

His concerns were still apparent during an appearance on The Joe Vulpis Podcast last week, when he discussed the circumstances that led to his casting on Breaking Bad.



Mitte explained that Walter White Jr. had been conceived as a character with cerebral palsy, making his disability integral to the original concept rather than an obstacle to overcome during casting.

“I think casting individuals with disabilities is very tricky,” he said.

“My character was written with someone with [cerebral] palsy [in mind]. That was from the beginning. That was always the case.”

He added that series creator Vince Gilligan had drawn inspiration from a college friend with cerebral palsy who used forearm crutches.

“And so it really felt real playing this character and getting into the groove with this character.”



Mitte was also preparing to lead the upcoming Western Forgotten Outlaw, playing Bub Meeks, a childhood friend of notorious outlaw Butch Cassidy.

Following his death, director Nik Tizekker told TMZ that he intended to proceed with the film in honor of the actor’s wishes, although a replacement would be needed for the leading role.

Mitte reportedly died in Brownsville, Texas, where he lived with his fiancée, Kennedy Suarez. TMZ reported, citing a county official, that his death was being investigated as a suicide.

The actor proposed to Suarez in October 2025 at a charity event supporting United Cerebral Palsy.

In a statement following his death, his representative remembered him as an actor, philanthropist and dedicated disability rights advocate who worked to raise awareness and encourage greater inclusion.



News of his death also devastated those who had worked alongside him on Breaking Bad. A source close to Cranston said that the actor was struggling to process the loss of his former co-star.

“The bond they shared, both on and off screen, is something he will never forget,” the source told MailOnline, describing the show’s cast as a family to Cranston.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Although the pair had not seen each other recently, the source said Cranston continued to remember Mitte fondly.

“Bryan hadn’t seen RJ in some time, but that doesn’t mean he wasn’t always thinking about him, it is just a really sad day.”

News.title: Girl, 8, crushed to death by tractor after children released handbrake by accident
News.content:
TRACTOR HORROR Girl, 8, crushed to death by tractor after children released handbrake by accident







Next

AN eight-year-old girl has tragically died after a parked tractor suddenly rolled backwards and crushed her.

Emine Temel was playing with friends in a garden in Turkey on October 9 when disaster struck.

Some of the children clambered onto the massive machine and started messing with its controls, according to local reports.

They then accidentally shifted the gear into neutral before releasing the handbrake, causing the vehicle to roll backwards.





Emine was reportedly standing behind the heavy tractor when it began to move and was unable to escape its path.

Emergency services rushed to the property in Ikisu, Mardin province after neighbours raised the alarm.

But little Emine suffered severe injuries in the horror accident and was pronounced dead at the scene.

The youngster’s body was later taken to Mardin Training and Research Hospital for a post-mortem examination.

Her remains were then handed over to her grieving family for burial, with Emine laid to rest following a ceremony at a cemetery in Ikisu.

Authorities have launched a probe to establish the circumstances leading up to the terrifying accident.

The investigation is set to examine how the tractor had been parked and whether anyone was responsible for failing to secure it.

The tragedy comes after a three-year-old girl died after being struck by a car just a day before her birthday.



Elif Mavi Avli and her mother Merve were walking in Odunpazari in September when the horrifying collision unfolded.

Harrowing CCTV footage shows the mother and daughter crossing the road when a vehicle, driven by 40-year-old Fatos Akil Bilgesoy, hits them.

Merve suffered minor injuries in the smash and immediately rushed to her daughter as horrified onlookers hurried to help.

Despite emergency medical treatment, the three-year-old succumbed to her injuries and sadly died.

News.title: We can win back the Red Wall, Badenoch insists – as she rejects accusations of cosying up to millionaires in South
News.content:
WALL TO PLAY FOR We can win back the Red Wall, Badenoch insists – as she rejects accusations of cosying up to millionaires in South







Next

KEMI Badenoch insisted the Tories can win back the Red Wall as she rejected claims she is courting millionaires in the South.

The Conservative leader told The Sun her party was targeting everyone who wants to “work hard and get on”.



Her comments came after Reform branded her inheritance tax proposal a “tax cut for multi-millionaires”, fuelling criticism that her pitch favoured wealthy voters.

But challenged over whether she could reclaim the Red Wall, she said: “Yes, because we are going after all of those people who want to work hard and get on.



“We’re not just looking for southern votes or wealthy votes.

“That’s why I had lots of policies. So the people who say that didn’t listen to the whole conference speech. They are focusing on inheritance tax.”

Mrs Badenoch, who was visiting an Essex beauty salon for British Beauty Week, also pointed to plans for housebuilding and her Britannia Shield missile defence system, arguing they would create jobs in construction, defence and technology.

She added: “We also have policies to get people off welfare and into work. So even people who aren’t earning, we’re going to help create jobs with businesses, so that there’s something for everybody. That’s what my conference speech was about.”

The Tory leader has been buoyed by a YouGov poll putting her party on 23 per cent, up three points and ahead of Reform on 21 per cent – although still behind Labour on 24 per cent, with the pollster cautioning the conference bounce could prove temporary.

Mrs Badenoch acknowledged the challenge of rebuilding trust, saying: “I know that many people felt let down by the previous Conservative government, and we have owned up to the mistakes that we’ve made.”



Appealing directly to voters who had deserted the party, she continued: “We want the people who left us to go to Reform to come back home, so we want to appeal to Reform voters. They’re the ones we want back.

“I tell people it’s the Reform voters that I’m talking to now, not the Reform politicians. They’re a different kettle of fish, but I think that the more people see about the Conservative Party with me leading it, the more they like it.”

On whether she could keep the Tories ahead of Reform, Mrs Badenoch declared: “Yes, because I’m just getting started. There is still a lot more to come.”

News.title: KFC and sordid toys – how paedo teaching assistant groomed boy for sex… was THIS obsession the key to her sick crimes?
News.content:
Next

SHE was known by pupils and neighbours for her very eye-catching car – but was it behind her twisted desire to play out a bondage sex fantasy with a 15-year-old schoolboy?

Teaching assistant Melanie Rock groomed the teenager with trips to KFC and an arcade before taking him home on Halloween and showing him her sex toys and pink fluffy handcuffs.





Her unique Ford Fiesta was wrapped with a picture of the “sexy” comic book character Harley Quinn, recently played by Margot Robbie.

She also had Harley Quinn hot pants which she paraded in front of the schoolboy at her home while they ate pizza, smoked vapes and went trick or treating.

In the DC Universe cartoons and films, Quinn is the maniacal and devious criminal girlfriend of the Joker, who undoes her enemies with tricks and guile.

Perhaps then the signs were obvious when Rock, 31, abused her power to begin a creepy campaign of grooming on her juvenile target.

The blonde, who looks older than her 34 years, was working at Medina College on the Isle of Wight when she ran into the boy in the school corridor after he had been kicked out of class.

She started messaging the teen on Instagram and lavished him with vapes and two designer Trapstar tracksuits costing £355.

A jury heard she wore low-cut tops to “tease and tickle his fancy”. And on Halloween during school half-term, Rock picked him up and took him to the seaside resort of Sandown where she gave him £25 to play on arcade machines.

The single mum then brought the lad home to her council flat in Cowes that she shared with her schoolgirl daughter and bought him a Domino’s pizza.





The court heard Rock invited him to her bedroom where he could smoke a vape and call his mother.

Rock then “koala hugged” him by stretching her legs around him on her bed.

The boy said: “It was like I was wearing her like a backpack.”

She also pointed him to a drawer containing a blue bag, pink fluffy handcuffs, black see-through lingerie and sex toys and paraded in Harley Quinn hot pants in front of him.

The boy said: “At first, it didn’t come across as weird at school.

“It felt like a teacher was actually there for me.

“But when I went around her house, and she showed me these things, it kind of freaked me out a bit.”

On another occasion she treated him to a meal at KFC.



But Rock was stopped from further action after she was busted eating with him at Pizza Hut just five minutes drive away from the school by another teacher who informed the authorities.

Rock told him to pretend to be her godson to avoid getting into trouble.

She realised her behaviour was about to be unmasked the next day in school when the lad texted her to say a teacher had asked about seeing them together.

Rock wrote to him: “I’m f***ed, I’m going to be sacked now.

“They’re going to ask a lot of questions and I’ll be sacked if they find out it’s me.

“If they keep asking I beg you don’t say my name please.

“Keep saying you was [sic] at the skate park.

“Delete my Instagram and the messages. I’ll do the same.

“Please no more contact unless in school. I beg beg don’t mention me as I’ll be done, trust.”

The school was told of the meeting and bosses called cops to investigate who arrested her two days later.



When officers searched the teaching assistant’s home they found nine sex toys, one pair of bondage shackles, and three evidence bags of lingerie.

The boy’s mother said she was alerted to the grooming by an assistant headteacher at the school.

She was told her son had spoken to safeguarding staff and the matter had been referred to police.

She said: “I was a bit taken aback and unsure what was happening.

“I asked her, ‘Has my son been groomed?’ and she just apologised.”

In her police interview Rock tried to deny the offences saying he had a “schoolboy crush” on her and that she felt “intimidated” by him.

She said: “I spoke to other teachers about the fact he’s followed me. I’ll turn around and he’s there, and I think this is ridiculous.

“Or I’ll be teaching in my unit and he looks in the windows. My boss said she thinks he’s got a schoolboy crush.



“I might have bumped into him outside of school, I can’t remember. I do remember one time at KFC.

“He was hungry and wanted food so I was like ‘fine’. I got him a little bit of food because he said he was hungry.

“I was doing my job. I’m a mum, I care too much and I was asked to keep an eye on him.

“I’m a staff member but I’m also a mum, when I hear a kid hasn’t been eating and everything I just go into mum mode.

“We did go to Pizza Hut because he said he was hungry. He said he had just eaten toast so I was worried for him.

“Then I had to take him to mine quickly because of a medical episode which was very embarrassing.”

She was also asked about her car.

The mum-of-one, who had previously worked at Carisbrooke College, another secondary school on the island, said: “I had a Ford Fiesta modified and covered in a Harley Quinn wrap.



“She’s a DC character, the Joker’s girlfriend.

“It’s like a sticker going around the car in bright bright colours, no one else on the island would have had it.”

Rock denied meeting a child following sexual grooming and sexual activity with a child by a person in a position of trust.

She said she had not behaved sexually towards the boy and denied the allegations concerning physical contact in her bedroom.

She firmly denied having a sexual motive.

Asked whether she had ‘koala hugged’ the boy, Rock replied: “No, hell no. Why would I hug a child apart from my own child?”

“Did you have a sexual interest in the child?” Ms Fargin asked.

“No,” Rock replied.



She also claimed not to remember having him in her house or why she sent him messages online.

Rock repeatedly said she could not remember meeting the teenager outside school, collecting him in her car or arranging to see him during the October half-term.

But she accepted that CCTV showed her with the boy at KFC.

After a four day trial the jury took less than two hours to find her guilty.

Judge Newton-Price KC adjourned the case for a pre-sentence report and granted her bail until the sentencing hearing on December 4.

Speaking to Rock following the jury’s verdict, the judge intimated she could face jail.

He said: “Melanie Rock, you have been convicted by the jury on compelling evidence.

“I want to know more about you before I proceed to sentence you on this matter.

“It’s obviously a serious matter. I am therefore going to ask a probation officer to interview you so I know more about you.

“I am going to give you bail pending your sentencing but that is no indication one way or another on the eventual outcome. This is serious, so the sentencing options must be open to me.”

News.title: MI5 chief warns of threats to UK from Russia, Iran and AI
News.content:
MI5 is devoting more resource to countering state threats than during the Cold War, the head of the intelligence service has said.

Sir Ken McCallum said threats from foreign adversaries had quadrupled in the last decade, with Russia "aggressor number one" as well as increased Iran-linked aggression against Jewish sites and military bases.

At an annual speech in London, MI5's chief said Russia was waging hybrid warfare at a time when AI was "supercharging the cyber-security contest between attackers and defenders".

He also warned of rising threats from "extreme right-wing terrorism" and said MI5 had "caught terrorists seeking to exploit Al," including by integrating the technology with drones.

He said the biggest threat from the misuse of AI was extremist groups using the technology to harness new and existing bioweapons.

However, he noted that work countering terrorism and state threats was now "pretty much of equal scale" which he described as a "huge shift" in recent years.

Sir Ken said Russia had stopped short of "conventional conflict" against Nato and is instead trying to unsettle European countries while its progress in its full-scale invasion of Ukraine is "minimal and horrifically costly".

Hybrid warfare or hybrid attacks are loose terms which tend to describe non-military methods, for example cyber-attacks, sabotage or misinformation, designed to exert pressure and destabilise an adversary.

These are quite often employed using proxies, but Russia always denies involvement in such attacks despite growing evidence to the contrary.

Sir Ken said MI5 successes in identifying and expelling Russian spies from the UK had left the Kremlin dependent on paying proxies for attempted attacks.

"With its traditional covert footprint eviscerated by almost 1,000 expulsions since the invasion, the Kremlin's global toolkit is weak, he said.

"So we see them scrambling to pay criminals to do their bidding."

He added: "These are not the actions of a great power with the strategic upper hand."

His comments come as a growing number of leaders across Europe have warned Russia may be preparing attacks to test their commitment to supporting Ukraine.

Asked after the speech about Prime Minister Andy Burnham's recent comments that Russia interfered with the Brexit referendum, Sir Ken said it was "not new news" that there had been attempts from Moscow but distinguished between "interference attempted" and "outcome achieved".

He said it was a matter of public record that there were pieces in Russian media and "so-called internet trolls and bot farms" seeking to influence the Brexit debate, but also stressed that the result of the 2016 referendum was "not in dispute".

He added that he was "worried" about the the ongoing debate on Russian interference.

"I am a little bit anxious that we don't play into our adversaries' hands by making these trolls look 10ft tall," he told reporters.

News.title: Man killed in tiger attack identified as William Chapman
News.content:
The man who was killed by a tiger after entering its enclosure at a wildlife park has been identified as William Chapman, the BBC understands.

Chapman entered the enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park near Doncaster shortly after 13:30 BST on Saturday and was pronounced dead at the scene, according to South Yorkshire Police.

An eyewitness described seeing him wearing headphones and "pacing around" near the enclosure before he went in and was attacked. Police confirmed he was visiting the park on his own.

A force spokesperson said his family was aware and was being supported by specialist officers. The park was evacuated after the incident and remains closed as investigations continue.

It is understood Chapman, who was in his mid-20s, was a former pupil of the Jackie Palmer Stage School in High Wycombe.

As a child, he appeared in the ITV production May Contain Nuts alongside Shirley Henderson, best known for playing Moaning Myrtle in the Harry Potter films, and Darren Boyd.

He also portrayed Edward Jenner in the BBC series True Stories.

News.title: Majority of English football clubs on the edge of financial disaster, report says
News.content:
English football's finances are "dangerously exposed, with the majority of clubs living on the edge of financial disaster", according to a landmark report by the independent football regulator.

Research by the watchdog found 94% of clubs are loss-making, and more than 60% of EFL and National League clubs are technically insolvent.

The regulator (IFR) warns of "a dangerous cocktail of rising debt and an over-reliance on owner funding, leaving clubs and their fans at risk".

The 'State of the Game' report also suggests that despite the economic success of the Premier League, the financial 'cliff-edges' between and within leagues have grown significantly.

The report says:

94% of clubs in the top five English leagues made losses in 2025-26

17 clubs across the EFL and National League would be loss-making even if their players played for free

66% of clubs could not survive for more than 90 days without new owner funding

29% of clubs reported they could not survive more than 30 days without such funding

68% of clubs have no contingency plan if their owner walks away

The IFR claims "the underlying foundations of the pyramid are under intense strain and require urgent reform", and its report "should serve as a wake-up call" for English football.

"Seventeen clubs are now trading in such a way that if their players played for free, their non-playing costs would mean they would go bust," IFR chair David Kogan told BBC Sport.

"Thirty-two clubs are operating on only 30 days' cash. If the owner chooses not to pay cash at the end of the month, those clubs go bust.

"That is a very, very risky scenario. This is the moment of addressing these problems before money starts to dry up.

"We can actually fix the house while the sun is still shining and that's essentially what our role is going to be in this."

News.title: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF
News.content:
There is increased concern about how much money countries are borrowing, but the IMF said the UK is doing better than all other major economies at this.

The IMF said the UK "basically stands out, along with India" when it comes to addressing the problem and by 2031 it is projected to have the lowest annual borrowing of the G7 group of countries, which includes Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the US.

Sir Howard Davies, former deputy governor of the Bank of England, said this was largely because the UK has a government with a majority which has committed to tackling the situation, which it is expected to achieve either through tax rises, cuts to public services, or a mix of both.

By contrast, he says the US has said little about reducing its deficit, while France and Germany don't have majority governments.

"So, we [the UK] are not great students, but we look somewhat better than some of the others we are sharing the class with," he said.

Meanwhile, the IMF's growth forecasts for the UK mean it is expected to have the second-fastest growing economy in the G7 this year along with Germany.

Sir Howard believes this should also be seen in context.

"We're still growing slowly. It's almost like saying we're winning a slow bicycle race here because other people are going backwards a bit more rapidly than we are."

News.title: Football regulator says he would quit over any political interference in Man City case
News.content:
The prime minister initially told the BBC of his concerns, before later denying his reaction had "downplayed the seriousness of the findings".

However, some Premier League clubs were so "astonished" by Burnham's stance that sources told BBC Sport they were "concerned" about political interference in the appeal process.

Burnham's previous role as mayor of Greater Manchester has led to questions about his relationship with City's Abu Dhabi ownership.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch demanded all details of meetings between the prime minister and senior figures at the club are released. The government released these details on Monday.

"As far as we, as the regulator, are concerned, we have a very, very clear course of action that is governed by statute and we are going to follow that course of action and no comment by any politician or indeed any individual is going to affect what we do", said Kogan.

"Process is going to drive what we do. Process will lead us to a conclusion.

"We cannot reach any conclusion at this stage because we don't know the outcome of any appeal and once we do then we will act accordingly."

The independent panel will hold a sanctions hearing - which could take months to convene - to decide the punishment.

City can appeal both the guilty verdicts and the sanction, leaving the club and the league in a state of chaos and uncertainty.

City's punishment could range from a huge fine, being deducted points or being ejected from the Premier League, to being stripped of the eight trophies they won in the affected period.

Asked how crucial it is that it was resolved as soon as possible, Kogan said: "I think it's very important."

Kogan added that the case was "raising very serious issues if Manchester City on appeal is found to be guilty of the allegations within those findings".

"We are waiting like everybody else to see what the independent panel will doâ¦ and then we will bring in a view in terms of our own investigation and statutory powers if we need to do so.

"Our powers relate to individual owners, directors and senior executives. They refer to whether people are in a position to run a club in a way that is safe, coherent and done with probity, and we will be examining those things."

An independent commission held a 42-day hearing in 2024 that led to the verdict announced last month, with City also guilty of all charges except one relating to non-cooperation with the Premier League investigation.

The commission's report said that "a number of important club witnesses gave false evidence in key respects and that some knowingly gave untrue and dishonest evidence".

News.title: Supreme Court hears appeal over Maids Moreton murder
News.content:
A former deputy church warden could not have have legally caused a university lecturer's death by giving him potentially sedated whisky, the Supreme Court has been told.

Benjamin Field, 35, was jailed for at least 36 years in 2019 after being found guilty of murdering 69-year-old Peter Farquhar in Maids Moreton, Buckinghamshire.

In April, appeal judges quashed Field's conviction and ordered a retrial, but said the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) could take the case to the Supreme Court first.

And on Tuesday, five justices at the UK's highest court were asked to consider whether Field could have made Mr Farquhar cause his own death without Field legally being responsible.

During his murder trial prosecutors said Field drove Farquhar to believe he was losing his mind, secretly drugging him and spiking his whisky so his death would appear to be suicide or an accident, allowing Field to inherit his home and money.

The case has previously been adapted into Bafta winning BBC drama The Sixth Commandment, starring Timothy Spall and Anne Reid.

Before his murder trial, Field admitted burglary and fraud offences connected with relationships he had formed with Farquhar and his neighbour, fellow pensioner Ann Moore-Martin, to persuade them to change their wills.

He received a concurrent 16-year sentence for those offences. He was cleared of conspiring or attempting to murder Moore-Martin and of possessing an article for use in fraud.

The hearing was due to conclude on Tuesday, with a decision expected at a later date.

News.title: BA flight forced to turn back over cracked window
News.content:
A British Airways flight en route to Portugal was forced to return to Gatwick Airport on Tuesday due to a minor technical issue, reported to be a cracked window.

Flight BA2660 was heading to Faro in the Algarve but diverted over north-western France in order to return to London Gatwick.

AirNav Radar, a flight data provider, posted on X that "a passenger window is cracked. Flight deck going through checks before deciding were to divert".

A spokesperson for British Airways said the plane landed safely at Gatwick due to a "minor technical issue" and passengers were due to resume their journey.

"We have apologised to customers for the delay to their journey, and our teams are working hard to get their travel plans back on track," they said.

Airnav Radar reported that the BA Airbus A321 squawked the 7700 emergency code, which is used when there are mechanical or technical problems on board aircraft.

Last week, a BA flight bound for Chicago spent five hours circling over Ireland, before turning back and landing at London Heathrow, where it had taken off.

The flight issued an emergency alert and passengers reported oxygen masks dropped in the cabin, as well as turbulence. Tracking data showed it rapidly descended from 37,000 feet to 9,000 feet.

And in August Serbian national Ljubisa KaroviÄ's head and right shoulder were sucked out of the window on a Ryanair flight, leaving him "seriously injured and in shock".

Ryanair subsequently said the window may have been damaged by a foreign object.

Additional reporting by Emily Coady-Stemp

News.title: Murder investigation after couple and two children die in fire
News.content:
His party colleague, Sinn FÃ©in councillor John Hearne, also knows the family and described it as a "terrible tragedy".

Hearne told BBC News NI that residents living in the estate noticed the blaze at about 05:00 and they went out to wake up their neighbours to try to help.

But he said it "all happened so fast" and was "hugely distressing for everyone involved".

Independent councillor Donal Barry had also been working with the family very recently.

Speaking to the BBC's Evening Extra programme, he was audibly upset by their deaths.

"Only last Thursday I was speaking to Kim on the phone in relation to a matter I was dealing with," he said.

"As soon as I went up there this morning and I looked and saw the house, my heart sank. I knew who it was then."

Barry said the immediate family were "well thought of" in Waterford and the community has been "numbed" by the attack.

The councillor added that there was "devastation" in local schools where the couple's children were pupils.

He praised the efforts made by the local council which set up a support hub at Butler Community Centre in St John's Park in the aftermath of the attack.

"Waterford City and County Council won't be found wanting in any support which they can give the community," he said.

News.title: UK growth forecast upgraded but higher energy prices to hit economy next year
News.content:
The UK economy is forecast to grow by more than previously expected this year before higher energy prices and interest rates hit the economy in 2027, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said.

The organisation's latest report, which is closely watched by the government, said the UK economy would expand by 1.3% in 2026, up from the 1% it predicted in July, before slowing in 2027.

Economies across the world have proved more resilient to the energy price shock caused by the US-Iran war, the IMF said, but it warned the economic fallout from the conflict remained "highly uncertain".

Chancellor John Healey said the government would look to "provide some breathing space" for households in the Budget.

Healey is making the final preparations to Andy Burnham's new-look government's tax and spending plans, which will be announced on 28 October.

Government borrowing costs have surged, placing pressure on the chancellor to ensure his plans are credible in the eyes of financial markets, which the UK relies on to borrow money.

But IMF chief economist Silvana Tenreyro told BBC News on Tuesday that the UK's process of managing its debts is now leading the major G7 economies.

"As you know, the UK has already started the consolidation process and it is the country that basically stands out, along with India", she said.

The organisation said the UK is one of the only major economies on course to stabilise levels of national debt. The UK is also projected to have the lowest annual borrowing in the G7 in 2031.

Asked if the UK was one of the countries the IMF was telling to reduce borrowing, Tenreyro said that the country had begun the process already and should "stay the course".

The head of the IMF has previously called on the world's advanced economies to cut borrowing and reduce debt levels.

While the IMF's forecasts are closely watched, the figures are only a prediction, a best estimate, of what will happen in the future. Forecasts often turn out to be incorrect due to world events.

Also, the chancellor's spending decisions at the Budget will be based on predictions from the UK's official forecaster, the Office for Budget Responsibility, not the IMF.

News.title: Hundreds more prisoners being freed in second phase of early release scheme
News.content:
About 650 more offenders are leaving jails in England and Wales on Tuesday, in the second phase of the early release scheme - the government's plan to tackle the prison population crisis.

It includes offenders sentenced to up to two and a half years who are leaving jail after serving a third of their sentence behind bars, rather than half.

The second wave of releases comes as the government takes its plan to radically overhaul criminal courts back to Parliament - but also as probation officers prepare to vote in a ballot that could lead to a strike over pay and workload.

Some 700 offenders left jail early on 1 October - all of whom were serving terms of less than 19 months.

Tuesday's second stage begins the process of releasing batches of offenders on increasingly longer sentences - culminating next June with those serving more than 12 years.

Around 5,000 prisoners are scheduled to be released, down from 6,000 after ministers intervened to make rapists and the most serious child sex offenders exempt.

Prisoners convicted of manslaughter are also excluded, meaning the killers of PC Andrew Harper, who died in the line of duty in 2019, will not be eligible. Those jailed for a range of offences, including members of child grooming gangs convicted of indecent assault are also ineligible.

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said "the programme is clearly not working," stating she is "worried about dangerous people being let out on the street when they haven't served their sentence, haven't been rehabilitated".

Victims' groups have also raised concerns about the scheme.

Alice Russell-Harris from the charity Refuge - which supports survivors of domestic abuse - told the BBC that domestic abuse perpetrators are among those being released.

This "will put survivors at serious risk of harm," she said, adding that even though there may be conditions such as electronic tagging and restriction zones, "we know that license conditions are frequently breached."

The early release scheme is "terrifying for survivors," said Veronica Oakeshott from the charity Women's Aid.

Reports of failures in the electronic tagging system have added to their concerns. The scheme is "dangerous and should not go ahead," Oakeshott told the BBC.

News.title: Heating oil customers face tough winter despite shake-up promise
News.content:
Heating oil customers facing soaring bills have been promised better regulation of the sector by the government.

Ministers say they will tighten up rules, promote competition and give customers clearer compensation routes if things go wrong. Minimum order levels, set for some customers, will be reviewed.

With prices close to having doubled in the past year, some campaigners have called for heating oil customers to benefit from the same cap as regular, variable gas and electricity tariffs in England, Scotland and Wales.

But there is no sign of the government proposing such a change, nor when the stricter rules will take effect.

Ministers said they would work with industry to "develop a regulatory regime for the heating oil market, protecting consumers and promoting competition".

In the meantime, oil users have been offered discounts on heat pumps, a code of practice is in place, and industry practices setting minimum order volumes at 500 litres for some consumers will be reviewed. Domestic tanks typically hold between 1,000 and 2,000 litres.

The government said this had left some people having to pay for more heating oil than they might need.

News.title: Raye hits back at ticket touts who 'overwhelmed' sign-up for Albert Hall show
News.content:
Raye has hit back at ticket touts who she says "overwhelmed" the sign-up process for an upcoming live show by using artificial intelligence (AI) bots to create "hundreds of thousands of fake registrations".

The Where Is My Husband! singer revealed there were 1.8 million sign-ups for her one-off 5,000-seat performance at the Royal Albert Hall on 23 October.

To avoid a pre-sale which she felt scalpers could exploit, Raye said the sign-up list had been manually reviewed to identify a shortlist of people believed to be "real fans".

A spokesperson for the Royal Albert Hall said they "invest heavily" in protecting their ticketing systems from "automated attacks" but the "law needs to catch up".

The award-winning artist said she had "never witnessed bots on this scale" and was changing the process as it is "so important" to her that fans can buy tickets at the face value price.

"I'm not sure what the future holds for ticketing, I do know this experience has really opened my eyes," she said in a statement shared on her social media accounts, external.

"Me and my team are going to think really hard about what we can do in the future."

Raye said the fans manually selected would receive a pre-sale link and code by email at 11:45 BST on Tuesday, and pre-sale opened shortly afterwards.

She added that the remaining tickets would be available to all on general sale.

This Symphony May Contain Hope show will showcase songs from her recent chart-topping second album, This Music May Contain Hope, that fuses old-school jazz with orchestral sound, blues, big band and soul.

The 17-track record is a concept album which explores overcoming heartbreak, self-doubt and internet trolling.

News.title: Ex-Met Police officer trained to support rape victims accused of rape
News.content:
He later phoned her and said nothing sexual had happened, the court was told.

Tyrrell is also accused of perverting the course of justice by trying to delete messages between them. In one, he apologised for "being a sex offender" and for ruining her life, jurors heard. When she told him not to say such things, he replied that they were true.

The prosecution alleges Tyrrell raped the woman by having sex with her after she had repeatedly said no.

Afterwards, he allegedly asked whether she realised that what he had done "was rape", and said he would report himself and would undoubtedly go to prison, Farrelly said.

The woman alleges that on several occasions she woke to find Tyrrell penetrating her, despite having refused sex the night before.

On one occasion, when she asked him what had happened, he shouted at her and asked whether she realised what she was saying and what could happen to him, the prosecutor told the court.

Jurors heard the woman kept a list of incidents involving Tyrrell, including the alleged sexual assaults.

In a police interview, she said she had felt pressured by him and feared no-one would believe her because she could not prove what had happened. She was also worried police would protect him because he was an officer, the court heard.

After his arrest, Tyrrell denied ever having sex with her.

Tyrrell, of Meltham, West Yorkshire, has admitted misconduct in public office. He has also pleaded guilty to a separate count of perverting the course of justice by persuading the woman to lie to police about why he was in her bedroom.

The trial continues.

News.title: Champion boxer Joe Cordina was 'retaliating' when he punched man to ground, court hears
News.content:
Former boxing world champion Joe Cordina was "retaliating" during a fight where he punched a man at a petrol station, a court has heard.

Cordina is standing trial charged with assault by beating relating to an incident on 27 February involving Jamie O'Brien.

Cardiff Magistrates' Court heard the altercation came to light days later after a video was published on WalesOnline, filmed by a witness at a Texaco garage in the Pentwyn area of Cardiff.

O'Brien's sister told police her brother "hated" Cordina, the court was told, and she feared he had "sought" him out.

A second assault by beating charge against Cordina was dropped on Tuesday. O'Brien previously admitted a charge of assault by beating.

CCTV footage of the incident "which took place over several minutes" was played to the court, showing Cordina filling up his car and walking over to O'Brien who stood on the pavement nearby.

Prosecutor Alex Orndal said O'Brien "pushed Mr Cordina with his shoulder" and Cordina then "punched him with sufficient force to push him to the ground", where he then pushed him "repeatedly".

"Mr Cordina has initiated the confrontation," Orndal said, adding "Cordina was not protecting himself but retaliating".

There was then "aggression" from O'Brien, the court heard, as Cordina raised a golf club and O'Brien lunged at him, before a number of blows were exchanged.

O'Brien was eventually restrained and "posed no further threat", the court heard, but Cordina threw a further punch at him.

In a police interview on 11 March 2026 Cordina denied the charges against him and said he was being stared at by O'Brien, initially thinking he wanted a photo.

The former world champion explained that "having been shoved, he felt threatened" and that "he punched him later out of instinct due to Mr O'Brien's actions", the court heard.

He also told police that Jamie O'Brien threatened to stab him and said he would blow up his and his mother's houses.

Cordina's defence barrister, Tom Crowther KC, told the court O'Brien had been identified by family members from the video circulating online, who had raised concerns about his behaviour.

During the hearing Crowther asked investigating officer PC Samuel Penman to watch the video that had circulated online.

He said it was plain to see that they were "watching and waiting" for Cordina, suggesting it was a set up.

Penman said it was not obvious but he did agree that the person filming "seemingly started recording prior to any physical altercation going on".

The court heard that when O'Brien was arrested he "argued with officers" and "challenged" them.

Penman admitted it was a "mistake" not to question O'Brien's sister about her concerns that her brother held a "vendetta" against Cordina.

Cordina told the court that people recognised him "four or five times a day", which was generally positive with people shaking his hand or asking for a photo.

But it was heard that a fortnight before the incident, the defendant had been told by police there was a threat to his life - something that left him shocked and "worried".

He denied knowing O'Brien, despite the suggestion they had boxed together at some point.

Explaining why he hit O'Brien, he said: "It was just a reaction, I felt a bit threatened. I wasn't going over to seek any trouble - I was just defending myself."

Asked why he pushed O'Brien down afterwards and repeatedly said "don't ever do that again", Cordina said he was protecting himself.

The court heard a number of character witness statements in support of Cordina, including from his agent Ian Bird and Llanrumney Phoenix boxing club who called him an "outstanding role model".

Cordina initially faced two counts of assault by beating but Judge Charlotte Murphy dismissed the second charge part-way into the trial, saying there was no case to answer.

She adjourned the hearing and will give her judgement on Tuesday 20 October.

News.title: Poundland in rescue talks as owners seek buyer
News.content:
Retail chain Poundland is in talks with potential buyers as it seeks a rescue deal, it has confirmed.

Executives are working with an Irish property development group on a management buyout, as first reported by Sky News, external.

But a union representing shopworkers warned that the retailer could fall into administration if that deal falls through, putting thousands of jobs at risk.

This outcome would be "a disaster for our members", the Usdaw union said.

Poundland has about 600 stores in the UK and Ireland, and 12,000 employees.

The chain has been struggling for a number of years due to pressures including rising costs and competition.

However, it expects sales to have grown more than 3% in 2026 compared with the previous year, which managing director Barry Williams said earlier this month was evidence that its recovery plan "is working".

The retailer was sold for Â£1 last summer by previous owner Pepco to US investment firm Gordon Brothers.

The current owners are in the process of seeking buyers, with the Poundland management attempting a buyout, a spokesman said.

Mr Williams, along with the firm's leadership team and Andy Bond, a former chairman of Pepco, have been working with Irish real estate firm Martin Property Group on a management buyout.

Martin Property Group is the management team's "preferred partner", the spokesman said, but the team will "work with whoever can deliver the best result for the business, colleagues and suppliers and build on the successful recovery that's already taking shape," he added.

However, Bally Auluk, a national officer at Usdaw, said there are "deep concerns that the business could go into administration" should this buyout fail.

"We are aware that a management buy-out has been attempted and we are told that their offers are being turned down," he added.

A Poundland source disputed this, however, saying the Martin Property Group is part of the sale process and remains the management team's preferred partner.

Retail analyst Catherine Shuttleworth said there were "tough times" on the High Street for all retailers.

She said retailers were struggling with "significantly subdued consumer confidence as prices continue to rise" due to higher fuel costs.

Poundland itself faces intense competition from rivals including B&M, Aldi, Lidl and from online retailers including Temu and TikTok Shop.

The business "lost its strong Â£1 identity leaving shoppers to think it was getting too expensive", Shuttleworth said, and a costly expansion into clothing and frozen food under past management had not been successful.

However, increased sales this year showed a deal with Mr Williams as boss "would make good sense", she added.

News.title: Almost 5,000 evacuated in City of London gas leak
News.content:
About 4,700 people were evacuated in the City of London after a gas leak.

The London Fire Brigade (LFB) said it was called to Old Broad Street at 10:55 BST, where crews found a ruptured six-inch gas main at a six-storey office building.

A 200m cordon was put in place between Threadneedle Street and London Wall, with nearby buildings evacuated as a precaution. The brigade has now removed its cordon, and people are being allowed back into affected properties.

A Cadent spokesperson said the pipe was "severely damaged by a private construction team" and stressed the work that caused the damage "had nothing to do with Cadent or its pipework".

Cadent is keeping a road closure in place on Great Winchester Street while engineers complete repairs to the damaged gas pipeline.

News.title: Trump pick Zacharia gets off to bumpy start in unusual first press briefing: ‘My president, I mean my husband’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia beat an abrupt retreat from the James Brady Briefing Room after just 14 minutes Tuesday morning, capping off an awkward appearance in which she mixed up the man who hired her with the man to whom she is married and spent the majority of her debut on prepared remarks filled with praise for the president.

Zacharia, whom President Donald Trump named Friday as successor to Karoline Leavitt appeared in the briefing room for the first time on just her second day on the job. She opened by telling reporters she was “so honored” to be working for Trump and noted that she’d “wanted to work for him for a very long time.” She spent the next six minutes reading haltingly from prepared remarks replete with praise for Trump and boasts about purported successes dating back months, including what she called a “historic one-day war” against Venezuela as the actual war Trump started with Iran approaches its ninth month.

When it came time to take questions, Zacharia first called on a reporter from the right-wing Breitbart News, who was in a seat normally used by White House staff that her predecessor repurposed for “new media” outlets that are generally friendly to the administration.

She then turned to Fox News correspondent Peter Doocy, who asked her if the U.S. has halted sharing intelligence with Ukraine amid Trump’s blow-up at Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Zacharia was unable to answer and told him she’d “have to get back to [him] on that.”

open image in gallery Zacharias fled the briefing room after less than 15 minutes ( AFP/Getty )

Next up on what appeared to be a prepared list of reporters was a correspondent from the Daily Mail, who first asked about whether Trump was still considering firing Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle after a spate of embarrassing headlines about her conduct before and during her tenure in Athens.

Here she made some news, telling reporters that Trump had indeed asked the ex-Fox News presenter (and ex-fiancee to his eldest son) to quit her post.

But it was a softball follow-up from the Mail that left Zacharias sputtering and led her to flee the room.

She was asked about how she will handle the notoriously tough press secretary role while juggling being a mother to four children given how her predecessor chose to resign over the burdens of balancing the job with caring for just two children.

That’s when things truly went off the rails.

open image in gallery At one point, Zacharia attempted to recover from the laughter in the room by pivoting to more praise for Trump, whom she called ‘the most family-friendly president we've ever had’ ( Getty Images )

“The idea of not spending evenings with my kid kids are is completely unacceptable,” she said, before confusing her spouse with her boss.

“So my president — excuse me, my husband — is out here,” she said.

She attempted to recover from the laughter in the room by pivoting to more praise for Trump, who she called “ the most family-friendly president we've ever had.”

“He has hired more women with families, and the fact that he knew I had four kids and he knew that this job would be demanding, and still placed his trust in me, shows that I know I'm capable of being able to step up to that,” she said.

At that point, she declared an end to the briefing because Trump was “heading out to Marine One for our historic trip to Alaska, and we can ask him all of the questions out there.”

The president was not scheduled to depart for Alaska for several hours.

Her brief performance left journalists stunned and MAGA insiders decidedly unimpressed.

One former Trump administration official who remains close to people serving in the administration texted The Independent to declare Zacharia’s debut “a train wreck” after previously describing her as a “joke hire” who’d likely be “gone in six months.”

Separately, a current administration official told MS NOW that Zacharia had “got off on the wrong foot” and needed to “get much better, fast” lest she lose her job faster than the 11-day record held by one of Trump’s ex-communications directors, hedge fund manager Anthony Scaramucci.

But the White House, at least publicly, is standing by the new press secretary, with White House Communications Director Stephen Cheung writing on X that Zacharias’ debut was “a tremendous start.”

“She commanded the room and effectively reminded the American people of all the great work President Trump and his Administration has done thus far,” Cheung added.

News.title: Everything to know about Amazon’s Black Friday sale, plus early deals to shop
News.content:
Amazon’s October Prime Day has been and gone, which leaves only the biggest shopping event of the year left for us to snap up some savings – Black Friday 2026. That’s right, all eyes are on Amazon to deliver even more bargains.

Last year, official savings began from Monday, 20 November, so we expect deals to start appearing around Monday, 23 November this time around, with the biggest offers landing around Black Friday itself. In 2025, Amazon UK ran its Black Friday week through to Cyber Monday.

When is Amazon’s Cyber Monday sale?

Cyber Monday is Monday 30 November 2026, giving shoppers one more big day of discounts after the Black Friday weekend. Amazon and other retailers may roll their Black Friday offers straight through to Cyber Monday, rather than treating it as a completely separate sale.

News.title: Wrestler fired after single appearance due to ‘insensitive’ Riyadh attack comments
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Professional-wrestling company TNA has parted ways with Max Caster after a single appearance, citing his “insensitive” rap about this week’s fatal attacks in Saudi Arabia.

In recent days, at least 14 people have been killed – with more than 300 injured – in a series of attacks on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport.

Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis claimed responsibility for the strikes, which have led to the closure of the airport and the cancellation of many flights.

Riyadh’s King Khalid Airport, after Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis said they attacked the location ( Social media )

On Sunday, former AEW wrestler Caster made his TNA debut, with the 37-year-old rapping at one point: “I drop bombs. You don't even have to fly to Riyadh.”

The American proceeded to wrestle TNA star Moose – real name Quinn Ojinnaka – and lose their match.

Following Caster’s appearance, TNA released a statement on Monday that read: “During Sunday’s Bound For Glory pay-per-view, insensitive comments were made by Max Caster referencing attacks in Riyadh that killed and injured many people.

“Making light of violent attacks is wrong. This should never have made it into the show, and that responsibility is ours. Our thoughts are with the victims, their families, and everyone affected.

“We sincerely apologize. We have removed the segment from replays and our social channels and are taking steps to ensure something like this never happens again.”

The statement concluded: “Max Caster will no longer be wrestling for TNA.”

Caster has spoken on the matter, saying in an Instagram video: “Just to address all the TNA stuff, I wanna say thank you to Carlos Silva [TNA president]. I talked to him in person; he was very generous, very professional, even after all this stuff happened.

“And I understand why he did what he did. It’s his show, he’s gotta protect TNA, and I went too far for him. So, I wanna apologise to him and everybody else in the office. I want to apologise to anyone who vouched for me to get that spot; I feel like I let those people down.

“Thank you to Moose for sharing your platform with me, and I wish things didn’t turn out the way they did, but I’m proud of that match and I’m sorry for how things have ended up.

“And then for anybody who’s offended: I just want everybody to know that when I do these raps, it’s never to offend people – it’s only to entertain. So, in my mind, it’s entertainment value first, and then if you’re offended by it, that’s your right.

“So, I can’t apologise for anyone being offended, but just know that it’s not my intention to make people upset. If it gets a reaction, I think I did my job. It was a very relevant part of the show and highly talked about, so I feel good about that, but the consequences of everything... I’m accepting that, I can accept the facts of that.

“And then to anybody who is asking if I’m good: I’m good, I’m just embarrassed how all this happened. You don’t want it to be one match and then that’s it, you get fired. But again, that’s the reality of the situation, I’m accepting it, and that’s life.

“In life, sometimes you’ve gotta man up and just accept it and move on. Whatever’s next, I don’t know, but we’ll see. Thank you everybody who’s reaching out and supporting.”

News.title: OpenAI ‘not racing to the bottom’ on AI safety, MPs told
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

OpenAI has said it is not “racing to the bottom” on AI safety as MPs questioned bosses from technology firms over the safety and security of their AI agents.

Meanwhile, Claude parent firm Anthropic suggested that there are risks that the fast-changing technology could be used by bad actors to “create biological or chemical weapons”.

It came as the Parliament’s business, innovation, science and trade select committee questioned executives from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind and Meta.

Tom Duff Gordon, vice-president and head of Europe, Middle East and Africa policy at OpenAI, said the group scrapped the release of its latest model, GPT-6.1 Astra, over safety concerns.

He stressed the decision to halt the model’s release highlighted a desire to maintain safety as it develops its technology.

He said: “We found it didn’t refuse enough, it hadn’t progressed enough with alignment.

“It is evidence that OpenAI takes safety really seriously, that we are not racing to the bottom.”

Lord Booth-Smith, head of Europe, Middle East and Africa policy at Anthropic, stressed that the company has “rigorous” safety processes.

He said: “For our deployed models, we think they are safe and we have mitigations in place.

“But it is also worth pointing out that we are learning a lot as we go about how these models are used.

“In Anthropic right now the surface area of immediate risk is definitely in the cyber domain. Mythos has been finding tens of thousands of vulnerabilities a month.

“It also makes sense that this surface area covers biology and other areas.

“It is possible that real harm could be caused in the space of helping people to create biological or chemical weapons.”
