Quite why Ruben Dias – who signed six years ago – cannot lead a charge of resistance against those who have never liked them anyway is anybody’s guess

Although a newcomer over the summer, Elliot Anderson tapped into the same attitude too. ‘It gives you the determination, where everyone is against you, to turn them over,’ the midfielder said. ‘We are more together than ever and things like this only bring you closer together.’

That was impressed on the players by Maresca in a meeting last Thursday when all convened after the international break, and the Italian is yet to make a misstep in the eyes of City and their supporters on taking the reins from Pep Guardiola, who will return for the first time as a show of unity when PSG arrive.

‘Probably it has been more tough for our fans than for the players or for me,’ he reasoned. ‘Probably because it's more complicated. Because if I am an Arsenal fan or a Man United fan, I can tell you, “Hey my friend, you cheat”, or these kind of things. It has been more tough for them. Anfield was unbelievable.’

Maybe the scenes and celebrations were for those singing behind that goal. And even if they weren’t, who are we to judge?

Sports.title: Newcastle's new Kiwi star MAX HICKS on feeding his pet eel butter chicken, growing up on AFL and hockey, waterskiing, working on a building site with Exeter's Ethan Roots and being compared to LeBron James - is an England call next?
Sports.content:
Newcastle Red Bull's new England-qualified arrival is full of surprises.

Let’s start with Max Hicks' childhood. He was born and raised in New Zealand. His father, James, is Maori, and his mother, Liane, comes from Cornwall.

‘I grew up in a little town called Coatesville, west of Auckland,’ explains the 27-year-old, his long limbs sprawled across a sofa at Kingston Park. ‘I had a pet eel called Scarface. We had this big creek that ran through the bottom of our property. We had agricultural day at primary school, where people would bring in sheep, calves, bunny rabbits.

'My old man was a builder and we had this old bathtub, so we went and caught one of the eels from the creek to take into school and I kept it as my pet. I put it back in the river but it would always come back. I always fed it left-over butter chicken. They don’t have good vision so it was something to do with the aromatics. It loved it. I’d pick it up and take it around the garden. I had a ram called Cookie, too. I would shout his name and he would run over to me. I was a pretty weird kid…’

His sporting journey has been equally unconventional. While the likes of Caleb Clarke and Tupou Vaa'i were nurtured through the All Blacks age grades, Hicks was often found playing hockey or Aussie Rules. A career in rugby seemed like an unlikely path.

‘My parents encouraged me to get into all sports possible,' he says. 'I played 100 games of first-team hockey at high school and played for the New Zealand Maori hockey team. I started playing AFL in my last year of high school, too, and spent some time with St Kilda (one of the AFL's most historic sides, based in Melbourne). AFL is such an athletic sport. The big men can all run, jump, kick off both feet, handle with both hands.

Newcastle Red Bull's new England-qualified arrival Max Hicks is full of surprises

While other rising stars were nurtured through the All Blacks age grades, Hicks was often found playing hockey or Aussie Rules. A career in rugby seemed like an unlikely path

‘I loved playing rugby but I was never the best. I got invited to a few of the Under 20s camps but I was built like a rake. AFL wanted me to be super fit and to be able to run forever. Rugby wanted me to bulk up. I was stuck between a rock and a hard place.

'Rugby never really hit me as a proper career path until I kind of left high school. Once I'd chosen rugby, I went on this big bulking journey to put on some weight. McDonald's, KFC, ice cream!’

Hicks became a trainee builder to fund his rugby dream. He upped his calorie intake and took on an early morning weights routine before going to work. By chance, his labouring colleague was school-mate Ethan Roots, the Auckland-born Exeter Chiefs flanker who has been capped by England.

‘We went to the same high school and we worked for the same building company, building houses around Auckland.' he says. 'We were setting out slabs, putting standing walls up, putting on cladding. You’re getting up at 4.30am and you’re in the gym at 5. I was still trying to make it in rugby but I was also planning for life if I didn't.

‘I wasn’t a young superstar who was picked up straight out of high school and straight into a rugby environment. I moved down to Tasman. They didn't offer me a full contract, but they kind of said, “Hey, if you come down here, work hard, you can earn yourself a spot on the team”.

‘The following year I joined the Highlanders. I remember going in for the first time and seeing all these guys I'd watched on TV. Guys like Aaron Smith and Shannon Frizell. Ben Smith and Tony Brown were coaching us. It was pretty surreal. I played for the Maori All Blacks, representing my dad's side, and I was really keen to have an adventure, so I shot over to France and joined Perpignan.’

Wearing the No6 jersey last season, Hicks’ turnover haul was second only to Jack Willis in the Top 14. With Europe on his doorstep, he had the opportunity to retrace his family roots.

‘My grandad was in the Royal Air Force and he got a posting in New Zealand. Mum was born in Truro and they moved over when she was around ten years old. I went to Cornwall with mum for the first time last year, that was cool. She got to show me where she grew up.

Hicks has only played two PREM games for Newcastle but he is already making a name for himself

Hicks became a trainee builder to fund his rugby dream. By chance, his labouring colleague was school-mate Ethan Roots (centre), the Auckland-born Exeter flanker capped by England

'We got an Airbnb and spent some time in St Ives. Ethan and Jimmy Roots popped over from Exeter, too. A lot of the family moved over to New Zealand but there will be a few relatives hanging around. I might have to do one of those Find My Family mouth swabs!’

Newcastle’s head of recruitment, Gavin Vaughan, learned of Hicks’ English roots last year. Vaughan previously worked for Scotland and unearthed Sione Tuipulotu and Huw Jones, scouring the rugby world for Scotland-eligible players.

In his new role with Newcastle, Vaughan has to hit targets of English-qualified players, making Hicks a particularly attractive proposition.

‘I wasn't actively looking to leave France but I was open to hearing what was out there. Red Bull approached me and my agent and it’s such an awesome project. The Red Bull influence is pretty cool. I thought, “How cool would it be to come into a new environment that's so unknown, with all this expectation, and really turn a place around?”

'You know, the Falcons had it tough for a couple years. It would be such a cool story to come here as a group of people from all around the world and fill the stadium out every week. That's what excited me. Mum was quite happy that I moved over. There’s a bit of patriotism there. I’ve represented my dad’s side and I guess now I’m representing my mum’s.’

During Newcastle’s pre-season camp at the Red Bull HQ in Austria, Hicks had another surprise for his team-mates. He wowed everyone with his wakeboarding skills out on the Wolfgang Lake – another skill he picked up living by the coast in New Zealand.

Hicks has only played two PREM games for Newcastle but he is already making a name for himself. During last weekend’s defeat by Leicester, Ireland legend Brian O’Driscoll compared his ability to hold a ball in one hand to NBA superstar LeBron James.

At 6ft 6in and 17st 9lb, Hicks resembles former Saracens flanker Theo McFarland, whose basketball background gave him an athletic point of difference. His eye-catching performances have thrown him into the mix of England’s World Cup bolters – although there has been no contact with Steve Borthwick.

During Newcastle’s pre-season camp at the Red Bull HQ in Austria, Hicks had another surprise for his team-mates. He wowed everyone with his wakeboarding skills out on the Wolfgang Lake

‘It was never my reason for coming over here but I would love to play international rugby,' he says, having represented the Maori All Blacks twice but never the full senior side.

'I'd love to represent my mum's side of the family. If that happens, it happens. If it doesn't, it doesn't. I’m here to throw all my eggs into the club. My reason for coming here was to be part of an exciting project with Red Bull.

‘I know we've had a tough start to the PREM and we've lost two, but the progress we're making as a group has been really positive. We’re still fine-tuning things, the fans are excited, and the group's gelling really well. It's just about finding those little connections with players you have never played with before.

'Some teams have been together for a few years and they know who's going to get a weak shoulder and throw an offload. We're still figuring that out with each other, but when that clicks, it's going to be exciting. We'll start getting more results come our way.’

Sports.title: Man United Confidential: Club hit back at Nicky Butt's 'sensationalised' claims on Michael Carrick, Real Madrid closing in on JJ Gabriel and will another academy star slip through United's fingers?
Sports.content:
Man United Confidential: Club hit back at Nicky Butt's 'sensationalised' claims on Michael Carrick, Real Madrid closing in on JJ Gabriel and will another academy star slip through United's fingers?

Manchester United are unhappy with Nicky Butt again after he revealed details of a private conversation in which Michael Carrick is claimed to have said he was not interested in football management, Confidential understands.

Sources at the club are bemused by Butt’s comments and wonder why the former Treble winner, who has not been shy in criticising his former team on his The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast with Paul Scholes, didn’t disclose the same information last season – when United were the best side in the Premier League after Carrick returned to Old Trafford in January, leading his old club back to the Champions League.

The feeling is that the comments were sensationalised, and the two men do not have a close relationship given they were never team-mates at United and have not spent a significant amount of time together.

Carrick is under pressure this season after overseeing United’s worst league start for 40 years ahead of Tuesday night’s European clash with Atletico Madrid, and Butt stunned fans with the revelation that the 45-year-old was not sold on management after he was sacked from his first job at Middlesbrough last year.

‘I was with Michael before he got the Man United job and spoke to him about management,’ Butt said. ‘He went, “No it's not for me, it's too much. My head's all over the show. I'd only do it for the big job. The big job is Man United”.’

It’s not the first time United have taken a dim view of Butt’s podcast, which he anchors alongside former team-mate Scholes and host Paddy McGuinness.

Last month, the former United stars appeared to mock Benjamin Sesko over a persistent shin injury. There has also been scathing criticism of Lisandro Martinez, with Butt claiming before the Manchester derby in January that City’s Erling Haaland would treat the Argentine defender like a ‘little toddler’.

Manchester United sources are bemused by Nicky Butt (left) claiming that Michael Carrick (right) was not sold on being a manager

Madrid fancy JJ chances

The noise around the future of JJ Gabriel has quietened down, but sources in Spain have told Confidential that Real Madrid are growing more confident they will win the race to sign the 16-year-old wonderkid.

Gabriel is not expected to play for United again after turning down scholarship forms and asking for his registration to be ripped up, with the Under 21s back in action on Friday.

While he continues his own training schedule away from Carrington, Madrid are increasingly hopeful they will beat rivals Barcelona to Gabriel's signature. Although Barca have publicly dismissed the idea of signing him, privately they are believed to have shown much more willingness to join the race.

United are willing to take legal action against another club or any unlicensed agents if it transpires that something untoward was behind Gabriel’s decision to turn down scholarship forms and play elsewhere.

While some felt a U-turn was possible, many of those individuals now believe a move to Spain is inevitable in the weeks between now and the end of the year.

JJ Gabriel (left) is continuing his own training schedule away from Carrington, with Real Madrid increasingly hopeful of beating rivals Barcelona to his signature

Tevez is a red again

The famous ‘ticker’ banner mocking Manchester City’s trophy drought returned to the Stretford End for Saturday’s draw with Tottenham, and it wasn’t the only old favourite with strong connections to the noisy neighbours that made a reappearance for United last weekend.

Over in Indonesia, Carlos Tevez was wearing the red of United again 17 years after his acrimonious move from Old Trafford to the Etihad symbolised by the ‘Welcome to Manchester’ billboard that soured relations between the two clubs.

Tevez played for a United Legends team against a North London XI made up of Arsenal players in the ‘Champions Impact: The Rivalry Returns’ exhibition game in Jakarta. The 42-year-old, who retired in 2022 at his boyhood club Boca Juniors, helped to set up the first goal for Ashley Young but United lost 3-2.

Back in 2009, the prospect of Tevez playing in red again alongside the likes of Ryan Giggs, Rio Ferdinand and Dimitar Berbatov appeared nigh on impossible when he moved across town at the dawn of the Abu Dhabi takeover. He helped to launch an era of success that brought down the banner in the Stretford End, and is now being called into question by the allegations of cheating levelled at City.

The cheeky billboard commissioned by City came to represent their challenge to United’s domination that so upset Sir Alex Ferguson, who branded them ‘a small club with a small mentality’.

The United Legends squad in Jakarta - how many former Red Devils can you name?

‘It’s City, isn’t it?’ added Ferguson. ‘All they can talk about is Manchester United. They can’t get away from it. That arrogance will be rewarded. It is a go at us, that’s the one thing it is. They think taking Carlos Tevez away from Manchester United is a triumph. It is poor stuff.’

When the two clubs met in the League Cup semi-final later that season, Tevez scored twice for City and clashed with Gary Neville as the United substitute was warming up on the touchline, later calling Neville a ‘boot-licking moron’.

O’Neill sways Jay… but can United?

As revealed by Confidential prior to the international break, there was a tug-of-war between Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland to recruit United youngster Jay McEvoy during the hiatus.

Well, Michael O’Neill’s intervention was significant as McEvoy turned out for Northern Ireland’s Under 19s, with the message that his pathway to the first team can be accelerated north of the border.

The intrigue now is whether McEvoy pens the pro contract he was offered by United in recent weeks. He stepped up to train with the first team last month, and while he will continue to play for the Under 18s, Under 19s and Under 21s, those around him want to see swift progress towards senior football.

Jay McEvoy stepped up to train with the first team last month, and while he will continue to play for the Under 18s, Under 19s and Under 21s, those around him want to see swift progress

Stars sign for brave Lola

United have donated a shirt signed by the first-team squad to eight-year-old Lola Berry, who is undergoing radiotherapy for a recurring brain tumour.

Lola has decided to wear a different football shirt for each of the 30 days she is having the proton beam therapy at Manchester's Christie Hospital, and the kits will be auctioned off to raise money for charity.

‘It's like a birthday present every morning,’ says Lola, who was first diagnosed with a brain tumour at the age of four and discovered in August that it had returned.

United sent a signed shirt to add to Lola’s collection which will be used to raise funds for The Christie Charity and Manchester Foundation Trust Charity.

Sports.title: Man United will 'NEVER' win the Premier League with Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez at centre-back, insists Paul Scholes
Sports.content:
Man United legend Paul Scholes believes the club needs to overhaul its defence after claiming they cannot compete for the Premier League title with Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez at centre-back. The Red Devils have endured a slow start to the Premier League season, winning one of their opening six matches of the campaign. Michael Carrick's side are 13th in the league following Saturday's 1-1 draw against Tottenham, leaving them 12 points adrift of leaders Man City. Man United had looked poised for a second victory of the season after leading 10-man Tottenham 1-0 but the visitors, who began the day bottom of the table, levelled in stoppage time through a Dominic Solanke header. Speaking on The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast, Scholes highlighted Lisandro Martinez's role in Tottenham's equaliser by stressing that the centre-back had been 'bullied' by Solanke in a physical duel. Scholes expressed concerns that Man United's defence has been overlooked in recent years regarding recruitment, with Martinez and Harry Maguire still lining up for the Red Devils. Man United legend Paul Scholes has called for Man United's defence to be overhauled, as he insisted they cannot win the league with Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez at centre back Scholes claimed Martinez being 'bullied' by Dominic Solanke for Tottenham's equaliser on Saturday was 'criminal' and 'beyond belief' ‘Tottenham were bottom of the league ahead of the game on Saturday and they absolutely run all over Manchester United,' Scholes said. ‘We talk a lot about recruitment, don’t we? The idea is to make your team better and someone like Elliot Anderson would make them better, but I’m not sure the players they brought in make them better. ‘I actually think they’re alright in the forward areas but look at the centre-halves, that’s an area of the pitch that hasn’t been addressed for a few years. ‘We’ve had the same centre-halves now for two or three years and we know you’re not going to be successful with them. You’re never, ever going to win the Premier League with them. ‘The goal on Saturday was a prime example – we know Lisandro Martinez is a good footballer but for your centre-half to be bullied like that, that was purely physical. 'Martinez, it is criminal, how he let them score that goal is beyond belief. ‘Manchester United need a new back-four, they need a new back-four.’ The Red Devils' backline will be put to the test on Tuesday when they face Atletico Madrid in the Champions League. Atletico are currently second in La Liga after winning six of their opening eight matches of the campaign. Man United will be without left back Luke Shaw and midfielder Kobbie Mainoo. Shaw’s second injury already this season is particularly painful given that United neglected to sign cover at left back in the summer. The two players who replaced him for three games in September – Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui – are also out of action at the moment so right back Diogo Dalot and young Harry Amass are Carrick’s options.
