Sports.title: Moses Itauma’s January Opponent Must Test His Flaws
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma’s January return needs an opponent who can test the weaknesses Filip Hrgovic exposed. David Adeleye, Guido Vianello or Frank Sanchez would be more worthwhile choices than another overmatched opponent who disappears before Itauma has to work.

Frank Warren confirmed the comeback plans, although he did not name an opponent.

“We told him to just have a little bit of a break and then, as I say, we’ll get back into it in January 2027,” Warren said to talkSPORT.

Adeleye, Vianello, and Sanchez represent the absolute baseline for a legitimate heavyweight contender. They are tough, capable ring operators who know how to survive early pressure and exploit basic technical flaws. If Itauma cannot clear that bar, the entire operation is a facade.

If taking clean shots from a fighter like Vianello or Adeleye causes Itauma to fall apart, then all the early knockouts were simply empty performances against terrified sparring partners. Either he possesses the toughness to belong among the division’s top ten, or he gets exposed as just another manufactured heavyweight who folds the second the script gets ripped up.

“His work rate was tremendous for eight rounds. I mean, he just did not stop throwing punches,” Warren said. “He showed, even though he ran out of gas, he showed he’s got a big heart, and he showed he’s got a good chin. He took some big shots.”

Choosing a soft domestic foe or an over-the-hill name merely sets up an easy stoppage that teaches him nothing.

Finding out right now if Itauma is cut out for the sport saves everyone the illusion. If Itauma lacks the mental fortitude, the engine, or the punch resistance to survive a live opponent firing back, hiding it behind sacrificial lambs only delays the reckoning.

Serving fans another run of manufactured showcases against harmless names is an insult to the ticket-buying public. If Itauma possesses the genuine fiber of a world champion, throwing him into the fire against a gritty operator like Adeleye, Vianello, or Sanchez will prove it immediately.

If he folds under that pressure, it confirms the Hrgovic night was not an off night or a premature test, but an accurate exposure of a fighter whose reputation was entirely engineered by matchmaking.

Sports.title: Frank Warren Offers Ben Whittaker Buatsi Or Hutchinson
Sports.content:
Frank Warren is offering Ben Whittaker a fight with either Joshua Buatsi or Willy Hutchinson, saying he would happily put the unbeaten light heavyweight in with the winner or the loser of their upcoming bout.

Eddie Hearn has already mentioned the winner as a possible opponent before Whittaker challenges Dmitry Bivol. Warren’s offer goes further. He believes either man would provide a serious test, regardless of how their fight ends.

“For me, he’s got a long way to go. I’ve got guys over here he can fight if he wants to fight,” Warren told talkSPORT.

Turning his attention directly toward the Buatsi vs Hutchinson pairing, Warren made his stance clear: “The winner, I have no problem with the winner or the loser fighting him.”

Offering the loser, too, shows how Warren rates Whittaker. He believes either Buatsi or Hutchinson would give him a hard fight, even coming off a defeat.

Whittaker locked down the IBF mandatory slot with his October 3 win over Conor Wallace, yet his ragged finish exposed glaring doubts about his readiness for Bivol. Exhaustion stripped away his legs down the stretch, forcing him into survival mode as Wallace pushed forward.

The theatrical showmanship that looked slick against lesser fighters disappeared once the pressure intensified. Wallace wore Whittaker down, leaving him exhausted and holding on to get through the final rounds. Against Buatsi or Hutchinson, he would need enough stamina to keep throwing punches and defending himself when the fight gets hard.

Buatsi would bring pressure and heavy punches, testing whether Whittaker can hold his technique together when he cannot dictate the pace. Hutchinson would present a different challenge with his speed and boxing ability. Either would be a considerable step up.

“Ben’s a nice guy. Good luck to him. But you’ve got to have some substance, and the substance at the end of the day just isn’t there,” Warren said.

Hearn also concedes Whittaker requires another outing before facing Bivol, keeping the Buatsi vs Hutchinson victor in play. Both promoters see the need for a sterner test, even though Warren shows far less belief in Whittaker’s actual ceiling.

Warren goes further by offering the loser, too. That’s the sharper part of his challenge: in his view, either man would test Whittaker, regardless of the result. Beating one of them would give Whittaker stronger evidence that he’s ready for Bivol.

Sports.title: Robert Garcia Risks Missing Naoya Inoue Fight
Sports.content:
Naoya Inoue has no intention of waiting around for Jesse “Bam” Rodriguez and will begin preparing for a move to featherweight. His response puts pressure on trainer Robert Garcia’s plan for another bantamweight fight before facing Inoue in April or May 2027.

Garcia wants Rodriguez in the ring with Christian Medina at bantamweight first, pushing an Inoue clash back to spring 2027. Antonio Vargas tested Bam with pure speed. Now Garcia wants a heavy hitter to see how Bam handles power at 118.

“I want Bam to feel punches, you know, block, be able to absorb some of those punches at 118 from a very strong fighter,” Robert said to Fight Hub TV.

That sounds like a trainer who still doubts his guy is ready. Garcia believes Bam can challenge Inoue, but he wants extra proof before taking the leap. Inoue has zero reason to plan his schedule around Garcia’s hesitation.

Robert also questioned Inoue moving to 126 so quickly, claiming the Japanese superstar is physically mature enough to stay put.

“He’s already a man. He’s already built,” Garcia said.

Physical maturity doesn’t mean sticking around at junior featherweight makes sense. Featherweight brings fresh challenges. A division lacking marquee names gives Inoue no real motive to linger. Moving up while he has elite years left beats waiting around for Bam.

Garcia also floated the idea that Inoue wants this matchup fast because Rodriguez gets sharper with time.

“He might think if the longer he waits, the bigger chance Bam has.”

That logic assumes Inoue cares to wait around. He could simply leave the division behind.

Taking another fight at 118 might calm Garcia’s nerves. It won’t prepare Bam for the threat waiting at 122. Team Bam can keep hunting for tuneups, or they can embrace the danger of chasing a superstar. They don’t get to dictate Inoue’s timeline.

Robert is misreading who holds the leverage. Inoue is an undisputed champion, an international superstar, and a massive ticket seller. He dictates the terms, the timing, and the division.

Bam’s side wants Inoue to pause his career, pass on 126, and wait for them to finish test runs at bantamweight, which doesn’t make sense. If you want the monster, you take the shot when the door is open.

Sports.title: Tim Tszyu vs Erislandy Lara WBA Title Fight Announced in Australia
Sports.content:
Tszyu secured the middleweight title shot by defeating Errol Spence Jr and will pursue a championship in a second division.

Tim Tszyu will challenge Erislandy Lara for the WBA middleweight title in Australia. Promoters have not announced the fight date, host city, venue or broadcaster.

The matchup sends Tszyu back into a championship fight after he outpointed Errol Spence Jr in Sydney in July. That victory extended his winning streak to three bouts and lifted his record to 28-3 with 18 knockouts.

Tszyu will remain at the 160-pound limit rather than return to super welterweight.

“At 160 I feel strong, I feel sharp and I feel dangerous. Middleweight is my division now. Spence was just the appetiser,” Tszyu said in the official announcement.

Tszyu Targets Championship in Second Division

Tszyu previously captured the WBO super welterweight title. Dethroning Lara would add a middleweight championship to his record and make him the first member of the Tszyu family to claim world titles in two weight classes.

His father, Kostya Tszyu, unified the junior welterweight division and captured every world championship of his career at 140 pounds.

“I’ve carried the Tszyu name my whole life. It’s a privilege and it’s pressure. This is my chance to write a chapter that belongs to me, and it’s the legacy defining moment of my career,” Tszyu said.

Jeff Fenech will command Tszyu’s corner for the title challenge. The former three-division champion joined Tszyu’s team in April 2026 and guided him through the Spence victory.

Lara Brings WBA Belt to Australia

Lara enters the matchup with a 32-3-3 record and 19 knockouts. The Cuban southpaw captured the WBA “Regular” middleweight belt in 2021 before the organization elevated him to full champion in 2023.

The 43-year-old has completed four successful title defenses and has never lost by stoppage as a professional. He also previously captured WBA championships at super welterweight.

Lara’s title reign and southpaw craft give Tszyu a seasoned champion to crack. Tszyu will bring pressure, body punching and home support into his bid to seize the belt.

Promoters expect to announce the date, location, ticket information and broadcast details in the coming weeks.

Sports.title: VIDEO: Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley II Preview & Prediction
Sports.content:
Coming up this Saturday on the 17th of October, from The O2 Arena in London, in a heavyweight championship showdown that will be streamed live worldwide exclusively on DAZN PPV – reigning WBO heavyweight champion Daniel Dubois puts his title on the line in a highly anticipated immediate rematch against former champion Fabio Wardley.

BUY Dubois-Wardley 2 on DAZN

The heavyweight landscape is absolute chaos right now, turning into the Wild West ever since Oleksandr Usyk vacated his collection of alphabet belts. With the rest of the division fighting over the pieces, the stakes could not be any higher. For Dubois, a victory confirms that his reign is the real deal and cements his standing as one of the premier heavyweights in the world. For Wardley, it is entirely about redemption – proving his storybook run was no fluke and reclaiming the world title he worked so hard to win.

Their first encounter just five months ago in Manchester was an absolute barnburner. Wardley stunned everyone early, scoring two dramatic knockdowns and pushing Dubois to the brink. But Dubois weathered the early storm, leaned on his piston-like jab, and systematically took over before halting Wardley in the 11th round.

Heading into Saturday’s return bout, the prevailing consensus is that Wardley shot his bolt, and Dubois will simply repeat the feat. Most observers are writing the former champion off completely. But is it really that simple? If Wardley makes the necessary tactical adjustments, can he pull off the upset?

Who will win the upcoming heavyweight championship rematch between Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley?

This edition of Rummy’s Corner will contemplate the question while providing a quick preview and official prediction. This is Rummy’s Corner (written, narrated, and produced by Geoffrey Ciani).

Sports.title: Chris Mannix Questions Jai Opetaia’s Return To Cruiserweight
Sports.content:
Jai Opetaia could cash in on a massive heavyweight payday against Deontay Wilder, but that detour could easily backfire once he returns to cruiserweight. Packing on size for Wilder only to strip it off for David Benavidez is the exact trap Chris Mannix sees ahead.

Discussing the fight with Sergio Mora, Mannix estimated Opetaia might scale around 210 to 212 pounds at heavyweight. His real concern centers on what happens if the Australian tries dropping back to 200 to meet Benavidez within six months.

“Adding that weight, adding that muscle, and then like within six months later dropping back down to 200 to fight the toughest opponent you could possibly face in the cruiserweight division. I think there’s a little bit of risk there as well,” said Mannix.

Mannix pointed to Roy Jones Jr.’s struggles after jumping to heavyweight and cutting back to light heavyweight. While Opetaia’s weight jump would be much smaller, Mannix questioned how easily the Australian could shed that newly built muscle at 31 years old.

That reality makes camp preparation for Wilder critical. Opetaia has to determine how much extra size he genuinely requires against a faded puncher whose work rate has fallen off. Bulking up recklessly could leave him facing an agonizing weight cut before dealing with Benavidez’s relentless pressure.

Mora favors Wilder as an opponent because the former champion scales lighter than most modern heavyweights. He believes Opetaia’s movement would thoroughly confuse the aging veteran, delivering far more mainstream eyes than an ordinary cruiserweight title defense.

Mannix agreed on the financial appeal, calling it “a ton of money” and “a ton of visibility.” Even so, he warned that Wilder’s right hand remains an eraser regardless of career decline.

A bout with Benavidez is still just a possibility rather than a signed deal. If that remains the target, Opetaia cannot focus entirely on handling Wilder. His team must plan the weight management carefully so he can drop back to 200 pounds at peak strength.

Sports.title: Brandon Figueroa Expects More Defenses Before Rafael Espinoza
Sports.content:
Brandon Figueroa has his sights set on Rafael Espinoza for a featherweight unification, though he admits fans might need to wait through a few more title defenses first. The delay sounds less about finding willing rivals and more about cooking the commercial appeal until it hits a boil.

First, Figueroa has business to handle on Saturday when he puts his WBA belt on the line against Tomoki Kameda. Espinoza sits at the top of his wish list right after that, even if calling for the fight doesn’t mean it lands immediately.

“[Espinoza] is the No. 1 in our division,” Figueroa said to The Ring, describing their potential meeting as a fight-of-the-year candidate.

Figueroa called Espinoza the number one guy in the division, telling The Ring that a clash between them would easily contend for fight of the year.

You can see the appeal for an inside grinder who loves breaking opponents down. Espinoza brings towering height and relentless activity, meaning Figueroa would have to walk through heavy fire just to cut the distance and work. Neither man would ever have to go looking for action.

The frustrating part for fight fans is Figueroa’s belief that promoters will keep the titleholders on separate tracks to build their profiles. In his view, he might need one or two extra defenses before those unification bouts actually materialize.

The business logic makes sense on paper. Keep winning, build the brand, and give promoters bigger numbers to sell once the belts finally collide. Still, every unnecessary detour opens the door to an upset, a bad cut, or endless delays that wreck the whole plan.

Figueroa targeting Espinoza definitely gives fans something exciting to look past Kameda for. At the same time, it makes you wonder how much more buildup a fight really needs when both guys hold world titles and their ring styles already guarantee pure fireworks.

For now, this is just Figueroa reading the landscape rather than an official plan on the calendar. Nothing is signed with Espinoza. His only real job this weekend is taking care of Kameda; anything after that just determines how long everyone has to wait for the showdown he wants.

Sports.title: Paulie Malignaggi Overrates Ben Whittaker After Wallace Struggles
Sports.content:
Paulie Malignaggi’s praise for Ben Whittaker is running ahead of his performances. Calling him an “amazing talent” is difficult to square with how he struggled once Conor Wallace refused to play along with the showboating.

Whittaker had been getting away with those antics against the lesser opposition Matchroom and Boxxer put in front of him. Wallace was his first quality opponent, and the tricks that looked impressive against overmatched fighters didn’t work nearly as well.

“I think Whittaker is a tremendous talent, an amazing talent, but he’s got some things to work on,” Malignaggi told Boxing King Media. “At a world-class level, there are things he’s got to fix if he’s going to be successful.”

Wallace exposed how much work remains. Whittaker struggled under pressure late, and there is an argument that he should have lost. The falls that went uncounted as knockdowns and the repeated holding he was allowed to get away with helped him survive with a decision.

That wasn’t simply a case of the entertainment falling flat. Whittaker needed answers when Wallace kept coming, and too often his answer was to grab. Making lesser opponents miss is one thing. Keeping a quality fighter off you when tired is another.

Malignaggi understands why Whittaker’s approach invites a harsh reaction when things go wrong.

“If you’re going to sell the sizzle, you got to sell the steak,” he said. “Ben Whittaker sells the sizzle a lot.”

Paulie argues that the showboating doubles the criticism when Whittaker leaves people disappointed. That is fair, but it doesn’t explain the scale of his praise. Against Wallace, Whittaker showed weaknesses that better light heavyweights could punish even more severely.

Whittaker has ability, but the Wallace fight gave us more reason to question his readiness than celebrate his gifts. Malignaggi believes there is an exceptional fighter there. Whittaker still has to prove it against opponents who can make him pay for his mistakes.

Ghana News.title: Mahama commissions Christian Tetteh Yohuno Ward Complex at Police Hospital
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama has commissioned an 85-bed ward complex at the Police Hospital in Accra, named after the Inspector General of Police (IGP), Christian Tetteh Yohuno.

The facility, commissioned on Tuesday, October 13, under the theme: “Christian Tetteh Yohuno Ward Complex”, was constructed to commemorate the Golden Jubilee celebration of the Police Hospital and is fully equipped with ultramodern healthcare facilities.

President Mahama described the new facility as an important investment in the health and welfare of personnel of the Ghana Police Service and a significant enhancement to the hospital’s capacity to serve the wider Ghanaian public.

He recalled that nearly a year ago, he joined the IGP and the Police Management Board at the Police Training School in Tesano for the Police Remembrance Day observance, during which officers who died in the line of duty were honoured and solidarity was shown to their families.

The President said that on that solemn occasion he discussed with the IGP the need to pay greater attention to the welfare of serving police officers.

"And today, we see a tangible outcome of that discussion. I commend the Inspector General of Police and the Police Management Board for their leadership in delivering this new hospital block, which is equipped with the most modern facilities," he stated.

President Mahama also expressed appreciation to the health professionals and all those whose efforts contributed to the successful completion of the project.

He noted that men and women of the Ghana Police Service undertake difficult and often dangerous assignments, including responding to emergencies, confronting violent crime and maintaining peace and security in communities.

According to him, the demands of policing affect both the physical and mental well-being of officers, making it imperative for them to have access to timely and high-quality healthcare whenever they are injured or fall ill.

The President said the responsibility of the State also extended to supporting the families of officers, whose sacrifices often enable them to perform their duties effectively.

"An officer's ability to protect the public is closely linked to the support the police service provides. Access to appropriate healthcare is therefore essential for operational readiness," the President said.

President Mahama disclosed that even before the formal commissioning of the facility, seven police officers who sustained injuries in the line of duty in Bunkpurugu and Porto had been admitted to the new ward complex.

He said the officers had been transported to Accra and were receiving treatment at the facility. He said they would get the best care at the new facility.

The President stated that the new block would strengthen the hospital’s capacity to provide quality healthcare services, particularly for officers injured in the line of duty and patients requiring urgent medical attention.

He also underscored the importance of addressing the psychological impact of policing, noting that repeated exposure to violence, tragedy and distress could have lasting effects on officers.

He said mental health support, counselling and appropriate treatment should be readily accessible without fear of stigma.

"When officers know that their health and welfare is being taken seriously, they can serve with greater confidence and focus. Investing in their care strengthens our collective national security."

President Mahama noted that the Police Hospital’s role extended beyond serving police personnel, as it formed part of Ghana’s national healthcare system and provided emergency medical services to the public.

He said the expanded facility would help strengthen healthcare delivery, particularly during emergencies, road accidents and public health crises.

The President emphasised that every patient who visited the hospital deserved to be treated with dignity and compassion.

He stated that the true value of the facility would be measured by the quality of healthcare provided and how well it was maintained over time.

President Mahama therefore urged the hospital’s management to uphold the highest standards of hygiene, patient safety and clinical practice.

He stressed the need for regular maintenance of medical equipment, uninterrupted availability of essential medicines and supplies, and continuous capacity-building for healthcare personnel.

The President also commended the doctors, nurses, pharmacists, laboratory technicians and support staff who would serve in the new block.

"And behind every patient record is a person who may be frightened, in pain, or uncertain about their future," he said.

"And so, when you are confronted with such patients, listen to them carefully, explain to them clearly, and treat every patient with the respect you would wish for your own family."

President Mahama reiterated the Government’s commitment to improving the safety, welfare and operational effectiveness of personnel of the Ghana Police Service.

The Minister for the Interior, Muntaka Mohammed-Mubarak, said President Mahama’s commitment to improving healthcare infrastructure and enhancing the welfare of security personnel continued to leave a lasting impact on the nation.

He said the facility stood as a visible symbol of the President’s dedication to building a stronger and more inclusive Ghana.

The IGP, on his part, expressed gratitude to President Mahama for his continuous support for the Police Service and his concern for the welfare of officers.

He assured that the Police Administration would continue to pursue initiatives aimed at improving the health, welfare and operational effectiveness of personnel of the Service.

Ghana News.title: Vice President calls for wider access to Ghana’s political party histories
Ghana News.content:
Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has called for wider access to publications documenting Ghana’s political party histories, stressing the importance of historical knowledge in deepening public understanding of the country’s governance institutions and constitutional arrangements.

She said making such records accessible to the public would enable citizens to better understand the political experiences that have shaped the Republic and equip them to participate more meaningfully in the country’s political life.

Speaking at the launch of six historiographies of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) on Tuesday, October 13, the Vice President emphasised that knowledge of political history should not be confined to people who experienced the events first-hand.

According to her, documenting the country’s political journey and making the resulting publications widely available would help preserve important historical records for present and future generations.

“Familiarity with our governance institutions, with our constitutional arrangements, and the political experiences that have shaped our Republic” is important for meaningful civic participation, she said.

Professor Opoku-Agyemang explained that citizens who have access to such knowledge are better positioned to understand the institutions and processes that govern the country, as well as the historical developments that have influenced Ghana’s political system.

She noted that historical understanding should extend beyond those who lived through particular political periods, arguing that younger generations and other members of the public should also have opportunities to learn from the country’s political experiences.

"When that knowledge is accessible, citizens are better placed to participate meaningfully in political life. The knowledge of history is also not restricted to those who have lived through it," she added.

The Vice President expressed the hope that the newly launched publications would be distributed to a broad range of institutions and individuals to ensure that the historical accounts reach a wider audience.

“It is my hope that these publications will reach libraries, research institutions, private spaces, and public officials too,” she said.

She also encouraged regional and constituency executives of the NDC to keep copies of the publications in their offices, alongside other important historical documents.

According to her, making the books available at the party’s various organisational levels would provide members and visitors with opportunities to engage with the party’s history and learn more about the developments that have shaped its evolution.

The launch of the six historiographies provides an opportunity to preserve accounts of the NDC’s political journey and make them available for research, institutional reference and public education.

The publications, she indicated, should therefore be treated as important reference materials that can contribute to a deeper understanding of Ghana’s governance structures, constitutional development and political experiences.

Ghana News.title: Republic Bank JoyNews Habitat Fair to connect prospective homeowners with exhibitors in Ho from October 16 to 18
Ghana News.content:
Financial constraints and difficulties saving enough money remain major obstacles for some prospective homeowners, as the Republic Bank JoyNews Habitat Fair prepares to open in Ho from October 16 to 18, 2026.

The three-day event, scheduled for the Ho Sports Stadium, will connect prospective homeowners with exhibitors and give participants the opportunity to explore options related to construction, interior decoration, furniture, home security, and other aspects of home improvement.

For Cecilia Asare, who currently lives with her parents, the cost of living independently remains a major concern.

She said moving out without sufficient financial resources could leave her struggling to meet her basic needs.

“Hmm, first, money. Second, if I leave my parents’ house, I’ll go hungry,” she said.

Despite the financial challenges, Cecilia hopes to gain ideas from the fair on how to create a comfortable home that reflects her needs and personality.

She said she would prefer interior designs and furniture that express who she is.

“When it comes to the design, I’ll go for something that really talks about my personality. The moment it comes to my home, it should show you that this is who I am without talking so much,” she said.

Another prospective homeowner, Michael Akomeah, identified saving towards a home as a challenge because of his existing investment commitments.

“I’m doing some investment. That’s why,” he said, explaining why he had found it difficult to save towards homeownership.

He welcomed the opportunity to participate in the fair, which is intended to help prospective homeowners explore products and services that could support their plans.

The Republic Bank JoyNews Habitat Fair aims to bring prospective homeowners closer to their homeownership goals by connecting them with businesses and service providers across the housing industry.

The event will run from October 16 to 18, 2026, at the Ho Sports Stadium, with activities scheduled from 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. daily.

Participants will have the opportunity to explore options in construction, interior decoration, furniture, home security and other home-related services.

The fair is expected to provide a platform for prospective homeowners to discover available products and services as they work towards turning their homeownership aspirations into reality.

Ghana News.title: Obaasima Summit: ‘AI is not a spiritual attack’ — Rev. Dr. Ofori-Boateng urges young women to embrace technology
Ghana News.content:
Young women have been urged to embrace artificial intelligence (AI) and continuous learning as technology reshapes the world, with an Anglican priest cautioning against interpreting AI as a spiritual threat.

Director of Programmes for the Anglican Diocese of Accra, Rev. Dr. Akua Buabema Ofori-Boateng, gave the advice at the 2026 Obaasima Summit, where speakers encouraged young women to prepare for leadership and build on the achievements of previous generations.

She said the rapid pace of technological change made lifelong learning essential for anyone seeking to remain relevant and effective in leadership.

“Embrace lifelong learning. I hold many degrees, and I'm still learning,” she said.

Rev. Dr. Ofori-Boateng stressed that academic qualifications should be viewed as the beginning, rather than the end, of the learning process.

“Your education does not end when you walk across the stage and they hand you a certificate. It begins there because the world is changing rapidly, and those who lead the world never stop being students,” she said.

Citing artificial intelligence as an example of a technology young women need to understand, she urged them to approach it with openness rather than fear.

“So, for instance, AI is here. And let me tell you on my authority as a priest, AI is not a spiritual attack,” she added.

Gomashie challenges women on values and mentorship

Meanwhile, Minister for Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts Abla Dzifa Gomashie challenged women to reflect on the values, knowledge and principles they pass on to younger generations.

She questioned whether the lessons being imparted to young people were appropriate for their development and whether the recipients were prepared to learn from them.

“Teach a child the way they should grow. And when they grow, they will not depart from it. But what are we passing on now? And those we are passing the things on to, are they ready to receive it?” she asked.

Drawing on the familiar analogy of leading a donkey to water without being able to force it to drink, the minister highlighted the limits of guidance when the person receiving it is unwilling to learn.

Her remarks underscored the role of mentorship and personal responsibility in preparing younger generations to take up leadership positions.

Women leaders share experiences

The summit also featured contributions from former Electoral Commissioner Charlotte Osei, Administrator of the Ghana Medical Trust Fund Secretariat Obuobia Darko-Opoku, and Special Aide to President John Dramani Mahama Joyce Bawa Mogtari.

The speakers shared experiences from their professional journeys and encouraged young women to develop their abilities, overcome barriers and take advantage of opportunities to contribute to national development.

Founded by Ama Pratt, Press Secretary and Spokesperson to the Vice President, the summit was held under the theme, “Legacy and Leadership: Ghanaian Women Shaping the Past, Guiding the Future.”

The event focused on sustaining the contributions of women in leadership while equipping younger generations with the knowledge, values and skills needed to carry that legacy forward.

Ghana News.title: GHS to distribute 80,000 pairs of  locally-made protective footwear to health workers
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Health Service (GHS) will distribute 80,000 pairs of protective footwear to health professionals implementing the Free Primary Healthcare programme, following a donation by Sanford, World Shoe Ltd. and Samaritan’s Feet Ghana.

The shoes are manufactured in Ghana using lightweight EVA foam and feature antimicrobial properties intended to help prevent infections. They are also designed to be biodegradable.

Director-General of the Ghana Health Service, Dr Samuel Kaba Akoriyea, said the Service would work with its regional and district teams to ensure the shoes reach the intended beneficiaries.

“We will communicate with our regional and district teams and support a process that is organised, transparent and consistent with the purpose of the donation,” he said.

Vice President of Sanford World Clinic, Karoliina Slack, said the initiative was inspired by the sacrifices health workers make, often in facilities with limited equipment and infrastructure.

“We wanted to give them a piece of something, a piece of hope, something that they will wear when they go to work, and they remember that across the ocean, in the US, there are lots of people that think of them and value them and understand the sacrifices that they make every day,” she said.

Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of World Shoe and Samaritan’s Feet International, Manny Ohonme, said the donation demonstrates how locally manufactured products can address healthcare needs while creating jobs and supporting economic growth.

“Our solution is not just about providing the shoes. So the shoes that you saw here today, 80,000, means people are employed,” he said.

The organisations say they hope to build on the partnership to attract more stakeholders to support healthcare delivery and improve the well-being of health workers in Ghana.

Ghana News.title: GoldBod boosts local jobs as 90% of gold undergoes refining in Ghana – Sammy Gyamfi
Ghana News.content:
Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi

The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) is strengthening local value addition in the gold sector, with between 80 and 90 per cent of the gold it purchases and exports now refined in Ghana, its Chief Executive Officer, Sammy Gyamfi, has disclosed.

He said the development was helping to create employment opportunities, retain revenue within the domestic economy and support the growth of local industries.

Speaking before Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee on Tuesday, October 13, Mr Gyamfi said the shift towards local refining represented a significant departure from previous practices, under which much of the country’s gold was exported without being refined locally.

He explained that the increased use of domestic refineries was helping Ghana capture more economic benefits from its mineral resources instead of allowing such opportunities to be realised in foreign destinations.

“I’m happy to report to this honourable committee that, as we speak, about 80 to 90 per cent of the gold we purchase and export is refined here locally,” he said.

According to him, the refineries operate around the clock and employ Ghanaians, particularly young people, while ensuring that refining fees that would otherwise be paid abroad remain in the country.

Mr Gyamfi added that the benefits extended beyond gold refining, as silver recovered during the process was also being retained locally to generate foreign exchange and provide raw materials for Ghana’s fabrication industry.

He said the approach was helping to strengthen domestic industrial activity, create jobs and increase the economic returns from the country’s gold resources, while advancing GoldBod’s broader mandate of supporting foreign exchange generation and the regulation of Ghana’s gold trading sector.

Ghana News.title: The search for the politically unblemished: Are we asking the impossible of public appointees?
Ghana News.content:
The controversy surrounding President John Dramani Mahama’s appointment of Emelia Afi Agbenyo as a Deputy Chairperson of Ghana’s Electoral Commission (EC) raises a question that deserves serious national reflection. How do we determine whether a person appointed to a sensitive public office can be trusted to discharge the responsibilities of that office fairly, independently and without political interference?

The question is important because the credibility of our elections depends, in part, on public confidence in those entrusted with managing them. On 12 October 2026, President Mahama swore in Emelia Afi Agbenyo and Dr Joseph Kwaku Asamoah as Deputy Chairpersons of the Electoral Commission, urging them to perform their duties without favour towards any political party, candidate or government. The appointments have prompted renewed political debate about impartiality and the selection of persons for positions of national importance.

Source: Ghana News Agency, 12 October 2026.

Mindset Transformation Initiative (MTI) believes this debate presents an opportunity to look beyond the immediate political contest and examine a more fundamental issue: Are we placing so much emphasis on finding individuals without perceived political associations that we risk neglecting the stronger safeguards needed to protect our public institutions?

The Difficult Search for a Politically Unblemished Person

In a politically divided society, the demand for neutral and impartial public officers is understandable. Citizens want judges who dispense justice without political considerations, electoral commissioners who administer elections without favour, and public officials who serve the Republic rather than the interests of the government that appointed them.

These are reasonable expectations.

However, we must also confront a practical difficulty. In a society where political parties influence public discourse, professional networks, civic participation and national debate, how easy is it to identify a competent individual who has never held a political opinion, associated with a politically active person, supported a public policy or been perceived as sympathetic to one political tradition?

The expression politically unblemished can become an elusive standard if it means that an appointee must have no past association, opinion, or circumstance that a political opponent might question.

A person may have a political history and still possess the integrity to serve impartially. Another may have no known political affiliation yet lack the courage to resist pressure, the discipline to follow the law or the moral strength to act against the interests of those who appointed them.

Political neutrality cannot therefore be established solely by examining a person's background. It must also be demonstrated through conduct, decisions and a willingness to uphold the law, even when doing so displeases powerful interests.

This does not mean that a candidate's political history should be ignored. Relevant associations, conflicts of interest and evidence of partisan conduct deserve careful scrutiny. It means that such scrutiny should be based on credible evidence and fair standards rather than political suspicion alone.

Consistency Matters, but So Does Institutional Integrity

MTI recognises the concerns being raised by political parties about consistency in public appointments. Where one party demands strict standards of neutrality while in opposition but applies a different standard when in government, public confidence suffers.

Political parties must be prepared to defend the same principles regardless of which party holds power.

If a party believes that an electoral commissioner should not have a close and demonstrable relationship with a political organisation, that principle should apply whether the appointment is made by an NDC or NPP administration. If a party argues that appointments to the judiciary must be protected from political influence, it should support the same protections when its political interests are not directly affected.

The test of a principle is whether its supporters are prepared to uphold it when doing so is inconvenient.

Nevertheless, political consistency alone will not guarantee institutional independence. Even where an appointment process is transparent, and the appointee has an impressive professional record, the institution must still have systems that prevent improper interference and make misconduct difficult to conceal.

The central question must therefore extend beyond who has been appointed to include the conditions under which that person will exercise authority.

Institutions Must Be Stronger Than the Individuals Who Lead Them

Ghana's Electoral Commission is a constitutional institution with a responsibility that extends beyond the interests of any government or political party. Article 46 of the 1992 Constitution provides that, in performing its functions, the Commission shall not be subject to the control or direction of any person or authority, except as provided by the Constitution or other applicable law.

This principle is fundamental. The Commission must serve the Republic and its citizens. Yet constitutional independence must be supported by practical arrangements that protect the electoral process from manipulation, undue pressure, administrative abuse and individual misconduct. No democratic country should have to depend entirely on the personal virtue of the people appointed to administer its elections. Good people can make mistakes. People can face pressure. People can change their positions. Institutions must be designed to withstand these human realities.

The same principle applies to the judiciary. We need judges of integrity, but we also need transparent judicial processes, clear rules of professional conduct, independent disciplinary procedures and decisions that can be examined against the law and the evidence. The objective should be to create institutions in which the rules are stronger than personal loyalties, and accountability is more powerful than political influence.

What Would Stronger Electoral Safeguards Look Like?

MTI proposes that Ghana's national conversation should give greater attention to the practical safeguards that protect the integrity of elections, irrespective of who occupies the leadership of the Electoral Commission.

First, strengthen the transparency of electoral procedures

The processes for voter registration, collation, transmission, verification and declaration of results must be governed by clear, publicly available rules. Any changes to those procedures should be properly explained, legally authorised and communicated in good time

Second, establish effective independent verification

Election results should be supported by verifiable records at each stage of the process. Party agents, accredited observers and other legally authorised stakeholders should have meaningful opportunities to observe procedures, obtain the records they are entitled to receive and raise objections through established channels.

Where electronic systems are used, they should be supported by appropriate security controls, independent technical audits and reliable contingency arrangements.

Third, strengthen accountability for electoral misconduct

There should be clear procedures for investigating credible allegations of interference, falsification, deliberate obstruction or abuse of electoral authority. Investigations must be impartial, timely and subject to the law. Proven misconduct should attract appropriate sanctions, regardless of the rank or political connections of the person involved.

Fourth, protect the independence of election officials at every level

Electoral integrity cannot rest on the character of the Chairperson and Deputy Chairpersons alone. Regional and district officials, returning officers, collation teams and other personnel must work under professional standards that protect them from improper political pressure. Their duties, reporting lines and disciplinary arrangements should be clearly defined.

Fifth, make electoral processes more open to public scrutiny

Public confidence grows when citizens can understand how results are produced and how disputes are resolved. Clear documentation, timely publication of legally releasable results, transparent reconciliation procedures and accessible complaint mechanisms can help reduce suspicion and strengthen trust.

Sixth, improve the appointment process itself

The selection of persons for sensitive constitutional offices should be transparent, merit-based and supported by credible scrutiny of professional competence, integrity, independence and potential conflicts of interest. The public should be able to understand the criteria applied and the reasons candidates are considered suitable.

The Constitution Review Committee's December 2025 recommendations on Electoral Commission appointments provide a useful starting point for examining reforms, including open competitive recruitment, a more structured selection process and parliamentary approval of nominees.

These recommendations should be considered on their merits as part of the wider national reform debate. The purpose of these safeguards is straightforward: to make electoral manipulation difficult, detectable and punishable, whoever might attempt it

Should We Abandon the Search for Neutrality?

MTI does not suggest that impartiality is unimportant or that political history should be irrelevant to public appointments. Nor should we lower the standards expected of people entrusted with sensitive constitutional responsibilities. Rather, we must distinguish between demanding impartial conduct and expecting to find a person whom nobody can accuse of political sympathy. The first is a necessary democratic standard.

The second may become an endless political exercise, particularly when rival parties judge the same individual according to their competing interests. Perhaps, therefore, Ghana should reconsider the weight it places on searching for a supposedly politically spotless candidate. We should retain rigorous scrutiny of an appointee's record, but direct more of our national energy towards building systems that ensure that no appointee can easily compromise the institution they serve.

This is particularly important because public appointments are made within a constitutional and political framework. The fact that an officeholder was appointed by a President does not, by itself, establish that the individual will act in the President's interest. Equally, the absence of a known party affiliation does not automatically establish impartiality. The fair approach is to examine the appointment process, the candidate's qualifications and record, any credible evidence of conflicts or partisan conduct, and the safeguards that will govern the exercise of the office.

In the case of the Electoral Commission, the ultimate test should be whether the electoral system can produce credible, verifiable and legally defensible results, irrespective of the political identity of the people managing it.

A Call for a Change in National Mindset

As a civic organisation committed to responsibility, integrity, discipline and national development, Mindset Transformation Initiative believes that Ghana's democratic maturity requires a shift in how we approach these matters. We must move from a political culture that concentrates almost exclusively on the perceived loyalties of individuals to one that demands competence, accountability and institutional resilience.

Political parties have a legitimate responsibility to scrutinise appointments. Civil society has a duty to ask difficult questions. The media must investigate and report responsibly. Citizens must insist on transparency. Appointees must understand that public office is a trust held on behalf of the Republic. All these responsibilities are complementary.

We must also resist the temptation to pronounce individuals guilty of political bias without credible evidence. Public confidence is not strengthened when allegations are treated as established facts simply because they suit a political argument. Equally, allegations should not be dismissed merely because they concern an appointee of the governing party.

The same standards must apply to everyone. A mature democracy should be able to scrutinise an appointment firmly while respecting the appointee's right to be assessed fairly. It should also be able to demand stronger institutional safeguards without making assumptions about the intentions of any particular officeholder.

Conclusion: Let Us Protect the Sanctity of the Vote

Mindset Transformation Initiative appreciates the concerns being expressed by political parties about consistency, impartiality and public confidence in appointments to the Electoral Commission. These concerns deserve a fair hearing, and the appointment process must always be open to legitimate scrutiny. However, we believe Ghana must look beyond the search for a person who is perceived to have no political blemish.

That search can become subjective, politically selective and difficult to conclude. Perhaps it is time to place less emphasis on the impossible expectation of finding a politically unblemished individual and greater emphasis on creating an electoral system that no individual can easily manipulate. We should insist on qualified, ethical and impartial public officers. At the same time, we must establish safeguards that make interference difficult, ensure that irregularities can be detected, provide effective remedies for disputes and hold offenders accountable under the law.

The sanctity of the vote must never depend solely on the goodwill of the person occupying an office. It must be protected by sound laws, transparent procedures, independent verification, professional electoral administration and effective accountability. Whether the Electoral Commission is led by persons appointed under an NDC, NPP or any future administration, the same safeguards must apply. No political party should have to trust the personal goodwill of its opponent to believe that an election has been conducted fairly.

Our national objective should be to build an electoral system in which the results reflect the will of the Ghanaian people, where that will can be independently verified, and where no amount of attempted manipulation can overturn the lawful outcome without detection and appropriate remedy. The ultimate safeguard for Ghana's democracy is not merely the hope that we appoint the right people. It is the determination to build institutions that compel every person, regardless of political affiliation or personal interest, to do what is right under the law. That is the mindset Ghana must cultivate.

*******

By Sidney Justin Tehoda

Ghana News.title: ‎Ghana seeks climate finance access for debt-restructuring countries
Ghana News.content:
Minister of State in Charge of Climate Change and Sustainability,‎ Issifu Seidu, has called for climate-vulnerable countries undergoing debt restructuring to retain access to climate finance, insisting that exclusion could undermine development gains and efforts to achieve debt sustainability.

‎The country said timely financing was essential to help vulnerable economies respond to climate shocks without diverting scarce domestic resources from development priorities or resorting to emergency borrowing.

‎He made the call in an interview with Ghanaian journalists after a ministerial dialogue on the margins of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Group (WBG) annual meetings in Bangkok.

‎The dialogue formally initiated the process to establish a US$500 million Lifeline Fund by the V20 group of climate-vulnerable economies.

‎The proposed facility is intended to provide rapid financial support to countries facing climate shocks.

‎Mr Seidu credited Barbados with leading advocacy for reforms to the international climate finance architecture to better address the needs of climate-vulnerable countries.

‎He said climate shocks repeatedly reversed development progress, compelling governments to redirect limited domestic resources towards emergency response and recovery.

‎“We realise that anytime these countries go through debt restructuring, they are excluded from the financing arrangement. So, if they are taking difficult decisions, these difficult decisions should not exclude them from these opportunities of climate fund,” he said.

‎Mr Seidu said the exclusion created competing fiscal demands for governments, which had to meet debt-servicing obligations, finance development programmes and respond to floods, droughts and other climate-related disasters.

‎He said the proposed Lifeline Fund would help address the financing gap by providing quicker access to resources for climate interventions, avoiding the lengthy bureaucratic processes associated with traditional climate funds.

‎The Minister said the exclusion of countries undergoing debt restructuring was counterproductive, particularly when they had taken difficult but necessary measures to restore debt sustainability in line with international expectations.

‎“If they are taking difficult decisions, those decisions should not exclude them from opportunities for climate finance,” he said.

‎Mr Seidu reaffirmed Ghana’s commitment to sustained advocacy to address structural inequalities at the intersection of climate justice and debt sustainability.

‎He said responding promptly to climate shocks could also support debt sustainability by preventing costly reversals in development and reducing the need for emergency borrowing after disasters.

‎The Minister called on strategic partners to complement government efforts to support vulnerable countries and communities.

‎He also urged investors to collaborate in developing sustainable solutions and share resilience-building successes across the Global South.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
