World.title: Majority in US say Trump prioritises personal wealth over all else: Poll
World.content:
A majority of US adults say President Trump and his family have inappropriately profited from presidency.

Share Majority in US say Trump prioritises personal wealth over all else: Poll on social media

Most US adults believe President Donald Trump has placed his personal financial interests and those of his inner circle ahead of the country’s since returning to the White House in 2025, according to a new nationwide poll.

The poll, conducted by the Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research and released on Tuesday, suggests that public perception of the Republican president leans heavily critical: Over half of surveyed adults view Trump’s second term as self-serving by investing in his own business and commercial pursuits “a lot”. Roughly one quarter believe he focuses on national interests, but only 11 percent feel Trump represents regular Americans. Fifty-five percent of Republicans surveyed said that Trump has prioritised his personal business interests “a lot” or “some”.

Half of the respondents report that Trump has placed zero priority on people “like them”.

As Trump’s family business pulls in record funds from new ventures helped by his policies, the poll results suggest that most US adults think growing his own finances has been the north star of Trump’s presidency, at least to some extent.

Trump’s June financial disclosure revealed massive post-election influxes of foreign and corporate capital into his business empire, stemming primarily from over $1bn in cryptocurrency ventures after he loosened regulation on the industry, as well as from international real estate.

During his first year as president, the Trump Organisation – Trump’s multinational family-owned enterprise dedicated to property development and global brand licensing – made eight real estate deals with authoritarian or one-party foreign states. Some speculate these countries were highly motivated to maintain favourable relations with the US to keep Trump happy on fronts like trade tariffs, military protection and private business dealings.



The administration, meanwhile, has repeatedly dismissed concerns over Trump’s business conflicts of interest, maintaining that he acts solely in the interest of Americans.

In late September, a separate Reuters/Ipsos poll found that Trump’s approval rating has fallen to 32 percent – the lowest of his ⁠political career – as his fellow Republicans soured on his handling of the cost of living crisis amid the deeply unpopular Iran war.

The dip in performance and approval ratings follows a high point in January 2025, when the newly inaugurated president boasted a 47 percent approval rating right after taking office.

According to the AP-NORC poll, which surveyed more than 2,000 US adults in late September, general sentiment around the administration’s ethical conduct is highly polarised, with far more citizens feeling that the president has neither prioritised the country as a whole nor everyday Americans.

Just over 40 percent of respondents believe Trump has “done something illegal” vis-a-vis allegations of personal enrichment while in office, with another 18 percent viewing his financial dealings as “unethical but not illegal”.

Opinions surrounding the lawfulness of the president’s financial practices split sharply along party lines, with Democrats overwhelmingly viewing the actions as illegal, compared with about three in 10 independents and about one in 10 Republicans, who largely see his behaviour as justified.

World.title: UK spy chief says Iran is stepping up targeting of military bases
World.content:
MI5 chief says operations linked to Iran led to 50 arrests during the past year.

Share UK spy chief says Iran is stepping up targeting of military bases on social media

The head of the United Kingdom’s domestic spy agency has said Iran is ramping up attempts to strike sensitive military targets after a series of incidents at airbases in Britain, even as Tehran has denied any involvement.

In his annual speech, M15 Director-General Ken McCallum on Tuesday said there had been a major shift in Tehran’s calculus this year and that “Iranian ambitions to come at harder targets, like military sites”.

McCallum’s warning came after UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) was “almost certainly” behind a suspected plot against Royal Air Force (RAF) Fairford, an airbase used by US bombers to carry out strikes on Iran. The incident prompted the United States to withdraw its military jets from the facility over security concerns earlier this month.

UK airbase incidents

British police declared a major incident after three “suspicious” vans drove close to the RAF Fairford airbase in Gloucestershire on September 27. Five British men in their 20s were arrested “on suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act”, but all were released on bail.

Police said they found a supply of petrol in three vans linked to the suspects, but no explosives. The men were later released without charge on police bail “under stringent conditions”.



Two others were arrested later, including a British-Iranian national, but were later released. None of the men have been charged.

Two Latvian men were arrested for trespassing at RAF Molesworth, which is used by the US military and NATO for intelligence operations, on Friday. The men were also released on bail.

UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said on Monday that the government was sanctioning two Iranians for their “role in facilitating or engaging in hostile activity on behalf of the Iranian regime”.

One is Ruhollah Bazghandi, the head of IRGC counterespionage operations, and the other is Shahram Ali Reza Tamarzadeh Jakki, whom British officials described as a facilitator for Iran’s Zindashti criminal network.

‘Not unique’

McCallum said he could not speak about the recent incident at RAF Fairford because it was an ongoing investigation, but added, “The RAF Fairford incident … is ⁠not unique. There have been other examples, not just in the UK but around the world.”

The spy chief said UK authorities had carried out 50 arrests over the past year to disrupt Iran-linked operations.

However, he said he doubted Iran’s ability to launch complex attacks, perhaps using explosive drones, due to the limited sophistication of operatives Tehran used in the UK.

“Given what we’ve actually seen in practice in the UK ⁠in recent years, that has not been anywhere near [that] level of capability,” McCallum said.

“That said, clearly it is the case that in countries closer to its own homeland, the IRGC has quite ⁠deep experience of using more conventional and hybrid technology in a more aggressive and ⁠sophisticated way,” the MI5 boss added.

Tehran has rejected accusations ‌of involvement in the Fairford incident or any other accusations of harmful activity in Britain.

World.title: US ambassador to Greece resigns amid misconduct allegations
World.content:
Kimberly Guilfoyle has faced mounting allegations, including offering access to Trump officials in exchange for money.

Share US ambassador to Greece resigns amid misconduct allegations on social media

United States President Donald Trump’s Ambassador to Greece, Kimberley Guilfoyle, has resigned following a series of allegations of misconduct, including claims that she offered a political donor access to senior administration officials in exchange for money.

“We have asked ambassador Guilfoyle to resign,” White House press secretary Katie Zacharia told reporters earlier on Tuesday. “She has been a wonderful asset to the team, and we wish her well.”

The announcement comes after weeks of damaging reports about Guilfoyle’s conduct.

Shortly after Zacharia’s comments, Guilfoyle posted on social media that she was resigning.

“While my time as Ambassador may be coming to an end, my commitment to President Trump, the America First movement, and the country I love will never end,” she wrote.

She also denied the allegations against her.

“These allegations are false, and I intend to vigorously defend my name, my reputation, and my integrity,” she said.

According to The Wall Street Journal, Guilfoyle asked a Trump donor to cover a $100,000 credit card bill shortly before her congressional confirmation hearing, promising him access to administration officials in return.

The newspaper also reported that she told guests at a reception that she could use US influence to undermine the Greek government, promoted the interests of a Greek construction and energy company, and allowed one of its lobbyists to attend private diplomatic meetings.

Guilfoyle’s lawyers have said the money she sought was payment for previous speaking engagements and public appearances that she had not received.



Trump had signalled on Monday that he was considering removing her from the post.

“Well, we’re looking at it,” he told reporters. “We’re not happy.”

Secretary of State Marco Rubio initially defended Guilfoyle, calling her a “strong ambassador,” but later declined to comment on the allegations and criticised reporters for asking about them.

Guilfoyle is a former Fox News host and California prosecutor. She is the former wife of California Governor Gavin Newsom and was previously engaged to Trump’s eldest son, Donald Trump Jr.

World.title: Sweden’s centre-left leader fails in second bid to form government
World.content:
The leader of Sweden’s left-wing Social Democratic Party, Magdalena Andersson, has said her efforts to form a government have failed, prolonging a political deadlock a month after parliamentary elections.

Speaking at a news conference Tuesday, Andersson said talks with the three other parties in the country’s left-wing bloc had hit an impasse.

Despite progress, she said she did not believe conditions were in place to “form a government that can be tolerated by parliament”.

It is her second time failing to form a government after Sweden’s parliamentary vote on September 13.

Shortly after the announcement, the country’s parliament speaker, Andreas Norlen, who had tasked Andersson with gauging conditions to form a government, said a vote on whether to make Andersson prime minister would proceed in parliament on Thursday. He conceded that Andersson would likely fail to pass the vote.

Under the Swedish system, a prime minister can secure office so long as a parliamentary majority does not vote against them.

Sweden’s centre-left opposition bloc narrowly defeated outgoing Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson’s right-wing bloc in last month’s election, winning 176 seats to the right-wing bloc’s 173. However, Andersson’s bloc has struggled to form a government due to competing terms from several of its members. The Centre Party has said it will oppose a government that includes cabinet posts for the Left Party, which has in turn insisted it will only support a left-wing government of which it is a member.

If Andersson fails in Thursday’s vote, Norlen is expected to ask Kristersson, who currently leads a caretaker government, to hold negotiations with other parties.



Speaking to reporters, Norlen said he considered Kristersson a potential next candidate, but the speaker did not wish to commit to that too soon and would “respect the process”.

To succeed, Kristersson would need to convince an opposition party to support him or at least not vote against him.

The speaker of parliament has four attempts at proposing a prime minister for parliament to vote on. If the fourth attempt fails, a snap election must be called.

After Sweden’s 2022 election, negotiations to form a government took more than a month, and those following the 2018 election lasted more than four months.

World.title: Houthis threaten Saudi Arabia’s Aramco facilities and airports
World.content:
Yemen’s Houthis have warned all employees and civilians near Saudi Arabia’s oil facilities to evacuate, calling the sites “a legitimate target”.

The warning on Tuesday from the group’s spokesman, Yahya Saree, was prompted by an evacuation order from the Saudi-led coalition urging civilians to evacuate Yemeni Oil Company’s al-Sabah central station in the Houthi-controlled capital Sanaa.

Shortly after the Saudi-led coalition’s evacuation order, Al Jazeera’s team on the ground reported hearing explosions in Sanaa. Media outlets affiliated with the Houthis said air strikes by the Saudi-backed forces struck an oil facility in the al-Sabaha area of the capital.

“We heard the explosion upon Saudi Arabia targeting the Yemeni oil al-Sabah Central Station here in the capital Sanaa,” Al Jazeera correspondent Yousef Mawry said.

Saudi Arabia also conducted two other air strike campaigns on the Ras Isa port targeting Yemeni oil storage tanks and on an oil station in the Houthi-controlled Hodeidah province, according to Mawry.

Following the reported explosions, Saree said Houthi fighters were confronting Saudi-backed forces in Sanaa.

Saree responded to the coalition’s evacuation order, warning that any strikes on Sanaa would be met with a “harsh and painful” response in the Saudi Arabian capital Riyadh.

In a statement on X, Saree said the Houthis would target the sites that were ordered to be evacuated if the Saudi-led coalition proceeded with an attack on Sanaa.

Civilians were told to evacuate the Aramco Company headquarters in Dammam, King Khalid International Airport and a refinery affiliated with Aramco in Riyadh.



“The Ansar Allah Houthi group have not yet launched any attacks, but people are expecting there to be retaliations,” Mawry said.

An attack on King Khalid airport on Saturday left at least 13 people dead and more than 300 injured, rocking the world’s top crude oil exporter. Another person was killed, and 11 were wounded on Sunday after a projectile struck the airport in Riyadh.

Many international airlines have since suspended flights to Saudi ⁠⁠Arabia and ⁠⁠neighbouring countries following the deadly weekend attacks by the Houthis, including Air France-KLM, Air India, Etihad, Lufthansa, Delta, Gulf Air and Qatar Airways.

The kingdom, which backs Yemen’s internationally recognised government, was still weathering new attacks on Tuesday, with the coalition saying its forces intercepted three drones north of Riyadh.

Saree also reiterated the Houthis’ warning to airports in Saudi Arabia following recent attacks on multiple airports and oil facilities across the country since last week in a spillover from the wider regional conflict between the US and Iran.

Saudi Arabia has in recent ⁠⁠weeks launched strikes against the Houthis and is backing a Yemeni government counteroffensive known as the “Dawn of Yemen” after the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast ‌‌last month.

Saudi Arabia’s cabinet, chaired ⁠by Crown Prince ⁠Mohammed bin Salman, said on Tuesday the Houthis would face “consequences” for their attacks across the kingdom, according to the Saudi Press Agency.

World.title: ‘Block, blunt, break’: What’s in NATO’s new Russia war plan?
World.content:
NATO’s top commander says he is revealing the plan to stop a Russian invasion of Europe, even though the threat is not ‘imminent’.

NATO’s top general has unveiled a new war plan for countering a Russian attack on members of the alliance, embedding lessons learned from the front lines in Ukraine.

Speaking about NATO’s so-called “theory of victory” at the Warsaw Security Forum on Monday, General Alexus Grynkewich, who has served as head of United States European Command and the Supreme Allied Commander Europe since 2025, said the plan rests on three strategies designed to stop an invasion in its tracks: “block, blunt and break”.

The announcement comes amid mounting warnings from European intelligence agencies of rising threats from Russia, including both the prospect of conventional military action and “hybrid warfare”, which can include tactics from cyberattacks to tampering with undersea cables.

In a bid to ease the alliance’s growing concerns, Grynkewich said: “What I want to do is assure the one billion citizens of our alliance that we’ve got this. We know what we need to do. We know how we would do it.”

But the new plan from NATO comes at a time when the alliance itself appears divided on how to deal with Russia, following a series of recent overtures from US President Donald Trump to Russian President Vladimir Putin, including his latest controversial plan for Russia to release stocks of diesel to global markets despite sanctions on Russian oil.

So, what’s in the new NATO plan, and what are European agencies warning about? How has Russia reacted? And is the alliance even on the same page on all of this?

What’s in the new NATO plan?

General Grynkewich told the Warsaw Security Forum that NATO does not view a military confrontation with Russia as “imminent or inevitable”, but that it will nevertheless be ready for one.



“Implementing the theory of victory I’ve described today would require me to issue orders that I hope to never give,” he said. “But let there be no doubt: should war come, we will block, blunt any attack, and then if it does not cease, we will break the forces conducting aggression against us.”

The “block, blunt and break” strategy, he explained, is aimed at stopping an attack rather than taking enemy territory.

Drawing directly on lessons learned on the front lines in Ukraine and from conflict in the Middle East, Grynkewich said the plan relies on the use of precision weapons with “affordable mass”, like drones, and other autonomous systems.

In the plan, he said, the alliance’s forces would “block” an attack at the border to halt enemy advances on the battlefield, then “blunt” the attack by hitting incoming troops from the air, sea, and land. Then, at last, they would aim to “break” the enemy by targeting the supply chain and command networks.

“If required, we will break the enemy’s forces and the operational warfighting system that is arrayed against us,” he said. “Enemy formations will be starved of replenishment. Enemy commanders will be unable to control their forces. Enemy forces and support capabilities will be reduced and destroyed.”

Are Russian threats in Europe on the rise?

Germany’s foreign intelligence chief, Martin Jaeger, warned last week that the country risked being drawn into a “violent conflict” with Russia, saying Moscow increasingly viewed Berlin as a principal adversary.

He cited an attempted drone attack on a Ukrainian cargo plane at Leipzig airport in August as an example of the escalating threat. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt has also warned of a Russian-linked “shadow war” involving sabotage, cyberattacks and other covert operations.

In France, President Emmanuel Macron warned last month that the Russian hybrid threat facing France and other European countries had intensified in recent weeks, and ordered the preparation of plans to protect critical infrastructure.

The United Kingdom’s Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said that he had received confirmation upon entering office that Russia interfered in the 2016 Brexit referendum, although he did not publicly detail the evidence behind that assessment. Last week, he travelled to Berlin to meet with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, in part to discuss plans to combat Russian hybrid warfare.



Russia issued a nuclear warning to NATO late last month, saying it was prepared to use its arsenal, including nuclear weapons, if the alliance attempted to isolate Kaliningrad, a Russian exclave bordering Poland and Lithuania.

In July, Romania’s Defence Ministry said it had recorded 33 instances of Russian drones entering its airspace since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022. Eighteen of those incursions had occurred this year, and Romanian F-16 fighter jets had shot down three drones during the year.

Poland has also accused Russian intelligence services of orchestrating an arson attack on a Starlink satellite-internet station in Wola Krobowska last month. Warsaw described the incident as part of Russia’s hybrid warfare campaign against countries supporting Ukraine.

Norway, too, has issued similar warnings. Beate Gangas, head of the country’s Police Security Service, said this week that Europe is facing its most serious security situation since World War II, echoing concerns over suspected Russian sabotage and covert operations across the continent.

What has Russia said?

In August, Russia warned the UK that it could face “consequences” for supplying drones to Ukraine that have been used in long-range attacks inside Russian territory.

“London’s actions will inevitably carry consequences for which ⁠it will have to answer,” the Russian embassy in London said in a statement on August 17. “The deeper its involvement in the conflict and the greater its support for Kyiv’s terrorist machinery, the higher the price it will pay.”

Despite this, Russia is not preparing for “any kind” of conflict with Europe, President Vladimir Putin said last month. He added that Russia had “no real motive” to escalate tensions and criticised European countries that have suggested otherwise.

“Many in Europe talk about expecting an attack from Russia and therefore believe they must themselves prepare for hostilities, for a war with Russia,” Putin told reporters in St Petersburg.

“I want to emphasise once again: we are not preparing for any kind of hostilities with Europe,” he noted.

Putin added that Russia was considering its stance on whether to resume peace talks with Ukraine following recent Ukrainian attacks on Russia, particularly on energy infrastructure.

“On proposals to resume negotiations, yes, they are all on the table, and it is all possible. But after everything they’ve done, we will give careful thought to what steps we need to take in response,” Putin said.

Is NATO united?

Since taking presidential office in the US, Trump has repeatedly attacked other NATO members for not shouldering enough of the financial burden for defence. He has also been angered by NATO members’ general refusal to join in the US-Israel war on Iran.

As a result, there are fears that Trump cannot be relied on to provide support if it is needed within the NATO alliance, analysts say.

In August, after the Russian consulate in London warned of “consequences” for the UK for providing Ukraine with long-range drones, former Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Andrei Fedorov told the BBC that could include the possibility of attacks. He said many of the military experts currently advising the Kremlin are “convinced” that NATO would not respond forcefully if Russia were to hit the UK. “Trump will not allow NATO to answer,” he said.



The alliance is facing a deepening divide over Russia, as Trump pursues engagement with Moscow while European governments insist that Russia must remain under pressure if the war in Ukraine is to come to an end.

Last month, Washington invited Putin to December’s Group of 20 (G20) summit in Miami, in a move that was seen as potentially ending Moscow’s diplomatic isolation since its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

The European Union responded that Russia remained a G20 member but said it would continue condemning the invasion regardless of whether Putin attended.

The divide deepened last week when Trump announced a deal allowing Russian diesel exports into US and global markets, temporarily easing sanctions on Russian fuel. His administration said the move could help lower energy prices and encourage Putin to return to peace negotiations.

Critics have warned that it would generate revenue for Russia while undermining Western efforts to constrain its war effort.

Meanwhile, Trump has also escalated his criticism of Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, and suggested that Ukraine should elect a new leader willing to make a deal with Russia. Zelenskyy had called Trump’s diesel agreement with Putin “not fair and not honest”, arguing it would benefit Russia.

EU foreign ministers also insisted that European sanctions against Russia would remain in place despite Washington’s deal with Moscow.

On Sunday, Trump claimed in a Truth Social post to have instigated an “energy truce” between Russia and Ukraine, under which both sides would refrain from targeting each other’s energy facilities with long-range strikes. However, Zelenskyy said such a deal was “news to me” – although he also said Ukraine would respect such a truce if Moscow honoured it as well. Regardless, Russia, which also has not confirmed agreeing to an energy truce, continued striking Ukraine’s facilities on Monday, according to Ukrainian officials.

World.title: Spain’s King Felipe makes first visit to Ceuta amid migrant crisis
World.content:
NewsFeed Spain’s King Felipe makes first visit to Ceuta amid migrant crisis

Spain’s King Felipe and Queen Letizia are visiting the Spanish territory of Ceuta for the first time in their 12 year reign, amid an ongoing migration crisis there. At least 10,000 migrants remain in the exclave after around 72,000 crossed from Morocco in July.

World.title: Russia's offensive ability is broken, Kyiv's former top general tells BBC
World.content:
Ukraine has stabilised the front line and "broken Russia's ability to advance" by killing so many of its men, Ukraine's former commander-in-chief has said in an interview with the BBC.

Gen Oleksandr Syrskyi made the comments in an exclusive interview, his first since he was dramatically forced from his post in the summer.

He addressed his sacking, disagreeing with his critics who declared him too "old school" to command Ukraine's new, technologically advanced forces.

He also pushed back against allegations made by soldiers who previously served under him, who told the BBC they were ordered to remain at their positions even when they were almost surrounded by Russians, leading to high losses.

Syrskyi said that Moscow's overall losses in the war were six times higher than Ukraine's. "If you count only dead, then it's up to 11 times," he added.

Neither Russia nor Ukraine officially release the numbers of their dead. Ukraine's military says it inflicted record losses this year on Russian soldiers in September, although that cannot be verified.

UK intelligence chiefs estimate Russia has lost around half a million men killed in Ukraine since launching its full-scale invasion in 2022. The US-based Center for Strategic and International Studies meanwhile believes, external Ukraine has lost up to 150,000 troops killed by June 2026.

He says this difference in death toll â as well as technological advances, and a strategy of attacking weak points in Russia's lines while containing their advances in other parts â accounts for the current stalemate at the front.

In the first six months of 2026, Russia managed overall to seize 61 sq km, the general said. "It's an indication that the front line has been stabilised."

The Institute for Study of War (ISW) has also confirmed this trend. One of its recent reports, external says that in September 2026, Moscow lost more territory than it took.

World.title: Horrified witnesses recount fatal rollercoaster incident at Six Flags
World.content:
Warning: This article contains some graphic details

One person has died and others were injured after an incident on a rollercoaster at an amusement park in the US state of Georgia.

The Cobb County Police Department is investigating the fatality at Six Flags Over Georgia, about 15 miles (24km) from Atlanta, a local official confirmed.

The ride involved has not been specified but aerial footage from news helicopters showed the Goliath rollercoaster stopped midway, with riders being helped off by workers.

Horrified witnesses have told local media they saw a man ejected from the ride - something the BBC has not verified.

Six Flags said it was temporarily closing nine rides across the US and Canada as a precaution.

It said it was "deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today. Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guest's family, friends, and loved ones".

Lisa Cupid, the chairwoman of Cobb County's governing body, said police detectives with the local major crimes unit "are investigating the circumstances surrounding this incident".

The man who died has been identified as Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, 42, who lived in nearby Atlanta, the Cobb County Police Department told the BBC.

Details about how he died and how other riders were injured have not yet been released but the BBC has contacted local police and fire authorities, as well as park officials.

Local outlet 11 Alive quoted a witness saying Kariem had come loose from his seat and had then struck the rollercoaster and some of his fellow riders before falling onto the roof of a nearby haunted house attraction.

The incident was captured in souvenir photos that were automatically taken of the rollercoaster while it was in motion, the witness added.

A husband and wife, who were on the ride, also told 11 Alive that Kariem fell from the ride and was struck by it. They said workers at the park had checked their safety harnesses before the ride set off.

"We were having a great time and to just screaming 'Oh my God, what is happening?'," the woman said.

World.title: Breaking Bad actor RJ Mitte dies aged 34
World.content:
Mitte, who grew up in Louisiana, was a young teen when he auditioned for the breakthrough role after moving to Los Angeles to support his younger sister's acting career in 2005.

He had said that his first audition in Los Angeles was for a California state public service announcement for an anti-meth commercial.

"Fast forward to auditioning for Breaking Bad, which is still, in my opinion, an anti-meth thing because it doesn't end well for anyone," he said on the Joe Vulpis Podcast earlier this month.

His character was based on the show's creator Vince Gilligan's late friend who had a more severe case of cerebral palsy and used forearm crutches, which Mitte did not require.

Mitte was seen as playing the role with honesty and accessibility, cracking jokes as a teen whose health condition was rarely mentioned in the series.

Breaking Bad aired on US cable broadcaster AMC for five seasons from 2008-13.

After shooting to fame, Mitte fought for more varied roles and complex depictions of characters with disabilities, both visible and invisible.

"Whenever awards season rolls around, we always hope to see a diverse group of projects that reflect all of us, in body and mind," he told the BBC in 2021.

"Watching the awareness grow around disability representation has been great to see, but breakthroughs sometimes come in pieces and moments instead of larger change," he said.

Mitte's other on-screen credits include Hannah Montana, Switched at Birth, Westhampton and his latest project, Talking to Strangers, which came out earlier this year.

Additional reporting by Rebecka Pieder.

If you have been affected by the issues raised in this story help and support is available via the BBC Action Line.

World.title: Watch: Emergency calls from botched Christa Pike execution released
World.content:
A series of newly-released calls made after the failed execution of US death row inmate Christa Pike reveal emergency services were delayed by confusion among first responders and Tennessee prison officials.

The recordings, first obtained by the Associated Press, show that minutes passed as officials and responders attempted to confirm whether the request for emergency help in the execution chamber at Riverbend Prison was legitimate.

Pike, 50, was sentenced to death after murdering Colleen Slemmer with her then-boyfriend in 1995. She survived two injections of the drug pentobarbital on 30 September and was taken to hospital in a critical condition.

The BBC's Mayeni Jones explains.

Read more about what happened that night.

World.title: Bulgaria summons Russian ambassador after ship sinks in Black Sea drone attack
World.content:
Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev has summoned the Russian ambassador after two merchant ships were struck by drones off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast and one of them sank.

Six crew members on the Guinea-Bissau-flagged HS Dignity were rescued and 10 others are missing, according to Defence Minister Dimitar Stoyanov, after it went down 17 nautical miles (31km) east of the village of Krapets having sent a distress signal.

The other ship, the Ukrainian owned Chelsea-3, was hit by drones 18 nautical miles from the town of Byala and all 15 crew were rescued.

The attacks come a week after two other commercial ships were hit by sea and aerial drones in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone.

One of the ships, the Alfa Watan, sank and all 10 crew, including nine Syrians, are presumed dead.

Radev convened an emergency meeting on Tuesday and said he had summoned Russian envoy Eleonora Mitrofanova. Although there was no conclusive evidence of blame on "either side... the logic suggests that the outcome benefits the Russian Federation", he said.

Mitrofanova was later quoted by Bulgarian media as telling Radev she had no information from Russia's defence ministry relating to the latest attacks. She also said these strikes could have been a provocation by a third party.

World.title: Pope admitted to hospital for surgery to remove lump on his lung
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV has been admitted to Rome's Gemelli Hospital for surgery to remove a lump on his lung, detected during what the Vatican has described as "routine checks".

It said the operation would take place on Tuesday afternoon.

The 71-year-old pontiff was met at the hospital by a large crowd, some of whom had been waiting outside for several hours to catch a glimpse of him.

They cheered greetings and well wishes as he passed, waving and smiling back through the lowered back window of his car.

He was then met by staff on the hospital steps. "I'm sorry," one of them commiserated, to which the Pope gave a smile and a shrug. "We're here for you," he was assured.

It was Leo XIV himself who on Sunday announced news of his operation to the world, speaking from the balcony in St Peter's Square after delivering the traditional Angelus blessing.

He said the nodule, or growth, on his lung was "contained" and had been found "at a very early stage", but that doctors had advised him to have it removed.

The Vatican said the Pope would be operated on by the Gemelli's thoracic surgery team and promised an update on his condition on Tuesday evening.

His schedule has already been cleared until 20 October to give him time to recover.

Nodules are quite common and not necessarily cancerous. But doctors say when a lump is removed it will usually be tested to check for any sign of the disease.

The Vatican has stressed that the pontiff, who is generally thought to be fit, had no symptoms of infection or illness.

World.title: BBC FM radio transmissions suspended in Afghanistan
World.content:
Afghanistan's Taliban government has suspended the transmission of BBC broadcasts from FM radio sites across the country.

A Taliban government spokesman said the BBC had been suspended because of "repeated violations" but did not elaborate.

The BBC has been the only international news organisation to broadcast inside Afghanistan since two US outlets were banned from operating in the country in 2022.

"Millions of people across Afghanistan rely on the BBC for accurate news and information and we are working with the authorities to address the situation," the broadcaster said in a statement.

The BBC said it was "continuing to report fairly and independently in Pashto, Dari and English to our audiences in Afghanistan, on shortwave and medium wave radio, online and via satellite".

It reaches more than 20% of the adult population in Afghanistan each week with news and other output, including educational programming aimed at girls who have been banned from secondary schools.

Taliban Ministry of Information and Culture spokesman Khubaib Ghufran told local media: "Due to some repeated violations by the BBC media outlet, it is decided that for time being its activity is suspended across the country."

The Taliban government has a tight grip on media operating in the country.

Music is not broadcast and women are less visible on screen than before the Taliban retook power in 2021. Women no longer appear on air together with men.

People can still use some social media platforms, but a lack of electricity in large parts of the country, high costs and low literacy rates remain major barriers.

The BBC's Afghan service has been operating since 1981.

World.title: Hungarian MPs scrap Orbán's anti-LGBTQ measures
World.content:
The Hungarian parliament has voted to amend child protection laws, scrapping measures that stigmatise gay and transgender people. LGBTQ and human rights activists warmly welcomed the move, but called for changes to other OrbÃ¡n-era laws.

The 2021 Child Protection Law, passed by the large Fidesz majority of then-Prime Minister Viktor OrbÃ¡n, banned the "portrayal or promotion of homosexuality or transgenderism".

Since OrbÃ¡n's April election defeat, the Tisza government of PÃ©ter Magyar has been working to dismantle the previous government's legacy.

Minutes after Tuesday's vote, Budapest said the EU had agreed to release â¬4.2bn (Â£3.5bn) of funds frozen in the last years of the Fidesz government.

The European Commission said last month that the Magyar government had addressed a number of "rule of law breaches affecting the EU budget", and urged EU leaders to unlock the funds , externaland readmit Hungary to two key EU programmes - Erasmus+ and Horizon Europe.

Hungary's 2021 law had affected a wide range of other laws, including education and the right of assembly.

Magyar's Tisza party commands the same two-thirds majority that OrbÃ¡n's party used to have, and the measures passed on Tuesday were bundled together by the new government in a package of laws designed to unravel the Fidesz legislation.

"We are very happy that this got adopted," TamÃ¡s Dombos of civil rights group the HÃ¡ttÃ©r Society told the BBC. "We've been fighting this so-called child protection law for five years. There have been problems with the bill submitted to parliament, but most of those problems have been fixed."

Both the Fidesz and Tisza governments made child protection central to their image.

But while Fidesz under Viktor OrbÃ¡n appealed to the conservative electorate by identifying gay and transgender people as a threat to public morals, Tisza under Prime Minister PÃ©ter Magyar is trying to remove or soften legislation, without actually identifying as a liberal-minded government in favour of full equality.

In June 2025, the Gay Pride march through Budapest drew an estimated quarter of a million people, despite a promise by then-Prime Minister Viktor OrbÃ¡n to his supporters that he would prevent it happening.

Police stood aside despite an official ban, and proceedings against the city mayor and others for organising the festival were later dropped. This year's event went ahead without restrictions.

The child protection issue turned from being a strong card in OrbÃ¡n's hand to become his Achilles heel, when the public found out that his government had supported the pardon of the deputy head of a children's home who had been found guilty of covering up the paedophile crimes of his boss.

In his own election campaign, PÃ©ter Magyar presented his party as a champion of the rights of children in state care, while painstakingly avoiding the issues of gay and transgender rights, for fear of alienating right-wing voters.

"We are still knocking on a closed door," Dombos told the BBC, "but at least they are listening on the other side."

This marked a major improvement on the OrbÃ¡n years, he said, where his community felt constantly targeted. Other issues he wanted addressed include the full recognition of same-sex marriage, same-sex couples' rights to adopt children, and the restoration of the right of transgender people to change their names in official documents.

"I'm very cautious," Magyar said in an interview published in Finnish daily Helsingin Sanomat on Saturday. "As prime minister, it's my duty to represent all Hungarians, and we have sensitive issues, such as the situation of sexual minorities."

Fidesz and its sister party, the Christian Democrats, voted against the new amendments to the law on Tuesday.

"There is no place for the promotion of LGBTQ content in schools or the media," the Christian Democrats said in a statement on their website.

World.title: Ekiti recruits 8,358 workers, generates N88.4bn IGR in four years – Gov Oyebanji
World.content:
The Ekiti State Governor, Biodun Oyebanji, on Tuesday, disclosed that the state government has employed no fewer than 8,358 workers into the state civil service, local governments, security outfits, among others in the last four years.

He also said that the state generated N88.4 billion as the Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) in the last four years.

Mr Oyebanji spoke while delivering the state of the state address at the Ekiti State House of Assembly complex, in Ado Ekiti, the state capital.

The governor, who said that the economy of Ekiti State continues to hold an exciting promise in all ramifications, added that a quick summary of Ekiti’s GDP performance from the recently released NBS Report indicates that the overall State GDP moved from 2.4 trillion in 2019 to 4.6 trillion in 2023, a growth of 90 per cent.

He said recent projections suggest that Ekiti GDP now inches towards the N8.8 trillion mark.

“This has moved Ekiti from the 33rd position to the 28th since APC was given the mandate to govern the state. Similarly, our contribution to the national GDP grew from 1.3 per cent to 1.6 per cent. Apparently, our economy is largely driven by trade, which contributed 1.7 trillion (37 per cent) and agriculture, which contributed 1.05 trillion (23 per cent). Both sectors contribute 60 per cent to the state’s economy,” he said.

On the employment created in the past four years, the governor said, “Since we assumed office, we have employed qualified persons in strategic places of need. The Civil Service Commission employed 41 senior officers in 2025 and the Office of Establishment and Service Matters has employed 340 junior officers.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Similarly, the Local Government Service Commission also employed 774 persons to fill consequential vacancies in 2025. So far, this administration has employed 6,530 teachers into both the public primary and secondary schools in the state. We employed 3,530 into the Teaching Service Commission and 3,000 into the State Universal Basic Education Board.

“In the security sector, we employed another set of personnel numbering over 600 to join the Ametokun Corps and the newly created Agro Marshal Corps, respectively, while Ekiti State Traffic Management Agency also took in an additional 73 traffic officers,” he said.

Speaking on the state IGR, Mr Oyebanji said when he took over in 2022, the average IGR of the state hovered around N650 million to N700 million monthly, totaling N8.7 billion in 2022, and that by the end of 2023, it had surged to N12 billion.

“The trend continued in 2024 with a reconciled figure of N17.6 billion; in 2025, we grossed N27.1 billion. As at the last reconciliation in June this year, we have already attained N15.6 billion, with all indications that we would near the N32billion mark at the end of the year, as we currently do average of N2.6 billion monthly.

“The growth per year indicated 38 per cent in 2023, 47% in 2024, 53 per cent in 2025 and about 60 per cent in 2026. Cumulatively speaking, we have generated the sum of N88.4billion as IGR in the last four years.

“The independent data from the Joint Revenue Board confirmed that 2025 was an exceptional year for Ekiti State’s revenue administration. The state grew Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) by 62.13 per cent, faster than any other state in the South-west and faster than 26 other States and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

“We increased our share of the national Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) and now fund a third of our total expenditure from our IGR. We hope to maintain this momentum going forward.

The governor attributed the achievements to the institutional re-organisation, transformation of the tax administration and improved business environment.

“All of this is possible because of the impact of the institutional re-organisation, digital transformation of tax administration, expansion of the tax net and improved business environment.

“It is for this reason that we have intentionally given more attention to trade, investment and agriculture since they have proved to be areas of our comparative advantage. With our deliberate investment in aviation and tourism, we hope to further diversify our economic base in the new tenure,” he said.

World.title: Reps panel backs Tinubu, NNPC, PINL over pipeline security gains
World.content:
The House of Representatives Committee on Host Communities has passed a vote of confidence in President Bola Tinubu, the management of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) Limited and Pipeline Infrastructure Nigeria Limited (PINL), citing improvements in crude oil recovery and pipeline security.

Chairman of the committee, Dumnamene Dekor (APC, Rivers), announced the resolution on behalf of the lawmakers following the adoption of a subcommittee report on a petition against PINL at a special sitting on Tuesday.

The committee also recommended that the federal government extend PINL’s pipeline surveillance contract after dismissing allegations of financial mismanagement and other improprieties against the company and its Managing Director, Osahon Okunbor, as unsubstantiated.

The decisions followed the adoption of a subcommittee report on a petition against PINL at a special sitting of the committee on Tuesday.

The petition, dated 5 September, was filed by the Niger Delta Oil-Producing Communities Reform Movement (ND-OCRIM), which accused the company of improper contract implementation, mismanagement of contract funds, neglect of surveillance personnel and alleged personal expenditure linked to Mr Okunbor.

The petitioners also called for a forensic review of PINL’s finances.

However, the subcommittee said the petitioners failed to appear despite three invitations issued on 14 September, 22 September and 5 October. It added that they neither sent representatives nor submitted documentary evidence to support their allegations.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

PINL appeared before the subcommittee and submitted a written report titled The Impact of PINL Operations on Oil Production and Stability of the Niger Delta, alongside geotagged photographic evidence.

Based on the submissions, the subcommittee concluded that the allegations against the company and its managing director had not been substantiated. It recommended that the committee dismiss the petition and discontinue further investigation into the issues raised.

The report also recommended a vote of confidence in Mr Tinubu, the National Security Adviser, NNPC Limited’s management and the pipeline surveillance contractors covered by the report.

Oil recovery and pipeline security

A key finding highlighted in the report was an increase in the proportion of crude oil reaching the Bonny Terminal through the Trans Niger Pipeline (TNP), according to data submitted by PINL.

The company reported that the proportion rose from three per cent in May 2022 to 98 per cent in September 2026.

The subcommittee also noted that “Oil Mining Lease (OML) 11, which had been shut in for 18 months, resumed operations within 90 days of PINL’s engagement.”

It further recorded that 2,049 illegal connections had been remediated and 1,010 illegal refinery clusters destroyed.

According to the company’s submission, its operations began in August 2022 and covered 215 host communities, with more than 35,600 surveillance guards deployed to support pipeline protection.

The operations were supported by 28 forward bases, 130 boats, 175 vehicles, 25 drones and 454 personnel from government security agencies.

The subcommittee attributed the reported operational gains to efforts to protect oil infrastructure and improve stability in the Niger Delta.

Community development initiatives

Beyond pipeline security, the report highlighted PINL’s community development initiatives, including more than 5,000 scholarships and skills training for over 4,000 women and girls.

The company also reportedly provided flood relief to more than 10 communities in Rivers State.

The committee commended NNPC Limited’s management for providing an enabling environment for pipeline security operations and urged PINL to sustain its engagement with host communities.

It also called on the company to maintain attention to the welfare of surveillance personnel.

The lawmakers’ position comes as Nigeria continues to pursue higher crude oil production amid persistent concerns about crude theft, pipeline vandalism and the underutilisation of oil assets.

According to production figures attributed to the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), crude oil production stood at approximately 1.50 million barrels per day in August 2026, while output including condensates was about 1.68 million barrels per day.

Average production reportedly rose from 1.388 million barrels per day in the first quarter of 2026 to 1.525 million barrels per day in the second quarter.

Despite the reported improvement, production remained below the 2026 budget benchmark of 1.84 million barrels per day.

The gap highlights the continuing challenge of increasing output to meet budget projections and strengthen government revenue and foreign exchange earnings.

The subcommittee consequently recommended that the federal government extend PINL’s pipeline surveillance contract and urged the company to sustain its operational performance and community development programmes.

The report will be presented to the House of Representatives in plenary for consideration and adoption.

World.title: Airport: Tinubu writes Senate, seeks approval to reimburse N100bn to Yobe govt
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has asked the Senate to approve the reimbursement of N100.5 billion to Yobe State Government for the construction of the Muhammadu Buhari International Cargo Airport in Damaturu, the state capital.

Mr Tinubu’s request was contained in a letter read by Senate President Godswill Akpabio during plenary on Tuesday.

In the letter, the president said the federal government had taken over the ownership and control of the airport, necessitating the reimbursement to the state government through a promissory note.

He said the Federal Executive Council (FEC) had approved the takeover, following which the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP) reviewed the project and recommended N100,509,017,234.55 as the amount to be reimbursed to the state government.

After reading the letter, Mr Akpabio referred the request to the Senate Committee on Local and Foreign Debts for further scrutiny.

The proposed reimbursement comes against the backdrop of the constitutional provisions governing aviation in Nigeria.

Item 3 of Part I of the Second Schedule to the 1999 Constitution, as amended, places aviation, including airports, aircraft safety and the carriage of passengers and goods by air, on the Exclusive Legislative List. This means the National Assembly has exclusive authority to make laws on these matters, to the exclusion of state Houses of Assembly, subject to the provisions of the Constitution.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Section 4(2) and (3) of the Constitution empower the National Assembly to legislate on matters on the Exclusive Legislative List. The constitutional arrangement provides the basis for federal regulation of aviation and the administration of airports under relevant federal laws.

The Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) Act also empowers the authority to maintain and manage airports transferred to it under the law, as well as other airports provided for under the relevant legislation.

However, the placement of aviation on the Exclusive Legislative List does not, by itself, establish that every airport must be owned by the federal government or automatically entitle a state that constructs an airport to reimbursement.

World.title: Military Plane Crash: Searchers build embankment, begin diversion of water from crash site
World.content:
The search and rescue team at the crash site of the Nigeria Air Force aircraft in Igbokoda, Ondo State has reviewed its search strategy by raising embankments around the crash area to limit the inflow of water and make for easy access to the remaining parts of the aircraft.

One of the operators of the Swamp Buggies, Adeleye Temitope, who disclosed this when PREMIUM TIMES visited the site on Tuesday, said the machines are helping in excavating heavy mud as an embankment to reduce the water level and allow divers and rescuers to reach the lower parts.

“The work is still ongoing and the swamp buggies are helping us lift the mud to the heights needed to keep the areas clear,” Mr Temitope said.

The NAF ATR-42 aircraft crashed into the swamp at Igbokoda, headquarters of Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State, on Monday, 5 October, killing 25 persons on board. It is believed to have plunged into the depths of the mud.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the divers and rescue teams had intensified their search for the plane’s black box and bodies of the victims.

However, on Tuesday morning, when our reporter visited the site, there were clues of the black box, which is now the main focus of the search operation.

It was also gathered that naval officials were available at the site using Geological Information Systems (GIS) to map the area so as to reach the rest of the wreckage.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It was also gathered that the operation is making efforts to completely remove all trees and other debris that would hamper the process, with a view to keeping the crash area completely free of debris.

Other technicians who visited the site returned with tales of how the area stinks, saying it was no longer safe for people to stay there for longer periods.

“You can go there to see what is going on, but to stay for more than 10 minutes is not good at all because of the way the place smells,” one of the technical officials, who would not want to be named, said.

However, Odunsola Dada, popularly known as General, who said he has been part of the rescue operation from inception, said ”the smell should not really be a thing of serious concern since the rescue must be done.”

“We all smell, and we will all die, so no matter what the situation is, someone will have to go down there and bring the dead out,” Mr Dada said.

“We are going to continue to work until we remove what is remaining.”

World.title: Tinubu transmits bills to strengthen drug enforcement, make NSIB independent authority to Senate
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has transmitted two bills to the Senate seeking to strengthen the enforcement of drug-related offences and reposition the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) as an independent, multimodal safety investigation authority.

The bills seek to repeal and re-enact the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) Act and the Indian Hemp Act, as well as amend the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (Establishment) Act, 2022.

Mr Tinubu transmitted the bills to the Senate in separate letters read by the Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, during plenary on Tuesday.

He transmitted the bills pursuant to Section 58(2) of the Nigerian Constitution.

NDLEA Bill

In his letter on the proposed NDLEA legislation, Mr Tinubu said the bill seeks to repeal the existing NDLEA Act and the Indian Hemp Act and establish a consolidated legal framework for combating drug-related offences.

He said the proposed legislation would strengthen enforcement against the cultivation, processing, sale, trafficking and use of illicit drugs. It would also empower the agency to investigate persons suspected of involvement in drug-related activities.

“The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency Bill 2026 seeks to repeal the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency Act, Cap. N30, and the Indian Hemp Act, Cap. I16, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2004, and to enact a consolidated framework to enforce the law against the cultivation, processing, sale, trafficking and use of hard drugs,” the president said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Tinubu urged the lawmakers to give the bill expeditious consideration.

After reading the letter, Mr Akpabio referred the bill to the Senate Committee on Rules and Business for further legislative action.

Nigeria remains a source, transit and destination country for illicit drugs, with trafficking networks dealing in substances ranging from cannabis and cocaine to methamphetamine and other synthetic drugs.

The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), in its 2025 assessment, reported that methamphetamine production capacity in Nigeria had increased by more than 40 per cent since 2020. The report also highlighted rising seizures of synthetic drugs across West Africa and the region’s continuing role as a transit corridor for cocaine trafficking between Latin America and Europe.

Despite enforcement operations, the scale of the trade remains a challenge for Nigerian authorities. The NDLEA said it arrested more than 18,500 suspected drug offenders and seized over 2.6 million kilograms of illicit substances in 2024.

If the proposed bill is passed, its effectiveness would depend not only on the scope of the new law but also on the agency’s capacity to investigate and prosecute offenders, disrupt trafficking networks, secure the country’s borders and ports, and address the financial proceeds of the illicit trade.

NSIB Amendment Bill

In a separate letter, Mr Tinubu transmitted the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (Amendment) Bill 2026, seeking to amend the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (Establishment) Act, 2022.

The proposed legislation seeks to reposition the bureau as an independent, multimodal safety investigation authority.

Under the proposed changes, the bureau’s mandate would extend beyond aviation accidents and incidents to cover occurrences involving rail, maritime and other modes of transportation.

The bill also seeks to transfer supervisory oversight of the bureau to the Presidency and strengthen its institutional, operational and administrative powers.

The president urged the Senate to consider the proposed legislation.

The senate president subsequently referred the bill to the Senate Committee on Rules and Business for further legislative action.

The proposed amendment to the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) Act comes amid agitation and the need for credible, independent investigations into transportation accidents and serious incidents.

The NSIB, formerly known as the Accident Investigation Bureau (AIB), investigates transportation accidents to establish their circumstances and probable causes and recommend measures to prevent similar incidents. Its investigations are intended to improve safety rather than determine criminal liability or apportion blame. The bureau’s mandate extends to aviation, maritime and rail transportation.

Repositioning the bureau as an independent, multimodal investigation authority could strengthen its ability to investigate accidents without undue influence from institutions whose activities or oversight responsibilities may be relevant to an investigation.

READ ALSO: Adeleke signs Osun park Management Bill into law amid opposition from APC

It could also help improve public confidence in investigation findings, support the implementation of safety recommendations and promote accountability across the transportation sector.

However, the practical implications will depend on the final provisions of the bill, particularly those governing the bureau’s financial autonomy, appointment of its leadership, access to evidence, publication of investigative reports and protection from interference.

Although the proposed bill seeks to transfer supervisory oversight to the Presidency, the extent to which this arrangement would guarantee operational independence will depend on the safeguards established by the legislation. Independence in accident investigation does not remove the responsibility of regulators, transport operators or law enforcement agencies to act on findings within their respective mandates.

World.title: WHO warns immunisation gaps leave Nigerian children vulnerable to disease
World.content:
The World Health Organisation (WHO) has warned that gaps in routine immunisation are leaving Nigerian children vulnerable to preventable diseases, urging the government to increase domestic health financing and strengthen disease surveillance and outbreak preparedness.

Pavel Ursu, the WHO representative in Nigeria, raised the concern on Tuesday during the organisation’s Health Diplomacy Dialogue in Abuja, which brought together diplomats and health officials to discuss health security, disease outbreaks, global health financing and antimicrobial resistance.

Mr Ursu said Nigeria continued to face challenges in containing vaccine-preventable diseases, including measles and circulating vaccine-derived poliovirus, despite support from international partners.

He said the country’s immunisation programme must reach approximately eight million additional children annually, placing increasing pressure on the health system.

“If we want to maintain the same level of performance, we have to invest more,” he said.

Mr Ursu acknowledged support from Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, and other partners in providing vaccines and related commodities but stressed the need for Nigeria to progressively increase domestic financing and assume greater responsibility for protecting its population.

He also highlighted changes in global health cooperation, including declining development assistance for health and ongoing discussions about reforming the global health architecture.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said African countries needed to strengthen domestic financing, improve health system resilience, expand digital health services and promote local manufacturing of health commodities.

Mr Ursu said the dialogue was established to provide a platform for the WHO and diplomatic missions to exchange strategic information on public health developments, emerging threats and international health policy, including for embassies without dedicated development cooperation programmes.

He called for stronger international cooperation, including timely information-sharing and coordinated responses to outbreaks that could cross national borders.

Outbreaks expose gaps in health security

Speaking on health security, Alex Chimbaru, the WHO emergencies adviser, said Nigeria’s disease outbreaks reflected persistent weaknesses in immunisation coverage, disease surveillance and access to safe water and sanitation.

He said more than 700 children had been disabled by circulating vaccine-derived poliovirus in previous years, warning that the actual number could be higher.

Mr Chimbaru also highlighted cholera as a major public health concern, citing inadequate water, sanitation and hygiene infrastructure, insecurity and population displacement as factors complicating prevention and response efforts.

He said Borno State accounted for 96 per cent of cases in the affected area discussed during his presentation, highlighting the need to prioritise interventions in vulnerable communities.

According to him, the WHO, other United Nations agencies, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) and other partners supported the response through surveillance, logistics, case management, vaccination, risk communication and infection prevention and control.

Mr Chimbaru called for sustained investment in water and sanitation, functional public health emergency operations centres, rapid response teams and stronger cross-border coordination to prevent and contain outbreaks.

He also urged development partners to reinforce government-led health systems rather than establish parallel structures, stressing that sustainable financing and stronger primary healthcare services were essential to health security.

Abuja to host global conference on antimicrobial resistance

The dialogue also featured discussions on Nigeria’s preparations to host a global conference on antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in Abuja from 6 to 8 December.

Mary Bartuo, the WHO team lead for universal health coverage and life course, said the conference would seek to translate international commitments into measurable action, stronger accountability and sustainable financing.

She said AMR was associated with about one million deaths annually in the African Region and posed growing threats to food security, livestock production and economic development.

Ms Bartuo said priorities under the proposed Abuja Compact included responsible AMR use, infection prevention and control, vaccination, water and sanitation, equitable access to medicines and diagnostics, research, local manufacturing and sustainable financing.

She urged diplomatic missions to participate in the conference and support efforts to strengthen national and international responses to AMR.

The WHO officials called for sustained investment and stronger collaboration among governments, diplomatic missions and development partners to improve health security and strengthen countries’ capacity to prevent, detect and respond to public health threats.

World.title: Senate to audit presidential, military aircraft, urges FG to replace ageing fleets
World.content:
The Senate has resolved to mandate its committees on Air Force and Aviation to conduct a comprehensive audit of aircraft in the presidential and military fleets to determine their condition and airworthiness.

The upper chamber also urged the federal government to prioritise funding for regular aircraft maintenance and the replacement of ageing military aircraft.

The resolutions followed a motion sponsored by Osita Ngwu, the senator representing Enugu West, on Tuesday to mourn the officers and crew members who died in the Nigerian Air Force (NAF) aircraft crash in the Igbokoda area of Ondo State on 5 October.

Mr Ngwu, a member of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), expressed concern that recurring military air crashes, which have claimed the lives of several personnel, might be linked to inadequate aircraft maintenance, ageing fleets and lapses in operational safety protocols and airworthiness standards.

He called for a transparent and comprehensive investigation into the circumstances surrounding the crash, arguing that future incidents could not be prevented without establishing their causes.

Twenty-five persons were on board the NAF aircraft when it crashed over a week ago. No survivors have been reported.

President Bola Tinubu subsequently declared three days of national mourning in honour of the deceased personnel and directed that national flags be flown at half-mast across the country.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Senate had earlier postponed indefinitely its national security summit, scheduled for 12 and 13 October, in honour of the crash victims.

The NAF had also promised a comprehensive investigation into the incident and assured the families of the victims that they would receive the benefits due to them.

Debate

Most senators who contributed to the debate supported the motion.

Tahir Monguno, the Borno North senator, who seconded the motion, called on the relevant committees to conduct a comprehensive audit of aircraft in the NAF fleet.

Mr Monguno, who is also the Senate Chief Whip, said the exercise should establish the aircraft’s serviceability, operational readiness and airworthiness to help prevent a recurrence.

Similarly, Adams Oshiomhole, the senator for Edo North, urged the Senate to direct the NAF to submit its aircraft maintenance budget proposals to the relevant committees.

Mr Oshiomhole, a former governor of Edo State, also called on the Senate to establish the amount allocated to aircraft maintenance.

Titus Zam (APC, Benue North-West) supported the proposal, noting that examining the Air Force’s maintenance budget would help determine the amount allocated for the purpose and whether the funding was adequate.

After the debate, Senate President Godswill Akpabio put the motion and its prayers to a voice vote, and the majority of senators voted in favour.

Mr Akpabio subsequently called on the air force and the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) to conduct a thorough, transparent and comprehensive investigation into the immediate and underlying causes of the crash and make their findings public.

He also directed the Senate committees on Air Force and Aviation to visit the crash site to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident.

The senate president thereafter asked his colleagues to observe a minute’s silence in honour of the deceased personnel and crew members.

World.title: Kano govt speaks on status of major projects
World.content:
The Kano State Government has monitored 106 projects valued at N48.9 billion across six local government areas to assess implementation, quality and service delivery within the year.

The Commissioner for Public Procurement, Projects Monitoring and Evaluation, Nura Iro-Ma’aji, disclosed this at a press briefing on Monday in Kano.

Mr Iro-Maaji said 80 of the projects, representing 75.5 per cent, recorded 100 per cent progress, while the remaining 20 were at various stages of completion, and six were recently awarded.

He said the monitoring exercise covered Kabo, Dawakin Tofa, Tofa, Shanono, Gwarzo and Bagwai Local Government Areas.

“The inspections covered roads, classrooms, school renovations, healthcare facilities, neighbourhood security offices, solar-powered streetlights, drainages, water supply and other essential facilities,” Mr Iro-Ma’aji said.

He said the exercise was aimed at assessing the physical implementation of projects, identifying challenges and determining their potential benefits to the communities.

The commissioner said the government would conduct follow-up inspections to address delays, incomplete works and quality concerns, while ensuring compliance with approved specifications and contractual obligations.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the monitoring records showed levels of progress on some major road projects.

The projects included the Janguza-Durum-Kabo-Karaye road corridor in Kabo, which recorded 48 per cent completion; the Hawan Ganji-Badari-Kadere road in Gwarzo, 67 per cent; and the five-kilometre road project in Shanono, which attained 65 per cent.

He also identified some education projects requiring further attention.

The projects, he said, included classrooms at Government Junior Secondary School (GJSS), Badau, in Bagwai, which recorded 55 per cent, and the GAA/GGSS Badau project at only 16 per cent.

He said the Government Technical College (GTC), Gwarzo, project stood at 72 per cent completion.

The commissioner added that rehabilitation of Shanono Primary Health Centre stood at 84 per cent, while neighbourhood security divisional offices had attained full completion in several LGAs.

“Dawakin Tofa recorded 85 per cent, while solar street lighting projects in Bagwai and Shanono stood at 35 per cent each,” he said.

He also announced that the state’s Digital Public Procurement Platform had gone live at procurement.kn.gov.ng.

According to him, the platform is expected to promote transparency, improve procurement documentation, strengthen audit trails, reduce administrative bottlenecks and enhance value for money.

Mr Iro-Ma’aji said the initiative supports the objectives of the Kano State Public Procurement Law, 2021.

He added that its success would depend on adoption by the 10 pilot Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs), capacity development and regulatory compliance.

The commissioner said the ministry would continue routine and follow-up monitoring across the state’s 44 LGAs and engage contractors and implementing agencies to resolve outstanding issues.

He added that the ministry would strengthen quality assurance, geospatial project reporting and public communication through town hall meetings across the LGAs.

The commissioner reaffirmed the government’s commitment to transparency and accountability, saying public projects must deliver measurable benefits to residents.

Mr Iro-Ma’aji called on implementing agencies, contractors, professional bodies, CSOs and the media to support the government’s efforts to improve project delivery and ensure responsible use of public resources.

(NAN)

World.title: Why Home Advantage Matters in Football, Tennis and Basketball
World.content:
Home advantage is one of the most widely accepted beliefs in modern athletics. It is the idea that teams often perform better in front of their fans. However, this does not mean that the home team will always win in reality.

Anything can happen in football, tennis, and basketball, and the win can go either way irrespective of how hostile the condition is. Although the general home-field advantage is worth considering, it’s just that it works quite differently for each sport. In team sports like football and basketball, the collective roar of thousands of fans can instantly shift momentum or even influence the referee’s decisions. So, don’t be surprised when the odds change drastically in the blink of an eye when betting on live matches at 1xBet Ghana, to reflect the match’s current momentum. Bettors should pay close attention to the smallest details that can contribute to the match’s outcome.

How Home Advantage Works in Sports

Home advantage is the belief that athletes and sports teams win more often and perform better at home than when they travel to face an opponent. In team sports, this usually means playing in front of the club’s own supporters. In tennis, it can mean playing in a player’s home country or at a tournament where they are comfortable with the conditions. Below are some factors that contribute to home advantage in sport:

Support from home crowds: A roaring stadium has a massive psychological impact on the players. The noise triggers an adrenaline rush, which helps home players fight through exhaustion during the dying minutes. A loud crowd can also make communication harder for the visiting team and add pressure during important moments.

Reduced travel demands: Traveling is stressful and can affect sleeping patterns, diets, and overall concentration. Home teams don’t experience these disruptions, giving them an edge.

Familiar playing surfaces and conditions: Home teams already understand their own training grounds and stadium layout. This makes it easier for them to easily execute tactics and play to instruction.

The demand to impress the fans: The natural instinct to give the fans bragging rights can bring a major mental boost during the game. Players naturally play with more aggression and confidence when playing in front of their fans.

Note that home advantage is not all it takes to win a match. A team with poor form can still lose at home. A strong away team can also perform well in hostile conditions.

Home advantage doesn’t work the same way across these three sports. For instance, Chelsea were unbeaten at home for 86 consecutive Premier League games from 2004 to 2008. During that time, they won multiple League titles, domestic cups, and played in several Champions League knockout matches.

Moreover, a tennis player may perform better at a certain tennis surface or tournament than another. For example, Rafael Nadal has a 90.5% career win percentage on clay, losing just 51 times and winning 484 games on the surface. Another notable home record win in the NBA is held by San Antonio Spurs in the 2015/16 season. The Spurs did 40-1 at home, and the single loss didn’t happen until game 39 of the home schedule.

So, it is difficult to conclude that a particular sport has the strongest home advantage over the other. Fans should instead focus on the entertainment that each sport has to offer.

Why Home Advantage Changes from Match to Match

Home advantage is only one of the things that can play a part in the outcome of a match. There are other contributing factors to consider. For instance, the quality of the competing teams can play a crucial role in how the game outcome will be. A bottom-tier football or basketball team will rarely beat a championship team simply because they are playing at home. In the same way, a major football match in a famous stadium can create a different environment from a low-profile league game.

Therefore, the importance of the game, the health of the roster, and the distance the visitors had to travel can also influence the match. In tournament formats, a massive cross-country road trip can drastically affect a team’s physical freshness compared to short, regular travel.

Home advantage is one metric gamblers should consider when forecasting sports betting selections. It is advisable to use home advantage as part of a wider analysis of sports bet, but it should not be treated as a guaranteed way to predict results.

In football, the most familiar market is the home win, draw or away win. A team’s home record can make it easier to forecast the possibility of getting any of these three outcomes. For example, a team that performs well at home may have an advantage over an opponent that struggles on the road. However, recent form, injuries, squad quality and the strength of the opposition still need to be considered. A strong home record alone does not mean a home win is the best choice.

In basketball, home advantage can be considered in both the moneyline and point spread markets. The moneyline focuses on which team wins the game, while the point spread gives the stronger team a points handicap. A home team may be more likely to win, but the spread can still make the matchup less straightforward if the visiting team is expected to keep the game close.

Tennis has its own set of betting options. The match-winner market is the most direct option, while set markets focus on how the match may develop. A player’s home advantage may come from crowd support, knowledge of the court and local playing conditions. But surface form can be more important than simply playing in front of a home crowd.

Other Factors to Consider Beyond Home Advantage

Home advantage should also be used carefully when analyzing the outcome of a match. A team’s old home record may include different players, coaches and opponents. A tennis player’s results from several years ago may say little about current form. The same applies to basketball teams after major roster changes.

The best approach is to treat home advantage as one piece of information, since it doesn’t reveal the full picture. The table below reveals the different factors that can affect football, tennis and basketball performances and results.

Home Advantage in the Modern Professional Sport Era

In modern professional sports, there is growing evidence that the traditional weight of home advantage is gradually shrinking. Professional athletes have better travel arrangements, training facilities and recovery methods than in the past. Teams also use data to prepare for different opponents and playing environments.
