Players are now more accustomed to international travel. Many compete in different countries throughout the year, so unfamiliar surroundings may not be as difficult as they once were.

While the physical gap between hosting and traveling is narrower today than it has ever been in sports history, Supporters still create noise. As such, the emotional spark of a passionate home crowd and the baseline comfort of local conditions will always matter.

When Home Advantage Matters Less in Sports

Home advantage doesn’t sometimes count in some matches. However, that doesn’t take away the game’s intensity and competitiveness. It’s just that playing at home doesn’t matter as much. Below are some conditions where the home advantage matters less:

Neutral venues: When neither side plays in its usual stadium, both teams have to adapt to an unfamiliar environment. The crowd may also be split between the two sides.

Low attendance: If there are few supporters, the home team may receive less of the energy normally associated with playing at home.

Players’ experience: Elite teams and athletes travel regularly and have professional support staff who help them manage their wellbeing. This can reduce some of the problems associated with playing away from home.

Opponent’s strength: A very strong team may be able to control a match despite playing away. In the same way, a weak home side does not automatically become a strong team because it is playing in familiar surroundings.

Conclusion

The venue in which a match will be played can dictate the atmosphere of the game. As such, home advantage can bring confidence, concentration, energy, and preparation to players.

Football teams can benefit from their stadium, supporters and familiarity with the pitch. Basketball teams can use crowd energy and court familiarity to their advantage. Tennis players can gain from local support, familiar surfaces and reduced travel. However, none of these factors guarantees success.

The better football team can still win away from home and the better tennis player can also win even when the surface conditions are not favorable. In the end, an outstanding performance will overcome any disadvantage caused by not playing at home.

World.title: France accuses Elon Musk of ‘online harassment’ of Europe leaders
World.content:
Musk

France’s foreign minister on Tuesday accused the billionaire tycoon and owner of the X social media platform Elon Musk of “online harassment” of European leaders, as he sounded the alarm over the risks of interference in the French 2027 presidential election.

Jean-Noel Barrot warned that ahead of the April-May election — in which far-right candidate Marine Le Pen has her best ever chance of winning the Elysee — “the enemies of democracy will do everything to destabilise us”.

“They exploit our divisions and exploit issues such as immigration, secularism, and the Israeli-Palestinian conflict to stoke hatred and tension,” he said at a conference organised by the Paris-based Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).

He singled out an Israeli company — which he did not identify — that he said had created fake French accounts to post over the Israel-Palestinian conflict.

But Barrot also took aim at the “massive online harassment campaigns by Elon Musk against European leaders, aimed at influencing national debates by exploiting the viral nature of his social network.”

With France rocked by several weeks of protests by high school students over their conditions, Barrot complained that some coverage of the demonstrations online had been marked by “hostile narratives originating from Russia and China, as well as Iran and the MAGA community” in reference to the supporters of US President Donald Trump.

Trump had last week written on his Truth Social network that “what’s happening in France is nothing less than out of control mass migration.”

Musk had then commented to his 241.5 million followers on X: “It’s an invasion in slow motion, but an invasion nonetheless. And those who support the invasion are traitors who deserve the fate of all traitors.”

Barrot vowed that France would hit back.

“We do not tolerate any foreign interference, from wherever it may come. It is a matter of sovereignty,” he said.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Monday it was “clear” Russia had interfered in the UK’s bitter 2016 Brexit referendum that resulted in its exit from the European Union.

AFP

World.title: Davido submits multiple entries for 2027 Grammy Awards
World.content:
Nigerian singer David Adeleke, popularly known as Davido, has submitted multiple entries for consideration at the 2027 Grammy Awards.

The Grammy Guru made the disclosure on its X page (formerly Twitter) – @thegrammyguru.

The entries include his album ‘Oriade’ and several songs in categories including Album of the Year, Best Global Music Album, Record of the Year, Song of the Year and Best African Music Performance.

‘Oriade’, his sixth studio album, was entered for Album of the Year, Best Global Music Album, Best Engineered Album, Non-Classical and Best Album Cover.

According to the News Guru, Davido’s hit “B4 B4″, featuring Mayorkun and FOLA, was submitted for Record of the Year, Song of the Year and Best African Music Performance.

Another collaboration, ‘Nakupenda’, featuring TxC, Zlatan, Shoday, Scotts Maphuma and Al Xapo, was entered for Song of the Year and Best African Music Performance.

Davido’s song ‘Le Show,’ featuring Ayra Starr and French Montana, was also entered for Best African Music Performance, while ‘I Know Who I Be,’ featuring JAZZWRLD and GL_Ceejay, was submitted for Best Music Video.

The submissions come as the Recording Academy begins first-round voting for the 2027 Grammys, scheduled to run from Oct. 12 to Oct. 22.

The academy is expected to announce nominees for the 69th edition of the annual awards on Nov. 16, while the awards ceremony is scheduled for Feb. 7, 2027.

Davido has previously received Grammy nominations for his album ‘Timeless’ and songs ‘Unavailable’ and ‘Feel’ at the 66th edition in 2024.

The reported submissions reflect the continued efforts of Nigerian artistes to secure recognition at international music awards. (NAN)

World.title: Ex-Chelsea owner Abramovich denies tax fraud after BBC report
World.content:
Abramovich

Russian oligarch Roman Abramovich denied allegations of tax fraud, his lawyers said Tuesday, after a BBC investigation alleged that documents were falsified to conceal his wealth and help one of his companies evade tax.

“No evidence has been provided that Mr Abramovich knew of, authorised or directed the falsification or backdating of any document, and he denies that he evaded tax or concealed his fortune,” said the law firm representing Abramovich, Kobre & Kim.

“Mr Abramovich denies any wrongdoing. He was not involved in the day-to-day operation of the companies concerned,” his lawyers added in a statement sent to AFP.

The BBC reported on Monday that superyachts, private jets and mansions worth $672 million disappeared from Abramovich’s company accounts, which were signed off by accounting firm Deloitte in Cyprus in 2006.

The BBC’s current affairs programme Panorama also reported that Abramovich’s associates hid the fortunes of two of his other companies, worth nearly $2 billion and more than $10 billion, respectively, from Cypriot authorities.

In all three cases, documents were backdated with the involvement of MeritServus, a company that is now closed and was owned by Deloitte until 2005, the BBC reported.

Deloitte is one of the world’s four largest accounting firms, known as the “Big Four”.

The BBC based its reporting on a leak of documents covering the period from 1995 to 2022.

Deloitte’s Cyprus branch told AFP it “acts in compliance with applicable laws”, but declined to comment further.

The Guardian reported in 2023 that Abramovich had tried to shield his wealth by transferring several billion dollars to his children just before he was targeted by sanctions in retaliation for Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

Britain sanctioned the oligarch for his close ties to the Kremlin and froze his assets.

The businessman was forced to sell Chelsea football club, which he had owned since 2003, and which was bought in May 2022 by a new consortium led by American businessman Todd Boehly.

The proceeds of the sale, totalling around £2.5 billion ($3.3 billion), were frozen in a British bank account.

The UK government wants the funds to be directed towards humanitarian purposes in Ukraine, but the oligarch has insisted they be used for all victims of the conflict, including ones in Russia.

AFP

World.title: ‘We moved on’ – Dias reveals Man City players discussed guilty verdict
World.content:
Manchester City’s players celebrate on the pitch after the English Premier League football match between Liverpool and Manchester City at Anfield in Liverpool, north west England on October 11, 2026. Manchester City won the game 3-0. (Photo by Paul ELLIS / AFP) / RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE. No use with unauthorized audio, video, data, fixture lists, club/league logos or ‘live’ services. Online in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No video emulation. Social media in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No use in betting publications, games or single club/league/player publications. /

By Adegboyega Adeleye

Manchester City captain Ruben Dias has revealed that the squad met to discuss the club’s guilty verdict over breaches of Premier League financial rules, saying the players sought “peace of mind” before moving on.

According to Sky Sports, Dias, who spoke at a news conference on Tuesday ahead of Manchester City’s Champions League clash against Paris Saint-Germain, said the players agreed to discuss the verdict as soon as they reunited after the international break, when an independent commission found City guilty of all charges relating to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules.

“When it broke, we felt we should have a conversation as soon as we got back,” Dias said on Tuesday.

“We did, for everyone to be on the same page, and be clear about our peace of mind. We moved on from there.

“It happened in a moment when we were not together but quickly we reached out to each other, found calm and progressed forward.”

Manchester City have maintained their innocence and lodged an appeal against the verdict.

Dias admitted that the squad could not completely avoid the public scrutiny surrounding the case but insisted the players remained focused on their work.

“There’s a lot of noise and it’s almost impossible to avoid seeing something even us being as private as we can be. On your phone, it’s impossible to avoid everything,” he said.

“We’re very good at focusing on our job and being happy every time we come to work. Our minds are there and only there. It’s the things we can control and the things we’ve always been doing and enjoying so much.

“We have full confidence in the club and trust the club.”

Asked whether the players were being told how to react to the situation, Dias replied: “No. We do what we do, we go on the pitch, play football and we win. The answer is no.”

The City captain also defended the squad’s celebrations after their 3-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, insisting the result was the main reason for their reaction.

“It all mixes together a little bit but mainly we know it’s not easy to get three points at Anfield. That is definitely the main reason. We’re here for the points and to win competitions, that’s the main thing on our minds,” he said.

Dias added that City would celebrate an Anfield victory regardless of the circumstances or stage of the season.

“I very much stand by the manager’s words. It’s a win at Anfield. In whatever circumstance, be it early in the season or late in the season, we will enjoy it just as much and celebrate however we feel in the moment. It’s a show of how much it means to us.”

He also dismissed the suggestion that criticism surrounding the club had changed the squad’s outlook, saying rival supporters were unhappy when City won.

“If there’s more or less noise, for whatever reason, it’s all the same. Same as before because people don’t love us winning and we love to win,” Dias said.

“It’s a normal scenario where whenever you win, there are people that are not happy with it because they have the same ambition to win.”

Meanwhile, City manager Enzo Maresca said the fallout from the verdict had been more difficult for supporters than for the players and staff.

“After we were very happy, sharing time with our fans. It has been more tough for our fans than for the players or for me,” Maresca said.

“It is more complicated. If I am an Arsenal or a United fan, I can tell a City fan, ‘Ay, my friend, you cheat’.

“It has been more tough for them. We were happy after the game, celebrating the three points.”

Maresca also praised Dias’s leadership, saying the defender had been a leader since the manager joined the club in the summer.

“Not just the last fews day, since I joined the club in the summer, I was in touch with Ruben. Since day one he has been a real leader and has done very well in all aspects,” he said.

World.title: Zverev celebrates year-end No. 1 ranking with Shanghai Masters win
World.content:
Germany’s Alexander Zverev hits a return to Kazakhstan’s Alexander Bublik during their men’s singles match at the Shanghai Masters tennis tournament in Shanghai on October 13, 2026. (Photo by Hector RETAMAL / AFP)

By Adegboyega Adeleye

Alexander Zverev celebrated securing the year-end world No. 1 ranking with a hard-fought victory over Alexander Bublik to reach the quarter-finals of the Shanghai Masters on Tuesday.

According to Sky Sports, the German defeated Bublik 7-6 (8-6), 4-6, 7-6 (7-1) in a fiercely contested encounter, despite struggling with an ankle problem during the match.

The victory marked Zverev’s 40th ATP Masters 1000 quarter-final appearance and his first time reaching the last eight in Shanghai since 2019.

The top seed had to dig deep against Bublik, saving four set points in the opening-set tie-break before taking it 8-6. The Kazakh responded by winning the second set 6-4, forcing a decider.

Zverev, however, raised his level in the final tie-break, dominating 7-1 to seal victory after two hours and 41 minutes.

Despite progressing, the German admitted that his ankle was troubling him during the match, raising concerns about his fitness ahead of the quarter-finals.

“My ankle was acting up, unfortunately,” Zverev said after the match, adding that he was beginning to feel the physical demands of his schedule.

“I’m starting to feel my body more and more, but happy to be through because it was a difficult match. He’s been playing amazing tennis this week. I think the most important thing was that I won today,” he added.

Zverev will face Australia’s Alex de Minaur in the quarter-finals after the ninth seed produced an impressive performance to defeat Karen Khachanov 6-3, 6-4 in straight sets.

De Minaur’s victory secured his place in the last eight, setting up a challenging encounter against Zverev, who will be looking to maintain his momentum despite his ankle concerns.

Zverev secures year-end No. 1 ranking

The Shanghai Masters victory was Zverev’s first match since he was confirmed as the year-end world No. 1 on Monday.

The German secured the distinction after Spain’s Carlos Alcaraz suffered a shock third-round defeat to unseeded Belgian Zizou Bergs, who won 7-5, 7-6 (7-4).

Alcaraz’s exit meant he could no longer overtake Zverev in the rankings before the end of the season, while current world No. 1 Jannik Sinner has been ruled out for the remainder of 2026 because of a knee injury.

Zverev will therefore finish the season at the top of the ATP rankings for the first time in his career, becoming the first German player to achieve the year-end No. 1 distinction.

The achievement adds to a remarkable season for the 29-year-old, who won the French Open and US Open to claim his first two Grand Slam titles.

The German will now turn his attention to the Shanghai Masters quarter-finals, where he is chasing his first title at the tournament and another opportunity to strengthen his position ahead of the season’s remaining competitions.

World.title: NAFDAC uncovers fake drinks den in Lagos, arrests two
World.content:
… Energy drinks, wine, whisky allegedly repackaged in secret facility at Trade Fair Complex

By Chioma Obinna

The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) has uncovered a suspected counterfeit drinks production facility at Zamfara Plaza, BBA Trade Fair Complex, along the Badagry Expressway, Ojo, Lagos State, arresting two suspects allegedly involved in the illegal operation.

The suspects, identified as Chibuzor Okafor and William John, were arrested during an enforcement operation in a two-storey building where equipment and materials allegedly used to repackage and produce counterfeit alcoholic and energy drinks were discovered.

The raid, according to NAFDAC, followed credible intelligence and surveillance on suspected counterfeiters operating within the Trade Fair International Market.

Speaking during the operation, the Assistant Director of the Investigation and Enforcement Directorate of NAFDAC, Mr Kunle Ojo, said the agency caught some of the suspects in the act and recovered drums, filters, packaging materials, a heating device and other equipment allegedly used in the illicit production process.

“Gentlemen of the press, as you can see today, when we came, we caught some red-handed people producing all kinds of alcoholic drinks,” Ojo said.

“What we have discovered today is a lot, and it’s mind-boggling. We are here to protect the lives of many Nigerians.”

Ojo said the agency intensified its enforcement activities ahead of the festive season, when demand for alcoholic and other beverages typically rises.

He warned that the circulation of counterfeit drinks posed a serious public health concern, urging suspected manufacturers to abandon the illegal trade. “You are killing Nigerians in order to make money, which is not good,” he said, appealing to those involved to stop the activities.

The NAFDAC official disclosed that the agency would investigate the source of the products, the raw materials used and the individuals allegedly financing or directing the operation.

“Where are they getting the products from? Where are they getting their raw materials? Who is employing them to do this kind of dangerous activity? ”.

He added that the agency would evacuate the recovered materials and products to its warehouse for further action, including destruction in accordance with applicable procedures.

“Those people that we have arrested today will be dealt with administratively and definitely will face the law,” Ojo said.

Ojo also appealed to Nigerians to support the agency by providing credible information about suspected counterfeit production facilities.

“If you see something, say something,” he said, assuring informants that their identities would be protected.

One of the arrested suspects, Chibuzor Okafor, who identified himself as a drinks dealer in the market, in an interview with Vanguard at the scene, said, “I deal in drinks. I change the bottle of the drink. It’s not that the bottle is not good. It’s the drink in there, because the other one is already damaged. So that’s why we are putting it in the next bottle,” he said.

Also speaking during the operation, Mrs. Christiana Obiazikwor, Deputy Director, NAFDAC Public Relations, said the agency routinely carried out surveillance, seizures, arrests and destruction of unregistered and counterfeit products, despite public criticism that it was not doing enough to tackle the menace.

“NAFDAC is still at work. We are on the streets. We are in the markets. We are everywhere,” she said.

Obiazikwor explained that enforcement teams often conducted operations without publicity to avoid alerting suspected offenders or triggering confrontations.

She said the agency decided to take journalists along on the latest operation to demonstrate its activities and reassure Nigerians that it remained committed to protecting public health.

“Most of the things they do, we don’t publicise them so that we don’t raise alarm,” she said, adding that enforcement officers continued to visit suspected production and distribution points.

She urged members of the public to report suspected counterfeit production and distribution directly to NAFDAC rather than merely posting allegations on social media.

“There’s no point going to social media to create fear. Report to NAFDAC, and we’ll do the needful.”

Obiazikwor assured informants that the agency would protect their identities, urging Nigerians to provide credible information that could assist investigations.

Speaking, the Assistant Director, Head Public Relation, Investigation & Enforcement, Mrs Victoria Jennifer Akudu, explained that the raid was part of the agency’s routine efforts to uncover illegal manufacturing activities and protect consumers.

“Every day, our people are in the field. Our enforcement department, they are on the field trying to uncover this. And they do a lot,” Akudu said.

She explained that the agency routinely confiscated products, carried out seizures and destroyed offending goods, adding that the latest operation was intended to demonstrate the work being done by enforcement officers.

“This is just a routine activity of our enforcement directorate,” she said.

Akudu further disclosed that the suspected operators had allegedly moved from an earlier location after enforcement action, prompting officials to continue tracking their activities.

“We have confiscated and sealed off the place. They moved to another place. This time around, we passed through the back door. And that is how we are able to get them,” she said.

She urged Nigerians to report suspected counterfeit products directly to NAFDAC rather than allow rumours and unverified claims to create unnecessary public fear.

Akudu assured the public that the agency remained committed to its responsibilities, stressing that its enforcement teams were continuing operations against suspected manufacturers and distributors of illegal products.

“I will ask Nigerians not to fear. We are alert, and we are alive. We are doing our statutory function the way it should be,” she said.

NAFDAC officials said the operation formed part of continuing efforts to remove counterfeit, adulterated and unregistered products from the Nigerian market.

The agency reiterated that consumers could be exposed to serious health risks when drinks were repackaged under the labels of established brands without proper quality controls or verification of their contents.

World.title: NAF Plane Crash: Igbokoda residents lament stench, fear disease outbreak, as body parts float
World.content:
By Dayo Johnson, Akure

More than a week after a Nigerian Air Force, NAF, aircraft crashed in Igbokoda, Ondo State, residents said they are battling offensive odour, polluted water and fear for disease outbreak.

Read Also: NAF PLANE CRASH: How hero pilot died saving town

The NAF ATR-42, which was flying from Benin City to Lagos, crashed into a swamp near the Air Force Forward Operating Base in Igbokoda on October 5, killing all 25 persons on board.

They appealed to the Federal Government, Ondo State government and the Nigerian Air Force to urgently evacuate the human remains, clean up the environment and provide safe drinking water for the community.

The aircraft was on a routine operation when it crashed on Monday, October 5, killing all 25 persons on board, comprising five crew members and 20 passengers.

It submerged into the swamp, prompting a joint search and recovery operation by the Air Force, other security agencies and emergency responders. More than a week after, locals say the operation is yet to be fully concluded.

Community leaders and residents told Vanguard that the decomposing bodies and spillage of aviation fuel have left the entire area polluted.

Body parts float

The Olu of Igbokoda, Oba Afolabi Odidiomo, said the stench from the crash site has spread to residential areas, making life unbearable for residents.

He said body parts were still seen floating on the river, while traces of fuel could be observed some distance from the wreckage site.

“The odour is extremely offensive and unbearable. So many parts of human bodies are floating around in the river. Some of the bodies have not been recovered, they have decomposed and it is affecting everything,” the monarch said.

According to him, the development has raised serious concerns over contamination of the river, which serves as a major source of water for domestic use.

“People are worried about cooking, bathing and other domestic uses. We are appealing to government to urgently remove the remaining bodies and debris, contain any fuel spillage and carry out full environmental remediation,” Oba Odidiomo said.

He also called for immediate provision of potable water for residents pending conclusion of recovery and clean-up operations, stressing that the welfare of the host community should not be overlooked.

Smell

For residents living near the river, the experience has been distressing.

Omogbemi Damola, a resident, said she has been perceiving the foul odour in her upstairs apartment for days.

“What happened in Igbokoda is a very sad experience. Since the accident occurred, different kinds of unpleasant odours have been carried by the breeze into our homes.

“I live upstairs and I have been perceiving the smell for at least four days now,” she said.

She appealed to the state government to expedite action on the recovery of bodies and measures to control the stench, noting that the community has already suffered enough trauma from the incident.

Another resident, Oroyo Levy, said the situation has gone beyond discomfort to a public health concern.

“We are appealing to government to act swiftly to contain the odour and prevent it from posing further health risks.

“The smell suggests air pollution and we are worried about its effect, especially on children,” Levy said.

He described the crash as an unusual and painful experience for the riverine community, and urged authorities to investigate the environmental impact of the incident to avert another crisis.

Levy added that more than a week after the tragedy, uncertainty over water safety has heightened anxiety among residents who depend on the river.

Residents therefore urged the National Emergency Management Agency, NEMA; State Emergency Management Agency, SEMA, and relevant environmental agencies to intervene and ensure that the aftermath of the crash does not trigger an outbreak of waterborne diseases.

Govt reacts

Reacting, the State Commissioner for Environment, Tob Loko, said the state government was collaborating with the Federal Government to ensure maximum recovery.

“The state government is collaborating with the Federal Government to ensure that we carry out as much recovery as possible.

“But you know that despite the number of days the recovery effort has been ongoing, no meaningful recovery has been made. None of the corpses has been recovered.

“Shortly afterwards, concerns about pollution were raised. What we are trying to do is make a holistic assessment of the level of public health impact and determine how we can embark on decontamination efforts because the surrounding area is surely contaminated.

“So, there is a case of pollution. But we are not resting on our laurels. As I have said, we are carefully undertaking holistic assessments of the environmental impact and the public health impact of what has happened there to ensure that we address it as quickly as possible,” he said.

‘They have drinking water’

On claims of drinking water pollution, the commissioner said the complaint was not entirely correct.

“That is not the water they drink. There are boreholes around. So, the claim that the water is no longer useful is not entirely correct.

“Let me also say this: Some people insinuate that the site of the crash is close to the metropolis. Of course, the crash site is at least 500 metres away from the bulk of the metropolis. So, the issue of not having water to drink and other associated concerns is not there.

“We are not ruling out the fact that there may be cases of pollution. But to say that the people do not have water to drink as a result of the crash is not a sustainable argument or concern, so to speak,” Loko added.

Vanguard News

World.title: Police Interrogate Okorocha, Release Him on Bail
World.content:
*Insist Ex-Governor Is Under Investigation

Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Nigeria Police Force has confirmed the arrest of former Imo State Governor Rochas Okorocha in connection with an alleged involvement in criminal conspiracy and forgery.

Confirming the arrest, the Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Anietie Iniedu, said the APC chieftain had been arrested, interrogated and released on bail.

CSP Iniedu noted that the former governor had been directed to report to the police on Tuesday for further interrogation following his release on bail on Monday.

Okorocha was arrested at a hotel in Abuja while attending a reception to celebrate a friend’s conferment of the rank of Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN).

The police, however, did not disclose the details of the alleged criminal conspiracy and forgery but insisted that the former governor was under investigation.

The police were said to have obtained a bench warrant following Okorocha’s alleged failure to honour invitations to appear for interrogation.

World.title: Shell Quits Domestic Gas Distribution, Sells SNG To Nigerian Firm, Vaaris Energy
World.content:
Peter Uzoho

Shell Petroleum B.V. has signed an agreement to sell its full interest in the Shell Nigeria Gas Group to Nigerian energy company, Vaaris Energy Limited.

Shell Nigeria Gas operates Nigeria’s domestic gas distribution business and has served industrial and commercial customers for more than 25 years.

Shell’s Country Chair in Nigeria, Elohor Aiboni, announced the transaction Tuesday, saying the deal provides a stronger platform for the business under new ownership, while allowing Shell to focus on its strategic deepwater and integrated gas positions in Nigeria.

“Shell Nigeria Gas has served industrial and commercial customers in Nigeria for more than 25 years, supported by the commitment and expertise of its people,” Aiboni said in a statement signed by Shell’s Country Communications Manager, Gladys Afam-Anadu.

“We believe this agreement provides a much stronger platform for the business’ next chapter under new ownership. Shell continues to focus on strategic Deepwater and Integrated Gas positions in Nigeria,” Aiboni added.

The transaction is subject to regulatory conditions and approvals. Until completion, the Shell Nigeria Gas Group will remain part of Shell and will continue to serve customers and operate as usual.

Shell Nigeria Gas Limited was established in 1998 and supplies natural gas to industrial and commercial customers. It operates around 170 kilometres of pipeline infrastructure across Ogun, Abia and Rivers states, serving more than 130 connected commercial and industrial customers.

SNG does not operate in upstream gas production, liquefied natural gas or international gas trading.

The transaction includes Shell Nigeria Gas Holding B.V., established in 2019, which holds all the shares except one in Shell Nigeria Gas Limited.

Vaaris Energy Limited is a Nigerian energy company with interests across the oil and gas value chain and an existing operational footprint in the country.

Shell said the sale is consistent with its strategy to simplify its portfolio and concentrate investment in areas where it has competitive strengths.

“In Nigeria, our continued focus on Deepwater and Integrated Gas, including our interest in Nigeria LNG, exemplifies our strategy,” the company said.

World.title: 2027: Bende Traditional Rulers Disown LP Candidate Anyaso on Rotation Document, Allege Forgery
World.content:
Traditional rulers in Bende Federal Constituency of Abia State have disowned and dissociated themselves from a document circulating as a purported 2019 agreement on representation and rotation for the seat of the constituency in the House of Representatives.

The document, linked to the Labour Party (LP) candidate for Bende Federal Constituency, Chima Anyaso over the weekend where in it was purported that the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Okezie Kalu alongside some traditional rulers from Bende North and Bende South, the two political blocs that made up the federal constituency signed an 8-year rotation agreement between them in 2019.

In a swift reaction to the development, the Director General of the Benjamin Kalu Movement (BKM), Hon. Emma Trumps Eke, whose name and signature appeared on the document as signatory debunked the claims, saying the document was forged and no such meeting ever held among Bende traditional rulers.

He distanced himself and the Deputy Speaker from the document in circulation, warning against deliberate attempts to cause division amongst the people of Bende and the traditional institution.

The document had stated that the agreement took place on January 10, 2019 whereas the proposal for negotiations was signed on February 4, 2026, a development that casts doubts on its source and authenticity.

In his disclaimer, Eke said: “I have been made aware of a document circulating as a purported proposal on representation and rotation in Bende Federal Constituency. The document is said to have been signed by me, Rev. Emmanuel Trumps Eke, and my Principal, the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Okezie Kalu, Ph.D., CFR.

“I wish to state categorically that neither I, nor my Principal, signed any such document. It is false and an outright fabrication.”

On the content of the document, Eke said: “The font and style of writing the names of Traditional Rulers and dates inserted on the signatory page of the document makes it clear that it is an outright forgery.

“Letter one was purported to have been produced on February 4, 2019. The date of the second document is 19th January, 2019. If the traditional rulers have already settled a matter in January, why do we need to seek the same reliefs in February?

“The Traditional Ruler who is purported to have signed as Chairman of Bende South in 2019, Eze Patrick Ude, was not Chairman of Bende South Traditional Rulers Council in 2019.”

“A document produced by Traditional Rulers of Bende will be placed on their official letter head with the appropriate official accouterments and not on a facsimile paper.

“The traditional rulers, whose names are listed as signatories and witnesses to the document, have, at various fora, denied that any such document exists or that they signed it.

“The first page is a bromide of a letter we wrote to Bende Stakeholders in 2019 soliciting their support. They have removed the original content of the letter and superimposed their forgery.

“I therefore state without equivocation that the document in circulation is fake and an outright forgery.

“For the avoidance of doubt, I reiterate again that no such conversation or agreement about tenure and turn took place with anyone, to the best of my knowledge.

“It is regrettable that this purported document is being used to advance a narrative about “turn” and political agreements. Those making such claims should focus on presenting their plans and proposals directly to the people of Bende, rather than relying on a forged document.

“I urge the public to exercise caution and verify the authenticity of any document before sharing it. Those responsible for producing, or knowingly distributing a forged document, will be held accountable in accordance with the law.”

Similarly, the traditional rulers whose names appeared on the document have also issued separate disclaimers.

His Royal Highness Dr. Patrick Ude, Isiobu 1 of Umuisiobu Autonomous Community, Bende LGA listed as Chairman/representative from Bende South, in a letter dated October 9, 2026 said he was never a part of such meeting, let alone signing any document.

“I hereby state clearly and without ambiguity to Ndi Bende, Abia State and the general public that I was never invited to, never attended any meeting where such agreement was discussed or reached. I did not sign, thumbprint or witness any document in respect of rotation of Bende Federal Constituency seat.

“My name and office was included in that letter without my knowledge or consent. I dissociate myself completely from the said publication and its content. The general public should disregard the publication as it concerns me. I will remain a father to all political actors and I am for peace, equity and progress of Bende federal constituency”, he said.

Also, HRH Eze Jerry Akpala Igwe (Aka-ji Ofo Item) of Ikwueze Okoko Item Autonomy Community, Bende Local Government Area of the State in his own letter dated October 10, 2026 dissociated himself from the documents.

“I wish to state categorically that the purported signature on that document does not resemble mine and was not signed by me. I hereby dissociate myself from the document circulating on social media as I was not part of such a document at any point in time and it should be discountenanced by the general public”, he said.

On his part, His Royal Majesty (HRM) Eze John Akaliro, Obasiukwu 11 of

Umuonuoha, Umuibe, Ogboko Umuobasiukwu Ozuitem Autonomous Community, Bende LGA in a letter dated October 9, 2026 said the document is fake.

“The document in circulation bearing my name is fake and should be discountenanced as I did not sign or witness such a document”, he said.

World.title: Army Chief: Contemporary Threats Demand Coordinated Military Capabilities
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, has said that contemporary threats demand coordinated military capabilities and sustained collaboration among security agencies to stay ahead of insurgents and other criminal elements.

He also underscored the need for enhanced joint operations, intelligence sharing and multi-domain integration to address Nigeria’s evolving security challenges.

He stressed that the increasingly complex and interconnected nature of modern warfare makes it imperative for the Armed Forces and other security agencies to operate in synergy, leveraging their respective capabilities to achieve decisive operational outcomes.

The Army Chief made the remark during the graduation lecture for Army War College Course 10/2026 at the Army War College Nigeria (AWCN), Abuja.

Shaibu explained that the ongoing expansion of the Nigerian Army from eight to 12 divisions represents a strategic repositioning of the force to address emerging security threats, strengthen territorial coverage and enhance operational responsiveness across the country.

He emphasised that the expansion goes beyond increasing the number of formations and personnel, noting that its ultimate objective is to build a more professional, adaptable, combat-ready and resilient Army capable of responding decisively to threats within a joint and multi-agency environment.

The army chief maintained that the effectiveness of the expanded force would depend largely on the integration of trained personnel, modern technology, actionable intelligence, robust logistics and efficient command and control systems.

He stressed that numerical strength and additional formations must translate into superior combat capability, operational flexibility and measurable security outcomes.

He further charged military commanders to embrace innovative approaches to warfare by effectively integrating intelligence, technology, information operations and combat capabilities across multiple domains.

According to him, operational success must also be anchored on professionalism, discipline and respect for the rule of law to sustain public confidence and institutional credibility.

The COAS urged participants of Course 10/2026 to translate the strategic knowledge and leadership competencies acquired during their training into practical solutions that would enhance operational effectiveness, strengthen inter-agency cooperation and advance the ongoing transformation of the Nigerian Army.

Delivering the graduation lecture, titled ‘Winning in Complex Security Environments: Reimagining the Nigerian Army Force Structure for Multi-Domain Operations,’ former National Security Adviser (NSA), Major General Babagana Monguno (rtd), emphasised the need for a fundamental reorientation of military structures, doctrines and operational concepts to address emerging security threats effectively.

Monguno highlighted the growing importance of integrating land, air, cyber and information capabilities in modern warfare, noting that emerging technologies, including unmanned aerial systems, artificial intelligence and digital communication platforms, are rapidly transforming the nature of military operations.

He advocated sustained investment in technological innovation, intelligence integration, institutional reforms and continuous professional military education to equip commanders with the competencies required to operate effectively in increasingly complex and contested security environments.

Earlier, the Commandant of the Army War College Nigeria, Major General Umar Alkali, expressed appreciation to the COAS for his unwavering support for efforts to strengthen the college’s capacity to develop operational-level commanders and strategic leaders.

He noted that participants of Course 10/2026 had undergone rigorous professional training designed to sharpen their critical thinking, operational planning and leadership capabilities for contemporary military operations.

The graduation lecture forms part of the activities marking the graduation of participants of Army War College Course 10/2026 and reinforces the Nigerian Army’s commitment to developing intellectually equipped, technologically adaptable and operationally proficient commanders capable of discharging their constitutional responsibilities.

World.title: Protecting Adolescent Health Key to Securing Nigeria’s Future, SAYPHIN Declares
World.content:
Yemi Kosoko in Jos

The Society for Adolescent and Young People’s Health in Nigeria (SAYPHIN) has declared that sustained investment in adolescent health remains critical to securing Nigeria’s future, as it unveiled the logo for its 2027 national conference scheduled to hold in Jos, Plateau State.

The logo unveiling ceremony, held ahead of the conference themed, ‘Beyond 2030: Protecting Adolescent Health, Securing the Future,’ brought together health professionals, government officials, development partners, academics and young people to advance discussions on adolescent and youth development.

Speaking at the event, President of SAYPHIN, Prof. Adesola Olumide, said the society was established in 2016 to provide a platform for addressing issues affecting adolescents and young people, who constitute a significant proportion of Nigeria’s population and future workforce.

According to her, while adolescents are often perceived as healthy, they remain vulnerable to communicable and non-communicable diseases, substance abuse, unsafe behaviours, mental health challenges and emerging digital-age risks.

She stressed that investments in adolescent health and development were essential for national stability and growth.

Olumide noted that the conference logo symbolises SAYPHIN’s commitment to protecting adolescents and young people, adding that it emerged from a nationwide competition open exclusively to youths between the ages of 10 and 24.

In his welcome address, Chairman of the Local Organising Committee, Prof. Moses Chingle, described the logo launch as the beginning of activities leading to the 2027 conference.

He said the theme underscored the need to sustain attention on adolescent health beyond the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) timeline, noting that healthy and empowered young people are indispensable to national development.

Representing the Plateau State Commissioner for Health, Dr. Nicholas Ba’amlong, the Director of Medical Services, Dr. Stephen Bishman, said the conference theme was a reminder that society’s responsibility to young people does not end in 2030.

He urged stakeholders to view young people not merely as beneficiaries of development but as active contributors to nation-building.

“Protecting adolescent health is not simply a health-sector responsibility; it is an investment in human capital and the future of our society,” he said, adding that governments, communities, families, schools and development partners must work together to create opportunities for young people to thrive.

Also speaking, Chief Medical Director of the Jos University Teaching Hospital, Dr. Pokop Bupwatda, pledged support for the initiative and commended SAYPHIN for keeping adolescent and youth health on the national agenda.

He noted that young people face increasing challenges arising from social media, artificial intelligence, substance abuse and other contemporary pressures, stressing that Nigeria must deliberately invest in its youthful population and create opportunities for them to contribute meaningfully to national development.

The stakeholders agreed that the success of the 2027 conference would ultimately be measured by the partnerships, policies and practical actions it generates to improve the health and wellbeing of adolescents and young people across the country.

World.title: AFP to Storm Made By Design Expo 2026 With New Designs
World.content:
Bennett Oghifo

The iconic furniture production arm of Julius Berger Nigeria Group, Abuja Furniture Production, AFP is set to storm the globally acclaimed annual assembly of top designers, Made By Design Nigeria 2026 expo scheduled to hold in Lagos from October 22 through 25.

AFP is positioning its participation in the forthcoming exhibition as an avenue to pursue new business opportunities, forge strategic partnerships and showcase its latest designs to industry professionals and related visitors.

The exhibition, scheduled to hold at the National Theatre, Lagos, will provide the company, with an opportunity to strengthen its presence within Nigeria’s design and built environment while engaging with potential clients, partners and other stakeholders.

Among its top-notch products set for display at the expo are the iconic height adjustable table, the privacy glass, mobile drawers, waiting area sofas, French doors, fire rated doors, bullet obstructive doors, Yorkshire sofa, chesterfield sofa, boiserie classic wall panels, and many more.

AFP will also present new designs at this year’s event while also showcasing its participation in evolving design concepts and responding to the interests and needs of the market.

It will also focus on creating opportunities for collaboration in the industry, with the main purpose of the brand being open to establishing new partnerships and building relationships that could translate into future business opportunities.

Since 2017, the company has participated in no fewer than seven editions of the annual MADE BY DESIGN Week. It was unavoidably absent from the 2020 and 2025 versions, but remains keen on establishing a consistent presence as usual at this year’s event.

Over the years, its exhibition booth has attracted considerable interests from a diverse audience, including wood technologists, students, architects, interior decorators, business owners and other professionals seeking to learn more about the brand, its products and its offerings.

The steady interest in AFP’s exhibition displays has provided a platform for knowledge-sharing, professional engagement and discussions on design possibilities and applications. The event also allows visitors to make enquiries, gain insights into AFP’s solutions and explore how its offerings can support their respective projects.

World.title: Housing Reforms Must Also Address Construction Finance, Says Mixta Africa
World.content:
Bennett Oghifo

Mixta Africa has called for Nigeria’s proposed National Housing and Built Environment Regulation Policy and National Mortgage Industry Policy to be supported by a credible construction finance framework, warning that regulation and improved access to buyer finance alone will not close the country’s housing deficit.

Speaking on CNBC Africa’s Closing Bell West Africa, Group Chief Commercial Officer, Adetola Akinsulire, said the proposed reforms address two of the sector’s three critical constraints: the trust deficit and buyer finance.

“All of these components address two core areas: the trust deficit in the industry, and buyer finance. There is still one leg missing, and that is construction finance.”

The reforms follow the Federal Ministry of Housing and Urban Development’s disclosure that real estate and construction contributed more than N77 trillion to Nigeria’s economy in 2025, despite the absence of a unified regulatory framework. The proposed reforms cover developer registration, escrow protection, land value management, construction quality, urban renewal and a National Housing Data Observatory, alongside proposals for a Housing Finance Authority and a structured diaspora investment window.

Akinsulire said the success of the reform agenda should ultimately be measured against three outcomes: greater trust in the housing market, improved access to buyer finance, and increased access to construction finance.

Commenting on the proposed National Housing Data Observatory, he welcomed the potential for improved transparency and market intelligence but cautioned that better data alone would not increase housing supply.

“Data does not provide funding to supply homes.”

Akinsulire also argued that the affordability debate should extend beyond the headline price of a property to consider the duration over which buyers can pay.

“Affordability is not just the price of the home. It’s the duration it takes for people to pay for it. A N60 million home is unaffordable if you have to pay for it in two years. But give someone the option to pay for that same property over 30 years, and it becomes affordable.”

Nigeria’s mortgage-to-GDP ratio remains between 0.02 and 0.07 per cent, compared with approximately 30 per cent in South Africa and 70 per cent in the United Kingdom, highlighting the significant gap in mortgage market depth.

Akinsulire also disclosed that Mixta Africa is working on starter homes designed to meet the needs of the mass market, noting that developer-led innovation remains an important lever for improving housing affordability.

He identified the proposed diaspora investment window as one of the government’s potentially quickest wins, given existing demand from Nigerians abroad and their familiarity with structured mortgage and property-financing products.

Mixta Africa reiterated its position that escrow releases should be tied to independently verified construction milestones, while buyer protection mechanisms must be accompanied by sustainable construction finance. The company believes this combination is essential to ensuring that credible developers can continue to deliver housing at scale.

World.title: Elections Campaign ‘ll Be Issue-based, Says APC’s PCC Women Directorate
World.content:
Jonathan Eze

The Director of Women Mobilisation of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), Dr Betta Edu, yesterday declared that the 2027 presidential campaign would be issue-based, expressing confidence that the achievements of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration will provide compelling evidence for his re-election.

Edu, who stated that in Abuja, said Nigerian women were increasingly recognising the direction of the Tinubu administration and had intensified grassroots mobilisation across communities, households, and voting constituencies to secure another mandate for the president and sustain the implementation of his policies and development programmes.

She maintained that the APC would approach the forthcoming election with a clear message anchored on its record in government, ongoing infrastructure projects, economic reforms, educational opportunities, and initiatives designed to improve the livelihoods of Nigerians.

According to her, the party has substantial achievements to present to the electorate and would campaign on policies, programmes, and measurable results rather than empty promises or personality-driven rhetoric.

Edu expressed profound gratitude to President Tinubu for his leadership and commitment to the Renewed Hope Agenda, as well as the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, for her consistent advocacy for women, families, and national development.

She also appreciated Vice President Kashim Shettima and his wife, Nana Shettima; the Senate President and his wife; the Speaker of the House of Representatives and his wife; the Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari; the Secretary of the APC Presidential Campaign Council; and Chairman of the Progressives Governors Forum, Governor Hope Uzodinma; APC governors and other party leaders, governors, stakeholders, and members of the APC leadership for their contributions to strengthen the women’s grassroots mobilisation and advance the administration’s agenda.

The APC PCC women mobilisation director also expressed appreciation to the various women’s groups, associations, support organisations, and political structures within the party for their unwavering commitment, solidarity, and continued support for the administration and the party’s mobilisation efforts.

She acknowledged the contributions of wives of governors, women leaders, and grassroots organisers whose activities across states, local government areas, and communities have continued to strengthen the APC’s engagement with women and expand its political reach.

Edu said their commitment, organisational capacity, and willingness to work collectively would remain indispensable to the party’s preparations for the 2027 general election.

According to her, women remain a formidable force in Nigeria’s electoral process, not only because of their numerical strength but also because of their influence within families, community associations, markets, professional bodies and local political structures.

She stressed that the APC’s mobilisation strategy would go beyond rallies and public declarations to sustained engagement, political education, and direct communication with voters, as well as election-day voters’ sensitisation and mobilisation.

Edu said the objective was to ensure that Nigerians understood the administration’s policies, assessed their impact on their lives, and made informed decisions about the country’s future.

The director identified the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) as one of the significant initiatives through which the Tinubu administration was expanding access to higher education and creating opportunities for young Nigerians to pursue their academic ambitions.

She noted that the student loan programme was helping to address financial barriers that could prevent eligible students from accessing or completing tertiary education while offering families additional support in meeting the cost of education.

According to her, “NELFUND reflects the administration’s recognition that investment in education is essential to human capital development, economic productivity, and the long-term prosperity of the country.”

She said the programme, alongside ongoing infrastructure development, economic reforms, and other sectoral interventions, formed part of the administration’s record that the APC would present to Nigerians during the election campaign.

Edu further maintained that the party would communicate these achievements in clear and practical terms, enabling citizens to understand the policies, opportunities, and reforms available to them.

She added that the 2027 election would provide an opportunity for Nigerians to evaluate the administration, of which we can proudly say that the president has performed well. “The reforms were demanding, but now is time for prosperity,” she said.

For the Women Mobilisation Directorate, she said the immediate priority was to consolidate existing structures, strengthen coordination among women’s groups, and ensure that the party’s message reached voters in both rural and urban communities.

She urged APC women to remain united, organised and committed to the party’s objectives, stressing that their collective contributions would be vital to presenting the administration’s achievements to Nigerians and consolidating support ahead of the 2027 general election.

The group noted that Umahi failed to deliver his own polling unit and ward for the APC in the 2023 presidential election and lost his senatorial bid even in his Uburu village.

World.title: 2 trophies secured: Can Sundowns win everything this season?
World.content:
Mamelodi Sundowns have 2 trophies already this season, with more silverware to play for. Image: Wikimedia Commons, Mamelodi Sundowns website.

Could we be witnessing an even greater era of Mamelodi Sundowns’ dominance?

Miguel Cardoso has led the Brazilians to 2 trophies so far, and more silverware could be coming their way.

Here’s what Sundowns have won so far, and what else they could achieve domestically and continentally.



What trophies have Mamelodi Sundowns won so far?

Mamelodi Sundowns ended Orlando Pirates’ 4-year MTN8 winning streak on 10 October.

The 2-0 win in Durban saw the Chloorkop giants claim their second piece of silverware this season.

On 19 September, Sundowns defeated Saudi Arabia’s Al Ahli to seal the African-Asian-Pacific Cup, with Nuno Santos scoring a decisive brace.



The clash formed part of the FIFA Intercontinental Cup, and the PSL giants have advanced to the Challenger Cup.

If Sundowns win there, they will face European champions Paris Saint-Germain for the main Intercontinental Cup title.

𝙈𝘼𝙎𝘼𝙉𝘿𝘼𝙒𝘼𝙉𝘼 𝙉𝙀𝙑𝙀𝙍 𝙎𝙏𝙊𝙋 𝙍𝙄𝙎𝙄𝙉𝙂 👆



Mamelodi Sundowns make history & conquer the Clash of the Continents and book a place in the Challenger Cup final! 🏆#Sundowns #FIFAIntercontinentalCup #NeverStopRising pic.twitter.com/nnDTWzjLj0  September 19, 2026

What other domestic trophies are still up for grabs?

Premier Soccer League

Sundowns are top of the PSL table as they head into their away clash with Richards Bay FC tonight (13 October).

Their lead over Orlando Pirates is just 1 point, and the Buccaneers also have a game in hand.

However, the MTN8 title could be the fuel Sundowns need, while Pirates must move past the result quickly.



The two main PSL contenders only meet again in January and April next year.

Carling Knockout Cup

Sundowns last tasted Carling Knockout Cup victory in the 2019/2020 season.

The new competition kicks off on 24 October, according to the PSL website.



Pirates are the defending champions, setting up a mouthwatering potential rematch down the line.

Nedbank Cup

We’re still a few months out from the Nedbank Cup.

The PSL website confirmed this competition would run from 27 January to 1 May next year.



Last season, Sundowns were shocked by TS Galaxy in the Round of 16.

Pirates also fell out in the last 16, losing on penalties to Casric Stars.

Durban City were the eventual winners, getting revenge on Galaxy on Sundowns’ behalf.



What continental silverware can Sundowns still claim?

Sundowns continue their CAF Champions League title defence with the second preliminary round against Angola’s Wiliete SC.

The first leg is on 18 October at the Ombaka National Stadium, as confirmed by the club’s official website.

The return leg comes 5 days later on 23 October at Loftus Versfeld in Pretoria.



Matchdays in the competition’s group stage will be held across November, December, and January.

Elsewhere, Sundowns also have the 2026 CAF Super Cup next month.

This competition pits the previous season’s Champions League winner against the Confederation Cup victor.



As confirmed by the CAF website, Sundowns face USM Alger – the date and venue have been listed as 8 November at Loftus by other sources.

World.title: These are South Africa’s best-rated shopping malls
World.content:
These are the 10 best-rated shopping malls in South Africa. Image: wikimedia commons

South Africa is home to hundreds of shopping malls, but a handful stand out when it comes to customer ratings.

A new ranking of almost 700 shopping centres has revealed the 10 best-rated malls in the country, based on more than 3.2 million Google reviews.

The research, conducted by SEO Backlinks, found that The Greenery in Polokwane is South Africa’s best-rated shopping centre, with an average score of 4.68 stars from 1 153 reviews.



It was followed by two high-profile Gauteng destinations, Melrose Arch and Nelson Mandela Square.

South Africa’s top 10 shopping malls

Rank Shopping centre Location Rating Reviews 1 The Greenery Polokwane, Limpopo 4.68 1 153 2 Melrose Arch Johannesburg, Gauteng 4.66 2 314 3 Nelson Mandela Square Sandton, Gauteng 4.63 14 515 4 The Neighbourhood Square Linksfield, Johannesburg 4.61 2 489 5 Marine Walk Sibaya, KwaZulu-Natal 4.60 1 011 6 Loftus Park Arcadia, Pretoria 4.59 3 413 7 Polofields Crossing Waterfall, Midrand 4.59 1 591 8 Constantia Emporium Constantia, Cape Town 4.58 2 378 9 Castle Gate Shopping Centre Waterkloof Ridge, Pretoria 4.58 6 644 10 La Lucia Mall uMhlanga, KwaZulu-Natal 4.57 3 251

Gauteng dominates the top 10

Gauteng has the strongest presence in the national top 10, with six shopping centres making the list.

These include Melrose Arch, Nelson Mandela Square, The Neighbourhood Square, Loftus Park, Polofields Crossing and Castle Gate Shopping Centre.

The province also has by far the largest number of centres included in the study, with 320 of the 678 shopping centres ranked.

Interestingly, Gauteng’s overall average was 4.17 stars, slightly below the national average of 4.18.

KwaZulu-Natal also performed strongly, with two centres in the national top 10. Marine Walk at Sibaya ranked fifth nationally with a 4.60-star average, while La Lucia Mall in uMhlanga came in tenth with 4.57 stars.



KZN had 88 shopping centres included in the study and an overall average of 4.18 stars, putting it third among the provinces ranked.

The Greenery in Polokwane took the number-one spot with a rating of 4.68, putting it ahead of some of South Africa’s most famous shopping destinations.

The Western Cape had just one centre in the national top 10: Constantia Emporium, which scored 4.58 stars.

The study’s overall average across all 678 shopping centres was 4.18 stars.

How the ranking was calculated

The research initially identified 1 197 South African shopping-mall listings with at least 300 Google reviews.

After excluding closed centres, markets, single shops, office parks, duplicate listings and other unsuitable entries, 678 centres with at least 1 000 reviews remained.

The researchers calculated each mall’s exact average using its one- to five-star review counts rather than relying on Google’s rounded rating.

The data was collected on 5 October 2026, meaning the rankings reflect Google reviews available at that time.

World.title: WATCH | Woman killed, nine injured in horrific Durban M4 crash
World.content:
A vehicle burst into flames following a deadly four-vehicle crash on Durban's M4 Ruth First Highway on Tuesday, 13 October. One woman died and nine others sustained injuries. Image: Arrive Alive

A woman died and nine others sustained injuries in a four-vehicle crash on Durban’s M4 Ruth First Highway on Tuesday, 13 October.

The collision occurred on the northbound carriageway near Hyper by the Sea after a bakkie overturned and landed in the path of other vehicles.

One vehicle caught fire, while the impact extensively damaged three others.



WOMAN DIES IN DURBAN M4 CRASH

ALS Paramedics spokesperson Garrith Jamieson said emergency crews found a woman, believed to be in her 40s, with fatal injuries.

“Unfortunately, paramedics found one female believed to be in her 40s, who had sustained fatal injuries in one of the vehicles involved,” Jamieson said.

🚨 SERIOUS CRASH / VEHICLE FIRE – M4 near Hyper by the Sea

13 October – 09:05

⚠️ Affecting both bounds – Active Scene



ALS Paramedics on scene.



Please avoid the area.#M4 #CrashAlert

#KZN #SANationalUpdates pic.twitter.com/RDTCKdL4Gp — SA NATIONAL TRAFFIC UPDATES (@lnnocent191535) October 13, 2026

Multiple ambulances and advanced life support paramedics responded alongside the eThekwini Fire Department, Durban Metro Police and SAPS Search and Rescue.

Firefighters extinguished the blaze while paramedics treated the survivors.

Ambulances transported nine people to hospital. Metro Police said none had sustained serious injuries.



POLICE INVESTIGATE CAUSE OF M4 COLLISION

The crash severely disrupted traffic along the busy coastal route, prompting authorities to urge motorists to use alternative roads.

Police have yet to establish what caused the bakkie to overturn.

World.title: Hours after Navi Pillay’s Nobel win, US sanctioned her former court [video]
World.content:
The US has imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court in The Hague. Image: Instagram @jozi_my_jozi

South Africa says it is “very concerned” by new International Criminal Court (ICC) sanctions imposed by the United States.

And it’s making it clear where it stands.

On Monday, 12 October, Deputy Justice Minister Andries Nel said South Africa remained committed to the court.



He said South Africa, as a founding member of the ICC, reaffirmed its support for the institution.

“South Africa is very concerned by the sanctions imposed by the United States on the International Criminal Court and its officials,” Nel said.

He also warned against political pressure on judges and prosecutors.

WHAT THE ICC SANCTIONS MEAN

The US announced the sanctions on Friday, 9 October, hours after South African judge Navi Pillay, a former ICC judge, won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize.

The timing raised eyebrows. But according to AP, via Euronews, the decision to impose the sanctions had been made well before the Nobel announcement.

For the first time, the US targeted the court as an entire institution, rather than individual officials.



The sanctions freeze any ICC assets held in the US.

They also give US companies and individuals six months to end their business dealings with the court.

The US also issued licences allowing some activities to continue.

According to The Tribune, these include a 180-day licence covering activities needed to keep the court running, along with authorisations for IT services, the ICC pension plan and activities related to detainees.

WHY THE US SAYS IT ACTED

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced the move on X.

The Trump administration has accused the court of political bias and of unfairly targeting Americans and Israelis over alleged war crimes.

Washington also cited concerns over American sovereignty.

Rubio said the action was intended to encourage American allies within the court to work towards addressing those concerns.

The US is not a member of the ICC.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu welcomed the sanctions.

The ICC has issued an arrest warrant for him over alleged crimes committed in Gaza.

WHAT THE ICC AND ITS ALLIES SAY

The ICC condemned the sanctions.

It said they were an attempt to obstruct the course of justice and prevent the court from doing what it was created to do.

The court has 125 member states, and many US allies have backed it.

In a joint statement, the foreign ministers of Britain, Denmark, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Canada and Japan said they “regret and strongly disagree” with the sanctions.

The European Union said it deeply regrets the move and stands ready to take all necessary measures to protect the court.

The European Commission said it hopes the six-month delay before the sanctions apply leaves room for dialogue.

Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten, whose country hosts the ICC in The Hague, said: “We will do whatever we need to defend the ICC.”

THE PILLAY CONNECTION

Pillay served as a judge at the ICC from 2003 to 2008.

She won the Nobel Peace Prize “for her efforts to promote peace and international law.”

The timing was striking, even if the decision was made earlier.

On the same day South Africa celebrated one of its own, the court she once served came under unprecedented pressure.

With six months before the sanctions fully apply, this row isn’t going away any time soon.

The 40-year-old hinted at being unfaithful to his partner.
