World.title: Africa: Rwanda Set to Welcome Formula One Back to Africa, 30 Years Later
World.content:
Frenchman Alain Prost claimed the last of his four Formula One world championships at the Kyalami Circuit near Johannesburg, South Africa, in 1993, the last time the continent hosted a Grand Prix. The event's subsequent collapse brought Formula One's presence in Africa to an abrupt end.

More than three decades later, Africa is preparing for a likely return to the sport's calendar, with Rwanda securing a 10-year partnership to host a Grand Prix, with the inaugural race projected for the early 2030s.

South Africa and Morocco have also been linked to efforts to bring Formula One back to the continent, but Rwanda's agreement marks a significant step towards making that ambition a reality.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

For Rwanda, however, the proposed Grand Prix is beyond motor racing. The government sees it as an opportunity to attract investment, boost tourism, create jobs and develop technical skills, while positioning the country as a regional hub for business and international sporting events.

During an exclusive interview with The New Times, Sports Minister Nelly Mukazayire said Rwanda viewed the agreement as a responsibility to the wider continent, with the potential to open new opportunities for African talent and businesses.

"The excitement of F1 had been for so long left out of Africa, and Africans are known to be good fans," she said, describing the partnership as a long-term commitment whose benefits should be felt beyond Rwanda.

With Africa's population estimated at around 1.3 billion, much of it young, Mukazayire said bringing Formula One back would offer opportunities to expand participation in a sport that has largely been absent from the continent for decades.

The announcement follows President Paul Kagame's declaration at the FIA Awards in Kigali in 2024 that Rwanda was bidding to host a Formula One Grand Prix.

ALSO READ: Kagame says Rwanda's bid to host Formula 1 Grand Prix 'progressing well'

Why Rwanda secured the deal

According to Rwanda Development Board (RDB) Chief Executive Officer Jean-Guy Afrika, the country's experience in hosting major international sporting events was among the factors that strengthened its bid.

Rwanda has hosted several high-profile competitions and gatherings, including the Basketball Africa League (BAL), the 2025 UCI Road World Championships, the FIFA Congress and the FIA Awards.

Afrika said the country had demonstrated its ability to organise large-scale events while presenting a broader vision that links the proposed Grand Prix to tourism, infrastructure and economic development.

"I think there are several reasons why F1 ended up choosing Rwanda. It's not the first time that we organise a large-scale sporting event. We've already shown an ability to execute and deliver large-scale events here in Rwanda," he said.

"The second one was probably vision, and it was very clear when we started bidding for the event to happen here that it was bigger than just F1 itself and was part of a larger project that ties with the airport and driving tourism," he added.

The government is pursuing the project through a consortium involving public institutions, private-sector partners and technical specialists, working alongside Formula One and the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA).

Afrika also emphasised that Rwanda's selection should not prevent other African countries from pursuing opportunities to host the sport in the future.

"We very much welcome other countries joining and placing bids and competing for Formula One," he said.

A huge boost for tourism

The planned Grand Prix will be presented by Visit Rwanda, extending the country's strategy of using international sports partnerships to raise its profile and attract visitors.

The tourism brand has partnered with prominent sporting organisations, including English football clubs Arsenal and Bayern Munich, French side Paris Saint-Germain, Spanish club Atlético de Madrid, the NBA's Los Angeles Clippers and the NFL's Los Angeles Rams. Rwanda has also been involved in the Basketball Africa League.

ALSO READ: Hamilton, Verstappen welcome Africa's potential return to F1 calendar

Afrika described Formula One as a natural extension of the strategy, offering access to a global audience while creating opportunities to attract more international and African tourists.

"It's a continuation of the strategy to use sports to increase the country's visibility and drive inbound tourism. The strategy has been very successful," he said.

According to Afrika, Rwanda recorded $685 million in tourism receipts in 2025 and is targeting $1.9 billion in 2026.

He said the Grand Prix would support efforts to grow tourism by attracting visitors beyond the race itself, with opportunities to promote Rwanda as a destination for leisure, business and other sporting activities.

More than 100 million Africans follow Formula One, according to figures cited by Afrika, with approximately 60 per cent of the audience aged below 35.

"The idea is to continue to use Visit Rwanda, which is presenting the F1 race, to drive tourism to the country and, in this particular case, not only global tourism but also African tourism," he said.

The size and age profile of the audience, he added, make the continent an important market for Formula One as it seeks to expand its reach.

Bugesera airport city at the centre of investment plans

Rwanda expects the Grand Prix to stimulate economic activity across hospitality, construction, transport, logistics, retail, financial services and real estate.

Afrika said the event should be viewed as a long-term investment rather than expenditure on a single race, with potential returns extending across the wider economy.

"It's an investment. It's not an expenditure for a single event. And it's a long-term investment with several ways in which we expect returns to come back to the economy," he said.

A key part of the plan is the development of Bugesera International Airport and an airport city around the facility. The proposed commercial hub is expected to accommodate logistics operations, hotels, apartments, restaurants and other businesses serving travellers and investors.

According to Afrika, the new airport is expected to increase passenger-handling capacity from about one million to more than five million, creating additional opportunities for businesses serving international arrivals.

He said the Grand Prix could amplify the economic potential of these developments by generating demand for accommodation, transport, food services, retail and other activities.

"Hotels, restaurants, retail outlets, but also logistics, because when tourists visit, they have to be able to move. Financial services, because there will be a lot of transactions happening," he said.

Construction is also expected to benefit as Rwanda develops the infrastructure needed for the race, including access roads and facilities for teams, officials, spectators and other visitors.

Beyond existing businesses, the government hopes the event will encourage new investors to establish operations around the airport city.

"We also expect it to drive new investments, not just for existing investments and hotels and hospitality to benefit, but for new investments to come in," Afrika said.

He added that new businesses could create jobs, expand the tax base and increase government revenue available for infrastructure and social and economic development.

However, the scale of those benefits will depend on how effectively Rwanda attracts investors and converts the expected increase in demand into sustainable business activity.

Preparing for a decade of racing

Under the agreement, Rwanda expects to host a Grand Prix annually for 10 years, with the first race projected for the early 2030s.

Mukazayire said preparations would extend well beyond the construction of a racing circuit, requiring investment in transport, accommodation, restaurants, entertainment, operational systems and the workforce needed to deliver the event.

She acknowledged that hosting Formula One would be a major undertaking but said Rwanda would draw on its experience in organising international competitions and seek expertise from across Africa and beyond.

"Our target is to make sure that we run an African Grand Prix that represents long-term value for Rwandans and for Africa," she said.

The government's ambition is to integrate the race into a wider ecosystem of infrastructure and services, ensuring that investments made ahead of the inaugural event continue to support economic activity throughout the partnership.

Afrika said the new infrastructures in Bugesera including the airport and other amenities that are part of the Airport City supporting will be important elements of that broader vision, with Formula One expected to help increase demand for the facilities and services being developed.

Close 

Creating opportunities for young Rwandans

Beyond tourism and investment, the government wants the Grand Prix to support local talent development and create career opportunities in motorsport.

Mukazayire said the initiative aligns with Rwanda's sports strategy, which prioritises talent development, increased participation and employment.

She noted that motorsport encompasses much more than professional driving, offering opportunities in engineering, mechanics, vehicle technology, technical support and event management.

ALSO READ: F1 in Rwanda: A gateway to opportunities for African youth

The government also envisages establishing a motorsport academy to help young Rwandans develop the skills needed to participate in the industry.

"We're being intentional in giving an opportunity to an African or a young Rwandan to also enter into that sport," she said.

"There is a place for a young Rwandan in this motorsport, whether it's behind the wheel, whether it's crafting the wheel or even running the event," she added.

The expected economic activity could also create employment in hospitality, construction, transport, retail and financial services, opening opportunities for people whose skills are not directly related to racing.

For Africa more broadly, the return of Formula One could provide a platform to develop technical expertise, strengthen participation in motorsport and connect local talent with the global industry.

Rwanda's challenge will be to translate the agreement into tangible benefits through infrastructure development, investment, training and job creation.

As preparations move forward, the government is betting that the Grand Prix can become more than a sporting spectacle, serving as a catalyst for tourism, business expansion and the development of motorsport in Rwanda and across Africa.

World.title: Rwanda: Kagame Announces 10-Year Formula One Grand Prix Deal
World.content:
President Paul Kagame has announced a 10-year agreement for Rwanda to host a Formula One Grand Prix, with the inaugural race expected in the early 2030s.

President Paul Kagame has announced a 10-year agreement for Rwanda to host a Formula One Grand Prix, marking a major step towards the championship's return to Africa after nearly four decades.

The inaugural race is expected to take place in the early 2030s, bringing Formula One back to the continent for the first time since the 1993 South African Grand Prix.

The agreement follows years of discussions between Rwanda, Formula One and motorsport authorities over the conditions required to bring the championship back to Africa.

ALSO READ: Hamilton, Verstappen welcome Africa's potential return to F1 calendar

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The race will be staged on a purpose-built circuit in Bugesera, about 40 kilometres south of Kigali and near the new Kigali International Airport.

The circuit will be developed to FIA Grade 1 standards as part of a wider sports, tourism and commercial development led by the Rwanda Development Board (RDB).

Designed around Bugesera's natural landscape and elevation changes, the track is expected to provide a challenging racing experience for drivers while offering strong viewing opportunities for spectators.

Beyond Formula One race weekends, the facility is expected to host other motorsport competitions, conferences, major events and entertainment activities.

Kagame said the agreement would give African motorsport fans greater access to Formula One while opening opportunities for young people to pursue careers in motorsport and related industries.

He added that the development of the circuit, alongside the new international airport, would support employment, tourism, investment and business growth in Rwanda and the wider region.

Formula One's return to Africa is also expected to open the championship to a growing audience on the continent. More than 100 million fans across Africa follow the sport, with nearly 60 per cent of fans in key Sub-Saharan African markets aged below 35.

Rwanda has in recent years expanded its profile as a host of major international sporting events.

The country has hosted the UCI Road World Championships, the Basketball Africa League, the 2023 FIFA Congress, the 2024 FIA General Assemblies and the FIA Awards Ceremony.

The Formula One Grand Prix, presented by Visit Rwanda, is expected to further support the country's efforts to attract tourists, investors and international businesses.

Beyond hosting the race, the project is expected to create jobs, develop local skills, support businesses and attract investment, with Rwanda and Formula One aiming to deliver long-term economic and social benefits.

Close 

Mohammed Ben Sulayem, president of the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), said Formula One's return to Africa would expand motorsport's reach and help develop talent across the continent.

He said the FIA would work with Formula One and its partners to ensure the new circuit meets the required international safety and technical standards.

ALSO READ: F1 in Rwanda: A gateway to opportunities for African youth

Stefano Domenicali, president and chief executive of Formula One, said Rwanda's addition to the calendar would bring the championship to every inhabited continent from the next decade.

He said the partnership would seek to deliver lasting benefits through tourism, investment, skills development and opportunities for local businesses.

Further details, including the inaugural race date, construction milestones and race-weekend plans, will be announced later.

World.title: Congo-Kinshasa: Ex-DR Congo President Kabila to Lead New 'Politico-Military' Alliance With M23 Rebels
World.content:
Former Congolese President Joseph Kabila signing the documents formalising the creation of the Front for the Rebuilding of the Nation (FRN), a political and military movement, on 12 October 2026 in Goma, in the east of the DRC.

Former Democratic Republic of Congo president Joseph Kabila has joined forces with the Rwanda-backed M23 armed group to lead a new political and military alliance, marking his most direct intervention yet in the conflict that has gripped the country's east.

The alliance was unveiled on Monday at a joint press conference at Kabila's residence in Goma - the main city in eastern DRC which has been under M23 control since January 2025.

The new organisation, known as the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation, or FRN, was presented as a "politico-military" movement that would bring together the resources and forces of Kabila's supporters and the rebels.

Its stated objective is to "put an end to tyranny by any means, including force".



Kabila will head the movement, with senior rebel figures serving as his deputies.

The announcement represents a significant escalation in the former president's confrontation with the government of his successor, Félix Tshisekedi, and brings together one of the country's most prominent political figures with an armed movement that controls large areas of eastern DRC.

Kabila, 55, ruled the country from 2001 until 2019 and has largely stayed out of public view since leaving office.

He was sentenced to death in absentia in 2025 after being convicted of "complicity" with the M23.

Congolese authorities have also accused him of being one of the driving forces behind the Congo River Alliance - known by its French acronym AFC - which previously served as the political wing of the M23 before being dissolved.

Kabila has denied those allegations.

Kabila death sentence deepens political and regional divides in DR Congo

Political tensions ahead of 2028

The alliance comes as political attention increasingly turns to 2028, when Tshisekedi is due to complete his second and final five-year term under the constitution.

Figures within the presidential majority have in recent months raised the prospect of constitutional changes, prompting opposition concerns over whether the rules on presidential mandates could be revised.

Kabila first came to power in 2001 after the assassination of his father, Laurent-Désiré Kabila. He was elected president in 2006 and re-elected in 2011, before eventually stepping down following the 2018 election that brought Tshisekedi to power.

DRC opposition postpones protest after Tshisekedi announces national dialogue

Conflict and stalled peace efforts

Close 

M23, whose leadership is drawn largely from the Congolese Tutsi community, first launched an insurgency in eastern DRC in 2012 and returned to arms in late 2021.

The group has since captured extensive territory in North and South Kivu, including Goma.

The United Nations and Western governments accuse Rwanda of supporting the rebels, a charge Kigali denies.

Eastern DRC has been affected by armed conflict for more than three decades, displacing millions of people despite repeated diplomatic efforts.

A Washington-backed agreement between Kinshasa and Kigali signed in December has so far produced little change on the ground, while a separate ceasefire process agreed between the Congolese government and M23 under Qatari mediation in July 2025 has also failed to halt the fighting.

Kabila's new role now ties the eastern rebellion more directly to the political struggle over Congo's future leadership.

(with newswires)

World.title: Nigeria: You Have Nothing to Fear If Tinubu Wins Second Term - Shettima to North
World.content:
The Arewa for Asiwaju group storms Aso Rock and declares full support for the president's reelection.

The Vice President, Kashim Shettima, has issued a rallying cry to the North for President Bola Tinubu's reelection in the 2027 presidential election, declaring that the region has absolutely nothing to fear from a second term for the president.

With urgent intensity, he implored northern leaders and citizens to unite behind the president's re-election bid, framing the administration's second-term agenda as a secure, bulletproof guarantee for the region's future prosperity and stability.

Mr Shettima made the call on Monday when he received, on a courtesy visit, a delegation from the Arewa for Tinubu (A4A) - a northern-based think tank -working for the re-election of President Tinubu.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

He called on leaders across the region to unite into a single front and work for the progress of the area and the well-being of its people, which are top priorities for the Tinubu administration.

According to the VP, the North has no reason to be scared of the re-election of Mr Tinubu, as it has benefitted immensely in terms of appointments and game-changing projects and programmes.

His words: "Let's unite as a people and work for the development of our region and the progress of our people through the re-election of this administration. We are benefiting, and we stand to benefit more from this government in many ways.

"The Bank of Agriculture has disbursed N450 billion to 700,000 smallholder farmers in Nigeria, and about 70 per cent of the beneficiaries are from the north.

"The present administration is working towards completing landmark and groundbreaking projects in parts of the country. I can assure you that the president loves the north and the president will work for the north."

The vice president thanked the group for their steadfast support for President Bola Tinubu at all times and appealed to them to work harder and galvanise across wards, communities and local governments in the northern region for the president's re-election.

Earlier, the Director General of the Area for Asiwaju and former Jigawa State Governor, Abubakar Badaru, said the organisation will not rest on its laurels until they make the North proud by reelecting President Tinubu.

He said the group plans to meet with religious leaders, including Muslim and Christian clerics, as well as other prominent Nigerians to explain to them the need to support the Tinubu/Shettima ticket in 2027.

"On discussions with the high profile, we have gone far. We have met them several times, and the BoT is meeting them again to consolidate our gains and to tell them why there is need to support this ticket.

"We are also supporting the Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) with whatever they want us to do that is micro in nature because they are so big and we really don't want to lose sight of the bigger arrangement that is there. We want to focus very well on the contacts at the grassroots - the local government areas and the wards."

Close 

Also, Chairman of the organisation's Board of Trustees (BoT) and former Kano State Governor, Ibrahim Shekarau, said the think tank which worked for President Tinubu's election in the 2023 general election will repeat the same feat in 2027.

He said the organisation had been meeting with northern governors and other stakeholders to compare notes and collaborate on areas of working together to achieve the President's reelection.

He noted that the organisation has concluded plans to have a full-fledged secretariat for purposes of coordination, where there will be offices for directors and state coordinators to compare reports, analyse them, and give out instructions to its members.

The BoT chairman formally invited the vice president to officially commission the A4A office complex on Saturday, October 17, 2027.

Also present at the meeting were former Governors of Plateau, Joshua Dariye and Simon Lalong; Taraba, Jolly Nyame; Kogi, Yahaya Bello; Katsina, Ibrahim Shema; Bauchi, Isa Yuguda; Special Adviser to the President on Policy and Coordination, Hadiza Bala Usman; Chairman of NDLEA, Buba Marwa, some top officials of government, and other members of the A4A BOT and Secretariat.

Stanley Nkwocha

Senior Special Assistant To The President on Media & Communications

(Office of The Vice)

12th October, 2026

World.title: Liberia: Sen. Konneh Asks U.S. to Sanction Mining Enablers, Warns Liberia At 'Most Dangerous Point'
World.content:
Monrovia - Gbarpolu County Sen. Amara M. Konneh has asked the United States to impose Global Magnitsky sanctions on people who enable mining licensing deals in Liberia and move the proceeds into US real estate, telling a Washington policy audience that the country faces its gravest threat since the civil war and the Ebola epidemic.

By Lennart Dodoo

Sen. Konneh made the request Oct. 7 at a private roundtable convened by the National Endowment for Democracy in Washington, according to a statement his office released Oct. 12. He also asked Washington to support court monitoring in Liberia, resume mentoring of law enforcement officers vetted by the US Drug Enforcement Administration "with appropriate oversight," and engage the Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network on active financial intelligence cases.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"Liberia is not yet a captured state. But we are at the most dangerous point since the civil war and the Ebola epidemic," Konneh said. "My request is straightforward: help us establish transparent regulations before agreements are finalized, and support impartial enforcement of the law after confiscation, whether the suspect is an airport baggage handler, a police crimes director, a former Vice President, or a multinational corporation."

Sen. Konneh, an independent who chairs the Senate Public Accounts and Audit Committee and previously served as minister of finance and development planning, described two threats he said are unfolding at the same time: corporate capture of the mining sector and the infiltration of state institutions by drug traffickers.

On mining, he said broad executive discretion in negotiating 25-year Mineral Development Agreements has created conditions for companies to capture the country's regulatory and fiscal institutions. Mining accounts for 12% of gross domestic product and 65% of export earnings, he said, yet affected communities receive less than 3% of direct revenue. The statement does not give a source for those figures.

On narcotics, Konneh said transnational trafficking networks have shown they can penetrate Liberia's law enforcement, judicial and financial systems. He pointed to two seizures this year: 237 kilograms intercepted at Roberts International Airport in June, valued at $19.2 million, and 3.9 metric tons seized in Duazon in July, valued at $317 million. He said the seizures had links to trafficking networks in Spain, Colombia, Serbia, Croatia and Ukraine.

He also described the spread of kush, a cheap synthetic drug now present in Liberia, Sierra Leone, Gambia, Guinea and Senegal, as both a public health and a governance emergency. Citing the UN Office on Drugs and Crime's World Drug Report 2025, he said opioid use in West and Central Africa stands at 2.35%, above the global average, and that Africa accounted for 57% of pharmaceutical opioids seized worldwide between 2019 and 2023.

Close 

Sen. Konneh said he is advancing a set of reforms in the Senate. They would require publishing all Mineral Development Agreements before ratification, create independent oversight of transfer pricing in iron ore concessions, mandate preserving evidence in drug cases, make financial investigations compulsory in all first-degree drug felonies, and introduce unexplained wealth legislation that allows assets to be forfeited without a criminal conviction.

World.title: Don Lemon's presidential ambitions met with skepticism, amusement from his former CNN colleagues
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Left-wing podcaster and former CNN host Don Lemon claims to be considering a run for president. Count his former colleagues as skeptical at best.

Lemon, an outspoken critic of President Donald Trump who started his own show after being fired by CNN in 2023, recently said there is a "65, 70%" chance he’ll launch a White House bid. Lemon, who has no political experience, has said he would make a better president than Trump and talked up his appeal to voters.

A CNN staffer knocked Lemon's apparent presidential ambitions.

"Doesn’t someone, according to Don Lemon, have to be in their 'prime' to run for president? That would certainly rule Don out," they told Fox News Digital.

DON LEMON CLAIMS TRUMP'S MAGA MOVEMENT IS 'CLOSEST THING' TO MODERN NAZI PARTY WITHOUT HOLOCAUST

The staffer was referring to the infamous 2023 moment when Lemon found himself in hot water for suggesting then-Republican presidential candidate Nikki Haley was past her "prime" at age 51, enraging female colleagues and sparking public fury. Lemon, who is now 60 and almost six years older than Haley, later apologized for the comments.

"I love it. Bring it on," another CNN staffer told Fox News Digital of Lemon's possible bid.

"It would be fun if he ran. Little bit less boring than the standard 18-people on-stage process that we’re about to watch unfold," they said. "Although, I doubt he actually does it."

Lemon's profile was raised earlier this year when slapped with a felony indictment for livestreaming a protest against Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) at a Minnesota church. He has insisted he was working as a journalist and was not part of the group that harassed churchgoers, but Lemon ramped up his criticism of Trump since the incident.

"Don does very much want to have influence and feel his contributions matter. Would seem other ways make more sense because running is merely raising money, which is f---ing miserable, and you can’t get anywhere," Lemon’s former colleague said.

"I think political office is probably appealing to him. I think a presidential run is obviously not serious, but he could engage in it as a way to launchpad into another office," they continued. "If Don has the itch, there are ways to scratch it that are more serious. It takes a single-minded focus, and he can’t be a media personality and do it at the same time."

EX-CNN ANCHOR DON LEMON AGREES TRUMP PLAYED LIBERAL NETWORK 'LIKE PUPPETS'

A third CNN staffer said Lemon has done a good job of remaining "relevant" since being fired.

"It’s the most open nomination process in 30+ years for the Dems, I think you gotta take it seriously," the second staffer told Fox News Digital. "I’m not saying he is serious, but I am saying he’s said it enough that I can’t dismiss it."

Lemon was fired by then-CNN CEO Chris Licht in 2023 and has since launched his own media company. Lemon's tenure at CNN came to a bumpy end, as he had recently been pushed out of his primetime hosting gig to an ill-fated morning show stint with co-hosts Kaitlan Collins and Poppy Harlow. His squabbles on the show and the flap over his infamous Haley comments sealed his fate.

DON LEMON REVEALS HE'S 'TOTALLY SERIOUS' ABOUT CONSIDERING A PRESIDENTIAL RUN

He wouldn't be the first CNNer to jump into politics. On-air analyst John Avlon launched a New York congressional bid as a Democrat in 2024 but was ultimately defeated.

Lemon suggested earlier this year he didn’t have political ambitions but said people had been asking him to do so, and therefore, he was thinking about it.

"I actually think I would be a really good president of the United States," Lemon said on the "Can’t be Censored" podcast.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"For the people to want me. What it would take is if I ran a political campaign, a presidential campaign, I would like to run it, and I don't know if this is realistic or not, without having to beg for money. I would like it to be a voter-citizen-driven campaign for as much as it can be," he continued. "Maybe at some point I might have to take a donation. I would rather not do that."

Lemon did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Dana Perino detailed her shocking White House press podium habit during a podcast interview Tuesday, admitting she secretly flipped off combative reporters while maintaining a polite smile during briefings under former President George W. Bush.

"I would just sit there with my hand over my cup and just flip him off the entire time he was talking," Perino told Sean Hannity on his "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" podcast.

"They'd be asking questions. I'd smile through it... [and] nod," she recalled.

LEAVITT PULLS BACK THE CURTAIN ON TRUMP'S 'TENSE,' UNFILTERED PRIVATE TALKS WITH PUTIN, XI, STARMER

Perino, who served as Bush's press secretary from 2007 to 2009, explained that she kept a cup of water at the podium and used it to shield her hand from view while discreetly delivering the middle finger during testy exchanges.

The gesture, which Perino jokingly likened to a form of "liquid courage," gave her a small sense of "defiance and confidence" while maintaining her composure.

CORNEL WEST AND SEAN HANNITY FIND UNLIKELY COMMON GROUND DESPITE DEEP POLITICAL DIVIDE

The story was kept under wraps for years until she revealed it to Hannity in the past, she recalled. Perino later published the story in her 2015 memoir, "And the Good News Is..." and garnered attention from late conservative talk radio host Rush Limbaugh.

"When I did [Limbaugh's] radio show, he said, this is the best story ever," she recalled.

Hannity agreed, calling it "the greatest story ever told" by a White House press secretary and marveling at Perino's unexpected display of defiance behind the podium.

WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENTS WIDELY PRAISE KAROLINE LEAVITT AS SHE ANNOUNCES EXIT FROM TRUMP ADMINISTRATION

Perino explained that her role as White House press secretary required her to remain respectful and composed, even when facing combative reporters who, she believed, were more interested in securing television airtime than getting answers.

"They would do anything to get on TV that night," she recalled. "They would give a big windup and try to hit you so that they could make sure that they could get on air for one of the networks."

Perino suggested that the pressure on reporters to produce memorable moments was already shaping exchanges during her tenure, but she believes the rise of social media has only intensified that dynamic.

World.title: Olympic legend Kaillie Humphries opens up on impact of women's sports advocacy on Team USA relationships
World.content:
Olympic champion Kaillie Humphries says her advocacy against transgender athletes competing in women’s sports has created "awkward, tense moments" with some Team USA teammates and strained existing friendships.

Humphries, a three-time Olympic gold medalist and XX-XY Athletics ambassador, told OutKick she recently received the brand’s "Courage Wins Award" and plans to direct the funding toward her foundation supporting female athletes’ careers and family-building needs.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

As a California resident, she plans to vote Republican in the coming gubernatorial election. She is currently pregnant with her second child, and if she has a girl, and if the state's current policy that allows males to compete in girls' sports continues, it could contribute to her leaving the state.

She says lending her voice to the "Save Women's Sports" movement has brought some disagreements with teammates and friends in the Olympic community.

"I have teammates within bobsled, I have teammates within Team USA who believe in a different side, for sure," Humphries said.

"For sure, it's created awkward, tense moments. I think it's created tense moments even within friendships that were there."

AMERICANS CLASH OVER TRANSGENDER ATHLETES AS DEBATE HEATS UP: ‘JUST GETTING OUTRAGEOUS'

She said disagreements have the potential to become heated, but emphasized that many fellow athletes have maintained respect for her despite their opposing views.

"And I think that while it creates a bit of tension, no one's willing to cross the line. It doesn't make you a bad person because you believe something different than somebody else," she said.

Humphries said her goal is to preserve the opportunities she enjoyed throughout her career for other female athletes.

"I've had these opportunities because it has remained for biological females. And that's something that I believe in and that I'm going to push," she said.

OLYMPIC CHAMPION NANCY HOGSHEAD HONORED FOR ADVOCACY AS SHE PUSHES WNBA ON FEMALE ELIGIBILITY RULES

She also argued that transgender athletes should have opportunities to compete in categories based on their biological sex.

"Sport is meant to be an open place for everybody. I do believe that," she said.

The International Olympic Committee adopted a policy in March restricting eligibility for the women’s category at IOC events, beginning with the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, through one-time SRY gene screening, with specified rare exceptions. The policy does not apply to grassroots or recreational sports.

Humphries said she is willing to discuss the issue with people who are respectful and open to hearing different perspectives, but does not approach those conversations with the intention of changing their minds.

When relationships involve broader disagreements or a risk of personal attacks, she said she sometimes keeps interactions focused on the sport.

"We don't talk outside of sport. We don't talk about personal stuff. We leave it to just in sport on a need-to-know basis, on minimum interaction, so that it's possible to keep that respect there," she said.

Despite the tension, Humphries rejected the suggestion that the issue would have undermined the chemistry behind her Olympic gold medals.

"I don't think it would have affected the chemistry with me and my teammates. Because I would have made sure that it didn't," she said.

"The common goal has to be achieved and be the number one priority above personal belief and above personal self."

The debate also figures into her decisions as a mother living in California. Humphries, who has a 2-year-old son and is expecting her second child in late January, said disagreements with the state’s politics have prompted her to consider moving.

"I have considered moving to other states because of it, for sure," she said.

She identified women’s sports and her children’s future schooling as personal concerns. California law permits students to participate in school athletic teams and competitions consistent with their gender identity.

Asked whether having a daughter could influence her decision to remain in California under its current sports policies, Humphries said, "It could," while stressing that a move would depend on more than one issue.

She said she plans to vote Republican, but did not name a candidate.

Meanwhile, Humphries is working to help other athletes overcome the financial pressures of pursuing elite competition while starting families.

XX-XY Athletics announced Oct. 2 that it was expanding its Courage Wins initiative through an investment in TrailBlazeHer, the foundation Humphries established with her husband.

The foundation’s published plans include $5,000 grants for athletes pursuing Olympic careers and $10,000 grants for family-building expenses, with distribution tied to fundraising milestones.

Humphries said her own experience with in vitro fertilization (IVF) and endometriosis forced difficult decisions about whether to spend available money on starting a family, medical needs or her athletic career.

"And it was excruciating having to make that choice," she said.

"And so, for me, regardless of what happens in sport, it was important I was able to start a foundation so that I can help other women. So hopefully they don't have to make those same choices."

World.title: Americans draw the line at livestreaming ‘spectacle’ of Fort Hood shooter's execution: ‘It’s an abomination’
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Americans are overwhelmingly against the Pentagon's decision to livestream the firing squad execution of convicted Fort Hood mass shooter Nidal Hasan later this year.

Those who spoke with Fox News Digital blasted the broadcast as "a shame" and "just weird."

"I think that's absolutely absurd," Anya from Virginia said when asked about the livestream announced by Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. "I think they should keep that discreet and off of the public news."

"It's an abomination. It should not happen," Paul from Illinois definitively stated. "And I'd hate to be one of the soldiers that's tasked with the job of pulling the trigger."

Hegseth announced last Thursday the decision to make viewing the execution publicly available. It is set to be the first U.S. military execution in over six decades.

PENTAGON CONFIRMS FORT HOOD TERRORIST'S FIRING SQUAD EXECUTION WILL BE LIVESTREAMED: 'DETAILS WILL FOLLOW'

The execution of the mass shooter who killed 13 people and injured 32 in 2009 at Ford Hood, is scheduled for Dec. 3, 2026. Hasan, an Army psychiatrist at the time of the shooting, is now 56-years-old and is wheelchair bound after he was left partially paralyzed after being shot by police officers during his arrest almost 17 years ago.

Several Americans interviewed by Fox News Digital supported Hasan's death sentence but drew the line at broadcasting his execution, warning it could turn capital punishment into a public spectacle and could be particularly dangerous in today's political climate.

"I'm not necessarily against giving him the death penalty, but I feel like livestreaming for people's entertainment is just weird," Nick from Virginia said.

"I agree with the sentence," Bobbie from Massachusetts said. "I don't agree with televising it."

He added, "Especially given the climate of today, I'm not sure it's something we need to see."

"It’s not a practice we should be doing in modern society," Reid from Ohio said. "It's rather medieval in my opinion. I'm certainly pro-death penalty for heinous crimes such as that, but I think that…turns it into something of a spectacle that it really doesn't have any business being."

FORT HOOD SURVIVOR SHOT IN HEAD VOWS TO WATCH TERRORIST FACE HISTORIC FIRING SQUAD

But one Virginia man took a drastically different position, suggesting the government should charge Americans to watch the execution and donate the proceeds to the family of a U.S. service members who died in the line of duty.

"I think they're missing an opportunity," Jason from Virginia said. "It should be pay-per-view and all the proceeds should go to Gold Star families."

He continued, "You have someone who was a murderous traitor to our country. And there's not a lot of coverage about that. So I think the public needs and deserves to know the consequences to, well FAFO."

Some raised concerns that the execution leaves children vulnerable to possibly accessing or being exposed to watching Hasan die on livestream.

"We have enough violence in our society," William from Virginia said. "I'm pretty sure he's guilty, but it doesn't need to be public. Children could be watching that."

"I just don't think that stuff like that should be put on the mainstream," Ferris from Massachusetts said. "Especially considering that children may have access to seeing it."

Another pointed out Hasan’s health status, arguing the issue could be approached differently if he was "up and around" but citing the shooter’s well-being as a reason he sees the livestreamed execution as that much more wrong.

"You're executing somebody who's not mentally stable, who is in this wheelchair situation," one respondent told Fox News Digital.

The Trump administration’s announcement of the livestream was largely widely seen as a power play for the United States, demonstrating the consequences of committing such an act of terror on American soil — particularly committing violence toward members of the U.S. military.

"I think they're trying to make an example out of him, you know?" Nick said. "I think it's like a show of power. They're trying to be like… 'don't mess with us.'"

GOP GOV DEWINE URGES OHIO TO ABOLISH THE DEATH PENALTY, SAYS IT IS NO LONGER A DETERRENT

"I think it's a message that we're big and tough, and we don't have much humanity left," Paul said.

Trump said Saturday that he will make the decision of whether to livestream Hasan’s execution, acknowledging that he knows "what the military would like to do" following Hegseth’s confirmation.

Vice President J.D. Vance also said Friday that he was not sure that the federal government will be livestreaming the execution, also adding that he would not personally view the livestream.

"The world's gone crazy," Anya said. "We need Jesus."

World.title: ‘Peace through strength’: Trump Gaza plan gains global backing one year on
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A year has passed since President Donald Trump made history by brokering a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas, setting in motion an ambitious peace plan aimed at bringing lasting stability to the region.

In the days and months since the ceasefire and Trump’s 20-point peace plan took hold, progress has drawn support from across the globe — including from unexpected quarters.

Senior advisor to the Board of Peace Josh Gruenbaum told Fox News Digital that the success of the last 12 months was largely attributable to President Donald Trump’s leadership and commitment to seeking peace.

TRUMP-BACKED BOARD OF PEACE, ISRAEL 'WILL TAKE ACTION' IF HAMAS REMAINS OUT OF COMPLIANCE: NETANYAHU ADVISOR

"The unlock was somebody who came in, who really knew the file because they had the chance to study it and understand it," Gruenbaum said. Trump and his team, including U.S. Special Envoy to the Middle East Steve Witkoff, U.S. Special Envoy for Peace Jared Kushner and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, "created working relationships with regional actors with trust, overlaid with peace through strength," while also forcing Hamas to finally understand that "this was either going to end the very hard way for them, or there was an off-ramp and a way to do this in a more dignified way, which is what the 20-point-plan was."

He said this has been achieved by "building consensus through the world, including through Europe, that this is the only game in town. This is the only pragmatic approach to make this thing stop." A particular point of strength for the Board of Peace, Gruenbaum added, has been "cultivating really strong relationships with the United Nations."

In Nov. 2025, the United Nations endorsed the Board of Peace through Resolution 2803.

European Union Commissioner for the Mediterranean and for Demography, Dubravka Šuica, announced at a high-level briefing at the Board of Peace in September that the European Union had "gathered about $1 billion for early recovery in Gaza," and would sign recovery projects with the UNDP and UNICEF. "We are doing this in alignment with the priorities of the Board of Peace and the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG)," Suica stated.

US URGES DONORS TO ABANDON UNRWA FUNDING AS UN DEFENDS AGENCY'S MISSION

The International Stabilization Force, which will train a future police force in Gaza and oversee demilitarization, has received commitments from Kazakhstan, Morocco, Albania and Kosovo, with other countries said to be in the pipeline for admission.

Notably absent from Gaza’s future, per the Board of Peace plan, is the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA). The Board of Peace has been unequivocal that UNRWA will have no involvement in Gaza. One U.S. agency, the USAID Office of the Inspector General, is currently investigating over 1,500 UNRWA employees for involvement in terror groups.

On X, the Board of Peace recently stated that it "will only work with trusted partners who deliver for the people of Gaza and contribute to a deradicalized Strip," and emphasized that "UNRWA fails on those litmus tests."

The Board of Peace’s effort has support from unlikely corners. Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton wrote in a June editorial in the Financial Times that while the plan was "not the one many of us would have drafted," she believes "it remains the only framework backed by sufficient leverage, political engagement and potential resources to move parties towards implementation."

The Board of Peace has received about $18 billion in pledges for reconstruction, the BBC recently reported. A Board of Peace official told Fox News Digital that next steps in the reconstruction program include a six-month program with 66 recovery initiatives, including rubble clearance, unexploded ordnance clearance, construction of temporary housing and destroying tunnel infrastructure. The initiatives are expected to cost $2.45 billion, and tenders for some projects have been submitted.

KUSHNER GIVES HAMAS STARK ULTIMATUM: DISARM OR ISRAEL GETS US BACKING TO ‘FINISH THE JOB’

In the year ahead, the Board of Peace must clear a number of hurdles, including a full demilitarization and de-radicalization of Hamasin Gaza. Gruenbaum says that the Board of Peace is "realistic and sober" but is also "in a historic place with Hamas," having secured verbal agreements and offering a path to amnesty for those who qualify.

Gruenbaum also says that the 20-point plan is Hamas’ best path forward and that regional dynamics leave them with few remaining options. Mediators are increasingly supporting the Board of Peace, Tehran is focused on its current war, and Israel is continuing to apply pressure, though Gruenbaum says the Board of Peace continues to stress that they must comply with the ceasefire.

Gruenbaum said that deradicalization will never be a top-down process led by the U.S., but will be managed through the NCAG. He said that the NCAG’s members "have kids that have been brought up" under the current UNRWA-run system, so "they understand the situation." The approach will involve the new technocratic government, whose members have extensive experience in civil service, taking the lead on "vetting teachers" and "vetting people who are involved in civil governance."

Gruenbaum celebrated the potential of bringing together the NCAG and Israeli authorities through the transformation of Gaza. "This is a monumental opportunity for the Palestinian people of Gaza where their governing body is going to be uniquely focused on delivering services for its constituents and if we could create this amazing relationship where we build trust between Israel and the NCAG, we deliver on both sides of the equation – security for Israel and freedom and a better life, self-determination and prosperity-building inside of Gaza. That’s a two-way trust building system."

Gruenbaum added that the successes in Gaza could lead to successes elsewhere. "Maybe these best practices get learned by the Palestinian Authority. Maybe Israel starts adding more trust with different people in the system. I think this is a huge moment in the history of the Middle East."

World.title: Romance scammers are getting harder to catch. The consequences are costly.
World.content:
For people looking for love online, a match with a scammer could cost them their life savings.

A congressional investigation, which began in September 2025 and lasted about a year, found that Tinder’s scam detection systems struggled for years to keep fraudulent accounts off the dating app. Parent company Match Group has since moved to address the shortcomings with new verification requirements and upgraded detection technology.

Romance scams have become a leading form of financial fraud in the U.S., costing Americans nearly $1.5 billion in reported losses last year, according to the Federal Trade Commission.

“There’s a lot of stigma to being a victim to scams,” Sen. Maggie Hassan, D-N.H., who launched the investigation alongside Sen. Marsha Blackburn, R-Tenn., said in an interview last week. “People should understand that really sophisticated people who are doing all the right things are still getting scammed because of the level of technology and resources that these criminal enterprises now do.”

I fell prey because of my personality and because I was lonely. And I was very ashamed of what happened. -Sue nuss, who spoke to Congress’ Joint Economic Committee about her experience turning to Tinder in search of companionship.

Scammers today can realistically pose as representatives from familiar organizations like the local YMCA or a bank, and the accessibility of AI tools makes it easier than ever to research family members and mimic their voices. But romance scams, Hassan said, can be particularly emotionally devastating.

That was the case for Pennsylvania resident Sue Nuss, who told Congress’ Joint Economic Committee about her experience turning to Tinder in search of companionship after she lost her husband. There, she met a man who claimed to be from New Jersey.

Nuss told NBC News that, over a month and a half, he won her trust with words that made her feel like he really “sees” and “understands” her.

The committee’s report, published Tuesday, stated that the man duped Nuss with a series of “fabricated” crises: job problems on an oil rig, an arrest in Mexico, his mom’s stroke and even her funeral — all excuses to ask Nuss, 77, for money. When the scammers behind the profile tried to trick her into believing the man she was dating had died, she said, she realized it was all a scam.

“I have always been a very giving person my entire life, and I’ve always been a caregiver,” Nuss told NBC News last week. “And I fell prey. I was very vulnerable. I fell prey because of my personality and because I was lonely. And I was very ashamed of what happened.”

Days after what she thought was a budding online relationship fell apart, Nuss’ scammer showed back up on Tinder with the same profile, she said in an interview.

Soon, another group approached her claiming they could recover what she had lost. Then, through an elaborate cryptocurrency scheme, that group managed to scam even more money from Nuss. She believes both scammer groups were connected, the report stated. It added that, in total, she lost more than $700,000.

“I struggle. Some days are really bad days and some days are good days. I do get therapy. I’m starting a very special therapy next week called EMDR because it’s a trauma,” Nuss said. “I don’t trust my decisions now.”

Congress last month passed the Romance Scam Prevention Act, which would require online dating service providers to notify and warn any users who get messaged by potential scammers. The bill awaits President Donald Trump’s signature.

This summer, Hassan also introduced legislation with Sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., to create a central reporting portal for victims of scams, an initiative that she said could give the federal government the tools to detect patterns in scams to shut them down more effectively.

Scammers stole more than $1 trillion globally in one year, according to a 2024 report from the Global Anti-Scam Alliance.

“Enterprises that run scams are now costing the global economy more than the illicit drug trade does,” Hassan said. “This is really important for individuals. It’s really important for our economy. And so, the more people speak up about the need to change the way the federal government handles scams, the faster it’s going to happen.”

The Joint Economic Committee’s investigation sought to combat the prevalence of romance scams on platforms owned by Match Group, the biggest online dating company in the world, with a portfolio that includes Tinder, Hinge, Match and Plenty of Fish.

It found that during the third quarter of 2025, nearly 1.5 million scammers or other bad actors on Tinder and Hinge matched with someone. Nearly 500,000 of those accounts then exchanged contact information with other users.

Internal documents shared voluntarily with the committee noted that most of Tinder’s machine-learning detection scam models hadn’t been updated in years, and Match Group staff members found that scammers could quickly circumvent the company’s patchwork detection rules. Excessive false positives also overwhelmed the human moderators trying to detect dangerous accounts.

The committee wrote that it welcomes the changes Match Group has made to address those concerns.

Match Group deployed new detection models throughout the latter half of 2025 and the first half of 2026 to better catch bad actors, according to the committee’s report. This year, it introduced 169 automated rules and “improved” 108 others aimed at targeting and removing inauthentic actors.

One of its key rollouts is a mandatory biometric face check for all new users on Tinder and Hinge, meant to prevent users from making multiple accounts and ensure banned users can’t make new accounts.

Yoel Roth, Match Group’s senior vice president of trust and safety, told NBC News the company is “grateful the Committee recognized our significant advancements to protect our users against romance scams.”

“That said, the report mischaracterizes both the historical scale of our investment and the work already completed. Alongside our engagement with the Committee over the past year, we’ve made the largest safety advancements in Match Group’s history,” Roth wrote in a statement. “Trust and Safety is a foundational priority, and we intend to continue leading the industry in building tools that promote authentic, safe connections.”

Much of that safety work, including the face checks, was already underway before the committee’s investigation, according to Match Group. It reports having seen a roughly 60% reduction in exposure to bad actors in every market since the face checks began.

Hassan similarly said those measures have “already been successful in dramatically reducing the number of matches that their customers have with a scammer.”

“They need to do more, though, because there are still gaps in their systems,” she added. “And they are going to need to stay vigilant in new ways, because the criminals are always changing their technology and their tactics, too.”

World.title: Bryan Cranston mourns ‘Breaking Bad’ co-star RJ Mitte: ‘My sweet son’
World.content:
Emmy winning actor Bryan Cranston on Monday lamented the death of “Breaking Bad” co-star RJ Mitte, calling the late actor and disability advocate “my sweet son.”

Cranston, 70, said he was in “deep despair” over Mitte’s death by suicide and wondered if he’d still be alive today had they only met up for lunch in recent days.

“It is especially devastating to hear that he took his own life. Why? We were texting each other just a few weeks ago — figuring out when we could meet for lunch,” Cranston said in a statement on Monday night.

“I don’t know if that lunch would have changed his future … But I do know that I loved him, and thoroughly enjoyed being with him throughout the years on the series.”

The 34-year-old Mitte, who played the son of Cranston’s lead character Walter White in the hit AMC series “Breaking Bad,” died Monday in Brownsville, Texas.

“I’m in deep despair as I write this tonight. RJ Mitte, my sweet son on Breaking Bad has died,” Cranston said. “I met him when he was only 14 years old when he was cast as Walter White Jr., a part he played with such joy and enthusiasm.”

Mitte had cerebral palsy and Cranston said that challenge never slowed down his late co-star.

“He met the demanding shooting schedule head on with great determination,” according to Cranston.

“He parlayed his experience on the show to be a vocal advocate for performers with disabilities, and was the head of a philanthropic organization with a focus on helping the disabled community.”

“Breaking Bad” ran for 62 episodes between 2008 and 2013, as one of the era’s most critically acclaimed shows.

Cranston won six of his seven Emmys for work on “Breaking Bad,” playing a high school chemistry teacher-turned-meth kingpin Walter White.

Cranston was in all 62 episodes of “Bad” and Mitte’s Walter White Jr. appeared 56 times.

“That kid was pretty raw when we started shooting the pilot in February of 2007, but little by little we watched him grow into a really fine actor,” Cranston wrote.

“All that promise and potential now is such a loss.”

If you or someone you know is in crisis, call 988 to reach the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. You can also call the network, previously known as the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline, at 800-273-8255, text HOME to 741741 or visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources for additional resources.
