What Prediction Markets Say

The midterm odds quoted here come from real-money bets, and Polymarket has drawn US$16.6 million in bets on House control, US$6.4 million on the Senate and US$22.6 million on its combined balance-of-power market. Kalshi, which is regulated in the US by the CFTC, has traded about 38.2 million contracts on its balance-of-power question, each paying US$1 if right.

The midterm odds barely moved in the past day, but over the past week the Democratic sweep slipped 3 points while a Democratic House with a Republican Senate gained 1. The largest weekly move among the key races came in Michigan, where the Republican side gained 3.5 points.

On impeachment, Polymarket’s contract on whether the House impeaches Trump before his term ends trades at 71%, and Kalshi prices an impeachment before 1 January 2028 at 66.5%. Kalshi’s separate contract on impeachment and removal from office trades at 17.5%, a gap explained below, and live prices are tracked on our Prediction Markets page.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Trump Could Still Do on His Own

Even if the midterm odds prove right, a Democratic Congress would not end Trump’s presidency, and many of his most-used powers do not need a vote. Each of them has limits, though, and the courts have already drawn some of them this year.

Executive Orders

Executive orders direct federal agencies and need no vote in Congress, which makes them the president’s fastest tool. They cannot override a law or spend money Congress has not provided, and judges can block them.

In August, for example, the Supreme Court paused a lower-court injunction against Trump’s executive order on election procedures while a challenge by several states continues. A Democratic Congress could pass laws to reverse specific orders, but each law would need Trump’s signature or a veto override.

Sanctions and Export Controls

Sanctions rest largely on the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), a 1977 law that lets the president block assets and transactions once he declares a national emergency. Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) writes and enforces the sanctions lists, and the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) runs export controls on sensitive technology.

The Supreme Court’s tariff ruling dealt only with tariffs and did not touch IEEPA’s power to block assets. Congress can end a national emergency or rewrite a sanctions programme by law, but such a bill would face a veto.

Military Action and the War Powers Clock

As commander in chief, the president can order US forces into action, and Trump did so in Venezuela in January and against Iran from 28 February. The War Powers Resolution of 1973 says he must end any such use of force within 60 days of reporting it to Congress, with up to 30 more days to withdraw safely, unless Congress authorises it.

The White House told Congress on 1 May that the hostilities with Iran that began on 28 February “have terminated”, according to the Congressional Research Service (CRS), Congress’s research arm. The administration also argues that the president’s constitutional authority to defend the country is enough, which is why it treats the 60-day clock as no bar.

The same law lets Congress direct a withdrawal by concurrent resolution, and the Senate adopted one on Iran by 50 votes to 48 on 23 June. Such resolutions never go to the president, and their binding force has been disputed since a 1983 Supreme Court ruling against legislative vetoes, so the purse remains the stronger tool.

Tariffs Under Sections 232 and 301 and Under Emergency Law

Tariffs are where the courts have already drawn a line. On Friday 20 February 2026 the Supreme Court ruled 6 to 3, in cases brought by small businesses and 12 states, that IEEPA does not allow the president to impose tariffs, because the Constitution gives the power to lay duties to Congress.

Trump ended the IEEPA duties the same day and replaced them with a 10% import surcharge under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows up to 15% for no more than 150 days unless Congress extends it. The Court of International Trade ruled that surcharge invalid on 7 May for the plaintiffs before it, the government appealed, and the 150 days ran out in July.

The same court has ordered the reliquidation of entries, the step that triggers refunds of IEEPA duties, in more than 4,000 lawsuits by individual importers. On 8 October it certified a class of importers who paid those duties between February 2025 and February 2026 and had not sued on their own.

What remains rests on Section 232, which covers imports that threaten national security, and Section 301, which targets unfair foreign trade practices. In July the Trade Representative imposed Section 301 tariffs of 10% or 12.5% on 60 trading partners over their failure to ban goods made with forced labour, and a separate 25% tariff on certain Brazilian goods.

Both laws require investigations and findings, which slows the president down but leaves courts less room to strike the tariffs down. A Democratic Congress could vote to repeal or limit them, but Trump could veto that bill.

Pardons

The Constitution lets the president grant pardons for any federal offence except in cases of impeachment, and Congress cannot review or reverse them. A pardon does not reach state crimes, and it cannot stop the House from investigating the conduct behind it.

The Veto

Every bill a Democratic Congress passes still goes to Trump, and the Constitution requires two thirds of both chambers to override his veto. In a full Congress that means 290 House votes and 67 Senate votes, far more than either party holds today.

Diplomacy and Recognition

The president alone receives ambassadors and decides which foreign governments Washington deals with, which is how the United States came to work with Venezuela’s acting government. Treaties need two thirds of senators present, but executive agreements, such as the June memorandum with Iran, need no vote.

Immigration Enforcement

The executive branch sets immigration enforcement priorities, such as whom agencies target for arrest and removal. The limit is money, since detention beds, deportation flights and border construction depend on appropriations that a Democratic House would have to approve.

What a Democratic Congress Could Stop

The Constitution says no money may be drawn from the Treasury except under appropriations made by law, which makes the House’s power of the purse the main check on any president. Current funding expires on Friday 11 December, so the first spending fight comes before the new Congress is seated, and every later spending bill would need the new House.

War money is the sharpest test, since the White House asked Congress on 24 June for US$87.6 billion in supplemental funding, US$67.1 billion of it for the Pentagon. The Congressional Budget Office estimates that the war with Iran had cost the Pentagon about US$38 billion by 1 August, and the Senate’s roll-call record shows no vote on the request so far.

A Democratic House could also refuse new money for immigration detention and deportations, although funds already appropriated stay available until they expire. Republicans argue that would weaken border security, while Democrats argue Congress must set limits on how enforcement money is spent.

House committees can issue subpoenas, demand documents and hold hearings, and a Democratic majority would chair every one of them. Oversight would likely start with the Iran war’s cost, the Venezuela oil accounts and the use of emergency powers.

Any new law needs both chambers, so a Democratic House alone could block Republican bills but could not pass its own. In the Senate, the filibuster rule requires 60 votes to end debate on most bills, which limits any majority short of that number.

If Democrats also win the Senate, they would control confirmations of cabinet members, judges and ambassadors, which need only a simple majority. This year the Senate confirmed Todd Blanche as attorney general by 50 votes to 49 on 8 August, the kind of narrow vote a Democratic majority could block.

Treaties need two thirds of senators present, so neither party can ratify one alone. A Democratic Senate would matter most for nominations and for deciding which bills reach the floor.

Impeachment needs only a simple majority in the House, which is why markets price it as likely if Democrats win, with Kalshi at 66.5% for an impeachment before 2028. Removal needs a two-thirds vote of senators present, 67 if all 100 vote, and no president has ever been removed, which is why the same platform prices impeachment and removal at 17.5%.

Republicans argue that impeachment would be a partisan exercise, while Democrats say the House has a duty to investigate possible abuses of power. Either way, the Senate arithmetic, not the House, decides whether Trump could be forced from office.

What It Means for Venezuela, Iran and Cuba

Venezuela

US forces captured Venezuela’s president, Nicolás Maduro, and his wife, Cilia Flores, on 3 January 2026, and both face narco-terrorism charges in federal court in New York. Delcy Rodríguez, Maduro’s vice president and oil minister from the ruling United Socialist Party of Venezuela (PSUV), has governed since then as acting president with US backing.

Washington lifted its own sanctions on Rodríguez in April, according to the CRS, while the European Union and Canada have kept theirs. Polymarket bettors give her a 93.5% chance of still being Venezuela’s de facto leader at the end of 2026, and give a US invasion by 31 December 3.1%.

The state oil company PDVSA remains under sanctions, but Treasury’s General License 46E, reissued on 28 September, lets established US companies buy, ship and refine Venezuelan oil. Payments to sanctioned parties must go into US-controlled Foreign Government Deposit Funds created by an executive order in January, and a State Department official told Congress in April that US$3 billion had passed through them.

A Democratic House could demand the audits of those accounts, which Secretary of State Marco Rubio promised in June to share with Congress, and could hold hearings on the oil deals and on the missing election timetable. It could not cancel the licences, which Treasury issues on its own authority (see also: House Democrats Demand Venezuela Oil Deal Papers).

Iran

The United States and Israel began strikes on Iran on 28 February, and a ceasefire announced on 7 April was followed by a memorandum of understanding signed on 17 June. US forces struck Iranian targets again on 7 and 8 July after attacks on commercial ships, and US Central Command has kept issuing releases on enforcing a naval blockade of Iran.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guard says the Strait of Hormuz is closed while Secretary of State Marco Rubio says it is open, and several tankers have been hit near it this month, according to The National, a newspaper in Abu Dhabi. Polymarket prices the chance that the US carries out no new strike on Iranian soil through 30 November at 46.5%, a US invasion before 2027 at 16.5% and a final nuclear deal by 31 December at 14.5%.

The Senate has voted on Iran war-powers measures at least 14 times this year, most recently rejecting one on 24 September by 50 votes to 49. A Democratic Senate could pass such a measure, but a binding version would still face a veto (see also: Panama Probes US Jet Strike on Its Ship).

Any final nuclear agreement would also trigger review by Congress under the Iran Nuclear Agreement Review Act of 2015. Beyond the midterm odds, bets put the chance of Hormuz traffic returning to normal by 31 December at 15.5%, a risk for oil prices whoever controls Congress.

Cuba

Cuba’s embargo is written into law by the Helms-Burton Act of 1996, also called the LIBERTAD Act, so it cannot be lifted unless the president first certifies that a transition or democratically elected government is in power. Even then Congress can override a suspension by joint resolution, and a separate 2000 law bars Treasury from licensing tourist travel to Cuba.

Tightening needs no vote: Trump declared a national emergency over Cuba on 29 January and, on 1 May, authorised sanctions on anyone operating in Cuba’s energy, defence, mining, financial or security sectors. A tariff on countries that supply oil to Cuba, created under IEEPA in January, was among the duties he ended after the Supreme Court ruling.

Military action against Cuba would fall under the same war-powers rules as Iran, and Polymarket prices a US strike on Cuban soil by 31 December at 10.5%. Bettors give 10% to President Miguel Díaz-Canel leaving office by year-end and 12% to a US-Cuba economic deal (see also: Cuba Denies Contract for 90 Fuel Shipments US Seized).

Mexico, Canada and Brazil

For Mexico, the policy at stake is the State Department’s February 2025 designation of cartels, including Sinaloa and Jalisco New Generation, as foreign terrorist organisations, which rests on executive power alone. Congress can revoke a designation by law, but such a bill would face a veto.

Canada faces 50% tariffs under Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930, announced on 20 July, and certain Canadian alcoholic drinks and dairy products have been barred from the US market since 29 September, according to the White House. Those measures rest on trade law, so a Democratic Congress could hold hearings but would need a veto-proof majority to undo them.

Brazil faces a 25% Section 301 tariff on certain goods, announced by the Trade Representative on 15 July over digital trade, ethanol, deforestation, anti-corruption enforcement and other practices. Because it rests on trade law rather than IEEPA, it survived the Supreme Court ruling, and only the president, a deal or a new law would remove it.

When the Change Would Take Effect

Whatever the midterm odds say, nothing changes on election night, because the current 119th Congress sits until noon on Sunday 3 January 2027, when the terms of the newly elected members begin. Until then, the Republican majorities can still pass bills, confirm nominees and settle spending.

The main deadline in that lame-duck session is Friday 11 December, when the stopgap funding law Trump signed on 2 September expires. A Republican Congress could use the next funding bill to lock in money for the Iran war or immigration enforcement, while Democrats would try to push those decisions into January.

Judicial confirmations are the other lame-duck priority, since a Senate that changes hands in January would end confirmations on party-line votes. Since July the Senate has confirmed several district and appeals judges by margins of five votes or fewer, according to its roll-call record.

What It Means for US Readers

For investors reading the midterm odds, a Democratic House would add uncertainty mainly to spending and war funding, not to tariffs, which now rest on trade laws the president controls. Importers should note that refunds of the struck-down IEEPA duties are moving through the Court of International Trade, which certified a class of importers on 8 October.

Oil traders will watch the Strait of Hormuz and the US blockade more than Congress, but a fight over the US$87.6 billion war request could affect defence companies’ order books. Funding deadlines under a divided Congress also bring shutdown risk, which bond and currency traders watch for its effect on Treasury yields and the dollar.

For Latin American assets, Venezuela’s debt is the clearest case, since a May Treasury licence lets the acting government hire US advisers to prepare a restructuring of debts that may total US$240 billion, according to reports cited by the CRS. Brazilian exporters face the 25% Section 301 tariff whichever party wins, because only the president or a new law can lift it.

Travellers should note that tourist travel to Cuba remains barred under US law, and that ships near the Strait of Hormuz are still being attacked. Americans in Venezuela, Cuba or the Gulf should follow State Department travel advisories, and our USA & Canada Intelligence Brief, Tuesday, October 13, 2026 tracks the campaign day by day.

What Is Not Known

Several Senate races, including Iowa, Maine, Ohio and Texas, are priced between 57% and 65%, so the midterm odds there leave real room for upsets. Alaska uses ranked-choice voting in its general election, and close races anywhere can go to recounts that delay the result for days or weeks.

A 90.5% price in the midterm odds is not a promise, since a favourite at 90% still loses one time in ten. Prices can also move fast on news, such as renewed fighting with Iran or an economic shock, in the three weeks before the vote.

It is not known whether a Democratic House would in fact impeach Trump, on what charges, or how the appeal over the Section 122 surcharge will end. The administration has not said what it would do with the Iran blockade or the Venezuela oil accounts if Congress refused to fund them.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is favoured to win the House in 2026?

Democrats. On the midterm odds, Polymarket bettors gave them a 90.5% chance of winning the House and Kalshi 90% (13 October, 11:14 a.m. ET). They need 218 seats and hold 214 today.

Who is favoured to win the Senate in 2026?

Democrats are favoured, but the Senate midterm odds are closer. Polymarket gave them 63.5% and Kalshi 61.5% (13 October, 11:14 a.m. ET). They need a net gain of four seats for a 51-seat majority, because Vice President JD Vance breaks ties.

Can Trump be removed if Democrats win the House?

A Democratic House could impeach him by a simple majority, but removal needs a two-thirds vote of senators present, 67 if all 100 vote. Kalshi prices impeachment before 2028 at 66.5% but impeachment and removal at 17.5%.

What can Trump do without Congress?

He can issue executive orders, impose sanctions under emergency law, order military action subject to the War Powers Resolution, set tariffs under Sections 232 and 301, grant pardons, veto bills and conduct diplomacy. The Supreme Court ruled on 20 February 2026 that he cannot impose tariffs under IEEPA.

When would a new Congress take over?

The newly elected Congress begins at noon on 3 January 2027. Until then the current Republican majorities stay in charge, and federal funding must be renewed by Friday 11 December.

COLOMBIA · FESTIVALS

Key Facts — The festival The 21st Cartagena Festival de Música, a classical music festival, runs from Saturday 9 to Sunday 17 January 2027.

— Opening night Saturday 9 January at 7 p.m. at the Teatro Adolfo Mejía, with the English Chamber Orchestra and pianist Gabriela Montero.

— Where it is Historic halls, hotel chapels and squares across Cartagena, Colombia’s Caribbean port city, with the old walled city at its heart.

— How to buy TuBoleta is the official seller; a presale for Davivienda bank cards gives 10% off from Monday 12 to Wednesday 21 October.

— Doors and age TuBoleta’s concert pages list doors one hour before the start and a minimum age of 10.

— Prices Ticket prices are not published on the festival’s event pages.

The Cartagena Music Festival returns from Saturday 9 to Sunday 17 January 2027 for its 21st edition. The British-based English Chamber Orchestra is the resident orchestra, the organiser says.

Tickets are sold through TuBoleta, the official seller, and a bank presale opened on Monday 12 October. For US visitors, it is a chance to pair a Caribbean winter trip with concerts by international artists.

What the Cartagena Music Festival Is

The Cartagena Festival de Música is a classical music festival now in its 21st edition, organised by the Fundación Salvi, a Bogotá-based foundation. Its English name, used on its own website, is the Cartagena Music Festival.

Colombia’s Congress declared it part of the nation’s cultural heritage under Law 2340 of 2023, the festival says. The 20th edition in January 2026 drew 15,000 people, according to the organiser.

The 2027 edition was announced on 30 September under the title “The Divine Proportion: Music in Perfect Balance”. It is built around the golden ratio, the old idea of perfect proportion in art and architecture.

It is also the first edition under a new artistic director, the Colombian composer and producer Julio Reyes Copello. The festival describes him as the winner of several Grammy and Latin Grammy awards.

The Stars and the Programme

The Cartagena Music Festival opens on Saturday 9 January at the Teatro Adolfo Mejía with the English Chamber Orchestra under Andreas Ottensamer. Venezuelan pianist Gabriela Montero plays Ravel’s Piano Concerto.

The same night includes Vivaldi and Bach and the world premiere of a work by Reyes Copello. It is inspired by Love in the Time of Cholera, the novel by the Colombian writer Gabriel García Márquez.

On Saturday 16 January, tenor Francesco Meli and soprano Benedetta Torre sing famous arias by Verdi, Donizetti and Puccini. They appear with the Filarmónica Joven de Colombia, the youth orchestra of the Fundación Bolívar Davivienda, under Francesco Lanzillotta.

Other guests named by the festival include Santiago Cañón Valencia, Elena Bashkirova, the Schumann Quartett and flautist Denis Bouriakov. Violinist Andrés Gabetta, harpsichordist Sebastian Wienand and viola da gamba player André Lislevand play Corelli and Biber on Sunday 10 January.

A strand called the Experiencia Gabo takes place in the Casa Gabriel García Márquez in Cartagena. New pieces by Latin American composers there draw on four of his books, including One Hundred Years of Solitude.

Pianist and neuroscientist Mei Rui, who directs the Music-in-Medicine programme at MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston, joins the festival as well. The programme lists her sessions at the Palacio de la Proclamación on 16 and 17 January.

Venues and How to Get Around

The opening night and the opera evening are at the Teatro Adolfo Mejía, which runs its own season too, as our 2026 season report shows. Smaller concerts fill the chapels of the Santa Clara and Charleston Santa Teresa hotels.

Other venues include the Salón de La Veracruz at the Four Seasons, the Palacio de la Proclamación and the Casa Gabriel García Márquez. The festival also uses the Convention Centre, the Parque Lineal de Crespo, the Plaza de San Diego and the port.

The festival says it turns the walled city, Cartagena’s colonial centre, into its stage. Check the venue on each ticket, and use a booked ride for venues outside the centre.

Cartagena Music Festival concerts mostly start at 11 in the morning, 4 in the afternoon or 7 in the evening. Cartagena keeps the same clock as New York in January, so 7 in the evening there is 7 p.m. Eastern.

Tickets and Free Events

Cartagena Music Festival tickets are sold through TuBoleta, which lists each concert as a separate event. The festival also sells tickets in person at the Fundación Salvi office at Calle 70 #7-60, Office 304, in Bogotá.

Holders of Davivienda and DaviBank cards get 10% off when buying from Monday 12 to Wednesday 21 October 2026. Davivienda is a Colombian bank, and TuBoleta labels the current stage a Davivienda presale.

The festival runs a ticket line in English on WhatsApp at +57 314 461 6002. Its call centre in Bogotá is +57 601 593 6300.

Several events are free, according to the official programme. They include talks by Giovanni Bietti, a Convention Centre concert and a screening of the opening night in the Parque Lineal de Crespo.

The programme also lists the closing concert on Sunday 17 January at the Puerto de Cartagena as free entry. TuBoleta’s concert pages set a minimum age of 10, with doors opening an hour before the start.

Tips for US Visitors

The Cartagena Music Festival lists partner hotels on its website, which is worth checking before you book. Concert tickets are sold per event, so you can plan a short trip around one or two nights.

The US State Department rates Colombia at Level 3, Reconsider Travel, in an advisory dated 31 March 2026. It cites crime, terrorism, civil unrest, kidnapping and natural disasters.

The advisory says robbery is common in many areas, drugging occurs often in some regions and street crime happens nationwide. Watch your drink, keep valuables out of sight and use booked rides.

Bolívar, the department that includes Cartagena, is not on the advisory’s do-not-travel list. That list names Arauca, Cauca outside Popayán, Valle del Cauca outside Cali, Norte de Santander and the Venezuelan border zone.

What Is Not Confirmed Yet

Ticket prices for individual concerts are not shown on the festival’s TuBoleta pages. The date general sale opens after the Davivienda presale has not been announced either.

The programme carries a note that the calendar may change. Check the Cartagena Music Festival website and TuBoleta before you book flights around a single concert.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the Cartagena Music Festival 2027?

The Cartagena Music Festival runs from Saturday 9 to Sunday 17 January 2027. The opening concert is on 9 January at 7 p.m. at the Teatro Adolfo Mejía.

Where do I buy tickets?

TuBoleta is the official seller, with each concert listed separately. The festival also helps buyers in English on WhatsApp at +57 314 461 6002.

Are any Cartagena Music Festival events free?

Yes, the official programme marks several talks, a public screening of the opening concert and the closing concert at the port as free entry. The calendar may still change.

World.content: Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa SOUTH AFRICA · FESTIVALS Key Facts — Dates Saturday 28 and Sunday 29 November 2026, the two days of the Taste of Cape Town food and lifestyle festival. — Where it is Green Point Cricket Club, 111 Vlei Road, in Green Point, the Cape Town neighbourhood that is also home to DHL Stadium. — Times Saturday 11:00 to 22:00 local time (4 a.m. to 3 p.m. US Eastern); Sunday 09:00 to 21:00 (2 a.m. to 2 p.m.). — Tickets Sold through Quicket, the South African ticketing site the organiser links to from its own tickets page. — Prices One-day entry R450 (about US$27); Taste Lux Pass with dish vouchers R895 (about US$54); children 12 and under free. — For US visitors No visa for stays under 90 days, and the State Department rates South Africa at Level 2, exercise increased caution. Taste of Cape Town takes over the Green Point Cricket Club on Saturday 28 and Sunday 29 November 2026. The two-day festival lets visitors sample signature dishes from some of the city’s most sought-after restaurants on one open-air ground. It is the South African edition of the Taste series, which its organiser says has run in over 20 cities, from London to Dubai. Tickets are on sale through Quicket, starting at R450 (about US$27) for one day. RT Ask Rio Times Latin American culture, food and life. The organiser promises twelve of the city’s hardest reservations cooking side by side in the open. The format comes from the Taste festival series, which the organiser says has filled grounds in more than 20 cities. Those include London, Paris, São Paulo and Dubai. Taste of Cape Town is produced by The Allure Group, a South African events agency led by group chief executive Bonnke Shipalana. Its announcements frame the festival around South African food culture, from shisa nyama, the township barbecue tradition, to fine dining. The LatAm Brief One email, every weekday morning. Taste of London fills Regent’s Park with 55,000 visitors every June, the Cape Town organiser says. The Allure Group holds the exclusive South African licence through IMG, the global sports and events company. For a US visitor, the appeal is simple: one ticket, one ground and a taste of a famous food city. Taste of Cape Town expects more than 12,000 guests across the weekend, its organiser says. Taste of Cape Town Schedule and What Happens The festival’s ticket terms set Saturday 28 November from 11:00 to 22:00 and Sunday 29 November from 09:00 to 21:00. Last entry is one hour before closing, and there is no re-entry unless your ticket type allows it. South Africa is seven hours ahead of US Eastern time in late November, after US clocks fall back on 1 November. Saturday’s gates therefore open at 4 a.m. in New York, and Sunday’s at 2 a.m. The ground is divided into five zones, one for each of the senses, according to the organiser. Its signature moment is the Sundown Ritual, when guests raise a glass as the sun touches Signal Hill. Taste School, a masterclass theatre, lets small groups learn knife work, plating and wine pairing from the chefs cooking on the ground. Slow Life offers long tables under the trees, acoustic sets and winemakers pouring. The SABC, South Africa’s public broadcaster, is the official broadcast partner, the festival announced on 20 August 2026. It plans coverage on television, radio and its SABC Plus streaming service before, during and after the weekend. Taste of Cape Town Tickets and Prices Taste of Cape Town tickets are sold through Quicket, and the organiser’s own tickets page embeds the Quicket sales window. The ticket terms ban resale, and tickets bought from anyone else can be refused at the gate. The basic Taste Pass costs R450 (about US$27) and is valid for one day of your choice. Conversions use about 16.54 rand to the US dollar on 12 October 2026. The Taste Premium Pass at R595 (about US$36) adds a voucher for one signature dish. The Taste Lux Pass at R895 (about US$54) adds dish vouchers and a welcome drink. A Lux package for four friends costs R3,222 (about US$195) in total. VIP table and lounge seats cost R4,700 (about US$284) to R5,200 (about US$314) each, booked for groups of two, four or six. VIP guests get priority entry, a hospitality lounge, a light meal and free drinks from 11:00 to 17:00. The VIP areas are closed to anyone under 18. Children 12 and under get in free with a ticketed adult, up to two per adult, and Quicket also lists a free Kids Pass. Teenagers aged 13 to 17 need a paid ticket and an adult companion aged 21 or older. Getting to Taste of Cape Town The Green Point Cricket Club sits at 111 Vlei Road in Green Point, close to the Atlantic seafront. DHL Stadium, home of the Cape Town Sevens, stands in the same neighbourhood. The Quicket event page carries a map and a directions link for the ground. Taste of Cape Town has not published parking or shuttle details, so a taxi or ride-hailing app is the simplest choice. The State Department advises travellers to verify all trip details before getting into a ride-share car. It also advises against driving outside cities at night. Visitors flying in land at Cape Town International Airport, the city’s main gateway. Plan the trip into town before you arrive, especially if your flight lands after dark. Tips for US Visitors US citizens do not need a visa for South Africa for stays of less than 90 days, the State Department says. Your passport must be valid for 30 days after you leave and have two consecutive blank visa pages. The State Department rates South Africa at Level 2, which means exercise increased caution. It warns that ATM and credit card skimming are common, so keep your card in sight when paying. Late November is late spring in Cape Town, and the festival is held outdoors, so bring sunscreen and a layer for the evening. Bags are searched at the gate, and glass, outside food and drink, and drones are banned. The same stretch of the calendar is busy across the city. Our Cape Town Sevens guide covers the rugby tournament at DHL Stadium on 5 and 6 December. Cape Town Tourism lists the Kirstenbosch Summer Sunset Concerts from 25 November 2026 to 29 March 2027. A food weekend in Green Point combines easily with a concert at the botanical garden. What Is Not Confirmed Yet The names of the twelve restaurants have not been published on the festival’s website. Line-up announcements go first to newsletter subscribers, the organiser says. The Taste School timetable and the acoustic acts on the Slow Life lawn have not been announced either. Masterclass places may be tight, since the organiser describes sessions in small groups. The Taste of Cape Town experiences page lists Saturday as 10:00 to 21:00, an hour off the ticket terms. Check the time on your ticket before you set out. The organiser’s announcements give the Lux Pass three dish vouchers, while the Quicket description lists two. Check what is included at checkout before you pay. Payment methods at the food stands, cash or card, have not been published yet. Carry a card and some rand in small notes to be safe. More: South Africa news in English, every day from The Rio Times. Frequently Asked Questions When is Taste of Cape Town 2026? Taste of Cape Town takes place on Saturday 28 and Sunday 29 November 2026 at the Green Point Cricket Club. Saturday runs from 11:00 to 22:00 and Sunday from 09:00 to 21:00, Cape Town time. Gates open at 4 a.m. US Eastern on Saturday and 2 a.m. on Sunday. Where do I buy Taste of Cape Town tickets? Tickets are sold through Quicket, the seller the organiser links to from its own website. One-day entry costs R450 (about US$27), and children 12 and under enter free with a ticketed adult. Do US citizens need a visa for Taste of Cape Town? No visa is needed for US citizens staying less than 90 days. Passports must be valid for 30 days after you leave and have two consecutive blank visa pages. Which restaurants are cooking at Taste of Cape Town? The organiser promises twelve of the city’s hardest reservations, but has not yet published their names. World.title: Ironman Cozumel 2026 Triathlon Guide
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

MEXICO · TRIATHLON

Key Facts — The event Ironman Cozumel is a full-distance triathlon: a 2.4-mile ocean swim, a 112-mile bike ride and a 26.2-mile marathon run.

— Date Race day is Sunday 22 November 2026, with athlete check-in from Thursday 19 November and awards on Monday 23 November.

— Venue and city The race is held on Cozumel island in Quintana Roo state, Mexico, and finishes downtown in San Miguel de Cozumel.

— Start times Professionals start at 6:55 a.m. (men) and 7 a.m. (women), age groupers at 7:10 a.m., all local and US Eastern time.

— Entry Registration is open at ironman.com, where general entry costs US$799.24 including fees, as of 13 October.

— How to follow in the US No TV broadcast has been announced, and the organiser offers live tracking and results in the IRONMAN Tracker app.

Ironman Cozumel returns on Sunday 22 November 2026, with a 140.6-mile race around a Mexican island in the Caribbean Sea. The organiser’s race page lists the 2026 edition as the Ironman Latin American Championship.

Registration is open, and the general entry costs US$799.24 including fees. The age-group start is 7:10 a.m. on the island, which is also 7:10 a.m. in New York that day.

What Ironman Cozumel Is

Ironman is the brand behind the classic long-distance triathlon, which strings swimming, cycling and running into one race. A full Ironman covers 140.6 miles in a single day.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 with 71.4 points. Strongest pillar: economic relationships (90); weakest: state capacity & security (46). Alignment group: Hedging. Watch21 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.7 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Cozumel is an island about 30 minutes by ferry from Playa del Carmen, on Mexico’s Caribbean coast. The organiser notes more than 14 miles of reefs, plus Maya ruins and a national park.

The organiser calls Cozumel a seasoned Ironman host city and a late-season race in paradise. In 2026 it carries the Latin American Championship title, which the race page says will draw top regional athletes.

We never share your email.

For US triathletes, Ironman Cozumel offers a warm, flat course late in the year. In November the island also shares the US East Coast clock, so travellers from New York or Miami face no time change.

The Ironman Cozumel Course

The organiser says the Ironman Cozumel swim takes place in the protected Cozumel Reefs National Marine Park, with clear water and rich underwater life. The 2.4-mile swim runs from the Cozumel ASIPONA Marina to Chankanaab Park, in water the organiser puts at 78°F (26°C) on average.

The bike leg covers three laps around the island for 180 kilometres, or 112 miles. The route runs along ocean roads, through the hotel zone and briefly through town.

The marathon is flat and passes the waterfront walk, the main plaza and older neighbourhoods of San Miguel de Cozumel. The finish line sits in the municipal park by City Hall, in the centre of town.

The organiser’s weather table shows highs of 81°F to 86°F (27°C to 30°C) for the 2023 to 2025 editions. It rates both the bike and the run course as flat.

Race Week Schedule in Local and US Eastern Time

Quintana Roo, the state that includes Cozumel, keeps the same time as US Eastern Standard Time all year. Once US clocks fall back on 1 November, every race time below is identical in New York.

Athlete check-in and the race expo open on Thursday 19 November, from noon to 8 p.m., at the Cozumel Convention Center. On Friday 20 November check-in runs from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. in designated time slots, the last chance to collect race packets.

English briefings at the Presidente Hotel are on Friday at 1:30 p.m. and 3 p.m. local time. Mandatory bike check-in at Chankanaab Park, the first transition area, runs on Saturday from 10:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

On Sunday the professional men start at 6:55 a.m. and the professional women at 7 a.m. local time. Age-group athletes follow in a rolling start from 7:10 a.m., and the awards are on Monday 23 November at 11 a.m. local time.

How to Enter Ironman Cozumel

Ironman Cozumel entries are sold only through the organiser’s registration page, which showed registration as open on 13 October. The general entry costs US$799.24, made up of US$729 for the race and US$70.24 in processing fees.

The organiser warns that pricing depends on remaining slots and rises automatically when a tier fills. Entries are personal, cannot be transferred to another athlete and are not refundable.

The entry includes a backpack, a finisher medal, on-course food and drink, medical support and a timing chip. Bibs are personalised with name and flag only for athletes registered at least one month before race day.

Age-group athletes can also earn a place at the 2027 Ironman World Championship here. Qualifiers must claim the slot in person at Monday’s ceremony, with photo ID and payment.

How to Follow the Race From the US

No television or streaming broadcast of Ironman Cozumel has been announced for US viewers. The organiser says race day will have live coverage with athlete tracking and running results.

Friends and family can follow any Ironman Cozumel athlete in the IRONMAN Tracker app, which the organiser lists for live tracking and results. The organiser also points fans to its @IRONMANLive account on X for the professional race.

Getting to Cozumel

Visitors can fly directly to Cozumel International Airport, the organiser’s travel page says. The island’s airport is being expanded, as described in our report on the Cozumel airport works.

The other route is to fly into Cancún, take an authorised taxi or an ADO intercity bus to Playa del Carmen, then the ferry. The organiser puts the crossing at about 30 minutes, with boats from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. that can change with the weather.

Athletes flying with a bike should check airline and ferry rules for bike boxes before booking. Ten official host hotels offer free bike support and race-morning shuttles for their validated guests.

Mexico’s other big late-season race for US fans is off-road, and our Baja 1000 guide covers that one. The Baja 1000 starts in Los Cabos on 13 November, nine days before the Cozumel triathlon.

Safety and Costs for Visitors

The US State Department rates Quintana Roo at Level 2, exercise increased caution, because of crime and the risk of terrorism. It notes that US citizens have been victims of crime in tourist areas.

The advice is to stay in well-lit pedestrian streets and tourist zones and to watch surroundings after dark. The organiser separately asks athletes and supporters to agree before the race on a meeting point for after the finish.

Spectators are not allowed into the finish area because of crowding, the organiser says. The swim start is also closed to spectators, while the organiser says hundreds of people line the downtown run course.

Beyond the entry fee, an Ironman Cozumel trip means flights, bike transport and lodging from Thursday check-in to the Monday awards. The organiser does not set these costs, so prices depend on travel dates and hotels.

What Is Not Confirmed Yet

The organiser has not published the Ironman Cozumel 2026 start list, the number of entrants or the names of professional athletes. The full course overview is still marked as coming soon, and the venue map online dates from the 2025 race.

The schedule sets the overall finish cut-off at 17 hours, but separate swim and bike cut-off times are not listed on the race pages. The organiser also warns that sea conditions can shift start times and that the schedule may change.

More: Mexico news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is Ironman Cozumel 2026?

Ironman Cozumel 2026 is on Sunday 22 November 2026. Age-group athletes start at 7:10 a.m., which is also 7:10 a.m. US Eastern time.

How much does Ironman Cozumel cost to enter?

The general entry costs US$799.24 including fees, as of 13 October. The organiser says prices rise automatically as slot tiers sell out.

Can I watch Ironman Cozumel on TV in the US?

No TV broadcast has been announced. Live tracking and results are available in the IRONMAN Tracker app.

How do I get to Cozumel for the race?

Fly directly to Cozumel International Airport, or fly to Cancún and take a ferry from Playa del Carmen. The crossing takes about 30 minutes.

World.title: Skateboarding Super Crown São Paulo 2026
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

BRAZIL · SKATEBOARDING

Key Facts — Dates Saturday 12 and Sunday 13 December 2026, the season finale of Street League Skateboarding, the professional street skating tour.

— Venue Ginásio do Ibirapuera, an indoor arena in the Ibirapuera sports complex in São Paulo, Brazil.

— Schedule Semifinals on Saturday and finals on Sunday, Brazilian sports media report; start times are not published yet.

— Start times Not set for 2026; in 2025 the stream began at 11:30 a.m. São Paulo time (9:30 a.m. ET) Saturday and 11 a.m. (9 a.m. ET) Sunday.

— Tickets On sale via Ticketmaster Brazil, linked from the league’s event page; general sale opened 30 September, with 2026 prices not posted by the league.

— Watching in the US The 2025 Super Crown streamed live on the league’s YouTube channel; the 2026 broadcast plan is not announced yet.

The Super Crown São Paulo 2026 decides the world champions of Street League Skateboarding on Saturday 12 and Sunday 13 December. The finale takes place at Ginásio do Ibirapuera, an indoor arena in Brazil’s largest city.

The league’s own event page says tickets are on sale now through Ticketmaster Brazil. Brazilian sports media report that a new team contest, the Nations Cup, offers US$100,000 to the winning country.

What the Super Crown Is

Street League Skateboarding, known as SLS, runs a professional tour in street skating, the style built on stairs, rails and ledges. Its Super Crown World Championship is the final event of each season.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Each season’s tour stops build toward the Super Crown, where the world titles are decided. On its 2025 page, the league said the whole season ‘all leads up to this moment.’

The 2025 final was held at the same arena on 6 and 7 December 2025, according to the league. For the Super Crown São Paulo edition of 2026, its page opens with a simple message: ‘The Super Crown is coming back to São Paulo!’

The LatAm Brief One email, every weekday morning. What moved in Latin American markets, politics and expat life. Yesterday’s subject line: “IMF cuts Brazil growth to 2.2% and Argentina's to 2.1%” Get the brief Free. We send a confirmation link first — nothing arrives until you click it. Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves, as we assume the interest is no longer there. See our privacy policy. We never share your email.

Why US Skate Fans Should Care

American Nyjah Huston won the league’s Paris stop on 3 October, so the US star heads to the Super Crown São Paulo finale in form. He also skated the 2025 men’s final in São Paulo, which 15-year-old Ginwoo Onodera won.

Brazil is a skateboarding power, and the finale gives its fans a world title event at home. Our report on Brazil’s rise in global skateboarding describes Brazilian skaters sweeping every medal at an SLS event in Brasília.

Brazil’s Rayssa Leal, an Olympic medallist, won the 2025 women’s title, her fourth Super Crown in a row, the league reports. The 2026 individual field has not been published yet.

The New Nations Cup

The Super Crown São Paulo weekend also marks the debut of a team contest, the Nations Cup, the league says. Brazil, the United States and Japan face a combined Rest of the World team.

The sports-business site Máquina do Esporte and the regional outlet ABCdoABC both report that the winning country takes home US$100,000. Máquina do Esporte says the Nations Cup takes place on Saturday 12 December, the first day of the event.

Super Crown São Paulo Schedule and Time Difference

Saturday 12 December is for the men’s and women’s semifinals, and Sunday 13 December decides the world titles, both outlets report. ABCdoABC adds that the trophies are presented on the Sunday.

The league has not yet posted start times or a running order for either day. In 2025 its Saturday stream went live at 11:30 a.m. São Paulo time, which was 9:30 a.m. ET.

São Paulo runs on Brasília time, three hours behind Greenwich, and Brazil no longer uses daylight saving time. Once US clocks fall back on 1 November, São Paulo is two hours ahead of New York.

How to Buy Super Crown Tickets

The Super Crown São Paulo page on streetleague.com reads ‘tickets on sale now’ and links to the event on Ticketmaster Brazil. Máquina do Esporte names Ticketmaster as the only sales channel and dates the general sale from 30 September.

Seats are split between the upper and lower rings, plus a premium SLS Experience area close to the course, Máquina do Esporte reports. The league has not posted 2026 prices on its own site, so check the Ticketmaster page for the current price list.

The Ticketmaster Brazil site is in Portuguese and shows prices in Brazilian reais. Buy only through the link on the league’s page rather than from resellers on social media.

How to Watch in the US

The league streamed its Paris stop on 3 October live on YouTube for viewers worldwide, its own guide said. Its site also lists Rumble, the video platform that carried earlier 2026 stops such as Sydney and downtown Los Angeles.

The league has not yet announced where the Super Crown São Paulo finals will stream or air. Last December, it sent fans to its YouTube channel for both days of the 2025 Super Crown.

Getting to Ginásio do Ibirapuera

Ginásio do Ibirapuera, officially Ginásio Geraldo José de Almeida, is part of the Ibirapuera sports complex near Ibirapuera Park. The park is São Paulo’s best-known green space and lies south of the city centre.

Most international flights from the US land at Guarulhos International Airport, northeast of the city. Allow plenty of time for the drive across the city to Ibirapuera by taxi or ride-hailing app, especially at rush hour.

Congonhas, the city’s domestic airport, is much closer to the arena if you connect through another Brazilian city. After the Sunday finals, a ride-hailing app is the simplest way back to a hotel.

Visa and Safety for US Visitors

The State Department says US citizens need a visa for Brazil ‘regardless of the purpose of travel,’ so apply well before December. Its entry table accepts ‘a valid Brazilian visa or e-visa’ for US travellers.

The State Department rates Brazil at Level 2, exercise increased caution, in an advisory dated 29 May 2025. It also warns that ‘any public event, including concerts and sporting events, can turn violent.’

Keep phones out of sight on the street and carry only the cash and cards you need. A plan to meet friends at a fixed point after the event helps if phones lose signal in the crowd.

What Is Not Confirmed Yet

The league has not published start times, door times or the list of skaters for the Super Crown São Paulo event. Nor has it named the Nations Cup team line-ups.

The league has not posted 2026 ticket prices on its own site, and the broadcast plan for US viewers is still open. We will update this guide once Street League Skateboarding posts its December schedule.

More: Brazil news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the Super Crown in São Paulo?

The Super Crown São Paulo 2026 runs on Saturday 12 and Sunday 13 December at Ginásio do Ibirapuera. Saturday brings the semifinals and Sunday the finals, Brazilian sports media report.

Where can I buy Super Crown tickets?

The league’s event page says tickets are on sale through Ticketmaster Brazil. Use the link on streetleague.com rather than resale offers on social media.

What time does the Super Crown start in US Eastern time?

Start times for 2026 have not been published yet. In 2025 the Saturday stream began at 11:30 a.m. in São Paulo, or 9:30 a.m. ET, and the gap is again two hours.

How can I watch the Super Crown from the US?

The league streamed the 2025 Super Crown and its 2026 Paris stop live on YouTube, and earlier 2026 stops on Rumble. It has not yet announced the 2026 Super Crown broadcast plan, so check streetleague.com in the days before the event.

COLOMBIA · TRAVEL

Key Facts — The route JetBlue plans one daily nonstop between Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport in South Florida and Cali, Colombia’s third-largest city.

— Start date Thursday 15 October 2026, the date in JetBlue’s 9 July schedule release, which made the route subject to government approval.

— Airline’s latest word JetBlue’s 1 October release says Cali service is set to launch later in October, its fourth Colombian city.

— Already flying JetBlue has flown daily from Fort Lauderdale to Barranquilla since 1 October 2026 and also serves Medellín and Cartagena.

— Where to book Book directly at jetblue.com or in the JetBlue app, which listed one-way Fort Lauderdale to Cali fares from US$139 for November on 13 October.

— Not confirmed yet JetBlue had not announced Cali flight times or said whether government approval was granted by 13 October.

— US safety advice The State Department rates Colombia Level 3, reconsider travel; Valle del Cauca is Level 4 except for Cali itself.

JetBlue Cali flights from Fort Lauderdale are due to start on Thursday 15 October 2026, giving South Florida a daily nonstop to Colombia’s salsa capital. JetBlue set that date in its 9 July schedule release, subject to government approval.

In its 1 October release, JetBlue said Cali service was set to launch later in October, making it the airline’s fourth city in Colombia. Flight times for the route had not been announced in that release.

What JetBlue Has Announced for Cali

JetBlue Cali flights were first announced in May, with daily service between Fort Lauderdale and Cali from 15 October, the Cartagena newspaper El Universal reported. The Colombian outlet Minuto60 gave the same start date for daily service that month.

Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (BB-); 26 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.8 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

JetBlue’s schedule release of 9 July lists Cali as a new JetBlue city with one daily flight from 15 October. A footnote makes the Colombian routes subject to government approval.

JetBlue’s own update came on 1 October, when it opened its Barranquilla route. The airline said Barranquilla joins Medellín and Cartagena, with Cali set to launch later in October.

With Cali, JetBlue’s Colombian network would reach four cities, the airline says. The route is part of what JetBlue called its largest-ever Fort Lauderdale schedule, announced on 9 July.

Why Cali Matters for US Travelers

Cali is Colombia’s third-largest city and the capital of Valle del Cauca department in the country’s southwest. Salsa is its calling card, and the mayor’s office runs a World Salsa Festival with a dance contest.

The 69th Feria de Cali opens with its Salsódromo dance parade on 25 December 2026, says Corfecali, the city’s events corporation. Our guide to the Cali Salsa Fair covers the parades, concerts and dance shows.

This year the parade has an international wing of 160 dancers born outside Colombia, chosen through an open call that closes on 19 October. JetBlue Cali flights start in time for the December holiday season and the fair.

The Barranquilla Route Already Flying

JetBlue launched daily Fort Lauderdale to Barranquilla flights on 1 October 2026, flying to Ernesto Cortissoz International Airport on Colombia’s Caribbean coast. The airline uses Airbus A320 jets on the route.

Flight 1957 leaves Fort Lauderdale at 11:05 a.m. and lands in Barranquilla at 12:55 p.m., local times. The return, flight 1958, leaves at 2:05 p.m. and reaches Florida at 5:56 p.m.

Atlántico governor Eduardo Verano welcomed the route in JetBlue’s release. “JetBlue’s decision to serve our airport is a vote of confidence in Atlántico’s potential,” he said.

Other US carriers are adding Colombia flights for the winter too. Read about Frontier’s Orlando flights from 10 December and United’s Dulles to Cartagena nonstop.

How to Book JetBlue Cali Flights

JetBlue sells its flights at jetblue.com and in its app, and the Cali route should appear there under the airport codes FLL and CLO. If the search shows no flights on 15 October, the start may have moved.

On 13 October, JetBlue’s own fare page listed one-way Fort Lauderdale to Cali fares from US$139 for November departures. JetBlue says such fares were found in the previous 24 hours, reflect the lowest fare available and exclude bag fees.

Fares in the other direction, from Cali to Fort Lauderdale, started at US$246 one way on JetBlue’s Cali page. Compare them with connecting fares before you buy, especially around Christmas and the Cali fair.

On the Barranquilla route, JetBlue sells Main cabin seats and EvenMore seats with extra legroom and early boarding, its release says. Main includes free Wi-Fi, seatback live TV and free snacks and drinks.

Travelers who live elsewhere in the United States can connect in Fort Lauderdale from other JetBlue cities. Leave enough time between flights, because international departures need earlier check-in.

Tips for US Visitors to Cali

The State Department rates Colombia at Level 3, which means reconsider travel, citing crime, terrorism, civil unrest, kidnapping and natural disasters. It puts Valle del Cauca at Level 4, do not travel, but excludes Cali from that warning.

US government employees may travel to Cali only with permission, the advisory says. That rule does not bind private travelers, but it shows how seriously Washington treats the region.

The advisory warns about dating apps in blunt terms. “Many U.S. citizens in Colombia have been drugged, robbed, and even killed by Colombian criminals posing as dates,” it says.

JetBlue Cali flights land at Alfonso Bonilla Aragón International Airport, which lies outside the city in neighbouring Palmira. Colombia’s civil aviation authority, Aerocivil, has run the airport since September 2025, when a private concession ended.

Colombia does not change its clocks, so Cali is one hour behind Fort Lauderdale until US clocks fall back on Sunday 1 November. After that date, both cities keep the same time.

Before you fly, check Colombia’s entry rules with Migración Colombia, the country’s immigration authority. Enroll in the State Department’s Smart Traveler Enrollment Program so the embassy in Bogotá can reach you in an emergency.

What Is Not Confirmed Yet

JetBlue had not announced departure and arrival times for its Cali flights by 13 October. Its Barranquilla launch promotion, from US$134 one way, has already closed for bookings.

The airline has not said whether the government approval mentioned in its July release has been granted. Its 1 October release says only that JetBlue Cali flights are set to launch later in October.

The exact 15 October date comes from JetBlue’s July release and from May reports in El Universal and Minuto60. Check jetblue.com for the live schedule before you book onward plans.

If the start of JetBlue Cali flights slips, travelers can still reach Cali by connecting through Bogotá or another hub.

Frequently Asked Questions

When do JetBlue Cali flights from Fort Lauderdale start?

JetBlue Cali flights are due to start on Thursday 15 October 2026 with one daily nonstop from Fort Lauderdale. JetBlue gave that date in its 9 July release, subject to government approval, and on 1 October said Cali launches later in October.

Does JetBlue fly to other cities in Colombia?

Yes. JetBlue has flown daily from Fort Lauderdale to Barranquilla since 1 October 2026 and also serves Medellín and Cartagena.

Is Cali safe for US visitors?

The State Department rates Colombia Level 3, reconsider travel, and Valle del Cauca Level 4, but Cali itself is excluded from the Level 4 warning. It also warns that criminals posing as dates have drugged, robbed and even killed US citizens.

Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times → MOROCCO · RUNNING Key Facts — Race day The 37th Marrakech International Marathon runs on Sunday 31 January 2027, starting at 7:45 a.m. local time (1:45 a.m. US Eastern). — Where it is Start and finish are on Avenue de la Ménara, behind the Sofitel hotel in Marrakech, with the runners’ village on Koutoubia Square. — The races A full marathon (26.2 miles), a half marathon (13.1 miles) and a new 5 km (3.1-mile) fun run on Saturday 30 January. — How to enter Online on the organiser’s website, marathonmarrakech.ma, or through Sport Up, the platform linked by travel partner Prêt à Partir (open until 24 January 2027). — Entry fees Runners visiting from abroad pay €80 (about US$89) for the marathon and €60 (about US$67) for the half. — Bib pickup Collect your bib with your passport at the runners’ village on Koutoubia Square, by Saturday 30 January at the latest. The Marrakech Marathon returns on Sunday 31 January 2027 for its 37th edition, with the start at 7:45 a.m. on Avenue de la Ménara. Registration for runners from abroad is already open online. The Marrakech Marathon loops past the 12th-century city walls, the Menara gardens and the palm groves of Morocco’s red city. For US runners it is a winter race abroad, with entry at about US$89. Why the Marrakech Marathon Draws Runners From Abroad The Marrakech Marathon, officially the Marrakech International Marathon, dates back to 1987 and is held under the patronage of King Mohammed VI. Its rules fix the date on the last Sunday of January, which in 2027 falls on 31 January. The organiser, the Association Grand Atlas, calls the course one of the fastest in the world. It is flat, with a few gentle rises in the palm grove, and the time limit is five hours and 30 minutes. Elite runners chase real money here. The two marathon winners each receive US$15,000 if they beat set times (2:07 for men, 2:25 for women), or US$12,000 otherwise. The French travel agency Prêt à Partir, an official partner of the race, expects more than 15,000 runners. It also sells packages with hotel, breakfast, airport transfer and a bib, five minutes’ walk from the start. Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Morocco expat life Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy How US Runners Can Enter and What It Costs Runners who live outside Morocco can sign up on the organiser’s own website, marathonmarrakech.ma, which takes payment in euros. The partner agency also links to the Sport Up platform, where entries stay open until 24 January 2027. The marathon costs €80 (about US$89) and the half marathon €60 (about US$67), according to the organiser’s registration page and Prêt à Partir. All US$ figures use the exchange rates of 12 October 2026, when one euro was worth about US$1.12. Foreigners who live in Morocco register directly with the organiser, the Association Grand Atlas, and pay a reduced rate. The race rules say that discount is set each year. Moroccan runners pay 300 dirhams (about US$31) for the marathon and 250 dirhams (about US$26) for the half, bib and T-shirt included. Dirham figures use about 9.71 to the US dollar on the same date. A medical certificate stating that you are fit for competitive running is mandatory for the marathon and the half. Runners must be at least 17 for the marathon and 16 for the half. The Race Weekend Schedule in Marrakech The 2027 Marrakech Marathon weekend adds a first “Course pour Tous”, a 5 km run open to everyone, on the morning of Saturday 30 January. It starts opposite the Koutoubia, the landmark 12th-century mosque, with sign-up at Jemaa el-Fna square. On race day the start area opens to runners at 7:30 a.m. on Sunday 31 January, and the gun fires 15 minutes later. The organiser’s programme lists the trophy ceremony for late morning, at 11:30. Bibs are handed out at the Marrakech Marathon village on Koutoubia Square in the last days before the race, up to Saturday 30 January. You need your passport to collect yours. The organiser also lists earlier pickup points at Marrakech railway station and Jemaa el-Fna from the weekend before race day. That helps runners who arrive early in race week. Getting to the Start Line The start and finish arches stand on Avenue de la Ménara, now officially Avenue Prince Moulay Rachid, behind the Sofitel hotel. The race rules place them about 150 meters from the fountain. Marrakech Menara Airport, the city’s international airport, is a short taxi ride from the start area. The partner’s hotel packages are within walking distance of the start line. Bicycles and all wheeled or motorized vehicles are banned from the course. Plan to arrive on foot or by taxi well before the start area opens at 7:30 on race morning. Our guide What to Do in Marrakech in October 2026 covers the city’s autumn festivals and events. Tips for US Visitors to Morocco US citizens do not need a visa for a Marrakech Marathon trip under 90 days, according to the US State Department. Your passport must be valid for at least six months on arrival, with one free page for the entry stamp. The State Department rates Morocco at Level 2, “Exercise Increased Caution”, because of the risk of terrorism. It says possible targets include tourist sites, transport hubs and markets, so stay alert in crowds. The State Department says Moroccan dirhams cannot be taken out of the country, so change only what you need. Sums of 100,000 dirhams (about US$10,300) or US$10,000 and up must be declared on arrival. The race’s partner describes the January climate in Marrakech as often mild. An old layer you can throw away helps during the early wait at the start. What Is Not Confirmed Yet The half marathon is set for 9:15 a.m., though one page of the official site still shows 8:30. Check the final timetable in your registration email before race week. The official site lists the new 5 km run at 9:00 a.m. on one page and at 9:30 a.m. in its programme. Sign-up for it takes place on site at Jemaa el-Fna. Opening hours of the runners’ village also differ between pages of the official site, so check them in race week. The organiser has not named the elite field or released a road closure plan. More: Morocco news in English, every day from The Rio Times. Frequently Asked Questions When is the Marrakech Marathon 2027? The 37th Marrakech Marathon is on Sunday 31 January 2027, with the start at 7:45 a.m. on Avenue de la Ménara. A new 5 km fun run takes place the day before, on Saturday 30 January. How much does it cost a US runner to enter? Runners living outside Morocco pay €80 (about US$89) for the marathon and €60 (about US$67) for the half. Sign up on the organiser’s website, marathonmarrakech.ma, or through the Sport Up platform, open until 24 January 2027. Do US citizens need a visa to run in Marrakech? No, not for stays under 90 days, according to the US State Department. Your passport needs six months of validity, and you must show it to collect your race bib. Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times → SOUTH AFRICA · COMEDY Key Facts — The shows British comedian Jimmy Carr brings his current stand-up tour, Laughs Funny, to Pretoria and Cape Town in March 2027. — Pretoria Saturday 13 March 2027 at the Sunbet Arena in Time Square, Menlyn Maine; doors 6 p.m., show 8 p.m. — Cape Town Sunday 14 March 2027 at the Grand Arena in GrandWest, Goodwood; doors 7 p.m., show 8 p.m. — How to buy Only through Ticketmaster South Africa and Big Concerts, the promoter; general sale opened on Friday 2 October 2026. — Age limit 16 and over only; the promoter’s listing says no under-16s are permitted, and it shows no ticket prices yet. — For US visitors No visa is needed for stays under 90 days; passports must be valid 30 days after exit, with two blank visa pages. The Jimmy Carr South Africa dates are set: the British comedian plays Pretoria on Saturday 13 March 2027 and Cape Town on Sunday 14 March. Both nights are part of his current world tour, Laughs Funny, which also takes him to Japan, Thailand and Australia. Tickets are sold by Ticketmaster South Africa and by Big Concerts, the promoter, and general sale opened on Friday 2 October 2026. US visitors need no visa for a short trip, but under-16s are not admitted to either show. Who Jimmy Carr Is and What the Show Is Like Jimmy Carr is a British comedian, writer and television host, famous for dark humour, dry wit, heckler comebacks and one-line jokes. His official site points fans to his Netflix special Natural Born Killer and his book Before & Laughter. Big Concerts, the South African promoter of the shows, calls him one of the biggest-selling comedy acts in the world. It says he plays to sell-out crowds around the globe and has performed in more than 50 countries. His last South African visit came in March 2024, when he brought his Terribly Funny tour to the country, Time Out Johannesburg reports. Bizcommunity, a South African trade site, listed those shows at the same Pretoria and Cape Town venues. Laughs Funny is the current Jimmy Carr show, built on fast-paced, edgy one-liners and banter with the crowd. The promoter is blunt about the tone, and says the show is not for everyone. “Some people are repelled by Jimmy’s dark brand of comedy,” Big Concerts writes. “This show is not for them.” Crowd work is part of the night, so think about where you sit. “Only the very brave sit in the front row,” the Big Concerts listing warns. Laughs Funny is on sale now, his official site says. For American fans, the South African dates pair a comedy night with a trip to Cape Town and the capital region. Privacy policy Tickets and How to Buy General sale opened at 9 a.m. South African time on Friday 2 October 2026, through Ticketmaster South Africa and the Big Concerts website. A presale for the Big Concerts Fan Club ran from Wednesday 30 September until Friday morning. Buy Jimmy Carr tickets only from those two official sellers, which the promoter names on its page. Big Concerts warns that tickets bought on Viagogo or other resale sites will be refused at the door, with no refund. The promoter’s event page does not list ticket prices. Check prices on Ticketmaster South Africa before you set a budget, and remember that they are charged in rand. The listing says no under-16s are permitted at either show. Families travelling with teenagers should plan around that rule before booking flights. Both arenas sit inside casino complexes run by Sun International, a South African hotel and casino group. Time Square’s own page says no one under 18 may gamble there. The Pretoria Show at the Sunbet Arena The Jimmy Carr Pretoria show is on Saturday 13 March 2027, the first of the two South African nights. Doors open at 6 p.m. and the show starts at 8 p.m. local time. The Sunbet Arena sits inside Time Square, which Sun International calls the largest casino in Pretoria. The group describes the arena as one of the best-loved entertainment venues in Gauteng, the province around Johannesburg and Pretoria. Big Concerts gives the address as 209 Aramist Avenue in Waterkloof Glen. Sun International places Time Square in the heart of Menlyn Maine, in Pretoria East. Pretoria is South Africa’s administrative capital, and most long-haul flights to the region land at OR Tambo International Airport near Johannesburg. From the airport, the simplest way to reach Time Square is by car or a ride-hailing app. The same arena hosts other big touring shows this season, including Riverdance 30 in April 2027. Our Kehlani guide covers a December concert at the same two venues. The Cape Town Show at GrandWest The Jimmy Carr Cape Town show is on Sunday 14 March 2027, in the Grand Arena at GrandWest. Doors open at 7 p.m. and the show starts at 8 p.m. local time. GrandWest is a casino and entertainment complex run by Sun International. Arrive in good time, because the doors open only an hour before the show. Big Concerts lists the address as 1 Jakes Gerwel Drive in Goodwood, a suburb of Cape Town. The complex is a drive from the city centre, so plan the trip there and back before the night. Seeing both shows means a flight from Gauteng to the Western Cape on the Sunday. Book it early in the day to leave time for the evening show. Running times have not been published, so arrange your ride back to your hotel before the show starts. Tips for US Visitors US citizens do not need a visa for South Africa for stays of less than 90 days, the State Department says. Your passport must be valid for 30 days after you leave and have two consecutive blank visa pages. The State Department rates South Africa at Level 2, which means exercise increased caution. It warns that ATM and credit card skimming are common. The advisory adds that some crime victims have been followed from OR Tambo Airport in Johannesburg. It urges travellers to drive with doors locked and windows closed. It also advises against driving outside cities at night. Before getting into a ride-share car, verify all the trip details, the State Department says. South Africa runs on South Africa Standard Time, two hours ahead of UTC all year. So 8 p.m. there is 1 p.m. in New York on Saturday 13 March, and 2 p.m. on Sunday after US clocks spring forward. What Is Not Confirmed Yet Big Concerts has not published ticket prices on its event page, and no opening act has been named. Running times have not been announced either. The promoter lists only Pretoria and Cape Town so far. It names no date in Johannesburg or Durban. More: South Africa news in English, every day from The Rio Times. Frequently Asked Questions When and where does Jimmy Carr play in South Africa? Jimmy Carr plays the Sunbet Arena at Time Square in Pretoria on Saturday 13 March 2027. He then plays the Grand Arena at GrandWest in Cape Town on Sunday 14 March, and both shows start at 8 p.m. Where can I buy Jimmy Carr tickets in South Africa? Tickets are sold by Ticketmaster South Africa and Big Concerts, the promoter, and general sale opened on Friday 2 October 2026. No under-16s are admitted. Do US citizens need a visa to see Jimmy Carr in South Africa? No visa is needed for US citizens staying less than 90 days. Passports must be valid for 30 days after you leave and have two consecutive blank visa pages. World.title: Institute of Archaeology to host International Archaeology Day activities at Cahal Pech Archaeological Reserve
World.content:
Institute of Archaeology to host International Archaeology Day activities at Cahal Pech Archaeological Reserve

By Zoila Palma: The Institute of Archaeology will host International Archaeology Day activities at Cahal Pech Archaeological Reserve on Friday, October 16, 2026, offering visitors an opportunity to learn more about Belize’s rich archaeological and cultural heritage.

The event will feature educational and interactive booths covering cultural heritage, education, the environment and other related topics.

Visitors will have the opportunity to explore different aspects of Belizean archaeology while engaging in activities designed to make learning about the country’s past both informative and enjoyable.

Participants will also be able to try their hand at excavation-themed archaeological activities and interact with archaeologists and researchers.

The event will also highlight the importance of protecting Belize’s cultural heritage and promoting greater appreciation for its historical significance.

World.title: BELTRAIDE offers FREE promotion for Belizean businesses in 2026 Krismus catalogue
World.content:
BELTRAIDE offers FREE promotion for Belizean businesses in 2026 Krismus catalogue

By Zoila Palma: Belizean businesses will have an opportunity to promote their products and services to customers nationwide through the 2026 Krismus Catalogue, with the Belize Trade and Investment Development Service (BELTRAIDE) inviting businesses to participate at no cost.

The initiative aims to increase the visibility of local businesses during the Christmas shopping season and encourage consumers to support Belizean products and services.

Through the catalogue, businesses can showcase their offerings to potential customers as they prepare for the holidays.

BELTRAIDE is encouraging entrepreneurs and business owners across the country to take advantage of the free promotional opportunity, which supports efforts to strengthen local enterprises and promote the “Buy Belizean” movement.

Interested businesses are required to submit their company information, one company logo and three photographs showcasing their products or services.

The deadline to register is November 13, 2026.

Businesses can complete the registration form online at https://forms.gle/gfPpUEBfVe8g1VGz9.

World.title: Belize City Cadets win National Police Youth Cadet foot drill competition
World.content:
Belize City Cadets win National Police Youth Cadet foot drill competition

By Zoila Palma: Region One, Belize City, emerged as the champion of the Belize Police Youth Cadet Corps’ 2nd National Foot Drill Competition, held on Sunday, October 11, 2026, at the Hill Top Basketball Court in Belmopan.

The event, hosted by the Belize Police Department through its National Community Oriented Policing Unit, brought together 11 cadet groups and more than 200 participants from across the country under the theme “Stepping in Unity, Marching Towards Excellence.”

The competition featured two rounds of drills, testing cadets’ ability to execute movements at the halt and in quick and slow time.

Five teams advanced to a third round, where they delivered creative displays judged on organization, coordination, confidence, readiness, creativity and innovation.

Commissioner of Police Dr. Richard Rosado, National Community Oriented Policing Unit Commander Senior Superintendent Gerald Jones, Deputy Commander for Stakeholder Engagement Superintendent Elroy Carcamo and other senior officers attended the event.

After all scores were tallied, Region One, Belize City, secured first place with 3,595 points, followed by Corozal District in second place with 3,371 points and Orange Walk District in third place with 3,323 points. Corozal District also received the award for Best Creative and Innovative Team, while Cadet Staff Sergeant Rigel Dominguez of Corozal District was named Best Commander.

The winning teams received trophies and medals in recognition of their performances.

The event also featured entertainment by the Belize Police Uprising Drum Corps, which showcased its talent following its second-place finish in the Drum Line category at the Love FM 2026 competition.

During the break, Nadia Davis, Cadet Corporal from Region Two, Belize City, won the Last Cadet Standing competition and received a trophy. Freddy Roches, a civilian from Region Three, Belize District, won the Last Police Instructor and Civilian Standing competition and received a medal.

The Belize Police Department thanked the competition’s judges, Assistant Superintendent of Police Neville Martinez, Sergeant of Police Adrian Flores and Belize Defence Force Sergeant Michael Bevans, along with the Belmopan City Council, SC Kay Flowers, the Belize Police Uprising Drum Corps and the logistics teams for their support.

World.title: China says sanctions against Francis Fonseca are a warning, assures Belizeans they can still travel to China
World.content:
China says sanctions against Francis Fonseca are a warning, assures Belizeans they can still travel to China

By Breaking Belize News Staff: China is defending its decision to sanction Belize’s Foreign Minister Francis Fonseca, describing the measures as a warning against support for Taiwanese independence, while assuring Belizeans that the restrictions will not affect other citizens wishing to travel to China.

In a written statement provided to Breaking Belize News after the newsroom sought comment on the diplomatic controversy, a spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in Jamaica defended Beijing’s actions, accusing certain politicians of allowing themselves to be used by Taiwan to advance its political interests.

The Embassy described such politicians as “chess pieces” for Taiwanese authorities seeking international support for independence and accused them of interfering in China’s internal affairs by receiving Taiwanese officials in their countries.

China maintains that Taiwan is an inseparable part of its territory and that the government in Beijing is the sole legitimate government representing China, a position rejected by Taiwan’s democratically elected government.

According to the Embassy, the sanctions were imposed under China’s Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law as an action of “warning and deterrence.”

The measures, announced on October 12, include freezing any assets Fonseca may hold in China, prohibiting Chinese organizations and individuals from conducting business with him, and barring him from entering mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau.

However, the Embassy sought to clarify to Breaking Belize News that the restrictions are directed at Fonseca personally and do not extend to ordinary Belizean citizens.
