The United States wants Poland to join the G20 “as soon as possible” and intends to raise the issue with other members of the international forum at its forthcoming summit in December in Miami, the US State Department has told the Polish Press Agency (PAP). Having previously endorsed Polish membership of the G20 in May, the US now says it intends to “continue discussions with G20 members this year on making Poland a full member as soon as possible”. “Poland’s long-term and steady economic growth, combined with its growing leadership position in the international arena, make it an ideal participant,” the State Department told PAP. Stany Zjednoczone oficjalnie zadeklarowały, że będą zabiegać o stałe członkostwo Polski w G20 https://t.co/lnZ583HIus — Fakty RMF FM (@RMF24pl) October 11, 2026 The G20, a major intergovernmental forum that brings together 19 major countries together with the European Union and the African Union, is set to meet at a golf resort owned by President Donald Trump in Miami on 14-15 December. Poland is also participating this year as a guest of the United States. PAP reports that the US has proposed that one of the points in the final declaration adopted by leaders at the conclusion of the summit refer to Poland’s permanent membership. However, this would require the assent of all current members, including Russia. The issue is likely to be discussed in a pre-summit online meeting of so-called “sherpas” negotiating the text of the declaration, reports PAP. After visiting Washington earlier this month, Marcin Przydacz, the head of President Karol Nawrocki’s international policy office, said that joining the G20 permanently is “Plan A”, but acknowledged that receiving a consensus from existing member states made this variant difficult. He added that Nawrocki would travel to London before the summit to discuss the possibility of continuing Poland’s guest status next year, when the UK will host the G20. At a meeting of G20 trade ministers last week, finance minister Andrzej Domański said that Poland has a good chance of being invited next year. Nawrocki also plans to visit G20 members Saudi Arabia and Argentina to canvass for support for Poland’s membership bid, Przydacz has confirmed. A third option would be for Poland to become a “permanent guest”, a status typically reserved for organisations like the International Monetary Fund and World Bank Group, but also held by Spain. The United States has expressed "strong support for Poland’s accession to the G20 as a permanent member" following talks in Warsaw, after which it also emphasised "strong and growing" Polish-American relations https://t.co/qTpCACnMfu — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 2, 2026 Poland has long lobbied for membership in the group. In 2010, then-President Lech Kaczyński said “the place of my country is among the members of the G20”. In 2022, following the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine, the Polish government argued that their country should replace Russia. Last December, the US invited Poland to join this year’s summit. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that Poland was “assuming its rightful place” at the forum. Poland has argued that its membership is justified by its economy being on the verge of becoming the 20th largest in the world. Though G20 membership is not decided solely on that basis, the G20 does include most of the world’s 20 largest economies (only Switzerland and the Netherlands have larger economies than Poland but no G20 membership). Polish President @NawrockiKn “does not like” the fact that Donald Trump has invited Vladimir Putin to the G20 summit in Miami, says his chief foreign policy aide. However, Nawrocki still plans to attend the event, which Poland is invited to as a guest https://t.co/JojsFB4NX6 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 26, 2026 In September, the United States provoked criticism from European leaders, including Polish foreign minister Radosław Sikorski, when it announced that Russian President Vladimir Putin would be invited to the Miami summit. Subsequently, Przydacz confirmed that, although Nawrocki, who is a close ally of Trump, “does not like” the fact that Putin has been invited, the Polish president was still planning to attend the summit. Sikorski likewise said he would attend a G20 meeting of foreign ministers in Atlanta in October even if a Russian representative was there and agreed that Poland should not boycott the summit in December. Łukasz Gibała, an independent, has won the mayoral election in Kraków, Poland’s second-biggest city, beating Monika Piątkowska, the candidate backed by Prime Minister Donald Tusk. With all votes counted by just after 1 a.m. on Monday morning, Gibała had 62.1% against 37.9% for Piątkowska, who had already conceded defeat shortly after 9 p.m. on Sunday night, when exit polls showed a large margin of victory for her opponent. Turnout was 44.3%. “Today in Poland, more and more people realise that we don’t have to live in the reality that politicians in Warsaw project upon us,” declared Gibała as it became clear he had won. “More and more people realise that we, in our own towns and cities, know better what’s good for us than they do in Warsaw.” The victory marks a blow for Tusk – whose Civic Coalition (KO) party has its strongest support in large cities – just a year before he seeks to win another term at parliamentary elections. The prime minister had visited Kraków to campaign alongside Piątkowska. Dziś 11 października 2026 roku, po 24 latach, mieszkańcy odzyskali swoje miasto. Chciałbym podziękować wszystkim Krakowianom, którzy mi zaufali i zdecydowali się oddać ma mnie głos. To nasze wspólne zwycięstwo. Dziękuję mojej partnerce Adzie, sztabowi i współpracownikom ze… pic.twitter.com/0FsNYwjPkj — Łukasz Gibała (@LukaszGibala) October 11, 2026 For Gibała, a wealthy businessman who has largely funded his own political career, this was victory at the fourth attempt, having stood in every mayoral contest since 2014, obtaining a growing share of the vote each time. He stood as an independent, promising to sort out the city’s finances, end cronyism in the appointment of municipal officials, improve public transport and reverse ticket-price increases, and hold a referendum on Kraków’s controversial clean transport zone for vehicles. He also pledged to favour residents over developers in planning decisions and to counteract the negative effects of tourism in what is Poland’s most-visited city, including by restricting short-term-rental properties. Gibała’s victory had been expected after he came top in the first round two weeks ago with 36.4% of the vote among the seven candidates who stood. Piątkowska trailed on 29.9%. The top two candidates then met in today’s run-off. Piątkowska was the joint candidate of Tusk’s centrist KO party and the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL), which are both part of the national government. She has, since last year, been a member of the Senate in Warsaw. Previously, she worked in Kraków city hall during the mayoralty of Jacek Majchrowski, who held office from 2002 to 2024. Piątkowska received the personal backing of Tusk, who announced her candidacy in June alongside PSL leader and deputy prime minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz (though critics noted that they held the event in Warsaw rather than Kraków). Tusk also visited Kraków before the first round to support his candidate. Among her campaign promises were to seek to locate an AI “gigafactory” in Kraków, to boost the availability of housing for young people, and to implement a package of policies for women, including free mammograms, pram-friendly infrastructure, free menstrual hygiene products, and safer nighttime public transport. Poland’s government has approved legislation that would allow local communities to ban short-term rentals of the type offered through services such as Airbnb. Such accommodation has boomed in recent years, often prompting a backlash from local residents https://t.co/8MRfRWTDxd — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 3, 2026 Kraków’s election was held in unusual circumstances after the previous mayor, Aleksander Miszalski, also from KO, was removed from his position in May, just two years into his term. He had faced accusations of cronyism and poor financial management, as well as criticism over the introduction of the clean transport zone. A petition to hold a recall referendum received more than the 58,355 signatures required. In the subsequent referendum, 97.3% supported removing the mayor (Miszalski had appealed to his supporters not to vote in an unsuccessful effort to keep turnout below the 27% needed for the result to be binding). Before today’s election, both Miszalski and Majchowski had called on Cracovians to vote for Piątkowska. After his victory had become clear, Gibała declared that “11 October 2026 will be remembered as the day when, after 24 years, the inhabitants of Krakow regained their city”. The vote had been particularly closely watched as it came just a year before the parliamentary elections. Gibała’s victory has been celebrated by figures from the right-wing opposition, though the new mayor is not politically aligned with them (and indeed previously served as an MP in Tusk’s party). World.title: Polish security services report alleged assassination plot against PM Tusk
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Poland’s security services say they have received “credible” information indicating a “high probability” of an assassination attempt against Prime Minister Donald Tusk and defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz. At the time of writing, no details have been released regarding where and how the alleged attacks were expected to take place, who might be behind them, or what the source of the information was. W związku z informacją, która wpłynęła do @PolskaPolicja i dotyczy możliwego zamachu na premiera @donaldtusk oraz wicepremiera, ministra obrony narodowej @KosiniakKamysz, minister koordynator służb specjalnych @TomaszSiemoniak oraz minister spraw wewnętrznych i administracji… — Jacek Dobrzyński (@JacekDobrzynski) October 11, 2026 On Sunday morning, Jacek Dobrzyński, the spokesman for the security services, first announced that the police had received “information…regarding a possible assassination attempt” on Tusk and Kosiniak-Kamysz, who, as well as serving as defence minister, is also a deputy prime minister. Dobrzyński revealed that the Internal Security Agency (ABW), police and State Protection Service (SOP), which provides security for high-ranking officials, would meet to discuss the potential threat. Speaking after that meeting, interior ministry spokeswoman Karolina Gałecka confirmed that the threat had first been identified by SOP, which passed the information on to the police. “We are taking this matter extremely seriously,” added Dobrzyński, speaking alongside her. He criticised “pseudo-experts” in the media who had expressed doubt about the announcement of a possible assassination attempt. “We’re talking about threats directed at the most important people in the country,” he added. “This information is so serious and credible that we’ve decided to share it with you now…We are talking about a high probability that these threats will be carried out.” Dobrzyński did not divulge any details about the nature of the attack or where the warnings had come from, but said that he would be able to provide further information once the police and security services had carried out further investigation. "Sprawę traktujemy śmiertelnie poważnie. Mówimy o dużym prawdopodobieństwie spełnienia tych gróźb" Rzecznik prasowy ministra koordynatora służb specjalnych o możliwym zamachu na premiera i szefa MON. pic.twitter.com/2xoWrZJT2w — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) October 11, 2026 Government spokesman Adam Szłapka, speaking to broadcaster TVN, acknowledged that the authorities constantly receive a “cascade of indications” regarding potential threats. However, “this signal was more disturbing than previous” ones, he added. Szłapka also indicated that one element of the warning had come via email, but added that “it was not just an email” that had raised concern. Like Dobrzyński, he said that further information would be released in due course. Gazeta Wyborcza, a leading daily, reports that an unnamed “official close to the prime minister” had said that the threat came from “right-wing extremists” and that the perpetrators were Poles. Another source within the intelligence services told the newspaper that the threat was treated more seriously than others because it contained information about addresses linked to Tusk and Kosiniak-Kamysz. Poland has charged a 17-year-old with planning neo-Nazi terrorist attacks on targets including a mosque and a school. Two other Polish teenagers who were part of the same online community promoting neo-Nazism and violence have also been detained https://t.co/86AnIHWFe8 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 22, 2026 Last month, police detained a 56-year-old man in the city of Przemyśl after he posted a video on social media threatening Tusk. Earlier in September, a 52-year-old man in the town of Oława was likewise arrested for making criminal threats against the prime minister online. Also in September, the security services detained three teenagers who were accused of being part of online groups promoting neo-Nazism and violence. One of them was additionally charged with planning terrorist attacks on targets including a mosque and a school. This week has also seen Poland facing an unprecedented security challenge after three knife attacks took place on schools, leaving one person dead and many injured. In response, the police have since Friday carried out checks at over 64,000 locations, including many schools, and detained over 100 people, most of them teenagers found to have made threats or been in possession of weapons. World.title: Polish prosecutors seek to drop case against South Asian men who slaughtered goat in kebab bar
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Polish prosecutors have asked a court to discontinue a case against three South Asian men who were caught illegally slaughtering a goat at the back of a kebab bar. They say that the men did not realise they were breaking the law, that such practices are normal in their home countries, and that that the meat was for their own consumption. Prosecutors therefore believe the crime was of low social harm and not worth the court’s time. 🔴Ubili kozę na zapleczu. Wkrótce decyzja sądu, zastanawia ruch prokuratury Sąd Rejonowy w Wałbrzychu w najbliższym czasie zdecyduje o losie trójki obcokrajowców, którzy pod koniec zeszłego roku niezgodnie z polskim prawem ubili kozę. Oskarżająca Hindusa i dwójkę Bengalczyków… — Wirtualna Polska (@wirtualnapolska) October 7, 2026 The case involves two Bangladeshi nationals and one Indian, all legal residents in Poland. The incident came to light in December 2025, after witnesses reported seeing the trio leading a goat through the centre of the city of Wałbrzych, before taking it to the back of a kebab bar. After killing the animal, the men began butchering it for meat, which they were still portioning out when the police arrived. They told officers that the meat was intended for their own consumption. The kebab bar was closed for renovations at the time. The men also said that such slaughter was customary in their home countries and they were unaware that, with limited exceptions, animals in Poland may generally be slaughtered only at authorised slaughterhouses, reports broadcaster RMF A spokesman for prosecutors, Mariusz Pindera, told the Wirtualna Polska news website that the men’s unfamiliarity with Polish law did not “absolve them of the obligation to comply with the regulations”. However, “the harmfulness of the act is relatively low, although I know that what these people did shocks many people”, he continued. “We must be realistic about the fact that the court proceedings will take some time, thus blocking the docket for other cases. A trial also entails costs for the state.” Prosecutors have therefore asked the court for a so-called conditional discontinuation of the case, a very common procedure under Polish law. Almost 25,000 such motions were submitted last year by prosecutors, citing the low social harm of the offences involved, reports Wirtualna Polska. The court must now decide whether to accept or reject the prosecution’s motion. In the latter case, prosecutors would be required to proceed with an indictment against the suspects and seek a conviction. No hearing date on the motion has yet been set. Indians are now the third-largest group of foreign workers in Poland, followed by Colombians, according to new data from the country’s Social Insurance Institute (ZUS). Ukrainians remain by far the largest immigrant group, followed by Belarusians https://t.co/hNiOqmeUfX — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 11, 2026 Not all cases involving illegal animal slaughter have been treated as causing low social harm. Last month, a court in the town of Limanowa convicted three men for carrying out illegal halal ritual slaughter and selling unapproved meat. The main suspect, a Polish man, was found guilty of overseeing the operation, while two Azerbaijani nationals were convicted of helping distribute the illegal meat. The verdicts can still be appealed. Although it has relatively small Muslim and Jewish populations, Poland is one of Europe’s biggest producers and exporters of kosher and halal meat. Almost a third of Poland's meat exports are halal and kosher, making it one of Europe's leading producers. Having fought off attempts by the ruling party to ban ritual slaughter, the industry is now hoping to expand further to cater to a growing market https://t.co/duOJTfHoLT — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 21, 2022 However, the country has itself been experiencing growing levels of migration in recent years. Most of the new arrivals are from neighbouring Ukraine and Belarus, but there are also growing numbers from outside Europe, too. Indians are now Poland’s third-largest immigrant group, numbering around 25,500, according to recent data from the country’s Social Insurance Institute (ZUS). Among first residence permits issued by Poland last year, Indians (9,230) and Turks (7,533) were the fourth and fifth largest recipients. Poland’s current government has blamed some immigrant groups for a rise in crime and has stepped up deportations of those found to have broken the law. However, data show that, overall, immigrants are less likely to commit crimes than Poles themselves. World.title: David Duchovny Brings New Album to Prague This Thursday
World.content:
David Duchovny, best known for his acting career, will perform in Prague on October 15, 2026, presenting songs from his upcoming album Prince of Pieces at Archa+.

Tickets are on sale through GoOut.

Duchovny has spent the past decade developing his career as a songwriter and recording artist, releasing music that combines melodic rock with introspective lyrics.

Prince of Pieces is his fourth album and brings together a small group of musicians and longtime collaborators.

The new record follows Hell or Highwater, Every Third Thought, released in 2017, and Gestureland, released in 2021. According to the album’s press release, the latest project is his most cohesive and collaborative work to date, reflecting the relationships he has built with fellow musicians over the years.

Duchovny’s music has received positive reviews from critics.

AllMusic described his sound as “eloquent, alt-rock-kissed country-folk in the vein of Wilco and the Wallflowers,” while The Boston Globe praised his voice for its “parched resonance and just a hint of rasp,” adding that he sings with feeling.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by David Duchovny (@davidduchovny)

The actor has said that the arrangements on his records are shaped by the mood and rhythm of each song, rather than following a single formula.

“The arrangements of the songs have always been in service of either the groove or the emotion,” Duchovny said. He added that he looks for sounds that complement the melody, including horns, bells and harmonies, while also experimenting with rhythms and beats.

World.title: Czech Doctors May Soon Prescribe Museum Visits to Prevent Depression
World.content:
Doctors in the Czech Republic could soon recommend museum visits, dance classes, singing and creative workshops to people at risk of depression, anxiety or social isolation.

The program, known as Art on Prescription, aims to connect healthcare providers with museums, galleries, libraries and other cultural institutions.

Rather than replacing medication or psychotherapy, these activities would complement existing treatment and help prevent mental health problems.



The National Institute of Mental Health (NUDZ) is preparing a National Platform for Prevention through Culture to bring together cultural organizations, healthcare providers, social services and schools. The goal is to make existing cultural activities more accessible to people who could benefit from them.

The initiative is not intended to turn cultural institutions into medical facilities. Instead, it seeks to use local resources to support mental well-being and strengthen social connections.

Research highlights benefits of cultural activities

International research suggests that participating in cultural and artistic activities can improve well-being, strengthen social ties and reduce symptoms of depression and anxiety.

According to Dominika Grygarová, a researcher at NUDZ, an analysis combining studies from more than 20 countries found significant reductions in symptoms of both depression and anxiety.

The benefits depend not only on exposure to art but also on active participation, Grygarová said. Creating something, learning a new skill, sharing experiences and interacting with others can help people focus on something beyond their difficulties and develop a sense of belonging.

However, the programs are intended primarily as a preventive and supportive measure, not a substitute for professional treatment. Researchers also want to assess their effectiveness and economic value, with preliminary analyses suggesting that some initiatives could be cost-effective.

Czech project looks to Northern Europe

NUDZ plans to build on similar programs already operating in several countries, particularly the United Kingdom and Northern Europe.

The Czech initiative intends to follow the so-called Baltic model, with researchers planning to work with Danish colleagues next year on a European project to introduce the approach more widely.

World.title: Who Is Petr Hlaváček? The Architect Set to Become Prague’s Next Mayor
World.content:
Petr Hlaváček is seeking to become the Czech capital’s next mayor after his political movement, STAN, won the municipal elections.

STAN received 23.16 percent of the vote, securing 17 seats in the Prague City Assembly and putting the movement in a strong position to negotiate the next governing coalition.



Hlaváček, currently deputy mayor for territorial and strategic development, has indicated that he wants to take the top job at City Hall.

His priorities include expanding housing construction, redeveloping former industrial sites and improving transport infrastructure.

A key role in Prague’s new zoning plan

Hlaváček’s main achievement as deputy mayor has been his involvement in preparing Prague’s new Metropolitan Plan, which replaced the previous zoning document from 1999 when it came into effect in September 2026.

The plan sets out where construction can take place and establishes rules for future development. It identifies capacity for up to 350,000 new homes, primarily through the redevelopment of brownfield sites.

One of the main projects is the transformation of Bubny-Zátory, an underused area expected to provide housing for around 20,000 people.

Hlaváček has also backed the Prague Development Company, which manages municipal land and aims to increase housing construction. According to him, the company could facilitate the development of up to 70,000 homes while helping prevent city-owned land from being sold off.

Transport and housing at the top of his agenda

If appointed mayor, Hlaváček wants to continue work on major transport projects, including Prague’s inner ring road and the Prague Ring Road. He also supports expanding public transport and reforming parking policy, arguing that parking in the city is often too cheap.

Before the elections, he said STAN would welcome continuing the existing coalition at City Hall but wanted a more prominent role, depending on its electoral support.

From architect to deputy mayor

Born in Zlín on July 31, 1961, Hlaváček graduated from the Faculty of Architecture at the Czech Technical University in Prague. He later established his own architectural studio, taught as a visiting professor at the University of Michigan and served as vice-dean at his alma mater.

His professional work includes the renovation of the Czech Embassy in Brasília, Brazil.

In 2015, he became director of the Prague Institute of Planning and Development. He was dismissed the following year amid criticism over delays to the Metropolitan Plan, a decision that prompted protests from institute employees.

Hlaváček entered Prague politics after the 2018 municipal elections and became first deputy mayor for territorial development and spatial planning in November 2021. He remained in the city leadership after the 2022 elections and took responsibility for territorial and strategic development in February 2023.

World.title: Sinatra Tribute Pairs Frank Sinatra Classics With 1930s Dining at Prague’s Mánes
World.content:
Prague’s Art Restaurant Mánes combines live performances of Frank Sinatra’s best-known songs with a three-course dinner inspired by traditional Czech cuisine of the 1930s.

The functionalist building offers views of the Vltava River and nearby Žofín Island, providing the setting for an evening dedicated to the music and style of Sinatra’s era.



The Sinatra’s Tribute musical programme features acclaimed soloists, including baritone Daniel Klánský and jazz singer Sophie Lamoš. They perform some of Sinatra’s best-known songs, including *My Way* and *Fly Me to the Moon*, accompanied by a group of musicians.

Rather than simply imitating the legendary American singer, the Sinatra Tribute offers its own interpretation of his musical legacy.

One of the programme’s highlights is a restored 1897 Steinway & Sons grand piano, an instrument once played by Czech composer and pianist Jaroslav Ježek.

The music is complemented by a three-course dinner served before the concert.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sinatra Tribute Koncert & Večeře / Sinatra Tribute Show & Dinner (@sinatratributeprague)

Created exclusively for the programme by Mánes Restaurant head chef Jaroslav Zahálka, the menu draws inspiration from Prague’s culinary traditions of the 1930s, reflecting the period associated with the evening’s musical theme.

Visitors can contact the venue for current dates, ticket prices and reservations.

World.title: From Lisbon to Hanoi, New Flight Options From Prague This Autumn
World.content:
The autumn school break is approaching, and travelers departing from Prague still have options for trips abroad.

However, those hoping to find cheap flights may struggle to secure a good deal, as fares tend to rise closer to departure and fewer seats remain available at lower prices.

Families face an additional challenge. When booking four tickets together, they may discover that the cheapest fare is available for only one or two passengers, forcing them to pay more for the remaining seats.



Airlines are also dealing with high fuel costs and strong competition, making it important to fill as many seats as possible.

A search conducted on Wednesday, October 7, found that Kraków and Gdańsk were among the cheapest destinations available for the autumn break week.

New flights from Prague and postponed routes

Prague Airport has announced several new connections for the autumn and winter seasons, although some airlines have postponed their planned launches until spring.

Smartwings, for example, has delayed the introduction of flights to Venice, Italy, and Bergen, Norway. Both routes were originally scheduled to begin before the autumn break but are now expected to launch in March.

Despite the changes, Prague Airport continues to list the destinations among its new routes, with their original launch dates still displayed. According to the current schedule, Smartwings’ next new connection is to Lisbon, with flights due to begin on October 23.

Travelers heading farther afield have another option. Vietjet Air launched its Prague–Hanoi service on Saturday, October 10. The route includes a stopover in Kazakhstan, rather than offering a nonstop connection to Vietnam.

Closer to home, easyJet’s new route from Prague to Hamburg provides another option for the break. Return fares were available for around CZK 4,000.

Marrakech joins the network as winter routes target skiers

EasyJet is also scheduled to launch flights from Prague to Marrakech, Morocco, on October 25. The new connection will increase competition on the route, although fares during the autumn break are relatively high.

A return ticket can cost as much as CZK 16,000, excluding baggage. Prices can be considerably lower outside the peak travel period.

Wizz Air is adding flights to Poprad, Slovakia, while Sky Alps is expected to begin services to Bolzano, Italy, in early December. Both destinations provide access to mountain regions popular with winter sports enthusiasts.

Another seasonal option is Eurowings’ planned route to Rovaniemi, Finland, which is scheduled to launch on December 20. Located on the Arctic Circle, the city is closely associated with Santa Claus and attracts visitors during the Christmas season.

World.title: RestaurantWeek Prague Returns With 75 Restaurants and Autumn Menus
World.content:
RestaurantWeek® returns to Prague from October 13 to November 18, offering diners the chance to try menus at around 75 restaurants across the capital at reduced prices.

The three-course menus available for CZK 490 or CZK 790, plus a reservation fee.



The autumn edition features a mix of established Prague restaurants and newcomers to the festival. Among the first-time participants are U Malířů 1543 in Malá Strana and Buddha-Bar Prague, both well-known names on the city’s dining scene.

Participating restaurants are incorporating seasonal ingredients into their menus, including pumpkin, game, poultry, forest fruits, plums and quince. Truffles and shrimp are also expected to feature prominently.

Pumpkin will appear in dishes ranging from soups to mousses, while restaurants focusing on seafood and creative interpretations of Czech ingredients will offer alternatives for diners looking to explore different flavours.

The festival aims to make restaurants more accessible while encouraging people to dine out and meet in person. This year’s edition includes a partnership with Singles Club, an initiative promoting face-to-face social connections as an alternative to app-based dating.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Singles Club (@singlesclubcz)

Connecting Prague restaurants with local producers

RestaurantWeek® is also collaborating with the Regional Food (Regionální potravina) project, which supports small Czech food producers. The partnership aims to connect restaurants with local suppliers and help regional products reach more customers.

For the first time, the festival will also recognise restaurants that work with regional ingredients, adding a new category to its traditional awards for popular and highly rated establishments.

Three-course menus cost CZK 490 or CZK 790, depending on the restaurant, with reservation fees of CZK 49 or CZK 79, respectively. Some venues offer a fourth course, an amuse-bouche, and are marked as premium on the festival website.

World.title: Prague’s SaSaZu Club to Host Central Europe’s Largest Halloween Party
World.content:
Bloody Sexy Halloween festival, described as Central Europe’s largest Halloween event, will return to Prague’s SaSaZu Club for its 2026 edition.

The two-night celebration will take place on Friday, October 30, and Saturday, October 31, promising an extensive lineup of shows, performances, and music acts.



Founded in 2009, the event has grown into one of the most attended Halloween parties in the region, regularly attracting more than 4,000 visitors each year. Organizers say this year’s edition will feature immersive decorations, live performances, and sets from both Czech and international DJs.

A traditional highlight of the weekend will be the Bloody Sexy Costume Contest, open to all attendees.

Participants can register at SaSaZu between 9 p.m. and midnight, with costumes judged on creativity, originality, and presentation. The winner, selected by audience applause at midnight, will receive a cash prize of CZK 40,000.

The event will run across both nights with multiple performances and themed productions throughout the venue.

Tickets for Bloody Sexy Halloween 2025 are priced between CZK 510 and CZK 1,450, depending on the category (Regular, Badass Babes, or VIP).

World.title: The Story Society Is Bringing an English-Language Book Community to Prague
World.content:
Meet Julia and Ioana, the founders behind The Story Society, a new English-language bookstore and community project in Prague.

Their idea combines a selection of books with a space for reading, book clubs, events and meeting other people.

The project is still in development, with the founders currently looking for a location and working towards opening the bookstore in early 2027.

Why a bookstore?

For Julia, the idea started from a personal need. “I wanted to create a place where introverted people like myself could spend time comfortably, discover books at their own pace and potentially meet others with similar interests,” she says.

But there was also a practical reason behind the idea. According to the founders, finding a wider selection of English-language books in Prague can be difficult, particularly when it comes to special editions. Ordering books from abroad can also mean higher shipping costs, taxes and waiting several weeks for delivery.

“I wanted to solve two problems. One is community, and the other one is buying books in English here,” Julia says.

The Story Society plans to source books from the UK and offer a selection that the founders feel is currently difficult to find locally.

What they hope The Story Society to be

The Story Society is intended to be more than a place to buy books, although the physical bookstore remains an important part of the idea. Julia and Ioana imagine a colorful, cozy space with areas for reading, book clubs and other events.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by The Story Society (@thestorysociety.prague)

They are also considering collaborations with authors and artists, pop-ups and other activities connected to books and the community around them. “We want to make a third place in Prague,” Ioana says.

The idea is that people could come not only to buy a book, but also to stay for a while, read, meet friends or take part in an event.

The expat/local divide

The Story Society was initially imagined largely with Prague’s expat community in mind. But “when the project took shape, we got a huge response from locals, and we learned that they are also interested in it,” Julia says. The attraction is the chance to have an English-language space where they can read books, meet people and be part of a bookish community.

That response has broadened the founders’ idea of who The Story Society is for. Rather than separating Prague’s expat and local communities, they hope the project can help mend the gap between them.

“If you like English, if you can speak English, and if you like books, we don’t care where you’re from,” Julia says. “Just be there and enjoy it with us.”

Where the project stands now

The Story Society doesn’t have a physical location yet. Julia and Ioana are currently exploring the market and looking for a suitable space in Prague’s city centre, while also working on the book supply and other practical foundations of the project.

In the meantime, they plan to take The Story Society to pop-ups and other events. These will give them an opportunity to introduce the project to more people, build a community around it and raise visibility for their crowdfunding campaign.

Everyone can help

For now, support can take different forms. Sharing the crowdfunding campaign, introducing the project to someone who might be interested or simply helping spread the word can help The Story Society reach more people as Julia and Ioana work towards opening their first space.

They also want people to feel that contributing does not necessarily mean making a financial donation. Ideas, feedback and suggestions can help shape the project as it develops. As the founders put it, “any thought counts.”

World.title: New 120-room hotel coming to Hungary’s second-largest city: opening date revealed!
World.content:
International hotel group IHG Hotels & Resorts is bringing its Holiday Inn Express & Suites brand to Debrecen, with a new 120-room hotel scheduled to open in 2029. The project, developed in partnership with Hungarian property group Xanga, will be the chain’s first hotel in eastern Hungary.

A new internationally branded hotel is planned for Debrecen, Hungary’s second-largest city, as the eastern Hungarian economic hub continues to attract major investments and business travellers.

IHG Hotels & Resorts has signed an agreement with the Debrecen-based Xanga Group to develop a 120-room Holiday Inn Express & Suites hotel. The property is expected to open in 2029 and will strengthen IHG’s presence outside Budapest.

The project forms part of a wider mixed-use development that will include residential apartments, offices and retail units, reflecting the city’s ongoing expansion.

Where will the new Holiday Inn hotel be built?

According to Turizmus.com, the hotel will be located approximately one kilometre from Debrecen city centre, making it accessible to visitors travelling for both business and leisure.

Designed around the hotel brand’s Next Generation concept, the property will feature 100 modern standard guest rooms and 20 suites. Guests will also have access to complimentary hot breakfast, free Wi-Fi and the brand’s Express Café & Bar facilities.

The combination of standard rooms and larger suites is intended to cater to different types of visitors, including business travellers staying in the city for investment-related projects and tourists exploring eastern Hungary.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Why is Debrecen attracting more hotels?

Debrecen has emerged as one of Hungary’s most important industrial and investment destinations in recent years. Major domestic and international investments, infrastructure improvements and expanding air connections have helped increase demand for accommodation.

The city is a key economic centre for eastern Hungary, and its rapid development has created a growing need for modern hotels operated by recognised international brands.

Willemijn Geels, IHG Hotels & Resorts’ vice-president of development for Europe, said the company was pleased to bring Holiday Inn Express & Suites to Debrecen. She described the city as one of Central Europe’s most dynamically developing urban centres and highlighted the hotel as IHG’s first project in eastern Hungary.

Geels added that the agreement reflected the company’s ambition to expand beyond Budapest and meet growing demand for quality international hotel brands in rapidly developing regional cities.

She also welcomed the partnership with Xanga, describing it as the two companies’ first joint project and expressing hope for a long-term, successful collaboration.

If you missed it: Two Budapest hotels named among Europe’s favourites by Condé Nast Traveler readers

IHG expands its Hungarian hotel portfolio

The planned Debrecen property will be IHG’s second hotel development outside Budapest in Hungary. Holiday Inn Express is the company’s fastest-growing brand, and the new hotel will become its 57th European property offering suites alongside standard rooms.

IHG currently has five operating hotels in Hungary, with another three in preparation.

The Debrecen development is part of the group’s wider strategy to expand in regional cities across Hungary and Central and Eastern Europe, where economic growth is creating new opportunities for internationally recognised accommodation providers.

World.title: Budapest residents say they fear walking certain streets: anger over crime grows
World.content:
Residents of Budapest’s inner districts say some streets have become places they avoid even during the day, while others feel unsafe after dark. Protesters are demanding hundreds of additional police officers, permanent patrols and tougher measures against drug dealing and public disorder at a demonstration in Józsefváros on Wednesday.

Residents concerned about rising theft, break-ins and open drug use are taking to the streets in central Budapest on Wednesday, 14 October. The demonstration is scheduled to begin at 5 pm in Horváth Mihály Square, in the city’s eighth district, Józsefváros.

According to Hungarian news outlet Reakció, the organisers believe several public areas in Budapest’s inner districts have effectively become “no-go zones”, where drug dealing, drug consumption and harassment of passers-by are recurring problems.

They claim that many residents no longer feel safe walking alone after dark, while some avoid certain streets even during the day. The protesters argue that these concerns extend beyond Józsefváros and affect several inner districts of the Hungarian capital.

Residents demand action over drugs and street crime

The demonstration brings together local residents, legal experts, community organisers and a district councillor, all of whom are expected to address different aspects of the problem.

Marcell Erős, an IT specialist and one of the petition’s authors, is due to speak about conditions in his own neighbourhood. According to the organisers, he regularly encounters reports of break-ins, drug use and drug dealing, as well as what he considers unsuccessful attempts to resolve the problems through discussions with the authorities.

Criminal lawyer, legal expert and university lecturer Dániel Tran will discuss the legal obstacles that can complicate prompt police intervention and the gathering of evidence. Bella Szűcs-Zágoni, founder of the Safe Újlipótváros Facebook group, will share experiences from community efforts to improve safety in Budapest’s 13th district.

Józsefváros councillor Aram Shakkour is also expected to speak about local public safety concerns, residents’ complaints and the social problems connected to policing and street disorder. The organisers say their aim is not simply to assign blame, but to develop solutions that could improve safety in central Budapest regardless of political affiliation.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official WhatsApp channel!

Petition calls for at least 500 additional police officers

The protesters intend to submit a petition to the Ministry of the Interior setting out a series of demands. One of their central requests is to increase staffing at police headquarters serving Budapest’s fifth to ninth districts by at least 500 officers. They are also calling for a general pay rise for law enforcement personnel.

The petition demands a permanent police presence at several locations that the organisers consider particularly problematic, including Blaha Lujza Square, Nyugati Square, Oktogon, Rákóczi Square and Pope John Paul II Square.

They also want foot patrols throughout the inner districts, including at night, and tougher police action against people who sell or use illegal drugs in central Budapest.

Another proposal is to prohibit the sale of glass pipes, which can be used to consume certain drugs, including synthetic substances commonly referred to as crystal. The full list of demands includes:

Higher pay for law enforcement personnel across the board.

across the board. Permanent police patrols at key locations in central Budapest, including Blaha Lujza Square, Nyugati Square, Oktogon, Rákóczi Square and Pope John Paul II Square.

Clarifying trespassing laws so that unauthorised entry into the communal areas of apartment buildings can be punished even if no material damage is caused.

A review of short-term rental regulations, including more effective financial accountability for landlords when short-term accommodation arrangements compromise the security of apartment buildings.

The proposals range from increased police resources and changes to criminal law to local government powers and the regulation of short-term accommodation.
