World.title: Foreign ministry: The state cannot directly control Silmet's business decisions
World.content:
Although the Ministry of Foreign Affairs says it has pressured Silmet to stop using Russian raw materials, the company has yet to do so.

Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) said the ministry has pressured chemical and metallurgical manufacturer Silmet to stop using Russian raw materials. The minister has now promised to set a deadline for the company to end its use of Russian raw materials. Tsahkna believes the company could stop using Russian raw materials as early as the beginning of next year.

ERR asked the Ministry of Foreign Affairs what specific pressure it had exerted, why the company had not complied and whether the ministry or the minister bears responsibility for the fact that, in the fifth year of the war in Ukraine, an Estonian company continues to purchase raw materials from Russia.

In its response, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs noted that the company's dependence on Russian raw materials has been publicly known for a long time. According to the ministry, Estonian media were reporting on the issue as early as 1995.

"However, dependence on Russian raw materials is not only a business risk but also a strategic vulnerability that Russia could exploit for its own benefit. It is therefore important to eliminate this dependence as quickly as possible," the ministry emphasized.

The ministry said it maintains regular contact with Estonian companies, including Silmet, stressing the need to find alternatives to Russian raw materials and end dependence on them.

"Silmet is a privately owned, publicly traded company that belongs to an international group based in Canada. The state cannot directly influence the company's business decisions or continuously monitor the details of its operations. Nor can the state independently assess when and to what extent the company has worked to identify alternative sources of raw materials," the ministry said.

At the same time, the ministry emphasized that it has consistently worked to support Silmet in identifying and establishing supply channels for raw materials from outside Russia. "To this end, we have, among other things, cooperated with the European Commission, which is responsible for the European Union's common trade policy."

According to the ministry, an important step in this direction was taken on October 9 when the European Commission selected Silmet's development project, Silmet 2.0, as one of 46 new EU strategic projects. The project aims to modernize the plant's production capabilities, enable the use of alternative raw material sources and reduce European industry's dependence on Russia.

The ministry noted that strategic project status will put Silmet in a better position to carry out its development plans and reduce its dependence on Russian raw materials.

According to the ministry's information, potentially suitable sources of raw materials for Silmet can be found in Latin America, Asia and Africa. The company itself is best placed to assess the technical suitability of specific raw material sources, taking into account the particular requirements of its production processes and technology.

"Silmet itself should explain to the public as soon as possible how it intends to end its dependence on Russian raw materials," the ministry emphasized.

The ministry also noted that growing international competition is making it more difficult to find alternative supply channels. Major industrialized countries are actively competing for limited raw material resources, affecting both their availability and supply opportunities.

"Estonia's goal remains to support Silmet's efforts to diversify its raw material supplies and reduce its dependence on Russian raw materials. Achieving this goal will require investment and technological changes by the company itself, as well as cooperation at the European Union level to improve access to alternative supply channels and strengthen Europe's security of supply for strategic raw materials," the ministry said.

ERR News reported on Thursday that a Russian company supplying rare earths to Estonia's Silmet was removed from the European Union's proposed 22nd sanctions package at Estonia's request.

World.title: Over 70 unexploded aerial bombs uncovered in Jõgeva nature reserve
World.content:
Dozens of Soviet-era aerial bombs, many of them live, have been excavated and safely disposed of in Jõgeva County, Maaleht reported .

The safety work was planned and covered a known danger zone at a former Soviet military facility.

On the penultimate weekend of September, Rescue Board and Defense League bomb disposal teams removed dozens of explosives from the former Utsali training ground in Jõgeva County.

They recovered more than 70 items from the area over the three days, including explosive devices and their components.

Most of the finds were aerial bombs, including both training and live versions.

The site was selected because the Soviet Air Force had once used it extensively for bombing exercises. Bomb disposal specialists had previously been called to the area, so it was a known danger zone.

Over 30 bomb disposal specialists and assistant specialists, along with more than 50 members of the Estonian Defense League and other support personnel, took part in the search operation.

Hazardous items were transported to a demolition site.

Marti Mereäär, head of the Southern Estonia bomb disposal unit, noted that explosive devices can remain dangerous for many years, and under no circumstances should they be handled. Members of the public should call 112 in such cases.

This is even the case with items of war memorabilia in the home, if there is reason to fear they are explosives. "Calling out bomb disposal specialists is free of charge, and there is no penalty for reporting an artillery shell found at home," Mereäär added.

What should you do if you find suspected explosives?

Under no circumstances should you touch the object

Move to a safe distance immediately

After moving a safe distance away, call the emergency number 112 as soon as you can

Note the location of the found object

World.title: Estonian court convicts gas station clerk who stole 67,000 liters of fuel
World.content:
A court has convicted a former Olerex employee who, according to the charges, stole a total of 67,000 liters of diesel fuel from storage tanks while working at a gas station in Jüri.

The Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs announced last week that a court had recently ruled on a case involving the theft of nearly 67,000 liters of diesel fuel from a gas station in dozens of separate incidents.

Toomas Tomberg, a prosecutor with the Northern District Prosecutor's Office who handled the case, told ERR that the thefts took place at the Olerex gas station in Jüri.

Prosecutors accused Igor Sorokin of using his access to the gas station's systems while working as a customer service representative to repeatedly steal diesel fuel from a storage tank.

According to the charges, he committed a total of 51 thefts between December 9, 2022, and January 25, 2024. To conceal the thefts, he switched off the gas station's video surveillance system before pumping diesel fuel into tanks installed in a vehicle he was using. Prosecutors accused him of stealing nearly 67,000 liters of diesel fuel worth almost €108,600.

The court found Sorokin guilty of large-scale, systematic theft and sentenced him to two years and six months in prison, suspended for a three-year probationary period. He was also ordered to compensate Olerex for €108,589 in financial losses. The ruling has not yet entered into force.

"The court proceedings confirmed that this was not an isolated act but a series of systematic thefts committed over an extended period. Although the defendant was caught in the act during one incident in January 2024, work schedules, video surveillance logs, storage tank records, witness testimony and other evidence gathered allowed the court to find that the remaining incidents described in the charges had also been proven," Tomberg said.

He added that the court agreed with prosecutors that the evidence formed a coherent and reliable body of proof establishing the defendant's actions throughout the period covered by the charges.

According to Tomberg, the case is notable both for the amount of fuel stolen and the length of time over which the thefts took place.

"It also demonstrates that prolonged, concealed activity causing financial losses to a company can be proven even when direct evidence relates to only part of the criminal activity, while the remaining incidents are established through a body of mutually corroborating circumstantial evidence," he said.

Recurring fuel theft on the rise

According to statistics from the Ministry of Justice and Digital Affairs, more than 2,000 fuel thefts have been recorded so far this year, nearly 50 percent more than a year ago.

The ministry noted that this does not necessarily mean people across Estonia have suddenly become twice as inclined to steal. Rather, the statistics suggest that thieves have become more systematic in their activities and that some incidents are being classified as criminal offenses because of their repeated nature.

A single theft may constitute a misdemeanor, but when someone repeatedly and knowingly engages in the same behavior, it becomes a criminal offense.

Fuel thefts are largely responsible for the more than 6 percent year-on-year increase in property crimes, the ministry said.

World.title: PPA: Migrants more visible in Tallinn's Nõmme, not more numerous
World.content:
The latest group of illegal migrants apprehended in Tallinn's Nõmme district does not mean that neighborhood has seen more cases than other parts of the city, authorities say.

The Police and Border Guard Board has detained two groups of illegal migrants in recent months, most recently on Sunday evening.

Overall, the PPA has detained 83 migrant groups in Estonia since mid-summer, and 352 individual illegal migrants since July 21, amid heightened migratory pressure on the Belarus-EU border.

In both reported cases in Nõmme, the PPA acted on neighbor tip-offs, as well as in other cases close to the nearby Tallinn University of Technology.

Rainis Sinikas, head of the PPA North Prefecture's border and migration supervision department, noted that the detained migrants are spread across different districts. It is largely Nõmme's character, he said, that makes detentions more likely for those accommodated there.

As a leafy suburb on the southern outskirts of the capital, Nõmme is a place where local residents tend to recognize each other by sight, Sinikas said. Outsiders, still more so those of a different ethnic background from the majority, tend to stand out more than they might in more central areas of Tallinn.

"The point of detention is largely connected to where migrants live. Through a trafficker, they find accommodation somewhere in a Tallinn district. Since Nõmme is a small garden suburb where many neighbors know each other, a number of people of another nationality attracts attention," Sinikas said.

"In the city center, people moving around during rush hour may not be noticed. But in a small garden suburb, far more attention is paid to who is moving around, and so more reports come in," he continued.

Sunday evening's operation in Nõmme began when residents reported what they said were two dark-skinned men outside a building. The men appeared not to be familiar with the area.

PPA officials went to the scene and detained both men. Checks revealed they were Sudanese nationals staying in Estonia illegally. During conversations, it emerged that several other illegal migrants were hiding in the area. Police then launched a search involving patrols, service dogs and the Rescue Board.

This led to eight additional men, also of Sudanese origin, being apprehended. They had been hiding in wooded areas.

"Generally the practice has been that running away and abandoning belongings doesn't happen very often, but this time it did," Sinikas said.

In the July case, it emerged that migrants had congregated at a short-term rental building. The PPA is still establishing the circumstances of Sunday's incident.

"In practically every case we establish whether they have already stayed overnight in Estonia. If they have, we check the accommodation or apartment used as short-term let. We also establish their route in detail: how many came in and where they came from. Through continuous and consistent procedural steps, we establish their background and whether we can apprehend more migrants at that address. Practice has shown that sometimes we do," Sinikas added.

October has so far seen no let-up for the PPA in detaining migrant groups, mainly in Tallinn but also in Pärnu and central Estonia.

On Monday, the PPA detained a group of seven illegal migrants in the city center. Migratory pressure is likely to continue and possibly rise ahead of winter, the PPA said.

The PPA says it receives constant tip-offs about possible illegal migrants. Sinikas denied that tip-offs had been primarily race-based. Actions and behavior stand out, he said — and even dirty clothing in the autumn weather.

"Since the weather is muddy, many of the detained groups get muddy too," Sinikas said.

Not only the PPA but other agencies are coming under heavy pressure. Over 250 people are now in the Tallinn detention center. The courts are overworked too, since detaining people is a legal process, on top of sentencing human traffickers caught in Estonia.

"The situation is difficult and could turn into a crisis situation. Various institutions, including administrative courts and local governments, are overloaded. We order interpretation and our entire network of cooperation partners is under great strain," Sinikas said.

The situation is complicated by the fact that different nationalities are placed in the detention center together, which has led to conflicts.

"It doesn't take much — there have been disagreements and pushing, even over a TV remote. So far we have managed to prevent and avert larger conflicts, but there are still such scuffles and quarrels," Sinikas said.

Sunday's group consisted of Sudanese nationals. The group apprehended Monday in central Tallinn were Somalis. "There are a lot of Bangladeshi, but also Pakistani and Afghan citizens. The circle is quite wide, and people from Ethiopia and Eritrea have also been detained," Sinikas said.

Regardless of country of origin, the migrants mostly arrive in Estonia from Belarus via Latvia, which it borders. They then make their way northwards.

Processing the return of one migrant usually takes over a month, including establishing that they did indeed cross the border illegally from another state. Estonia has so far sent 105 migrants back to Latvia.

The migrants themselves have said during proceedings that their intended destination was a western EU country, for instance Finland, Germany or Spain.

Sinikas said that while some have stated a desire to remain in Estonia, it is not clear whether this is their genuine wish or a script they have been taught.

That "also has to be established during proceedings," Sinikas noted.

Interior Minister Igor Taro (Eesti 200) discussed the Belarus-backed migration pressure on Latvia's border with his Polish counterpart Marcin Kierwiński at the ongoing Warsaw Security Forum. Taro said the migratory pressure should be treated as an attack on the whole EU, and that escalation must carry a cost beyond the existing sanctions on Minsk.

"All our allies are ready to support Latvia, just as we have previously stood alongside Poland and Lithuania. Responsibility lies entirely with the Belarusian regime, which supports and incites illegal border crossings and contributes to damage to Latvia's border infrastructure," Taro said.

Taro is set to take part in a panel discussion on Tuesday about government resilience in the era of hybrid attacks.

World.title: Despite Rail Baltica delay, Tallinn's Ülemiste terminal on track for 2028
World.content:
The new Ülemiste passenger terminal in Tallinn is still due to open in late 2028, despite Rail Baltica's completion being pushed back to 2034.

Although Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania agreed to complete Rail Baltica by 2034, making maximum use of the next EU budget period, construction already underway will continue, Infrastructure Minister Kuldar Leis (Reform) said last week.

Work on the main building and outdoor areas at Ülemiste Linda Terminal is progressing as planned, Rail Baltic Estonia communications chief Silvia Pärmann told ERR.

One platform is already in use by passenger rail operator Elron, she noted, and trains to Tartu and Narva will continue serving the terminal via the existing railway ahead of its full completion in late 2028.

"Even before Rail Baltica is completed, the terminal will bring together trams, connecting passengers to destinations including the airport and port, as well as buses and domestic rail connections," Pärmann said.

Render of Tallinn's future Ülemiste Terminal. Source: Rail Baltic Estonia

The structure's concrete frame is due to be completed by the end of this year, making its overall scale and architectural design more clearly visible, she added.

Tallinn's Rail Baltica terminal was designed by Zaha Hadid Architects.

Major urban center plans

This February, Rail Baltic Estonia, Tallinn Airport and Mainor Ülemiste also unveiled plans to develop the area into a new urban center, with nearly €500 million in combined investments over the coming years.

Projects include a new high-rise with a conference center and a European-themed park, while Tallinn Airport also pursues its own more than €66 million expansion project.

The city has also proposed building a 10,000-seat multifunctional arena in Ülemiste.

World.title: Experts: Full damage of Germany's August Hanning scandal yet to be revealed
World.content:
Former German foreign intelligence chief August Hanning's detention on suspicion of espionage has raised concerns about damage to Germany's national security and the credibility of its intelligence services, Estonian experts find.

Last week, police searched the home of August Hanning, the former head of Germany's foreign intelligence service, in Nordwalde, western Germany, near the Dutch border. Hanning was detained on suspicion of espionage amounting to treason.

The allegations concern a period after Hanning had stepped down as head of the foreign intelligence service and begun providing consulting services. It emerged that he had enlisted the help of his former chief of staff, Manfred Dankesreiter, who was still working for the foreign intelligence service.

"Specifically, it is alleged that Mr. Hanning received nearly 2,000 documents from Manfred D. up until June 2022, some of which were confidential, meaning they were intended exclusively for use by the leadership of the foreign intelligence service. In one case, Mr. Hanning is suspected of using classified information to prepare an analysis for an employee of a foreign intelligence service. In another case, he is alleged to have passed information to an employee of another intelligence service following an extensive exchange of information," said German prosecutor's office spokesperson Ines Peterson.

Prosecutors have not specified which two countries' intelligence services were involved. German media have speculated about China and Azerbaijan, while Hanning's previous ties to Russia have also been highlighted. The leaked materials reportedly included primarily security assessments and documents concerning matters such as Iran's nuclear program and an analysis of the Russian armed forces.

"I think the extent of the damage is impossible to comprehend at this stage. The fragments that have appeared in the media do not allow us to properly assess its scale, partly because it is unclear which country Hanning was working for. Russia, China and Azerbaijan have all been mentioned. The timing is also important — whether he was recruited while he was still in office or after he left. When all this could have happened is extremely significant," said Arnold Sinisalu, former director general of the Estonian Internal Security Service (ISS/KAPO).

The precise extent of the damage remains to be determined. Germany's foreign intelligence service is a large organization, but its powers have so far been relatively limited. It is therefore possible that the information leaked was not particularly sensitive. However, other countries' secrets are also at stake and the overall reputational damage is enormous.

"The damage to the foreign intelligence service, the BND, is enormous. That is simply because a betrayal of this kind causes long-term damage to the BND's credibility, particularly among the intelligence partners on which it relies," said ARD journalist Michael Götschenberg.

"The other aspect is the purely symbolic damage that has been done. This affects not only Germany's intelligence service but German state institutions more broadly. How can these institutions be trusted if the head of an intelligence service has engaged in secret cooperation? At the same time, it must be emphasized that the very fact that something like this was uncovered is extremely positive," Sinisalu said.

"The Germans used to be very self-assured and believed they understood how Russia and China operated far better than we did and so on. History has made its own corrections. Perhaps this is partly a consequence of overconfidence and a sense of infallibility. I hope the substance of the case is not too serious. We will see. At present, too little is known," said Eerik-Niiles Kross, member of the Riigikogu Foreign Affairs Committee.

Hanning headed Germany's foreign intelligence service from 1998 to 2005, more than 20 years ago when Gerhard Schröder was German chancellor. Prosecutors say his alleged espionage activities took place between 2010 and 2022. How far has today's Germany moved on from that era?

"Germany is undergoing enormous change, with different forces pulling it in different directions. We are all concerned that the AfD, a far-right party that is at times openly pro-Putin, is the most popular political force. It has won some local elections. Whether that means a major shift at the next German Bundestag elections is too early to say, but the political atmosphere there is somewhat turbulent. The major established parties are doing rather poorly. At the same time, Germany is trying to move away from its highly restrained post-World War II approach. On the military front, the Germans have spent decades trying to prove to the world that they have learned from their mistakes. They have, of course, started making different kinds of mistakes, as tends to happen. Where Germany is headed is now one of the key questions for Europe's future," Kross said.

Germany is currently debating whether to grant its foreign intelligence service greater powers. Footage from last week also illustrates the contrast between the present and the past. In one clip, the current head of Germany's foreign intelligence service warns of the threats facing the country.

"Germany is at risk of being drawn into a violent conflict by Russia. The attempted attack in Leipzig is one example of this. No other country currently poses such a direct, extensive and concrete threat to Germany," said Martin Jäger, head of Germany's foreign intelligence service.

Meanwhile, former Chancellor Gerhard Schröder celebrates Russian President Vladimir Putin's birthday and visits a store belonging to a Russian retail chain on whose supervisory board he now serves.

World.title: Iraq changes bank card limitations for use overseas
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) has directed financial institutions to implement a monthly transaction limit for bank cards and to establish a maximum daily limit for purchases made at points of sale outside of Iraq.

According to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the CBI underlined that the decision relates to point-of-sale transactions made outside Iraq, notably those that require the actual presence of the card with the merchant.

Holders of bank cards may use them for point-of-sale purchases outside Iraq up to a daily limit equivalent to $3,333 (or five million Iraqi dinars), provided that total monthly transactions do not exceed five million Iraqi dinars.

The measure replaces the previous daily limit of $333.3 (equivalent to 500,000 Iraqi dinars) specifically for this type of transaction.

The CBI emphasized that electronic payment cards operate based on the officially approved exchange rate to meet the needs of Iraqi citizens abroad.

Last week, Iraq has officially depreciated its national currency, with the baseline dropping from about 1,300 Iraqi dinars to 1,500 dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet approved the structural adjustment, which marks a 14.5 percent decline compared to the previous official framework that had been in place since early 2023.

The forceful monetary policy shift acts as a direct fiscal stabilization mechanism in response to significant macroeconomic shocks.

World.title: Linde supplies 20 explosion-proof forklifts to Iraq’s Ministry of Oil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Ministry of Oil is preparing to introduce a fleet of 20 German-manufactured forklifts equipped with specialised explosion-protection systems for use in the country’s oil and gas industry, according to Plant & Equipment.

Linde Material Handling provided the H50/600D diesel-powered forklifts, each of which has a maximum lifting capability of five tons.

The forklifts are being modified in Italy before being sent to Iraq.

Miretti, an Italian industrial safety expert, has been tasked with modifying the equipment for use in places where combustible compounds pose heightened safety threats.

The forklifts are being modified to meet ATEX 2GD requirements, which encompass industrial situations defined as Zone 1 (possibly explosive gas atmospheres) and Zone 21 (combustible dust).

The upgrades include increased protection for essential components as well as changes to the cars’ operating systems to lessen the chance of sparks, excessive heat, and other ignition dangers.

Such precautions are especially crucial in oil and gas operations, where equipment must fulfill stringent safety standards while working near potentially combustible chemicals.

The delivery package also includes spare parts to facilitate service and maintenance once the forklifts are operational.

Plant & Equipment mentioned that production and safety modifications are still in place, with the equipment being prepped for deployment in Iraq’s petroleum industry.

The procurement is planned to provide the Ministry of Oil with more material-handling capability appropriate for hazardous industrial sites.

World.title: Iraq seeks enhanced cooperation with Algeria in gas sector
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is working to enhance its collaboration with Algeria in the natural gas sector as part of its strategy to better utilize its natural resources, particularly associated gas, to maximize economic benefits and minimize waste.

Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair discussed on Monday cooperation opportunities in the hydrocarbons sector with Algerian Minister of Hydrocarbons and Mines Mohamed Arkab.

The meeting took place on the sidelines of the WPC Energy Congress held in the Saudi capital, Riyadh.

The discussions focused on leveraging Algerian expertise in the recovering, processing, and utilizing associated gas, as well as developing investment partnerships between oil companies in both countries.

The step takes place as Iraq carries out projects aimed at boosting domestic gas production, reducing gas flaring, and securing additional fuel supplies for power plants.

Developing capabilities for associated gas recovery and processing was a key focus of the Iraqi-Algerian talks, reflecting Baghdad’s interest in maximizing the use of available gas resources.

Both sides emphasized the importance of leveraging Algerian expertise in this field to help improve the utilization of associated gas and increase the value added to hydrocarbon resources.

Baghdad faces challenges related to the flaring of gas associated with oil production, despite possessing resources that could be harnessed to meet some of the needs of the electricity and industrial sectors.

World Bank data indicates that Iraq and Algeria were among the top nine countries globally for gas flaring in 2025, highlighting the importance of developing the necessary infrastructure to capture and process the gas.

Iraq seeks to eliminate gas flaring entirely by the end of 2028 through the execution of various projects.

World.title: Saudi Arabia faces economic contraction as war woes mount
World.content:
Riyadh – Saudi Arabia, the world’s top oil exporter, faces a major economic contraction this year, the IMF said Tuesday, as deadly attacks by Yemen’s Houthis squeeze a country already suffering from the Middle East war.

Saudi Arabia’s GDP is expected to shrink by 3.3 percent, the International Monetary Fund said in its latest World Economic Outlook report, predicting a regional drop over Iran’s blockading of the Strait of Hormuz.

The report was compiled before 13 people were killed on Saturday — the deadliest attack in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade — during a series of lethal Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s international airport.

The kingdom was already facing headwinds from Iran’s chokehold on Hormuz, a vital shipping route for oil and gas, since the start of the Middle East war in February, when the US and Israel attacked Iran.

But the restart in July of Yemen’s frozen civil war, pitting a Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally-recognised government against the rival Houthis, has further roiled the kingdom and brought the fight to its own soil.

Houthi attacks have targeted Saudi oil facilities, oil tankers in the Red Sea — Saudi Arabia’s alternative export route — and transport hubs including airports.

Blasts resounded over the Saudi capital again late on Monday, with the Saudi coalition saying it had intercepted a Houthi missile and the group announcing it had once again targeted the airport, whose operations remain suspended.

In the evening, mobile phones received a government alert warning of a “hostile aerial threat”, before the announcement of the interception.

Saturday’s airport attack prompted US President Donald Trump to say he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis, after having reportedly rebuffed previous requests for help from the kingdom.

– Houthi warning –

The Houthis warned the US against intervention, with political bureau member Mohammed Al Bukhaiti telling AFP they would target American interests in the region.

Bukhaiti said the purpose of the campaign against Saudi targets was to send a message to the crown prince “that he can no longer wage aggression against Yemen from a safe position”.

Riyadh’s coalition has supported Yemen’s government militarily since 2015, in a long-running civil war that has created a deeply entrenched humanitarian crisis in the impoverished country.

In its latest global report, the IMF said the regional economy was projected to contract by 0.3 percent this year, compared to its projected 1.9 percent growth six months ago.

It cited “a longer closure of the Strait of Hormuz, compared with the baseline assumptions in the April” report, predicting a major rebound in 2027 based on the expected reopening of the waterway.

Since the Middle East war began in late February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, Tehran has sought to impose its control over the Strait of Hormuz, repeatedly attacking ships that transit without its authorisation.

The US has imposed its own counter-blockade on Iranian ports, and has escorted friendly ships through the waterway in increasing numbers.

The fund noted that Saudi Arabia is among the least affected exporters in the region, pointing to “an economy with more diversified export routes”.

Saudi Arabia has made use of its East-West oil pipeline to bypass the Hormuz strait and send crude to its Red Sea coast.

However, the pipeline was temporarily shut in September after it was hit by strikes blamed on Iran-backed groups in Iraq.

World.title: Trump says does not believe China, Russia helping Iran
World.content:
Washington – US President Donald Trump said on Monday that he does not believe that China and Russia are helping Iran, adding that they have “too much to lose.”

Trump has faced pressure over reports that Chinese and Russian entities have supplied Iran with intelligence for attacks on US troops.

Responding to comments that China and Russia are helping Iran, Trump said in a post on Truth Social: “If they are, it’s at a very low level, but I don’t believe they are at all.”

“They have too much to lose, and we would know about it, and know about it very fast!” he added.

Trump said in July that he did not believe China and Russia were selling weapons to Iran, warning that “it would be very bad for them” if they did.

China and Russia both maintain strong ties with Iran but have refrained from getting directly involved in the Middle East war, which began with US-Israeli strikes on February 28.

Since the outbreak of the war, Russia has sent humanitarian aid to Iran, but has otherwise not officially announced any concrete assistance.

The Kremlin has denied US media reports claiming that Moscow passed sensitive intelligence to Iran, including the locations of US warships and aircraft in the region.

China has sharply condemned US and Israeli strikes while also criticizing Iranian attacks on Gulf states and the blocking of the Strait of Hormuz.

China has previously supplied Iran with drones as well as equipment that can be used for both civilian and military purposes.

Beijing has denied reports that the country’s top semiconductor firm, Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation, has sent chipmaking tools to Iran.

China and Russia have also been accused of helping Iran circumvent international sanctions targeting its oil sales.

Trump has frequently taken a more deferential tone toward Chinese President Xi Jinping and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin than he has toward some of Washington’s own allies, saying that they must be respected as the leaders of major world powers.

World.title: Formula One to return to Africa in ‘early 2030s’ in Rwanda
World.content:
Paris – Rwanda will host Africa’s first Formula One Grand Prix since 1993 in “the early 2030s” after the circuit announced a decade-long deal with the country on Tuesday.

The East African nation has been chasing a Grand Prix race for years, having already used football, basketball and other sports to enhance its image and attract investment.

President Paul Kagame formally announced the bid when Rwanda hosted a gathering of the FIA in December 2024.

The last time an F1 race was held in Africa was the 33rd South African Grand Prix, won by Alain Prost 33 years ago.

The first African Grand Prix in Rwanda will take place “once a new purpose-built circuit in Bugesera, Rwanda, has been completed”, F1 said in a statement.

“Today is a landmark moment for Formula One,” F1 president Stefano Domenicali added.

“With Rwanda joining the calendar from the next decade, our sport will race in every inhabited continent, bringing the world championship closer than ever to fans around the globe.

“Africa has always been part of Formula One’s future, and from the beginning we were determined to return in the right way, with the right partner, a long-term commitment and a clear vision for creating meaningful impact.”

A landlocked country still widely associated with a horrific genocide in 1994, Rwanda has used sports to revamp its image, attract tourists and impress investors with its organisational efficiency.

It has spent lavishly on football sponsorship deals with clubs including Arsenal and Paris Saint-Germain, partnered with the NBA to be the main hub of its African basketball league, and hosted last year’s cycling world championships.

– ‘Today belongs to Africa’ –

Critics have called this “sports-washing” — using glitzy events to distract from accusations of serious human rights abuses, including a brutal crackdown on any opposition or dissent.

Others see that as Western hypocrisy, arguing that no one described this year’s World Cup in the United States as “sports-washing”, despite the country’s rights abuses.

“Today belongs to Africa,” said Kagame.

“For more than three decades, the world’s premier motorsport championship has raced without this continent, and that changes with this agreement.”

The announcement will delight one of F1’s biggest stars, Lewis Hamilton.

The seven-time world champion has long called for an African stop on the F1 circuit, backing Rwanda’s plans in 2024 and calling the country “one of my favourite places”.

South Africa had also been bidding to host an F1 race, and its sports minister emphasised last week that it should not be ruled out.

“(Rwanda) have worked on it longer than (South Africa) and deserve it,” South Africa’s sports minister Gayton McKenzie posted on X last Thursday after the expected Rwanda deal was reported.

“Remember though that one country, Italy, has had two F1s a year, and some react like a continent of 55 countries can only get one.” He predicted that “SA will get F1, even before 2030.”

World.title: IMF projects Iraq’s economy to contract by 16% in 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The International Monetary Fund (IMF) forecasts a 16 percent contraction in Iraq’s real GDP in 2026, followed by a 19 percent growth in 2027, according to statistics from the October 2026 World Economic Outlook report.

Estimates indicate rising inflation and a widening current account deficit in 2026.

Iraq’s economy fell by 0.4 percent in 2025. Meanwhile, the IMF forecasts a 3.5 percent inflation rate in 2026, compared to 0.3 percent in 2025, before falling to three percent in 2027.

The IMF predicts Iraq will have a deficit of 10.8 percent of GDP in 2026, up from 3.8 percent in 2025, before moving to a 2.2 percent surplus in 2027.

According to these predictions, Iraq is one of the region’s oil-exporting economies that will decline in 2026; the numbers show a 3.8 percent contraction for these oil exporters, followed by 7.4 percent growth in 2027.

According to the analysis, Saudi Arabia’s real GDP would fall by 3.3 percent, the UAE’s by 3.9 percent, Qatar’s by 15.6 percent, and Kuwait’s by 16.7 percent in 2026, before rising again in 2027.

Figures for Iraq show a sharp contrast between the 2026 and 2027 predictions, with the economy transitioning from severe decline to solid growth—according to the IMF.

The projected growth in 2027 does not imply an increase in living standards or household financial situations, as these metrics are still dependent on other factors such as employment possibilities, income levels, inflation, and public finance performance.

World.title: ‘No choice’: IMF says developing countries must cut spending despite war shock
World.content:
Bangkok – The International Monetary Fund warned on Tuesday that while low-income developing countries were dealing with the disproportionate impacts of the Iran war-fuelled energy shock, many had “no choice” but to cut spending or potentially face debt restructuring.

Speaking to AFP on the sidelines of the organisation’s Annual Meetings in Bangkok, IMF deputy director of research Petya Koeva Brooks said heavily indebted, oil-importing countries were facing the worst of the energy shock, and had difficult choices in helping their citizens through the crisis.

“Unfortunately, after years of the global economy being hit (by) shock after shock, debt levels have increased quite a lot, and at the same time, inflation has become a problem,” she said.

The US war on Iran has plunged the Middle East into conflict and sent global energy prices soaring, as Tehran’s retaliatory action targeted Washington’s Gulf allies and curtailed oil and gas supplies.

Those prices have begun to bleed into other goods, with the crisis also having an effect on crucial fertiliser supplies.

The IMF has called on countries to offer narrow, targeted subsidies in the wake of the crisis, while also recommending all governments work to rebuild fiscal buffers and address rising debt after years of fighting economic shocks since the pandemic.

“Our messages indeed apply to most countries, but again, the trade-offs and the choices that have to be made are much more difficult for the most vulnerable countries,” Koeva Brooks said.

The IMF’s World Economic Outlook, released on Tuesday, identified low-income developing countries that are net oil importers and are not exposed to the ongoing artificial intelligence technology investment boom as being the most vulnerable to the shocks from the Iran war.

“For those countries that are most vulnerable, this is where the consumption basket is heavily weighted towards energy and food, and so indeed it is much much more difficult,” she said.

“But unfortunately there is no other choice.”

The senior IMF official added that “many” low-income countries were in debt distress, or close to it, and that they should seek debt restructuring if they were not able to address the issue.

“Where debt is not sustainable, then resolving that debt and having orderly and timely restructuring is always better than waiting, because then the cost of restructuring down the road is going to be much higher,” she said.

– ‘Domino effect’ –

In its World Economic Outlook, the IMF raised its forecast for 2026 global growth, largely on the back of advanced economies enjoying a boost from AI-related investments and economic activity.

Growth outcomes were highly uneven across economies, depending on their exposure to the war and whether they were integrated into AI supply chains.

The world’s advanced economies were forecast to grow 2.1 percent in 2026, with those in the AI supply chain such as Taiwan and South Korea posting significantly higher figures.

Koeva Brooks told AFP that if AI investment activity were to slow, the world economy “would see a negative impact on output, not only in advanced countries like the US but again through trade linkages also in Asia”.

In the IMF’s worst-case scenario — of AI not delivering promised productivity gains — global GDP forecasts for 2028 would fall by as much as 0.4 percent.

Climate-related risks were another key part of the World Economic Outlook this year, and Koeva Brooks told AFP that some of the effects of a particularly intense El Niño phenomenon had already been taken into account in higher prices for certain food items.

The warming phase of a natural climate cycle, El Niño raises sea temperatures in the tropical Pacific, triggering changes in weather that can increase the risk of drought and flooding, and exacerbate man-made global warming.

“We have a significant increase in beverage prices, in the prices of rice, and so on,” said Koeva Brooks. “Of course, it could turn out that the domino effect is even bigger than what we currently have.”

NEW DELHI: Zydus Lifesciences and Formycon AG, an independent developer of biosimilars, jointly announced that the US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) has accepted for review the biologics license application (BLA) for a proposed biosimilar to Merckâs Keytruda (pembrolizumab), a key cancer drug. Keytruda is the worldâs best-selling biologic medicine with global sales at $16.4 billion for the first half this year, and over $31 billion in 2025.This could be the first publicly announced acceptance by the USFDA of the application for a Keytruda biosimilar, FYB206, according to the company.The BLA was submitted in the third quarter of 2026.Under the Biosimilar User Fee Amendments, the USFDA aims to complete its review within twelve months of submission, comprising up to 60 days for the filing review and 10 months for the substantive review. TMC MP Saket Gokhale alleged that a drug addict had reached Banerjeeâs residence and attempted to attack her with a knife. He questioned the security arrangements for the former chief minister, who has Z+ category security cover.

World.title: Omair Ahmad on Love, Loss and the Lingering Spirit of Lucknow
World.content:
Q: How did this book come about?

A:

Q: It is a form of storytelling which is disappearing as we are moving more and more into very nuclear and urban families.

A:

Q: There's a sentence you use: Memories are such flimsy things.

A:

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Omair Ahmad is the author of âEncountersâ, âThe Storyteller's Taleâ, âTall Tales by a Small Dogâ, âThe Kingdom at the Centre of the World: Journeys Into Bhutanâ and âJimmy, The Terroristâ, which won the Crossword Award for Fiction and was shortlisted for the Man Asian Literary Prize. He is also a prominent columnist and a political and social commentator. In this conversation, he discusses his latest novel, âHomecomingâ. Excerpts:The genesis of this was when I was in DC. I just finished my second master's and I was missing home. Being a brown guy with a Muslim name in America, just when the war on terror was at its apogee leaves you a little off the place. And I hadn't been able to travel home since Iâd gone, which was in 2001. So I met this person, a friend, and she invited me to a book club and everyone was writing little bits and they asked me to write something. And so I wrote the beginning of this novella, which is no longer the beginning. Much has changed, everything has changed. But there is a strong emotion behind it and I think that has carried through even now... My wife says it's about love, loss and Lucknow. I've gone very much for mood and the feel of a place.So there's a bit of history, there's. But it's largely about people. So there's characters I've known, characters I've imagined, bits of stories that I've heard about Lucknow.This was one of those things that I really struggled with. The novel as a form is very much a product of the European enlightenment pathway. It has the individual at the centre... If you pick up most novels, it's a very narrow thing of who they are. But for me, as a product of this country, of this culture, I always wanted to know what's behind them. Because we always understand people as being part of this family, this mahalla, this web of relationships. No person just is a person standing on their own... They are so much more than a person. They're also part of the past. They're also part of the relationship in their environments... The idea of the novel as a European construct and the way that we communicate is sometimes different, and we think that that's wrong. But I think one of the things which I have improved on is I'm no longer very apologetic about that. This is who I am. This is who we are. This is how we tell our stories...We are multilingual people. We talk in lots of languages. Even like, say, the Urdu or Hindi that I use at home and on the street and with elders versus young. These are all almost different languages. The way we use them, trying to transpose that into any language.. you're really struggling, because the forms aren't there. There's no correct way to go about it... I know that while I'm writing in English, I'm not necessarily thinking in English when I'm writing. And I'm writing about people who will be only partially thinking in English, if at all, or speaking in it. And so it's guesswork. It's just trying to bully my way through somehow to make this language work like that.Things are clearer in our memories than they were in real life. And if you ever had an argument with anybody, you know this true. Because in your memory, your argument is very clear. And in their memory, the argument is very clear. The reality is it was never clear. It was always messy.But there is truth there. And memory is important for us, especially as a country where so much of our history is actually oral history. And so much of our history has been badly reinterpreted by colonial administrators for their own design, and that we have swallowed wholesale. And then we spend our whole time... like how you take fish bones out once you've taken a bite... But I struggle with this because I don't know what is true in all of this. And I wanted to register that little thing that, yes, we think our memories are clearer than what is recorded, but should we be that trusting of our own memories or other people's memories as well?

World.title: Karnataka sets 2030 goal to strengthen disaster prevention and resilience
World.content:
Karnataka deputy chief minister G Parameshwara announced a 2030 target for the state to emerge as a national leader in disaster prevention and preparedness.

Focus on risk assessment and resilient infrastructure

Departments urged to strengthen coordination

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Livelihood protection to remain a priority

Karnataka deputy chief minister G Parameshwara on Tuesday announced a 2030 target for the state to emerge as a national leader in disaster prevention and preparedness, stressing the need to make risk reduction an integral part of governance and development planning.Speaking at the inaugural meeting of the state platform for disaster risk reduction, held on the International day for disaster risk reduction, he said preventing disasters, safeguarding livelihoods and building long-term resilience must be key priorities for the state.Parameshwara said development should not be judged merely by investment, infrastructure creation or economic growth, but also by the extent to which people's lives and livelihoods are protected. Floods, droughts and landslides can wipe out homes, agricultural produce and livelihoods built over many years, he pointed out.âFor a government, a disaster may be an administrative emergency. For an affected family, it can mean a lifetime of hardship,â he said, calling for a shift from post-disaster relief and rehabilitation towards preventing avoidable damage and loss.Referring to the United Nations' sendai framework for disaster risk reduction 2015-2030, Parameshwara said Karnataka must improve risk assessment, early warning mechanisms, disaster preparedness and investment in resilient infrastructure.He noted that the state faces multiple hazards, including droughts, floods, landslides across the Western Ghats and threats to coastal communities. Rapid urbanisation, changing land-use patterns and growing pressure on natural drainage systems have further heightened disaster risks, he added.The deputy chief minister called for comprehensive disaster risk assessments of major public infrastructure projects. He urged government departments to identify vulnerable assets and incorporate risk-reduction measures into their annual plans and budgets.He said the revenue department, working through the Karnataka state disaster management authority and district administrations, should strengthen disaster planning, vulnerability assessments, coordination of early warnings and measures to protect livelihoods.Emphasising the need for coordinated action across departments, Parameshwara said the urban development department should prioritise flood prevention and drainage management, while the rural development department must improve disaster preparedness at the village level.The agriculture, education and health departments, he said, should focus on protecting farmers, schools, hospitals and essential services during emergencies.He also called for wider adoption of technology, including satellite imagery, geospatial data, artificial intelligence and predictive analytics, to strengthen risk assessment and improve early warning systems.Merely issuing alerts would not be enough, he said, emphasising that warnings must reach vulnerable communities in time for people to take appropriate protective measures.Parameshwara advocated a people-centred disaster preparedness network linking scientific institutions, district administrations, gram panchayats and households.He stressed the importance of developing local preparedness plans, building community volunteer networks, identifying safe shelters and evacuation routes, and conducting regular mock drills, particularly in areas prone to disasters.Children, senior citizens, persons with disabilities and economically vulnerable households must receive special attention in disaster planning, he added.Highlighting the economic consequences of disasters, Parameshwara said disaster management efforts must account for the losses suffered by farmers, fishermen, small traders and daily-wage workers, rather than focusing only on damage to physical infrastructure.He said the Karnataka state disaster risk reduction roadmap 2025-2030 must be implemented through measurable targets, time-bound action plans, clearly assigned responsibilities for departments and regular monitoring.The state platform for disaster risk reduction, he added, should concentrate on tangible improvements, including stronger infrastructure, uninterrupted essential services and timely assistance for families affected by disasters.

World.title: Sunak meets Modi, hails his leadership as UK-India ties go ‘from strength to strength’
World.content:
Former UK prime minister

met Prime Minister

in New Delhi on Tuesday and congratulated him on completing 25 years in public service. Praising PM Modiâs commitment and work ethic, Sunak said the UK-India relationship was going from âstrength to strengthâ under his leadership.

In a post on X, Sunak recalled working with PM Modi during his tenure as prime minister and highlighted the importance of closer cooperation between the two countries in trade, technology and artificial intelligence (AI).

âPrime Minister Narendra Modi great to see you in New Delhi today. Congratulations on 25 years in public service, a remarkable achievement. It was a pleasure to work with you when I was Prime Minister,â Sunak wrote.

Praising Modiâs approach to public service, he added, âYour commitment, your work ethic, your energy is an example to us all.â

On bilateral ties, Sunak said, âThe UK India relationship is going from strength to strength under your leadership. Our two countries cooperating more on trade, tech and AI is vital in a less predictable world.â

He also expressed confidence in the future of the partnership, writing, âI know that Britain and India will continue to grow ever closer in the years ahead.â





Earlier on Tuesday, Sunak spoke about the changing global order and the growing ability of countries such as India and those in the Gulf to pursue independent foreign policy positions amid increasing geopolitical uncertainty.

Speaking at a panel discussion titled âThe End of Predictabilityâ at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum 2026 in New Delhi, Sunak said the world was moving away from the multilateral, rules-based framework that had shaped the global economy.

âWe all grew up investing in, operating in a multilateral rules-based framework, largely enforced by US President Trump is not a cause for that; he's a symptom of that, and the world that we're in now is one where we don't quite know what we've settled down to, and that creates an enormous amount of geopolitical uncertainty and indeed danger,â he said.

Sunak also described Chinaâs emergence as a strategic competitor to the United States as a significant shift.

âSo, China is a peer competitor for the US across economic, military, and technological domains. That is a new feature of the world economy,â he said.

Meanwhile, India and the UK have agreed to exchange annual data on the utilisation of tariff concessions under their Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA). The decision was taken at the 16th meeting of the India-UK Joint Economic and Trade Committee (JETCO) in New Delhi on Monday.

The annual data exchange is intended to support smoother implementation and help more businesses, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises, benefit from the pact.

World.title: ‘Get ready to lose 2029 polls’: Amit Shah warns Rahul Gandhi with Congress poll history
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union home minister

on Tuesday said Congress leader

should âintrospectâ rather than blame the Election Commission (EC) or the SIR exercise for the opposition partyâs electoral setbacks, citing its defeats in the recent byelections and the Gandhinagar Municipal Corporation polls.

"I also wish to ask Rahul ji: is this the result of an 'SIR'? You dismiss the popularity of the

and Modi ji by attributing it to an 'SIR'. You need to introspect," Shah said.

Shah also highlighted the Congress's continued poll losses in Gujarat, pointing to its defeat in the Gandhinagar Municipal Corporation polls, held in the state capital.

âIn a major state (Gujarat) where you (Rahul Gandhi) once held power, you have failed to win a single election in 41 years.

This is a matter that demands serious introspection on their (Congress') part,â the senior BJP leader added.

The home minister then listed the BJP's victories in the byelections to the Nandigram and Rejinagar assembly seats in West Bengal and the Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency in Assam, where the party's candidates won by large margins in last week's bypolls.

He also mentioned the Thattanchavady assembly seat in Puducherry, the byelection for which was won by the BJP's ally, the All India NR Congress.





"Recently, byelections were held in Assam, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry. I want to inform the people of the country today that the

Congress party

did not win a single seat. In Nagaon, the BJP candidate won by a margin of 1,42,000 votes, wresting the seat from the Congress. In Nandigram, the BJP candidate won with 76% of the vote, securing a massive lead of 1,22,000 votes. In Rejinagar, the BJP won by over 75,000 votes, snatching the seat from the Trinamool, while in Puducherry, the NDA candidate from ally AINRC won by 8,482 votes.

The Congress secured only 22% of the votes," Shah said.

He also predicted that the BJP-led NDA would secure a massive majority in the 2029 Lok Sabha polls and the Congress would suffer another "crushing defeat."

"I want to tell Rahul Gandhi that the people of this country have fully understood your strategy of shielding infiltrators under the guise of the SIR, and they will no longer fall for your ruses. I also wish to tell Shri Rahul and his associates to brace themselves for a crushing defeat in 2029.

The NDA is set to secure a massive majority in the 2029 general elections, and the Congress is headed for yet another defeat, its fourth consecutive loss," he remarked.

Shah's remarks came shortly after leaders of the Congress-led opposition INDIA bloc held a joint press conference at Rahul Gandhi's residence in New Delhi, where they vowed to continue their campaign for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the invalidation of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls over alleged irregularities in the exercise.

The Indian Express reported last month that the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, had raised objections at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions they claimed were taken without their knowledge, including those related to the SIR.

The report brought further scrutiny on Kumar, who has repeatedly been accused by the opposition of facilitating âvote choriâ (vote theft) in favour of the BJP since becoming CEC in 2025.

'Diabolical duo clearly rattled': Congress

Responding to Amit Shah, Congress MP Jairam Ramesh called him a "co-architect of vote-chorti" and claimed that both the home minister and Prime Minister Narendra Modi were "rattled seeing the surge of sentiment against them."

World.title: 'We've found missing head of 11th century Khajuraho Vishnu idol, will be restored soon': ASI chief
World.content:
Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) has found the missing head of an 11th-century Vishnu idol at Khajuraho, whose restoration became the subject of a recent controversy involving the Supreme Court, and plans to reattach it after expert examination.

ASI has also introduced a three-year deadline for archaeological excavations to curb delays in research and cut approval times for most conservation projects to 15-20 days, director general Yadubir Singh Rawat told TOI in an exclusive interview. He also revealed plans for a preliminary excavation at Ujjain's Vaishya Tekri, where a Buddhist stupa could be larger than Sanchi's, although its actual scale and significance remain to be established.

Controversy over the beheaded Vishnu idol at Khajuraho's Javari temple reached the Supreme Court last year when advocate Rakesh Dalal sought restoration, replacement or reconstruction of the seven-foot statue.

While dismissing the petition, then CJI BR Gavai had remarked, âGo and ask the deity itself to do something now.â

Though Gavai later clarified his remark in court and said he respects all religions and that his statement was taken out of context, his words drew criticism, and a lawyer subsequently attempted to throw a shoe at him inside the courtroom.





Rawat said the missing head had been found in an ASI store. âDuring a visit to Bhopal for the BRICS summit, I learnt that the statue's headâwhich had been kept in our storeâhad been found. The person in charge informed me that someone likely tried to break off the head to steal it but failed to do so. We are having experts examine it and will soon reattach it to the statue.â

On delays in archaeological research, Rawat said ASI had introduced a three-year timeframe for completing excavation projects, with permissions continuing automatically across financial years.

He acknowledged that some researchers showed enthusiasm during fieldwork but delayed finalising reports, holding up publication of findings.

ASI had also granted circle officers financial powers ranging from Rs 50 lakh to Rs 1 crore, reducing the need for approvals from HQ. Rawat said most annual conservation programmes now received clearance within 15-20 days, except those requiring expert consultation.

At Vaishya Tekri in Ujjain, a recent survey identified a cluster of Buddhist stupas and a water reservoir.

Rawat said the structures differed from Sanchi because they were built using unbaked bricks. The last excavation there took place in 1973.

ASI plans to begin with a limited vertical excavation to establish the site's significance before committing to a larger project estimated to cost Rs 60 crore. âThe true picture will only emerge after excavation. We will proceed only after confirming its significance, although the site already falls within a protected area,â Rawat said.

He said acquiring and excavating the entire site would require substantial resources, making preliminary investigation necessary to determine whether a full-scale project was justified.

On encroachments at protected monuments, Rawat questioned the continued reliance on a colonial-era list prepared under the Ancient Monuments Preservation Act of 1904.

âThe root of this problem lies in the list prepared by British rulers in 1904 under the âAncient Monuments Preservation Actââa list that the then-central govt adopted post-independence without any review.

The British had included cemeteries and graves of their obscure soldiers, horses, mules, and petsâwhich they deemed highly significantâamong the monuments protected by the ASI. Before adopting that list, a review should have been conducted to determine what was truly important in the national interest,â he said.

Rawat said a review in 1953 incorporated state monuments into a definitive list, but the central list remained unchanged.

The resulting difficulties eventually led to 17 monuments being removed from it.

Explaining disparities in funding, he said allocations depended on visitor numbers, maintenance requirements, security expenses and public facilities. Taj Mahal and Red Fort, he said, served as showcases for ASI, while Taj Mahal's maintenance required substantial expenditure because of its delicate structure and heavy tourist footfall.

ASI paid around Rs 3 crore monthly for more than 200 CISF personnel deployed there.

Rawat acknowledged that lesser-known monuments, including the pyramid-like Bhim ki Gada structure in Bareilly, had received inadequate attention. He said ASI circles had been instructed to prepare conservation and tourism development proposals for such sites.

On skeletal remains excavated at Rakhigarhi in Haryana, Rawat said ASI had signed an MoU with Anthropological Survey of India and Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences.

ASI would lead the project, while the two institutes would examine the remains to determine physical characteristics, age, diet, diseases, sex and other details. A one-year deadline had been set for submitting the report.

For Uttarakhand, Rawat outlined plans to trace the historic walking route from Rishikesh to Badrinath and Kedarnath along the left bank of Alaknanda river.

Ancient markers or surviving remains could provide information about travel and settlement patterns.

World.title: 'Lady hiding in Dehradun': Who was Rahul Gandhi referring to at INDIA bloc presser?
World.content:
NEW DELHI: âIt is our commitment to you that the people who have done this, Mr. Modi, Mr. Shah, Mr. Gyanesh Kumar, the lady who's hiding right now in Dehradun, and others are going to be brought to justice," Rahul Gandhi said announcing a united INDIA bloc's resolve to continue its agitation against alleged SIR irregularities.

A day after the INDIA bloc's high-voltage protest march against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral irregularities, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi hosted a high tea for opposition leaders at his residence. Following the meeting, INDIA bloc leaders addressed a press conference.

"Yesterday, you saw an expression not of the political party standing here, but an expression of the people of India...We

would like to thank the people of Delhi, the people of India, who stood with us against what is being done. This is not about us. This is about the people of India," Rahul said.

But then who was the 'lady hiding right now in Dehradun' whom the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha was referring to in his statement?

Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders have been relentless in their attacks on the Prime Minister and the Union home minister, but it was his reference to a 'lady hiding in Dehradun' that added an element of mystery to the press conference.





Was the Congress leader referring to Seema Khanna, the Election Commission's Director General (IT), whose name has figured in opposition allegations of 'vote theft'?

There is no confirmation that Khanna is the woman Rahul was referring to. The Congress leader did not identify her, and there is no independently verified information linking her to Dehradun. However, her name has repeatedly surfaced in allegations raised by opposition leaders against CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

Why is Seema Khanna's name in the controversy?

Khanna's name came into focus following a report by The Indian Express, which said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Among the concerns raised was the growing centralisation of control over electoral-roll software and restrictions on the powers of Electoral Registration Officers (EROs), who are legally responsible for maintaining voter lists.

The controversy centred on the Election Commission's digital systems, including ERONet and ECINet, which are used to manage electoral rolls and election-related services. ECINet is a unified digital platform developed by the Election Commission to streamline electoral processes and improve transparency and accessibility.

The investigation raised questions about whether local election officials had adequate access to make corrections, restore voters' names and exercise their statutory powers, or whether some of these functions had become concentrated within the Commission's IT department headed by Khanna.

Last month, Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra filed a police complaint against CEC Gyanesh Kumar at Delhi's Parliament Street Police Station, alleging procedural violations, unilateral decision-making and manipulation of electoral rolls.

Speaking to ANI, Moitra directly named Khanna while accusing the Election Commission of manipulating voter lists through its software.

"Very important things like the crores of new voters were not being allowed to come on the list because of the addition of a new question on Form 6, the new voters list.

And we now find that the two other election commissioners had said this is completely illegal; still, the question linking parentage was put in," Mahua Moitra had said.

"We find how the EROs and the BLOs and the ground-level officials were not kept in the loop and denied access to the software, and Seema Khanna, who was DGIT, along with Gyanesh Kumar, played with the software from the back end to manipulate voter lists while keeping EROs and block-level officials in the dark.

This is a very serious charge," she alleged.

She also questioned changes to Form 6, used for registering new voters, and alleged that 33 lakh valid voters in West Bengal had been kept off the electoral rolls through questionable appeals.

Moitra argued that decisions taken without the consent of the other two Election Commissioners could not be treated as decisions of the full Commission. These allegations have not been established.

The Election Commission, however, has maintained that differing views among its commissioners are part of the decision-making process and that its decisions were unanimous. It has also described ECINet as a unified platform intended to improve electoral services.

While Khanna's name has repeatedly figured in the wider controversy, there is still no confirmation that she was the woman Rahul Gandhi referred to during Tuesday's press conference.

World.title: Koodathil case: Crime Branch uncovers crucial evidence in mysterious death of Jayamadhavan Nair
World.content:
The Thiruvananthapuram District Crime Branch probe into the mysterious death of Jayamadhavan Nair of the Koodathil family in Kalady, near Karamana, nine years ago, has found crucial evidence against the family’s former caretaker, Raveendran Nair, the prime accused in the case. The deaths of the members of the Koodathil family over a period of 26 years from 1991 had piqued interest, considering its eerie resemblance with the Koodathayi serial murder case in which a woman had allegedly murdered six people in Kozhikode over a span of 14 years.

Jayamadhavan Nair was brought unconscious to the Thiruvananthapuram Government Medical College Hospital on April 2, 2017, and his death was subsequently confirmed. In the subsequent investigation, the police found discrepancies in statements regarding the time of his death as well as the manner in which the body was brought to the hospital.

During an examination conducted with the assistance of medical and forensic experts, bloodstains were found on a cot and a piece of wood in the house. These were confirmed to be human blood, and crucial details were obtained through comparative testing with a blood sample from a relative of the deceased.

The histopathology report revealed that a head injury was the cause of death. Besides, a report from the Biomechanics department of National Institute of Technology (NIT) Calicut confirmed that the head injury suffered by Jayamadhavan Nair was not caused by a fall.

Jayamadhavan Nair’s bloodstains were also found during an examination of the car belonging to Anil, a friend of Raveendran Nair and another accused in the case. The vehicle was found to have been used to transport the body to the hospital. The investigation revealed that the car was driven by a person named Saju. The investigation also examined the complaint alleging that Raveendran Nair had prepared a forged will in order to usurp Jayamadhavan Nair’s properties. Forensic examination revealed the signature on the will did not belong to the deceased.

On the basis of such findings, the investigation team intensified the probe against Raveendran Nair by evaluating medical reports, forensic evidence, witness statements and other investigative findings. Scientific tests, including Brain Electrical Oscillation Signature (BEOS) profiling, were also conducted. The medical opinion that head injury and asphyxiation caused the death was also considered during the investigation.

The Crime Branch investigation found that the motive behind the murder was the accused’s intent to usurp properties worth crores of rupees. The crime was also driven by hostility over the fear that if the unmarried Jayamadhavan Nair were to marry, another legal heir would emerge for the properties claimed under the forged will. The crucial findings were uncovered by the investigation team comprising City Crime Branch Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) M.I. Shaji, Sub-Inspector Bipin Prakash, Assistant Sub-Inspector Jayakumar, and senior civil police officer Prathapan.

World.title: 100 cases, a milestone in minimally invasive spine care
World.content:
Experts at Sri Ramachandra Medical Centre described the advantages of awake spine surgery using percutaneous and endoscopic techniques.

Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, Karthik Kailash, professor and HoD, Spine Surgery, Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education and Research, said: “We have completed 100 cases. This is an important milestone for our institution. What makes this achievement particularly meaningful is our ability to offer spinal fusion procedures to selected high-risk patients without the need for conventional general anaesthesia. High-tech surgery should reach everybody. The awake spine surgery concept is used in foreign countries such as the U.S. We do the surgery when the patient is awake, particularly for high-risk patients who are unable to walk. We are able to operate and discharge them the next day.”

G. Sudhir, Senior Consultant Spine Surgeon, SRIHER, said: “The same day we make the patient walk. Bone damage and muscle damage are minimal. Endoscopic spine procedures performed under awake spine surgery represent an evolving approach to minimally invasive spinal care, combining the benefits of muscle-sparing surgical techniques with the potential advantages of avoiding general anaesthesia in appropriately selected patients. Awake spine surgery, using local anaesthesia with carefully titrated sedation, allows patients to remain responsive during selected stages of the procedure, facilitating real-time neurological assessment and communication with the surgical team.”

“In endoscopic spine fusion, through small keyhole incisions, specialised endoscopic instruments enable targeted removal of structures compressing the neural elements while minimising disruption to paraspinal muscles, ligaments, and surrounding tissues. Potential benefits include reduced postoperative pain and nausea, lower analgesic requirements, earlier mobilisation, shorter hospital stays, and faster functional recovery. Endoscopic spine procedures also offer the biggest advantage of enhanced magnification and visualisation of the neural structures, which is vital in preventing intraoperative complications,” said Dr. Sudhir.

Aruna Parameswari, HoD, Anaesthesiology, said: “There is no need for neuro monitoring, which is expensive. We just give a sedative dose, analgesic, so the patient is sleeping, if you call them, they will respond, but they won’t feel the pain. The role of anesthesiologist is as important in awake spine surgery as general anesthesia. The procedure is done with a combination of intravenous sedation and ultrasound guided fascial plane blocks with continuous monitoring of the patient’s vitals like ECG, blood pressure, oxygen saturation and capnography. It provides pain relief for 24 hours avoiding postoperative opioids, enabling early ambulation. It can be used in patients with cardiac and respiratory conditions that make them high risk for general anesthesia.”

World.title: AWHO moves HC against panel directive to take possession of Chanderkunj Army Towers in Kochi
World.content:
The Army Welfare Housing Organisation (AWHO) has challenged before the Kerala High Court an order of the committee led by the Ernakulam District Collector (DC Committee) directing the organisation to take possession of Chanderkunj Army Towers before their scheduled demolition.

A Single Bench of Justice P.V. Kunhikrishnan issued notice to the company that was awarded the contract to demolish the apartments and adjourned the matter to October 14 for further consideration.

The AWHO claimed that the towers and apartments were no longer under its ownership or possession and that it was not obligated to collect the keys from the owners.

The DC Committee had directed the organisation to take possession of the apartments from their respective owners by collecting the keys and issuing certificates in a prescribed format. The AWHO stated that the District Collector was about to enter into the demolition contract and that it had earlier been resolved that the Tahsildar would take over possession.

The organisation stated that accepting the keys and signing the prescribed certificates would expose it to serious legal complications and prejudice its interests in matters pending before other courts, including the Supreme Court, in connection with the apartment towers.

The AWHO also pointed out that the District Collector had affirmed before the Supreme Court that the Tahsildar was in the process of taking over possession of the apartments.

The High Court had directed the demolition and reconstruction of Chander Kunj Army Towers B and C, noting serious structural problems. The Kerala Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA) had also directed the AWHO to compensate certain apartment owners for the internal fixtures installed in their respective apartments.

The petition stated that disputes arising from these orders were pending before the Supreme Court and that accepting possession of the apartments would prejudice the AWHO’s interests in the pending litigation.

World.title: Alleged mobile snatcher caught by passengers, dragged alongside running train in Bihar’s Bhagalpur
World.content:
A mobile snatcher in the Bhagalpur district of Bihar was caught by the passengers when he made an attempt to allegedly snatch a mobile of a passenger from a running train.

The passengers caught the youth as he tried to snatch a mobile phone through the window of the moving train’s general coach and dragged him alongside the train for some distance. He eventually fell and sustained injuries when his grip slipped near the end of the platform. Passengers at the railway station also witnessed the incident.
